segs.text: MINUTES OF A WORKSHOP MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA APRIL 14, 2016 - 4:00 P.M. A workshop of the Town Council was called to order on April 14, 2016 at 4:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: LVJ10auTAM-A M 1 COUNCIL MEMBERS: TOWN CLERK: TOWN ATTORNEY: TOWN ENGINEER: TOWN BUILDING OFFICIAL: ROBERTO MARTELL JACK MORROW EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO SUSANA GUASCH ;1 : 1 I_iL\ 7_\7_1 STEPHEN HELFMAN JORGE CORZO RICHARD McCONACHIE The purpose of this workshop was to discuss the Unsolicited Proposal submitted by The Miami Sportscenter LLC, (MSC). Joseph Timpone and Brian Tuffin were present representing The Miami Sportscenter LLC, (MSC) for any questions if needed. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo stated that the property is a parcel of land recently acquired by the Town from FEC with no restrictions on it and it is located adjacent to the Medley Lakeside Retirement Park. It is zoned M-1 and consists of 4.8 acres. If the proposal is approved the Council has to correct the Master Plan as the area in question is Zoned Residential. The appraisal value of the land is $2.5 million with a market value of $1.7 million. The Town's parcel is one of three parcels to be acquired by the proposer for the project. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo stated that the Miami Sportscenter LLC, (MSC) proposes to construct a 3 -story, 489,367 SF Sports, Entertainment & Commercial Facility to include the following: Functional Athletic Training Areas: 292,000 SF or 60% of the total building area: Olympic size pool (164' x 64'); Hydrotherapy classes pool; Surf & Splash Zones; 2 Regulation size Ice Hockey Fields (85' x 200'); 1 Regulation size artificial football field; Basketball and Volleyball Courts; 2 Tennis Courts; and Fitness Center. Commercial & Office Space: 157,000 SF or 32% of the total building area: Class "A" Office Space; Pro -Shop; Sports Clinic and Restaurants. Mr. Timpone stated that they have already engaged the owners of the other two properties and Section 5, LLC has agreed to relocate their business and come into a long term lease for the property. The proposal for the Town property reflects a long term lease for ninety-nine years at an assessed rate of $1.00 per year. In exchange for the favorable lease, MSC will build at no cost to the Town of Medley a mixed use project combining Indoor Sports, Recreation Facilities, Class "A" Office Space, Sports themed Restaurant, Concessions, and also include an Orthopedic and Sports Medicine Clinic. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC INFORMATIONAL MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA APRIL 27, 2016 5:00 P.M. A Public Informational Meeting was called to order on April 27, 2016 at 5:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE -MAYOR: JACK MORROW COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO SUSANA GUASCH TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA (ABSENT) TOWN ATTORNEY: STEPHEN HELFMAN (ABSENT) LILLIAN ARANGO The purpose of this Public Informational Meeting was to discuss the Unsolicited Proposal submitted by The Miami Sportscenter LLC, (MSC). Joseph Timpone and Neida Reyes were present representing The Miami Sportscenter LLC, (MSC) for any questions if needed. Also, in attendance were: Jorge Corzo - Town Engineer; Olga Quin - Assistant to Town Engineer; Victoria Martinez Executive Assistant to the Mayor/Legal Department; and Mary Taylor Assistant Town Clerk. The Public Informational Meeting was held at the Lakeside Retirement Center located at 10601 N.W. 105 Way, Medley, Florida 33178. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo made a presentation in Spanish and English highlighting some of the details of the proposed project including but not limited to the project being indoors and having its own climate control. He also added that the security aspect is very important to the Town and that the lease with the Lakeside residents will not be affected in any way. He explained that the property in question is the recently acquired property known as "The Wetlands". He further explained that certain improvements will have to be done including the road and possibly a new bridge. It was mentioned that on Monday, May 2, 2016 the Town Council will consider and will make a determination on whether or not the Town owned Parcel will be leased for the proposed project. Mr. Corzo explained details of the project and guaranteed that the Town takes the residents comments very seriously and will consider benefits to the residents. Nothing in the project will impact the current lifestyle or the current living accommodations of the residents. Lakeside Resident Margarita De Jesus stated that not only the Council approves the project but the residents should have a say in it. Lakeside Resident Virgilio Lantigua asked "so the residents don't vote"? Town Engineer Jorge Corzo stated that for that reason the Public Information Meeting took place so that comments from the residents are received. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA August 17, 2016 1:00 P.M. A Public Meeting was called to order on August 17, 2016 at 1:00 p.m. The following were present: EMPLOYEE REPRESENTATIVE: FPE REPRESENTATIVE: FINANCE DIRECTOR: TOWN LABOR ATTORNEY MARY TAYLOR: VICTORIA MARTINEZ: CAMILO MARTIN JACQUELINE DELGADO WILLIE BAILEY ROY DANZIGER ALISON SMITH ASSISTANT TOWN CLERK EXECUTIVE ASST. TO TOWN ATTORNEY/ LEGAL DEPARTMENT The purpose of this Public Meeting is to discuss Labor Negotiations between the Town of Medley and the Federation of Public Employees (FPE). FPE Representative Willie Bailey stated that we should reiterate where the FPE and the Town left off. The Town moved as follows: Communications Officers: COLA Increase after eight (8) years OK with Town. Shift Differential Pay: Midnight Shift: $17.00 per week; Relief Shift: $12.00 per week; and Afternoon Shift: $9.50 per week. Retirement/Pension alignment with officers: No. Mr. Bailey stated that we would like to clarify the wage language. The original proposal was to address those employees who make less than $12.00 per hour and that is not a finance impact to the Town. Attorney Smith stated that it is not what was presented to the Council so we will have to go back to them. In the past, the language proposed has been for the first year of the contract only. If we go back to the Council to revisit wages again the results will not be favorable. Council approved a 3% COLA increase. Article #2 Stewards will be Ok to be paid for grievances but Town prefers that all negotiations be done after working hours so that all employees have the opportunity to attend. Both parties reviewed clauses on current and consented on the rest of the clauses with changes as negotiated. Signatures were exchanged as proof of mutual consent. Articles #5 & 6 Changes will be worked among Attorney and FPE Representative so that both parties don't have to come back to negotiation sessions. Wages Willie Bailey asked why would the Council object to the $0.35 increase. Attorney Smith stated that the Town feels they are more than generous with all the benefits they provide. Willie Bailey stated that he had a concern which is why the FPE presented the original proposal. segs.text: Resolution C-1457, which is to approve and accept the bid amount in excess of the official estimate for utility work pursuant to the utility work by Highway Contractor Agreement between the Town of Medley and the State of Florida Department of Transportation for adjustment and installation of utilities in connection with the N.W. 87 Avenue roadway project. Town Attorney Arango read Resolution C-1457, approving and accepting the bid amount in excess of the official estimate for utility work pursuant to the utility work by Highway Contractor Agreement between the Town of Medley and The State of Florida Department of Transportation for adjustment and installation of utilities in connection with the N.W. 87 Avenue Roadway Project. Town Attorney Arango stated that sometime in March 2015 by Resolution C-1305 the Town previously approved a utility work by Highway Contractor Agreement with FDOT. That Agreement provides for the FDOT contractor simultaneously with the road project to perform certain utility installations on behalf of the Town primarily the re -location of a 16" water main. Pursuant to that Agreement the FDOT did provide a very specific official estimate for the work which at the time was $1,467,865.00 and that amount included certain contingencies and allowances pursuant to the contract. The Town did deposit that amount into an escrow account with the State of Florida pending bidding of the job by FDOT. Recently FDOT did bid the overall road project which included as a portion this utility work and pursuant to that bid, eleven (11) bids were received for the overall road project and the bid for the utility portion of the work came in significantly higher than the official estimate the Town had approved. Therefore, the total increase is $527,515.52. That includes an increase on the actual bid or construction cost the car allowance which is for re -mediation environmental issues in the event something is found on the road and it also includes certain allowances for traffic, mobilization, construction engineering and administration. Pursuant to the Agreement that the Town has with FDOT they are required to notify us of the bid amount and if that bid amount exceeds the estimate which it does by more than 10% the Town has the ability and the election to then remove the utility work from the project if it so chooses or it can move forward and pay the additional amount that is due. segs.text: MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA FEBRUARY 1, 2016 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on February 1, 2016 at 7:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: VICE -MAYOR: COUNCIL MEMBERS: TOWN CLERK: TOWN ATTORNEY: ROBERTO MARTELL JACK MORROW EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO SUSANA GUASCH HERLINA TABOADA STEPHEN HELFMAN LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice -Mayor Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by Kasandra Milian and Deyana Morera from the Medley Police Department Explorers Post 67, the Town Council and audience. The Minutes of the Regular Meeting of December 1, 2015 were discussed and approved. Mayor Martell asked if anyone in the audience wanted to speak. No one came forward. The first item on the agenda was the presentation by Waste Management Florida, Inc. of a symbolic check on the amount given to the Town in 2015. Alex Gonzalez and Henry Sori were present. The symbolic check was in the amount of $1,452,424.00. Mr. Gonzalez then presented the Mayor and Council a check in the amount of $15,000.00 to the Town of Medley Foundation. Mayor Martell then called Mr. Bailey from the Federation of Public Employees. Mr. Bailey stated that he wants to meet with the Mayor and Council on an item that was on the October 19, 2015 agenda regarding Longevity Bonuses. He stated that he wanted fair benefits for all employees and wants to sit down and meet with them to discuss the matter.

Town Engineer Jorge Corzo gave no verbal report on the ongoing Capital Projects. The request by Chief Said Jinete for Federal Forfeiture Funds was then discussed. She requested approval for the following: Communications furniture for new dispatch area on 1St floor ftom Office Express Supply, Inc. in the amount of $4,873.35. Councilperson Digiacomo moved to approve this expenditure. Councilperson Guasch seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Mayor Martell then requested for a discussion and action on modification to eligibility for Medical insurance for all part time employees. He stated that he would like for part time employees to have medical insurance after one (1) year of service instead of the current ten (10) year of service requirement. He stated that currently there are seven (7) part time employees that do not receive insurance. After a brief discussion Councilperson Guasch moved as follows: "TO GRANT ALL PART TIME EMPLOYEES MEDICAL INSURANCE AFTER ONE (1) YEAR OF SERVICE." Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Since there was no further business to be considered Councilperson Guasch moved to adjourn. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 8:09 p.m. on February 1, 2016. segs.text: MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 5, 2016 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 5, 2016 at 7:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: VICE -MAYOR: COUNCIL MEMBERS: C / [y11 l ifa STI ./] -0V.11" ] Rff= ROBERTO MARTELL JACK MORROW EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO SUSANA GUASCH DANIEL ESPINO The Invocation was given by Vice -Mayor Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by Odeni Ascunce and Josue Hernandez from the Medley Police Department Explorers Post 67, the Town Council and audience. . The Minutes of the Regular Meeting of June 6, 2016 7:00 p.m. were discussed and approved. The first item was the swear -in of a new Police Officer. Chief Said Jinete presented Guillermo Lagos to the Mayor and Council. Mr. Lagos is currently a Communications Officer. He was sworn in by Town Clerk Herlina Taboada. Councilperson Digiacomo moved to approve the swear -in of Guillermo Lagos. Councilperson Guasch seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Chief Said Jinete then presented Communications Officer Angela Arango to the Mayor and Council. Ms. Arango has been a Communications Officer with the City of Hialeah Gardens Police Department for almost (13) thirteen years. Councilperson Ayala moved as follows: "TO HIRE ANGELA ARANGO AS A FULL TIME COMMUNICATIONS OFFICER." Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The next item on the agenda was recognition to all of the Medley 2016 Graduating Seniors. Lizmari Valido then presented each graduating senior with a Certificate of Recognition and $250.00. They were: Amber Luna, Ashley Maldonado, Brian Porras, Yanesa Torres, Richard Alfonso, Telvis Hernandez, Victoria Perez and Yadira Rivero. The next item on the agenda was a discussion and action on the request by Baila Con Micho, Inc. for a Non -Exclusive License to use the Tobie Wilson Park facilities for their summer camp participants. Anais Gonzalez representing Baila Con Micho, Inc. was present and requested permission for her summer camp participants to use the Tobie Wilson Park playground. Councilperson Digiacomo then asked what exactly are they going to be doing. Ms. Gonzalez stated that several times a week they will be going to the Tobie Wilson Park playground for approximately (1) one hour. Councilperson Digiacomo asked if they were going to be transporting the kids from their location to the Tobie Wilson Park.

Mr. Corzo presented the Mayor and Council with a monthly report on all Town of Medley projects. He stated that he will continue to provide monthly updates on the status of each project and grants for informational purposes only. He specifically mentioned that the Park will be completed by mid August except for the lights. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that we would only be able to use the park during the day. Mr. Corzo also stated that the N.W. South River Drive Project received clearance from the Health Department and will be able to start on the drainage work sometime next week. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA July 19, 2016-2:00 P.M. A Public Meeting was called to order on June 19, 2016 at 2:00 p.m. The following were present: EMPLOYEE REPRESENTATIVE: FPE REPRESENTATIVE: FINANCE DIRECTOR: TOWN LABOR ATTORNEY VAr_vffiaIF-Ayjtel ; VICTORIA MARTINEZ: CAMILO MARTIN JACQUELINE DELGADO WILLIE BAILEY ROY DANZIGER ALISON SMITH ASSISTANT TOWN CLERK EXECUTIVE ASST. TO TOWN ATTORNEY/ LEGAL DEPARTMENT The purpose of this Public Meeting is to discuss Labor Negotiations between the Town of Medley and the Federation of Public Employees (FPE). FPE Representative Willie Bailey asked if the Town had the opportunity to review the FPE's counter proposal. He stated that the FPE also had a new proposal from the Communications Officers. Town's counter proposal is as follows: Article #2 Union Representation - Negotiations No; Grievances Yes. Town's rationale is to give every employee the opportunity to attend negotiations if scheduled after hours . Article #10 Grievances and Arbitration Procedures - Council wants to keep it as is. Article #11 Section 2 To be corrected to show current practice four (4) days ten (10) hours a day and Monday Wednesday 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Thursday 7:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m and add "or as determined by the Town". Article 11 - Section 1: Town noticed that Social Services Department is not listed. Another change is to add the Code Compliance Department to the last sentence as it would pertain to the operations of the Code Compliance Department . Article #24 Health Insurance Needs clarification. Article #25 Uniforms Boot allowance is O.K. as proposed by the FPE. Article #26 Wages Town is O.K. with 3% but not with the $1.00 increase to the certification/license benefit proposed. The Town feels the increase would benefit every employee instead of the certification/license proposal that applies to only a hand full of employees. Actual language for set wages was given to Mr. Bailey and is as follows: Effective 10-01-2016 employees with a current base hourly wage less than $ 10.00 per hour will receive a base hourly increase of $ .50. Effective 10-01-2016 employees with a base hourly wage between $ 10.00 per hour and $ 12.00 per hour will receive an increase of $ .35 or an amount necessary to increase their base hourly wage to $ 12.00, whichever is less. In addition, after this adjustment, effective 10-01-2016 all employees shall receive a 3% increase to their base hourly wage. The $ .50 and $ .35 wage in

segs.head: Article #11 OK with Town's language.
segs.text: Article #11 OK with Town's language. Article #25 Uniforms OK Article #26 Wages OK with 3% Cola increase. Nothing else is changing. Town does not want to add any additional certifications. OK with language provided by the Town about those employees who make less than $12.00 per hour. Article #12 OK with leaving as is. New job classifications to be added: Public Works Laborer II - $12.50 to $17.00 per hour; Building/Zoning Licensing Clerk II - $17.00 to $25.00 per hour; Senior Licensing Clerk - $28.00 to $36.00 per hour and Jet Vactor Operator - $12.50 to $17.50 per hour. Effective upon ratification of agreement. The next scheduled meeting will be held on August 17, 2016 at 1:00 p.m. Since there was no further business to be considered the meeting was adjourned at 3:25 p.m. Victoria Martinez, In absence of Herlina Taboada, Town Clerk

segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 25, 2016 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 25, 2016 at 5:15 p.m.
votes: Mayor Morrow then moved as follows: "TO ADOPT A TENTATIVE MILLAGE RATE OF 5.700 MILLS FOR THE FISCAL YEAR BEGINNING OCTOBER 1, 2016 AND ENDING SEPTEMBE 30,2017". Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 25, 2016 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 25, 2016 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: VICE -MAYOR: COUNCIL MEMBERS: TOWN CLERK: TOWN ATTORNEY: ROBERTO MARTELL JACK MORROW EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO SUSANA GUASCH HERLINA TABOADA STEPHEN HELFMAN The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Vice -Mayor Morrow announced that Alfredo Leon's grandmother had passed and prayed for his family. The Mayor announced that the purpose of this special meeting was to have a discussion on the proposed Budget for the fiscal year October 1, 2016 through September 30, 2017; and to discuss and establish the proposed tentative millage rate based upon the Certification of Taxable Value of real and personal property within the Town of Medley for the fiscal year October 1, 2016 through September 30, 2017. Proper notice had been given. Mayor Martell then asked Finance Director Roy Danziger to proceed with the Budget. Roy stated that he had submitted a budget package to the Mayor and Council with a millage rate of 5.700 mills with a rolled back millage rate of 5.0765. He explained the Budget page by page, and no major changes were made. He also stated that the Town will have approximately a $4.4 million deficit for the next two (2) years which will be covered by reserves or the Town can raise the millage rate and that would be up to the Council to decide. Once the millage is set it can be lowered but it cannot be raised. Roy stated that the proposed budget includes a 3% salary increase for all employees except for the Police Officers salary which can increase from 2.50% to 6.50%. The total estimated payroll for year 2016/2017 is approximately $7.5 million. Medical insurance is estimated an increase of 8% which is approximately $2 million. Pension expense including General Employees and Police is approximately $2 million. The estimated General Fund Capital Expenditures for two (2) years 2015/2017 is approximately $8.7 million. Estimated net loss for the Water Department for year 2016/2017 is approximately $404,000.00. Estimated Capital Expenditures for Water Department for years 2015/2017 is approximately $5.8 million. Estimated reserves for the Water Department for year ending 09/30/2017 is approximately $3.6 million. Estimated Revenue for Storm

Lizmari stated that there are two (2) pick up locations one at Tobie Wilson Park and the other at Lakeside Retirement Park. That is why they switch busses in order for the Town to take them home. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that they have to move from one bus to the other with their groceries. Lizmari said yes. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that it is a hassle for the residents to come in and out of the bus and carry their groceries. She asked if there is something the Town can do so they don't have to change busses. Finance Director Roy Danziger stated that the Town is following the County's rules but he will speak with the County to see what can be done. A Public Meeting was called to order on June 22, 2016 at 10:00 a.m. The following were present: EMPLOYEE REPRESENTATIVE FPE REPRESENTATIVE: FINANCE DIRECTOR: TOWN LABOR ATTORNEY MARY TAYLOR: VICTORIA MARTINEZ: CAMILO MARTIN JACQUELINE DELGADO WILLIE BAILEY ROY DANZIGER ALISON SMITH ASSISTANT TOWN CLERK EXECUTIVE ASST. TO TOWN ATTORNEY/ LEGAL DEPARTMENT The purpose of this Public Meeting is to discuss Labor Negotiations between the Town of Medley and the Federation of Public Employees (FPE). Attorney Alison Smith mentioned that at the last meeting the FPE did not have the opportunity to add some items and the Town wanted to give the FPE the opportunity to add said items should they need to. FPE Representative Willie Bailey suggested going over the items they had proposed first from the last meeting and then we can visit. The articles of the Agreement were addressed as follows: Article #2 Union Representation: Section 5 and 7: The Town proposes that all bargaining sessions be done after working hours. Also, the Town rejects to compensate representatives for grievances procedures, predetermination hearings and any other meetings that warrant the presence of onsite stewards. Article #11 Section 1 To strike 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Mr. Bailey stated that it needs to be corrected to show the current schedule. Alison Smith asked what exactly does the FPE propose? Willie Bailey stated that he is willing to work on some language so the Town and the FPE are in agreement. Article #19 Section 1 Bereavement Leave The Town currently gives 5 days of bereavement leave. The Town also wants the language to read "Registered Court Partners". Willie Bailey stated he is O.K. with that. Article #24 Health Insurance The Town's current medical policy already provides a discount towards what is asked. In addition, this information is provided to all the employees during open enrollment period every year. Roy Danziger will sit down with Morris & Reynolds (Agent) to come back with exact coverage and details as requested by FPE representatives. Article #25 Uniforms Boot allowance proposal is accepted by the Town. Town proposes allowance to Blue Collar employees to be reduced from $700.00 to $500.00. FPE will respond next time. A Public Informational Meeting/Workshop was called to order on June 22, 2016 at 5:00 p.m. The following were present: TOWN ENGINEER: UTILITIES DIRECTOR: PROJECT MANAGER: VICTORIA MARTINEZ: JORGESOTO BARTON FYE- KIMLEY HORN & ASSOC. EXECUTIVE ASST. TO TOWN ATTORNEY/ LEGAL DEPARTMENT The purpose of this Public Meeting/Workshop on N.W. 89 Avenue and N.W. 93 Street Road Improvements Project (FMA -South), also known as Town of Medley project #SW -0103 is to provide an opportunity to discuss with Town staff and project consultants proposed improvements and gather information from the public or any other interested organization regarding benefits and concerns/impacts of said project. Said meeting was held at the Waste Management Facility 2nd Floor Training Room located at 8801 N.W. 93 Street, Medley, Florida 33178. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo stated that according to the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) the bidding will start in December. Construction is expected to begin in mid 2017. We will keep pressuring them. This is an ongoing effort by the Town on an area that is one of the worse areas. In 2015 we completed the first phase of the project in the other section of the Town which covered drainage and resurfacing of the roads. This project is a big approach as it includes widening of the roads as well as drainage. This will not eliminate the flooding issue but it is a start. N.W. 95 Street and N.W. 89 Avenue will have a widening of the road with 3 lane sections. N.W. 93 Street drainage will be resurfaced and portions of the road will be widened to 3 lanes. Areas of this project will have curb and gutter. Sidewalk will be available between the curb and gutter on one side. The total cost of the project is 3.3 million. 1 million is from Miami -Dade County, $150,000.00 from the Department of Environmental Protection and 2.15 million from the Stormwater Utility Funds. This project is not the ultimate solution to the flood issues but it is a step in stone. Minutes of Public Informational Meeting/Workshop of June 22, 2016 Someone from the public asked about the difference between resurfacing and reconstruction of the road. Mr. Corzo then explained that the reconstruction of the roads fixes wrong elevations while resurfacing addresses the pavement of the road. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MAY 17, 2016 10:00 A.M. A Public Meeting was called to order on May 17, 2016 at 10:00 a.m. The following were present: EMPLOYEE REPRESENTATIVE: FPE REPRESENTATIVE: FINANCE DIRECTOR: TOWN LABOR ATTORNEY MARY TAYLOR: VICTORIA MARTINEZ: CAMILO MARTIN JACQUELINE DELGADO WILLIE BAILEY ROY DANZIGER ALLISON SMITH ASSISTANT TOWN CLERK EXECUTIVE ASST. TO TOWN ATTORNEY/ LEGAL DEPARTMENT The purpose of this Public Meeting is to discuss Labor Negotiations between the Town of Medley and the Federation of Public Employees (FPE). Town Labor Attorney Allison Smith stated that we are here today to listen to the FPE's proposal. Hand outs were given to everyone present (attached). FPE Representative Willie Bailey stated that he would like to be in union with the PBA Contract. Mr. Bailey addressed all the articles of the Agreement as follows: Article #2 - Union Representation: Section 5 and 7: To have the bargaining team and /or stewards attend bargaining sessions, address grievances, attend predetermination hearings, and any other meetings that warrants the presence of the onsite stewards without the loss of pay or having to utilize any leave time. Article #5 Management Rights: Section 2-G: Proposed to strike "without cause" to say "with cause" for reclassification purposes only. New employees under probationary periods will not fall under this. Article #7 OK no changes. Article #8 OK no changes. Article #9 OK no changes Minutes of Public Meeting of May 17, 2016 Article #10 Grievance and Arbitration Procedures: Proposed to correct the word "Step 2" to "Section 2". Proposal to have all steps 1, 2, and 3 to follow a period of 10 calendar days for both parties. Article #11 Section 1 Proposal to delete "from 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., Monday -Friday" for General Services "and replace with "as determined by the Town" language. This does not include the General Administration employees. Section 8 Proposal to delete the following sentence ..."Such cash conversion will only be permitted in twenty (20) or forty (40) hour blocks and no fractional hours will be converted". Article #12 OK no changes. Article #13 OK no changes. Article #14 OK no changes. Article #15 OK no changes. Article #16 OK no changes. Article #17 Seniority Mr. Bailey wants to make sure that "Overtime" is given to every employee equally and that perhaps a rotation schedule should be followed to ensure equal opportunities for all employees. This is not an issue

segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA SEPTEMBER 12, 2016 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on September 12, 2016 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: lu Awe] 13 VICE -MAYOR: COUNCIL MEMBERS: TOWN CLERK: TOWN ATTORNEY: ROBERTO MARTELL JACK MORROW EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO SUSANA GUASCH HERLINA TABOADA STEPHEN HELFMAN LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Ayala and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Mayor Martell announced that the purpose of this special meeting was to discuss and establish the proposed tentative millage rate by Resolution based upon the Certification of Taxable Value of real and personal property within the Town of Medley for the fiscal year October 1, 2016 through September 30, 2017; discussion and establishment of a proposed tentative Budget for the fiscal year October 1, 2016 through September 30, 2017; and first reading of Ordinance C-413 adopting Budget for fiscal year 2016-2017. Proper Notice had been given. Mayor Martell then asked Attorney Helfman to address the meeting. Attorney Helfman stated that under the law we need to adopt the Millage first but the better order of business is to have a discussion on the budget first. He then read Resolution C-1439, establishing and adopting the tentative millage levy rate at 5.5000 mills per thousand dollars of taxable assessed property value, which is 8.30% above the rolled back rate computed pursuant to State Law for the 2016 tax year and then also read Ordinance C-413, adopting and approving the Budget of the Town of Medley Florida for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2016 and ending September 30, 2017. He then asked Finance Director Roy Danziger to proceed with the Budget. Roy then went briefly through the Budget and explained the changes that had been made since the last meeting. He stated that he had one (1) additional change that was not discussed at the prior budget meeting and it was the request by Jorge Soto from the Utilities Department to add $150,000.00 to the Budget to purchase a front end loader for the Department. Another minor change was made to the Organizational Chart. No other changes were made to the Budget. Attorney Helfman then stated that the Budget discussions were complete and asked if anyone from the public wanted to speak on the matter. No one came forward.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA SEPTEMBER 26, 2016 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on September 26, 2016 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: VICE -MAYOR: COUNCIL MEMBERS TOWN CLERK: TOWN ATTORNEY: ROBERTO MARTELL GRISELIA DIGIACOMO EDGAR AYALA SUSANA GUASCH JACK MORROW HERLINA TABOADA STEPHEN HELFMAN The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Mayor Martell announced that the purpose of this special meeting was to discuss and announce the percentage change, if any, in the millage rate for the fiscal year 2016-2017; adoption of a final operating millage rate for fiscal year 2016-2017 by enactment of a millage Resolution; and Adoption of the Budget Ordinance for fiscal year 2016-2017. Proper Notice had been given. Mayor Martell then asked Attorney Helfinan to address the meeting. Attorney Helfman stated this is the Town's Budget and Millage meeting. This is where we adopt the final millage and final budget for the 2016/2017 fiscal year. He stated that he will read both the Resolution and Ordinance first so that we can combine any discussion or any public comments together. He then read Resolution C-1440, Establishing and Adopting the Town of Medley Final Ad Valorem Tax Operating Millage Levy Rate for the fiscal year October 1, 2016 through September 30, 2017. Thereafter, Town Attorney Helfinan read Ordinance C-413, adopting and approving the Budget of the Town of Medley for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2016 and ending September 30, 2017. The Statutes requires that the first thing we need to do is to discuss the percentage change, if any, in the millage rate from one year to the next. In this instance the millage rate is 5.5000 Mills which is 8.30% above the rolled back rate computed pursuant to State Law. However, both of these items are a public hearing and the public is entitled to speak on both the millage rate that is being adopted which is 5.5000 mills and the Budget itself. He stated that if anyone in the public wanted to speak on the millage rate or budget now is the opportunity to come forward and speak. No one came forward. He then asked if anyone from the staff wanted to speak on this item. segs.head: (1) This Ordinance amends the M-1 Zoning District Regulations to provide for a Solid Waste Facilities Overlay District as a separate sub -district within the M-1 category.
segs.text: (1) This Ordinance amends the M-1 Zoning District Regulations to provide for a Solid Waste Facilities Overlay District as a separate sub -district within the M-1 category.

segs.head: (2) It defines Solid Waste as Class I Landfill, Class III Landfill, materials recovery facility, waste -to -energy facility, and recovered materials processing facility, which have received required Florida DEP and locally required permits.
segs.text: (2) It defines Solid Waste as Class I Landfill, Class III Landfill, materials recovery facility, waste -to -energy facility, and recovered materials processing facility, which have received required Florida DEP and locally required permits. Composting facilities are excluded.

segs.head: (3) Creates a new Section 62.91 of the Town Zoning Code establishing a special exception process for the application of the Overlay District to a specific property.
segs.text: (3) Creates a new Section 62.91 of the Town Zoning Code establishing a special exception process for the application of the Overlay District to a specific property. Special exception process applies to all types of Solid Waste Facilities.

segs.head: (4) Application for special exception must be filed and may be granted by Town Council after public notice and hearing.
segs.text: (4) Application for special exception must be filed and may be granted by Town Council after public notice and hearing. The Town council may grant a special exception upon findings that the application complies with detailed standards of review and criteria established in the Ordinance.

segs.head: (5) Provides for permitted and accessory uses within the Overlay District.
segs.text: (5) Provides for permitted and accessory uses within the Overlay District.

segs.head: (6) Special exceptions may be granted to: (a) permit uses described in the Ordinance, and (b) authorize deviations from the terms of the Town's Zoning Ordinances relating to setback and frontage requirements, height limitations, lot size restrictions, yard and building requirements, subdivision regulations, and other requirements unrelated to use, except for the buffer requirements established in the Ordinance.
segs.text: (6) Special exceptions may be granted to: (a) permit uses described in the Ordinance, and (b) authorize deviations from the terms of the Town's Zoning Ordinances relating to setback and frontage requirements, height limitations, lot size restrictions, yard and building requirements, subdivision regulations, and other requirements unrelated to use, except for the buffer requirements established in the Ordinance.

segs.head: (7) Storage or stockpiling of materials is not permitted within 100 feet of a public right of way unless screened by a masonry wall or a wall composed of similar material.
segs.text: (7) Storage or stockpiling of materials is not permitted within 100 feet of a public right of way unless screened by a masonry wall or a wall composed of similar material. Florida DEP permitted Class I Landfills and accessory uses are not subject to this requirement. Storage or stockpiling of materials is only allowed in accordance with this requirement for uses approved by special exception or determined by the Town to be a lawful use existing at the time of passage of the Ordinance.

segs.head: (8) Requires a Development Agreement between the Town and Property Owner for Class I and Class III Landfills, but not for other types of Solid Waste Facilities.
segs.text: (8) Requires a Development Agreement between the Town and Property Owner for Class I and Class III Landfills, but not for other types of Solid Waste Facilities.

segs.head: (9) Provisions relating to existing uses of land and buildings, even if the use does not conform to the new Ordinance, have been included.
segs.text: (9) Provisions relating to existing uses of land and buildings, even if the use does not conform to the new Ordinance, have been included. An existing lawful use of a building may be continued: (a) as long as no structural changes are made, unless required by law or Ordinance, and (b) the use is not extended to occupy any land outside the existing building. An existing lawful use of land may be continued provided: (a) the use shall not be enlarged or increased; and (b) the use may not be extended to occupy a greater area of land than occupied by the use at the time of adoption of the Ordinance. A "Lawful Use" shall be evidenced by either: (a) Town Council approval of the use prior to adoption of the Ordinance; or (b) a Final Certificate of Use authorizing all components of the use issued prior to the adoption of the Ordinance. (10)Solid Waste Facilities and accessory uses authorized and existing pursuant to a Development Agreement that is valid and effective prior to the adoption of the Page 2 September 26, 2016 Ordinance on Solid Waste Facilities Ordinance are exempt from the provisions of the Ordinance. Modifications, alterations or expansions are subject to Town approval to be included in either a new Development Agreement or amendment to the existing Development Agreement. segs.text: MINUTES OF A COUNCIL WORKSHOP OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA APRIL 18, 2017 1:00 P.M. A Council Workshop Meeting was called to order on April 18, 2017 at 1:00 P.M. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA SOCIAL SERVICE DIRECTOR: LIZMARI VALIDO MAYOR S EXECUTIVE ASSISTANT: | SUSANA GUASCH ASST. Finance Director Roy Danziger submitted expense report from 2008, 2011, 2015, 2016 anda projected 2017. He indicated the meals program has increased significantly. Lizmari stated that it was hard for her to determine who is or who is not using the Hot Meal Program. Ifa person has not picked up their lunch in two (2) weeks they are taken off the list. Also, do not deliver the meals unless they have a cooler with ice; if when delivering the meal there is a meal left from the day before, no meal should be delivered on that day. It was also suggested that lunches should be given to residents based on income. Councilperson Digiacomo asked what amount of income? It was suggested to raise the age to sixty-five (65) years or older. segs.text: MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA APRIL 3, 2017 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on April 3, 2017 at 7:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: STEPHEN HELFMAN (ABSENT) LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by Yoel Guerra and Deyana Morera from the Medley Police Department Explorers Post 67, the Town Council and audience. . The Minutes of the Regular Meeting of March 6, 2017 7:00 p.m. were discussed and approved. Mayor Martell stated that Item D and Item K under Town of Medley items were being tabled on the Agenda and he wanted to move forward Items A, B and C under Town of Medley items. Councilperson Digiacomo moved to approve his request. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Chief Dave Downey from Miami-Dade Fire Rescue gave a brief presentation on the services they provide the Town of Medley.
segs.text: Chief Dave Downey from Miami-Dade Fire Rescue gave a brief presentation on the services they provide the Town of Medley. He stated that they have sixty-nine (69) fire stations, their personnel is 2400 of which 2000 are fire fighters. They receive approximately 246,000 calls a year of which 916 were services in the Town of Medley. They will be adding approximately 120 fire fighters this year and they look forward to continue working with the Town. Mayor Martell and the Council thanked him for their services. The appointment of three (3) General Administration/Building and Zoning License Clerk II Positions for the Town of Medley General Administration was the next item on the Agenda. Director of Building & Zoning Department Richard McConachie informed the Mayor and Council that Jenny Digiacomo, Maglory Montano and Rosa Palau were selected to fill the above referenced full time position. After a brief discussion Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO APPOINT JENNY DIGIACOMO, MAGLORY MONTANO AND ROSA PALAU AS GENERAL ADMINISTRATION / BUILDING AND ZONING LICENSE CLERK II FULL TIME POSITION TO BE EFFECTIVE APRIL 4, 2017. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and the following votes were cast:

segs.head: Vice-Mayor Pacheco: Yes Councilperson Digiacomo: Abstained Mayor Martell: Yes Councilperson Ayala: Yes Councilperson Morrow: Yes The motion was carried by majority vote.
votes: Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO APPROVE THE HIRING OF JUAN RAMOS AS CIVILIAN RANGE EMPLOYEE FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY GUN RANGE ON A PART TIME BASIS EFFECTIVE APRIL 4, 2017. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Vice-Mayor Pacheco: Yes Councilperson Digiacomo: Abstained Mayor Martell: Yes Councilperson Ayala: Yes Councilperson Morrow: Yes The motion was carried by majority vote. Mayor Martell asked if anyone in the audience wanted to speak on the matter. Lowell Dunn II stated that he wanted two (2) points of clarification on the Ordinance. They are on page 3 Items B and F. Item F where it states the contiguous wall of Shipping Containers to secure the property He wanted to clarify if it could be a combination of shipping containers, fence or wall. The containers cannot be contiguous all the way because otherwise there will be no access to the property. The other item is Item B where it states 600 feet of residential area or district he would like it to read 600 feet of Lakeside . He stated that Page 2 April 3, 2017 when you look at the Town of Medley Zoning map the residential District out west of the Palmetto expressway is Lakeside and about approximately 400 acres of his property which is a lake. Since this only pertains to residential areas west of Palmetto expressway he would like to change it to read 600 feet of Lakeside because that is the only residential component out West. Attorney Arango stated that moving forward there could potentially be other residential developments in that area that could come in (5) five, (10) ten years. That is meant to protect any residential area that may be developed. Mr. Dunn stated that there is no place for residential areas except in his land. His concern is that right now he has containers where it is zoned residential. Attorney Arango stated that what he has is a legal non-conforming use that pre existed this Ordinance and we do have a provision in the Code which allows you to maintain a use the way it was approve legally and move forward. So if an Ordinance comes around ten (10) years later and your use or your building was legally approved you would have a non-confirming use. Mr. Dunn asked if the previous approvals from the Council negates Section 4 of the repealer clause. Attorney Arango said no that what she is saying is that, that repeals any inconsistent Ordinances in the Code that might conflict with this. segs.head: The next item on the agenda was discussion and action regarding the use of the Tobie Wilson Facility for the Town of Medley Chamber of Commerce.
votes: Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: TO ALLOW THE TOWN OF MEDLEY CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO USE THE MEDLEY MUNICIPAL SERVICES FACILITY TO HOLD THEIR MONTHLY MEETINGS. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The next item on the agenda was discussion and action regarding the use of the Tobie Wilson Facility for the Town of Medley Chamber of Commerce. Juan Rubi appeared before the Town Council and stated that the Chamber of Commerce has used the Medley Municipal Services Facilities building in the past to hold their meetings but since the new fee schedule was adopted Page 3 April 3, 2017 the Medley Municipal Services Facility building is only being used by staff or Town personnel for meetings. Councilperson Digiacomo asked why they cannot use the building now. Mayor Martell stated that the Municipal Services Facility has limited parking and the majority of the times the Council Chambers, Conference Room and other areas are used in meetings daily. Mayor Martell stated that they can use the Tobie Wilson Park once a month and that the fee to use Tobie Wilson can be waived. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that she would prefer that they use the Medley Municipal Services Facility building to hold their meetings. Mayor Martell stated that in that case then they can park in front of the Tobie Wilson Park. After a brief discussion Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: TO ALLOW THE TOWN OF MEDLEY CHAMBER OF COMMERCE TO USE THE MEDLEY MUNICIPAL SERVICES FACILITY TO HOLD THEIR MONTHLY MEETINGS. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: Resolution C-1478, approving and adopting Medley Town Council Meeting and Agenda Procedures was read by Town Attorney Arango. Councilperson Digiacomo requested a change on page 6 and continues on to page 7 titled Council Work Requests of the exhibit where it states when a member of the Council makes a request to the Town Attorney for information or legal analysis that in the opinion of the Town Attorney will involve a substantial or extensive expenditure of time and labor she would also like to add any staff member or Department Head. She also stated that we should also add some kind of language as to how much would extensive be . Attorney Arango stated that it is a good point, what is substantial or extensive time of Page 4 April 3, 2017 labor. Perhaps it should be any amount that exceeds the Mayor s spending authority of $25,000.00. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that if she is going to call the Town Attorney and it will cost more than $2,000.00 or $3,000.00 she should get Council approval. Councilperson Digiacomo believes that $25,000.00 is too much money. Attorney Arango stated that she can set the amount and whatever she believes is reasonable just as long as the staff or Mayor s hands are not tied in getting the work done. Some type of limit should be set but it is at the Council s discretion. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that everything should go through the Mayor s office. Councilperson Digiacomo believes that the Council should get approval from the rest of the Council to bring issues to the Attorney s and that also applies to Staff or Department Heads. Attorney Arango stated that a substantial expenditure that a staff member may have needs to be approved through the Mayor. Mayor Martell stated that when a Council member has a substantial or extensive expenditure of time and labor in excess of $5,000.00, the Council member shall place the item on the agenda. All requests from Town Department Heads to the Town Attorney for legal work involving substantial or extensive expenditure of time and labor shall first be submitted to the Mayor for approval. Everyone was in agreement. Thereafter, Councilperson Morrow moved to approve the Resolution with the changes. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

LI E safe ACh COUNCIL, CO ITY, OR COMMITTEE eV@uera ae) a (UG?PUA WN oc Ned MAILINGJADDRE = BOARD, COUNCIL, COMMISSION, AUTHORITY GR COMMITTEE ON on : WW 13 Ary 2 [naa vn ra edlay (# ZZ, - De cl e SEE <aNE ae THER LOCAL AGENCY \ DATE ON WHI Cu VOFE 0 ot e MY POSITION IS: Be) / t+ Br ELECTIVE Q APPOINTIVE T WHO MUST FILE FORM 8B This form is for use by any person serving at the county, city, or other local level of government on an appointed or elected board, council, commission, authority, or committee. It applies to members of advisory and non-advisory bodies who are presented with a voting conflict of interest under Section 112.3143, Florida Statutes. Your responsibilities under the law when faced with voting on a measure in which you have a conflict of interest will vary greatly depending on whether you hold an elective or appointive position. For this reason, please pay close attention to the instructions on this form before completing and filing the form. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 112.3143, FLORIDA STATUTES A person holding elective or appointive county, municipal, or other local public office MUST ABSTAIN from voting on a measure which would inure to his or her special private gain or loss. Each elected or appointed local officer also MUST ABSTAIN from knowingly voting on a measure which would inure to the special gain or loss of a principal (other than a government agency) by whom he or she is retained (including the parent, subsidiary, or sibling organization of a principal by which he or she is retained); to the special private gain or loss of a relative; or to the special private gain or loss of a business associate. Commissioners of community redevelopment agencies (CRAs) under Sec. 163.356 or 163.357, F.S., and officers of independent special tax districts elected on a one-acre, one-vote basis are not prohibited from voting in that capacity. For purposes of this law, a relative includes only the officer s father, mother, son, daughter, husband, wife, brother, sister, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law, and daughter-in-law. segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL SITTING AS THE LOCAL PLANNING AGENCY OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA APRIL 3, 2017 5:15 P.M. A special meeting of the Town Council sitting as the Local Planning Agency was called to order on April 3, 2017 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: VICE -MAYOR: COUNCIL MEMBERS: TOWN CLERK: TOWN ATTORNEY ROBERTO MARTELL IVAN PACHECO EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW QrA : 8 11 t A LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice -Mayor Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Town Council and audience. The Mayor announced that the purpose of this meeting was for the Local Planning Agency (LPA) to consider and make recommendations on the following Ordinances: First he announced that Ordinance C-415 needs to be added to the agenda which states as follows: An Ordinance of the Town of Medley, Florida amending Article II "Development Process and Concurrency Management of Chapter 32 "Land Development Code" to establish an Administrative Site Plan Review Process for Development; providing for inclusion in the Medley Municipal Code; providing for severability and conflicts; and providing for an effective date. Councilperson Digiacomo moved to add the item to the agenda. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA AUGUST 2, 2017 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on August 2, 2017 at 5:15 p.m.
votes: Mayor Martell moved to approve this Resolution as read. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA AUGUST 2, 2017 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on August 2, 2017 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Mayor Martell announced that the purpose of this special meeting was for a Resolution Approving a Local Agency Program (LAP) Agreement with the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) for partial funding of a Multimodal Mobility Study and Impact Assessment. Town Attorney Arango then read Resolution C-1505, approving a Local Agency Program (LAP) Agreement with the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) for partial funding of a Multimodal Mobility Study and Impact Assessment; authorizing the Town Mayor to execute the LAP Agreement with FDOT; providing for implementation; and providing for an effective date. Mayor Martell moved to approve this Resolution as read. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Since there was no further business to be considered, Councilperson Digiacomo moved to adjourn.
votes: Councilperson Digiacomo moved to adjourn. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Since there was no further business to be considered, Councilperson Digiacomo moved to adjourn. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 5:19 P.M. on August 2, 2017.

segs.head: MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA DECEMBER 4, 2017 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on December 4, 2017 at 7:00 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA DECEMBER 4, 2017 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on December 4, 2017 at 7:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Town Council and audience. The Minutes of the Regular Meeting of November 6, 2017 7:00 P.M. were discussed and approved. Mayor Martell announced that Item A under Special Presentation and Items J, K, L, M and N under Resolutions have been tabled until the next scheduled Regular Council Meeting. A unanimous approval was given.

segs.head: Mayor Martell then had a Key Exchange presentation between the Town of Medley and the City of South Miami.
segs.text: Mayor Martell then had a Key Exchange presentation between the Town of Medley and the City of South Miami. Mayor Philip K. Stoddard from the City of South Miami was present and accepted the Key. Mayor Martell asked if anyone from the Public wanted to speak. No one came forward. Mayor Martell then asked Town Attorney Arango to proceed with the meeting.

votes: Councilperson Digiacomo moved to approve this Resolution as read. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA DECEMBER 4, 2017 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on December 4, 2017 at 5:15 p.m.
votes: Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO RENEW THE TOWN S DENTAL INSURANCE, EMPLOYEE ASSISTANCE PLAN (EAP), LIFE, SHORT/LONG TERM DISABILITY AND THE VOLUNTARY COVERAGE WITH THE CURRENT PROVIDERS EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2018 AS SPECIFIED ABOVE. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA DECEMBER 4, 2017 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on December 4, 2017 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Mayor Martell announced that the purpose of this special meeting was to have a discussion and action on the renewal of the Employee Medical Insurance that expires on December 31, 2017. Mayor Martell then asked Bob Reynolds from Morris & Reynolds to proceed with the meeting. Mr. Reynolds stated that we are here tonight for the Employee benefits renewal. He stated that he was going to explain the less complicated part first. As of the first of January 2018 the Town has renewing the Dental Insurance in addition to Medical, the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Life, Disability and the Voluntary Coverage. He informed the Council as follows: Cigna Dental Insurance has been with the Town for many years. Last year the coverage was renewed and negotiated with no change in rates. Cigna has stayed firm and has offered a renewal with 4% increase on the DHMO and a 6% increase on the DPPO. His recommendation is to renew with Cigna Dental. The Employee Assistance Program (EAP) is through Ceridian and in January 2016 an extended term of a three (3) year Agreement was signed and the current annual rate was extended to January 14, 2019. Life and Disability is through The Hartford and it currently provides the Group Life, Ad & D as well as the Short and Long Term Disability Plans. The Hartford has advised that they have offered the Life and Disability renewal for January 1, 2018 with a Rate Pass and a two (2) year rate guarantee and shall renew again in January 1, 2020. The Voluntary Coverage is through Allstate and they have offered the Voluntary Plans for the employees with the same plans and rates as last year for the January 1, 2018 renewal. After a brief discussion Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO RENEW THE TOWN S DENTAL INSURANCE, EMPLOYEE ASSISTANCE PLAN (EAP), LIFE, SHORT/LONG TERM DISABILITY AND THE VOLUNTARY COVERAGE WITH THE CURRENT PROVIDERS EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2018 AS SPECIFIED ABOVE. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion

segs.head: Bob Reynolds then addressed the Employee Medical Insurance.
votes: Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO RENEW WITH CIGNA THE IN-NETWORK PLAN ONLY FOR ALL ELIGIBLE TOWN OF MEDLEY EMPLOYEES AT THE QUOTED INCREASED RATE OF 9.6% - TO BE EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2018. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Bob Reynolds then addressed the Employee Medical Insurance. He submitted to the Mayor and Council a worksheet on other Cities and what they offer their employees. He stated that Cigna s initial offer was to renew the same coverage that the Town has in place with an increase of 23.22%. Based on the offer, he advised the insurer that Cigna s long term relationship with the Town could end if rates were not dramatically reduced. Cigna advises that this year s increase in rate is driven, in part by the Town s loss ratio over the last twelve (12) months as medical claims have gone up by 61%. After aggressive negotiations Cigna has proposed an alternative plan that would reduce the costs with slight changes to the benefits and a Single Plan Option of the Current In-Network Only Plan with a 9.6% increase over current rates. Meaning to say that if the Town does not renew with the Open Access POS Plan and renews with the In-Network Plan only the renewal rate will only be increased 9.6%. After a brief discussion Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO RENEW WITH CIGNA THE IN-NETWORK PLAN ONLY FOR ALL ELIGIBLE TOWN OF MEDLEY EMPLOYEES AT THE QUOTED INCREASED RATE OF 9.6% - TO BE EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2018. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Councilperson Ayala thanked Bob Reynolds for taking the time and explaining all of the options the Town had before making a decision.
votes: Mayor Martell moved to adjourn. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Councilperson Ayala thanked Bob Reynolds for taking the time and explaining all of the options the Town had before making a decision. He also thanked the Council for making a good decision and renewing with Cigna because there were Directors and Employees that were very worried. Councilperson Digiacomo also stated that she considered all of the other companies who quoted us, but she believes we should stay with Cigna because we have been with Cigna for many years, they have given great service to the Town and yes we might go to another company and the prices are lower now, but after they have an account with us their rates can also double or triple in the future. Page 2 December 4, 2017 Finance Director Roy Danziger thanked the Mayor and Town Council for renewing with Cigna. Also thanked Bob Reynolds for an excellent job. Public Works Director Heriberto Cabrera thanked everyone for renewing with Cigna and also thanked everyone on behalf of his employees. He said his employees were very worried. Since there was no further business to be considered, Mayor Martell moved to adjourn. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 5:42 P.M. on December 4, 2017.

A Public Meeting was called to order on February 15, 2017 at 12:30 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE -MAYOR: JACK MORROW COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO IVAN PACHECO FINANCE DIRECTOR: ROY DANZIGER LABOR ATTORNEY: ALISON SMITH ROBERT MEYERS TOWN ENGINEER: JORGE CORZO TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN STAFF: VICTORIA MARTINEZ LIZMARI VALIDO MARY TAYLOR SUSANA GUASCH JOSE GUASCH RICHARD McCONACHIE JORGE SOTO HERIBERTO CABRERA FATIMA FUENTES ALFREDO LEON POLICE CHIEF: JEANETTE SAID JINETE The purpose of this Public Meeting was to have an Ethics Refresher Training. The training was conducted by Attorneys Alison Smith and Robert Meyers. Attorney Alison Smith gave a presentation on the Sunshine Law. She explained that the law is codified in Chapter 286 of the Florida Statues. It provides a right of access to governmental proceedings of public boards or commissions at both the State and Local levels. It applies to elected officials and appointed boards or committees and if there is deliberation or formal action. The basic requirements of the Sunshine Law are: Meetings open to the Public, reasonable notice of meetings and Minutes taken. The Florida Supreme Court holds: "any gathering, whether formal or casual, of two or more members of the same board or commission to discuss some matter on which foreseeable action will be taken by the public board or commission". Individual Meetings with Commissioners, a manager may not act as a liaison for board members by circulating information and thoughts of individual members. Staff Meetings - does not ordinarily apply to staff meetings and staff committees performing fact finding or advisory functions. If staff committee is delegated a "decision making function" the Sunshine Law will apply. Generally public meetings must take place in public buildings and should not be held in any venue that unreasonably restricts public access to the facility. Exemptions: Attorney -Client Sessions, Collective Bargaining Executive session with City Manager and Town Commission to discuss strategy. Applies only in the context of actual and pending collective bargaining negotiations. Penalties: Any person who knowingly violates the law by attending a meeting not in compliance with Sunshine Law commits a second degree misdemeanor and is subject to up to 60 days in jail; $500.00 fine. TO TOWN ATTORNEY/ ASSISTANT TOWN CLERK The purpose of this Public Meeting is to discuss Labor Negotiations between the Town of Medley and the Federation of Public Employees (FPE). FPE Representative Willie Bailey stated that the FPE has reviewed the proposed DROP Ordinance as submitted by the Town and wanted to know if the Town was to offer the same program to the Police Bargaining Unit (PBA). Town labor attorney Alison Smith stated that those were the Town's plans for the upcoming negotiations. Mr. Bailey asked if the Town was planning to include a percentage rate or rate of return to the plan. Finance Director Roy Danziger explained that as the plan is structured, the rate of return is whatever the plan earns. After a brief discussion, FPE representative stated as follows: FPE does not object to the DROP program but would like the Town to consider a five (5) year plan instead of a three (3) year as proposed. In addition, Mr. Bailey stated that he would like to have some time to have the FPE's legal team review the language proposed by the Town. Town labor counsel agreed to the FPE's request and mentioned that, with the permission of Town personnel, she could address any FPE's comments and/or concerns directly. The discussion then moved on to the members of the Town's pension board and the FPE mentioned that the FPE would like the Town to look into including an FPE appointed member. Mr. Bailey then went on to discuss that the Ordinance, as proposed, does not reflect any pay out details. Finance Director Danziger answered that he would get in touch with the Town's pension attorney and the Town will get back to the FPE on the issue. After a brief discussion on the structured of the program, a question from Julio Chardon, sitting in the audience, was attended to. segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 19, 2017 A workshop meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 19, 2017 at 5:15 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 19, 2017 A workshop meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 19, 2017 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Town Attorney Arango announced that the purpose of this special meeting was to have a discussion on the proposed Budget for the fiscal year October 1, 2017 through September 30, 2018; and to discuss and establish the proposed tentative millage rate based upon the Certification of Taxable Value of real and personal property within the Town of Medley for the fiscal year October 1, 2017 through September 30, 2018. Proper notice had been given. Mayor Martell then asked Finance Director Roy Danziger to proceed with the Budget. Roy stated that he had submitted Budget worksheets to the Mayor and Council for the General Fund, Water Utilities Fund, Stormwater Fund, Lakeside Fund and Police Gun Range Fund. Included in the worksheets are Capital items which are not going to be discussed tonight because there will be a separate Budget Workshop for that fund. Right now it is just estimates what is on the worksheets and any changes that are made will affect the surplus or deficit. Tonight the goal is to set the tentative millage rate. The current millage rate is 5.5000 mills with a rolled back rate of 5.1107. What we want to propose is a millage rate of 5.375 mills but tonight his recommendation is to set a tentative millage rate of 5.5000 mills. We can always go lower to the 5.3750 mills. He said he also included an employee list in the packages. He then started explaining the Budget worksheets page by page. He stated that he is predicting a projected deficit of $1,785,000.00 due to Impact Fees and Seawall Grant being deferred to next year, income from Red Light Camera and Permit Fees are down. The Town is working to stabilize the fund balance. We cannot go into reserves every year. If reserves are too low and the Town needs to borrow money it might have to borrow at a

segs.head: higher interest rate.
votes: Councilperson Ayala moved as follows: TO INCREASE THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL S SALARY BY $11,000.00 A YEAR. Motion died for lack of a second. Councilperson Digiacomo then moved as follows: TO APPROVE A SALARY INCREASE OF $12,000.00 A YEAR ACROSS THE BOARD FOR THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL . Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: higher interest rate. Councilperson Digiacomo asked Roy how much money has the Town spent on Eminent Domains. He said approximately $900,000.00 this year; the prior year was $2 million, and the year before that was $1.2 million. Roy stated that the proposed budget includes a 3% salary increase for all FPE Union employees and 3% for all non-union employees including part timers. Councilperson Ayala stated that he realized that there are still some employees that are making under $10.00 per hour. He asked if there was any way we could help those employees and raise them to at least to $10.00 per hour. Mayor Martell stated that it could be done, but not for the employees who are in the union. If they are in the union it has to be negotiated through them. Mayor Martell asked Roy to make a projection as to how much money that will cost and present it at the next Budget meeting. Roy said that it should not cost that much and that he would do it. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that she believes it is only four (4) employees who are under $10.00 per hour. Roy says that he will do a proposal for those employees under $11.00 per hour. Roy stated that he has an estimated increase for the PBA Employees in the Budget but he does not want to say because they will be going into negotiations. Councilperson Digiacomo asked Roy what does the actual PBA contract say right now. Roy says that it varies and for those who are in Step increases get 4%, Roy said he would like to talk about the Town Council compensation. He said he is hearing that the Council wants their salaries adjusted and he needs to know by what amount so he can put it in the Budget. Councilperson Ayala said that we spoke about this a few years ago and the Mayors recommendation at that time was to leave it alone. He then said that when Vice-Mayor Pacheco came in he was the one who asked for a raise. He stated that he believes they deserve a raise. There has been talk about raising the salaries by $10,000.00, $11,000.00 or $12,000.00 a year. He said that he heard that the Mayor was not going to accept the increase. Mayor Martell said that by seeing how this was developing he spoke to Roy and told him that whatever the Council receives he will receive it as well. The Mayor said that this is the time to decide what the Council wants to do in order to advise Roy of the amount in order to put it in the Budget. After a lengthily discussion Councilperson Ayala moved as follows: TO INCREASE THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL S SAL

segs.head: Page 2 July 19, 2017 prescribed by Ordinance and fixed in the annual Budget.
votes: Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: TO AUTHORIZE THE CHANGES AS FOLLOWS: INCREASE THE COUNCILS PENSION TO $3,800.00 A YEAR AND INCREASE THE MAYORS PENSION TO $8,500.00 A YEAR SUBJECT TO FINANCE DIRECTOR OBTAINING AN ACTUARIAL EVALUATION AND AUTHORIZATION FROM PENSION ATTORNEY; CHANGES TO BE EFFECTIVE OCTOBER 1, 2017. segs.text: Page 2 July 19, 2017 prescribed by Ordinance and fixed in the annual Budget. Councilperson Morrow then requested an increase to the Mayor s and Council s Pension. Roy stated that he will need to get an actuarial evaluation. Mayor Martell stated that this will help everyone in office now and for everyone that comes in the future. After a brief discussion Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: TO AUTHORIZE THE CHANGES AS FOLLOWS: INCREASE THE COUNCILS PENSION TO $3,800.00 A YEAR AND INCREASE THE MAYORS PENSION TO $8,500.00 A YEAR SUBJECT TO FINANCE DIRECTOR OBTAINING AN ACTUARIAL EVALUATION AND AUTHORIZATION FROM PENSION ATTORNEY; CHANGES TO BE EFFECTIVE OCTOBER 1, 2017. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: Vice-Mayor Pacheco then stated that he has been sitting in this seat for seven (7) months and the least the he expects from his colleagues and from everyone that works in this building is professionalism and ethics. I think we need to learn a lot and we need to start putting it into practice. We are not here to call each other names. That is all I can say, seven (7) months and I have seen a lot of stuff going on here. It does not look or sound fair to me. Mayor Martell stated that we need to respect one another as professional people that we all are. That is all he is requesting. Councilperson Ayala stated that we had spoken about this before and in tonights meeting it is not the time to stay quiet, we have to move on. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that no one was planning on keeping quiet, she was not planning on keeping quiet, but she says that she has been accused by him that she always tries to talk more than everybody else. That is why she is giving everybody else time to talk. Mayor Martell asked that the comments stop and to please continue with the Budget. Roy continued explaining the Budget. He is projecting an 8% increase in medical insurance and requested a 30% reduction in office expense, operating expenses and vehicle maintenance. Page 3 July 19, 2017 Roy stated that he was hearing that the salaries at the Public Works Department are down and they are working shorthanded. Mayor Martell asked Public Works Director Heriberto Cabrera how many employees were picking up trash last Thursday. Mr. Cabrera said only three (3) employees. Councilperson Digiacomo told him that she believes that he lost two (2) employees in this fiscal year. He said yes. She asked if the Town was going to replace those employees. Mayor Martell stated that it was due to the budget. She said that two (2) employees will not hurt the budget besides they had already been budgeted. Vice-Mayor Pacheco asked Mr. Cabrera as to how many employees was he short. Mr. Cabrera said four (4) employees and he needs to replace at least two (2). Councilperson Digiacomo stated that his employees are saying that they need more help and it is also the Department that gets the least paid. Mayor Martell stated that he wants to help this Department. He said that there is a shade meeting scheduled for July 31, 2017 and he would like to discuss this issue and then bring the request before the union. Mr. Cabrera said that he would like to challenge any one to work one day with his employees on a truck, in the sun on summer days so everyone can experience what his employees do. Mayor Martell stated that he will go out there one day to work with them. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that he does not have to challenge her she believes him and she has seen what they do and they deserve everything he is asking for them. She wants Mr. Cabrera to tell his employees to please be patient that it will happen. Vice-Mayor Pacheco stated that he will also go out there one day and work with them also. Capital Improvement and Economic Development Department Roy stated that he had budgeted and added an extra full time employee as assistant to Town Engineer Jorge Corzo.
