segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL SITTING AS THE LOCAL PLANNING AGENCY OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 3, 2017 6:30 P.M. A special meeting of the Town Council sitting as the Local Planning Agency was called to order on July 3, 2017 at 6:30 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL SITTING AS THE LOCAL PLANNING AGENCY OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 3, 2017 6:30 P.M. A special meeting of the Town Council sitting as the Local Planning Agency was called to order on July 3, 2017 at 6:30 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: VICE -MAYOR: COUNCIL MEMBERS: TOWN CLERK: TOWN ATTORNEY ROBERTO MARTELL IVAN PACHECO EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW HERLINA TABOADA STEVEN HELFMAN LILLIAN ARANGO (ABSENT) The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by Josue Hernandez and Clifford Gurdian from the Medley Police Department Explorers Post 67, the Town Council and audience. The Mayor announced that the purpose of this meeting was for the Local Planning Agency (LPA) to consider and make a recommendation on the following Ordinance:

segs.head: Ordinance C-420, an Ordinance of the Town of Medley, Florida, amending Chapter 30 "Flood Damage Prevention" to amend the Town's Floodplain Management Regulations; providing for codification; providing for conflicts; providing for severability; and providing for an effective date.
votes: Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: "TO RECOMMEND APPROVAL OF THIS ORDINANCE AND FIND THAT THIS ORDINANCE IS CONSISTENT WITH THE TOWN'S COMPREHENSIVE PLAN." Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
Councilperson Digiacomo moved to adjourn. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Ordinance C-420, an Ordinance of the Town of Medley, Florida, amending Chapter 30 "Flood Damage Prevention" to amend the Town's Floodplain Management Regulations; providing for codification; providing for conflicts; providing for severability; and providing for an effective date. Town Attorney Helfman asked if anyone in the audience wanted to speak on this item. No one came forward. Thereafter, Ordinance C-419 was read by Town Attorney Helfman. After a brief discussion Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: "TO RECOMMEND APPROVAL OF THIS ORDINANCE AND FIND THAT THIS ORDINANCE IS CONSISTENT WITH THE TOWN'S COMPREHENSIVE PLAN." Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo stated that this Ordinance is for compliance with Federal Regulations and it updates the flood criteria. Since there was no further business to be considered, Councilperson Digiacomo moved to adjourn. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 6:36 p.m. on July 3, 2017. Herlina Taboada, Town Clerk Page 2 July 3, 2017

segs.text: (1) Deluxe 90 Targetry Refurbish Package including labor and Targetry from Action Target in the amount of $51,606.00. Before moving to approve the above request Finance Director Roy Danziger stated that every year the Town gets audited and the Auditors do a compliance test and when they see something Page 3 June 5, 2017 that the Town is doing wrong they write it down and then we have to respond. One of the things the Town is not following is the purchasing Ordinance which requires three (3) bids and if it is over a certain amount it requires an RFP. He believes that the request from Action Target needs an RFP or at least three (3) bids. If this is approved without the proper requirements it will be in our report next year. The Auditors will be looking for the three (3) quotes or the RFP. Mayor Martell asked Lt. Jinete if he could obtain three (3) bids on this. Lt. Jinete stated that that was the company that they had been using. Finance Director Roy Danziger stated that it could also be a sole source, but he does not know. If it is sole source and they cannot buy it from no one else it has to be documented. Town Attorney Arango stated that the Town needs to comply with the Town purchasing code which is the Ordinance that the Town has adopted. If you are not going to you must have an exemption in the code, sole source, bid of another governmental entity, impracticality etc. so she agrees with Roy and the Ordinance has to be followed and if not it has to be documented with one of the exemptions in the Ordinance. Councilperson Digiacomo asked if we were undoing the motions that already passed. Roy stated that we can do it subject to. Councilperson Morrow then moved as follows: SUBJECT TO VERIFICATION THAT THE TOWN IS FOLLOWING THE PROPER PROCEDURES EITHER BY PIGGY BACKING ONTO ANOTHER AGENCY, AND/OR BY MEETING THE REQUIREMENTS OF THE ORDINANCE AND GETTING THE NECESSARY QUOTATIONS OR MEETING ONE OF THE EXCEMPTIONS IN IT. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. This motion includes all (3) requests above. segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 5, 2017 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on June 5, 2017 at 5:15 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 5, 2017 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on June 5, 2017 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: STEPHEN HELFMAN (ABSENT) LILLIAN ARANGO SPECIAL COUNSEL: ALISON SMITH The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Mayor Martell announced that the purpose of this special meeting was for the Appeal of Termination by Former Town Employee. Special Counsel Alison Smith stated that we have to ask a question procedurally to make sure that there is no one here that needs to recues themselves on the basis of a conflict or a bias. Councilperson Morrow then stated that he would like to abstain from discussing and voting on this matter based on his helping bias. He stated that Ms. Sosa is his neighbor and in an effort to be helpful he assisted her son in preparation of her appeal letter. Eddie Rodriguez son of former Town Employee Lilia M. Sosa translated for his mother. He stated that she said that her termination was not fair. That even though there are certain standards that she was suppose to meet there should have been a little more clarification on her schedule and time. She believes the Town should take some consideration that she has been working for the Town for quite some time and she feels that she should be given a second chance. Lilia M. Sosa then spoke in Spanish to the Mayor and Council and asked for forgiveness and for the misunderstanding of her schedule, she said she thought that all she had to do was to go to work, work and go. She thought she did not have to be there all of the time. She said she did not do it just to be bad, I have given all the best in me and I have done my work the best possible. Everywhere they have sent her she has done the work and have never denied to work in anything. She has always done the best in her for all she does. She would like to have a second chance to make it work better. Councilperson Ayala asked Eddie Rodriguez her son if he understood Councilperson Morrow s request on not to vote on any decision. votes: Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO AMEND THE TOWN OF MEDLEY CODE AND PREPARE AN ORDINANCE THAT ALLOWS FOR THE PARKING OF RV S, CAMPER TRAILERS, BOATS, AND JET SKIES IN RESIDENTIAL PROPERTIES. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The next item was a discussion and action on the Town of Medley hiring process. Mayor Martell wanted clarification as to whether or not the Council wants to sit in during the interview process whenever there are positions available. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that it was not ethical. No one else had any comments. Mayor Martell then stated that we need to trust the Department Heads. Discussion and action on request by Councilperson Ayala for the parking of campers on Residential properties in the Town of Medley was then held. He stated that he wanted to give Eric the opportunity to come back tonight and clarify what he wants to do with the trailer. He stated that Eric does not need to live in the camper trailer. All he wants is for the Council to approve the parking of his camper trailer back on his property. He stated that if it needs to be moved every 180 days he will do so. He stated that Medley needs a Resolution or Ordinance that allows for the parking of camper trailers on their properties. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that she was not present at the February Council Meeting but she heard the audio recording. She stated that his request at that time was to live in the camper trailer, now tonight Page 4 March 6, 2017 that has changed. The Code needs to be changed in order for someone to park RV s or boat on their property. Eric wants to bring his camper trailer back home and stated that he will abide by the Rules and Regulations of RV s. He would like to obtain a copy of a Resolution or Ordinance regarding these rules. Town Attorney Helfman stated that by him being here tonight it has been very helpful and clarifies that he has no intention of living in the camper trailer. Attorney Helfman asked that everyone disregard the memo from him that was in the packages. He stated that there are places that allow for the parking of camper trailers. The Town needs to have an Ordinance within the R-1 District to permit the parking of camper trailers, boats, jet skies, RV s etc. Currently the Town of Medley Code does not provide for that. Eric again asked for permission to bring his camper trailer back home and that he will abide by the rules and regulations of RV s. Mayor Martell stated that the only thing they want to do is to abide by the law. An Ordinance needs to be prepared. After a brief discussion Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO AMEND THE TOWN OF MEDLEY CODE AND PREPARE AN ORDINANCE THAT ALLOWS FOR THE PARKING OF RV S, CAMPER TRAILERS, B

segs.text: Discussion and Action regarding the Social Service Programs was the next item to be discussed. Lizmari Valido Social Services Director stated that in the packages there was a breakdown of the recommendations that were made at the Workshop Meeting of April 18, 2017 to the Social Service Programs which included Housekeeping, Bathing, Blood Pressure/Glucose, Medical Transportation, Hot Meal Program and Cold Lunch Program. She stated that the changes that were made to the programs will apply to new applicants and it will not affect the persons currently enrolled in the programs. The Blood Pressure/ Glucose check program was cancelled for all current and future applicants. Councilperson Digiacomo asked her how was she going to verify the income. She stated that she will ask for Income Taxes and/or Social Security Income of everyone in the household. Councilperson Digiacomo also suggested that income verification be done every year and that a letter be sent out every year to remind the residents that they need to re-apply in order to continue receiving the services. Whoever does not re-apply will not receive the services. After a brief discussion Councilperson Digiacomo moved to approve the changes to the programs. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

ALISON SMITH, ESQ. JEANETTE SAID-JINETE EXECUTIVE ASST. TO TOWN ATTORNEY/ ASSISTANT TOWN CLERK The purpose of this Public Meeting was to discuss labor negotiations between the Town of Medley and the Miami -Dade County Police Benevolent Association (PBA). Town attorney Alison Smith informed the PBA of the Town's position regarding the PBA's previously proposed items. They are as follows: Section 8.9 (New) Language Addition to Article 8 -Personnel Records- Town accepts language proposed by PBA. Article 9 Hours and Overtime Section 9.3 (a) - Town approves proposal. Would like to add "hours physically worked" to this section. Article 16 Uniforms, Safety and Equipment- PBA had proposed to add GIU to this section. Town accepts proposal. Article 17- Compensation- Town accepts the three percent (3 %) increase for all three (3) years of the agreement Section 17.4- Shift Differential: Town does not accept shift differential increase as proposed. However, Town proposes a ten cent ($0.10) increase to the afternoon and midnight shift. Section 17.7: PBA proposed a slight increase of one and a half (1 %) hours of compensation leave. Town accepts proposal. Article 20. Holidays- Town proposes to remove Columbus Day holiday and replace it with one (1) additional floating day. The reason for this change is because most business operations do not recognize this holiday and are open for business. The change will provide for a better operation and service on this day. Article 26 Awards- Section 3 -PBA proposed an incentive of sixteen (16) total hours instead of eight (8) hours. Town proposes either eight (8) or ten (10) hours of Administrative Leave depending on the shift assigned. Article 27- Retirement Benefits Section 27.2 (a): PBA proposed to discuss the language adopted in the DROP Ordinance for retirement program. - Town is ok with early retirement program not including the DROP program, meaning there is a ninety (90) days to submit documentation. Town will have to come up with the details of such program. Section 27.2 (b): Pension Benefit Cap. The PBA has noticed that the Town has begun to hire young officers. segs.head: (2) The method of compensation and its limitations are illustrated by the following examples: (i) If an employee is scheduled to begin his/her shift at 3:00 p.m., and appears in court for the period from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. [four (4) hours], the employee will receive off-duty court time compensation for the actual four (4) hours spent on off-duty court time. (ii) If an employee is scheduled to begin his/her shift at 3:00 p.m., and appears in court for the period from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. [two (2) hours], the employee will receive off-duty court time compensation for the three (3) hour mi
segs.text: (2) The method of compensation and its limitations are illustrated by the following examples: (i) If an employee is scheduled to begin his/her shift at 3:00 p.m., and appears in court for the period from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. [four (4) hours], the employee will receive off-duty court time compensation for the actual four (4) hours spent on off-duty court time. (ii) If an employee is scheduled to begin his/her shift at 3:00 p.m., and appears in court for the period from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. [two (2) hours], the employee will receive off-duty court time compensation for the three (3) hour minimum. votes: Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: TO RENEW THE BUSINESS INSURANCE WITH THE TOWN S CURRENT INSURER THE TRAVELERS; TO MAINTAIN THE $10,000.00 DEDUCTIBLE FOR GENERAL AND AUTO LIABILITY; AND TO REDUCE THE WIND STORM DEDUCTIBLE FROM 5% TO 3% PER OCCURRENCE TO BE EFFECTIVE NOVEMBER 1, 2017. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA OCTOBER 16, 2017 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on October 16, 2017 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO (ABSENT) COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Councilperson Morrow announced that resident Lester Wheeler had passed and prayed for his family. Mayor Martell announced that the purpose of this special meeting have a discussion and action regarding Business Insurance Policy Renewal effective November 1, 2017; Resolution approving the Town of Medley State Legislative Priorities for 2018. - Bob Reynolds from Morris & Reynolds presented the Mayor and Council with a binder with insurance premium comparisons for 2016 vs. 2017and multiple insurer responses for 2017. He stated that the commercial insurance market is stable at this time and while insurers seek modest increases for most lines other than workers compensation, the impact of recent storms such as Hurricane Harvey and Irma remain to be seen, but for now the market place remains stable. The Travelers the current insurer has offered renewal of the primary and excess coverage with a premium of $309,554.00. They continue to be, in his view, a strong, loyal partner to the Town. Currently the storm deductible is 5% per occurrence, calendar year, per location subject to a minimum deductible of $25,000.00. AmRise has also provided optional quotes for a 1%, 2% or 3% storm deductible. After a brief discussion Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: TO RENEW THE BUSINESS INSURANCE WITH THE TOWN S CURRENT INSURER THE TRAVELERS; TO MAINTAIN THE $10,000.00 DEDUCTIBLE FOR GENERAL AND AUTO LIABILITY; AND TO REDUCE THE WIND STORM DEDUCTIBLE FROM 5% TO 3% PER OCCURRENCE TO BE EFFECTIVE NOVEMBER 1, 2017. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: The second reading of Ordinance C-422, Amending Chapter 62 of the Town Code, Article II In General to establish regulations and requirements to provide for Compliance with Section 337.401, Florida Statutes as amended on July 1, 2017, relating to the use of Public Right-of-Way for Broadband or Wireless Facility Infrastructure was read by Town Attorney Arango. Mayor Martell then asked if anyone in the audience wanted to speak. Attorney Hope Calhoun representing Crown Castle asked that the matter be deferred at this time for clarification purposes on certain items in the Ordinance. Town Attorney Arango stated that there was recent Legislation adopted effective July 1, 2017 called The Advance Wireless Infrastructure Deployment Act that requires that we create an Ordinance to regulate the placement of what we call Small Wireless Facilities on Municipal poles for facilities in the Public Right-of-Way. In response to that we received a letter from Crown Castle on July 3, 2017 indicating that it was the initial request under the Statute that triggers the ninety (90) days compliance to create an Ordinance to regulate the Small Wireless Facilities. In response to that letter they prepared this Ordinance and tomorrow is the ninety (90) days and her recommendation at this time is to move forward adopting this Ordinance and they are happy to sit down with Ms. Calhoun after this Ordinance is adopted, go through it and if there is any ambiguity or issues we can always bring back an amendment to the Ordinance. No one else from the audience came forward. After a brief discussion Councilperson Morrow moved to approve this Ordinance on second reading. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 112.3143, FLORIDA STATUTES A person holding elective or appointive county, municipal, or other local public office MUST ABSTAIN from voting on a measure which would inure to his or her special private gain or loss. Each elected or appointed local officer also MUST ABSTAIN from knowingly voting on a measure which would inure to the special gain or loss of a principal (other than a government agency) by whom he or she is retained (including the parent, subsidiary, or sibling organization of a principal by which he or she is retained); to the special private gain or loss of a relative; or to the special private gain or loss of a business associate. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA OCTOBER 5, 2017 5:30 P.M. A Public Meeting was called to order on October 5, 2017 at 5:30 p.m. The following were present: Willie Bailey, Federation of Public Employees Alison Smith, Esq., Town Attorney Herlina Taboada, Town Clerk Roy Danziger, Town of Medley Finance Director Victoria Martinez, Assistant Town Clerk/Legal Assistant Jackeline Delgado, Steward Camilo Martin, Steward Town attorney Alison Smith opened the meeting explaining the reason for which it was called to order and explained that its purpose was to discuss Labor Negotiations between the Town of Medley and the Federation of Public Employees (FPE) regarding five employees and their pay increases. The employees in question are: Gabriel Diaz, Osvaldo Martinez, Elisbel Rivera, Omar Sanchez and Nancy Torres. Town Special Counsel Alison Smith stated that the main reason we are here today is to discuss the FPE's issue with the three (3) men's salary and their position to revoke the increase given and approved by the FPE back in the month of June. She stated that the FPE requested an impact bargaining because the men's increase had made the ladies request surfaced once again. She then stated that the two (2) women had asked for raises last year during negotiations and said raise was denied because they had received several increases in a short period of time as opposed to the men. Ms. Smith then went on to reiterate that in June 2017 Willie Bailey, the FPE Representative, was e -mailing back and forth and asked that the raises given to the men not only be taken back but also retroactively. Willy Bailey then stated that if the two (2) women are given the raises the FPE is asking for then the three (3) men can keep their increases, but if the two (2) women are not given any additional compensation then the raises on the three (3) men will have to be taken back and retroactively. Mr. Bailey added that If the Town does not take back the raises of the three (3) men then the FPE can file an unfair labor practice complaint against the Town. Special Counsel Alison Smith asked Mr. Bailey the reason why he has a problem with giving the three (3) men a raise. He said that he did not have a problem with the three (3) men just as long as the two (2) women received their additional raises. Town Attorney Arango then asked if anyone in the audience wanted to speak on any item. No one came forward. Mayor Martell then stated that there was an add-on item which was Resolution C-1530, approving a contract with Metro Express, Inc. Councilperson Digiacomo moved to add the item to the agenda. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA SEPTEMBER 25, 2017 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on September 25, 2017 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: VICE -MAYOR: COUNCIL MEMBERS TOWN CLERK: TOWN ATTORNEY: ROBERTO MARTELL IVAN PACHECO EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW HERLINA TABOADA STEPHEN HELFMAN The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Mayor Martell announced that the purpose of this special meeting was to discuss and announce the percentage change, if any, in the millage rate for the fiscal year 2017-2018; adoption of a final operating millage rate for fiscal year 2017-2018 by enactment of a millage Resolution; and Adoption of the Budget Ordinance for fiscal year 2017-2018. Proper Notice had been given. Mayor Martell then asked Finance Director Roy Danziger to address the meeting. Roy stated that this is the Town's Budget and Millage meeting. This is where we adopt the final millage and final budget for the 2017/2018 fiscal year. He then read Resolution C-1531, Establishing and Adopting the Town of Medley Final Ad Valorem Tax Operating Millage Levy Rate for the fiscal year October 1, 2017 through September 30, 2018. The Statutes requires that the first thing we need to do is to discuss the percentage change, if any, in the millage rate from one year to the next. In this instance the millage rate is 5.4000 Mills which is 5.66% above the rolled back rate computed pursuant to State Law. Mayor Martell stated that this was a public hearing and if anyone in the public wanted to speak on these items. No one came forward. Thereafter, Attorney Helfman read Resolution C-1531, Establishing and Adopting the Town of Medley Final Ad Valorem Tax Operating Millage Levy Rate at 5.4000 Mills per thousand dollars of taxable assessed property value, which is 5.66% above the rolled back rate computed pursuant to State Law for the 2017 Tax Year. Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: "TO APPROVE RESOLUTION C-1531, ESTABLISHING AND ADOPTING THE TOWN OF MEDLEY FINAL AD VALOREM TAX OPERATING MILLAGE LEVY RATE AT 5.4000 MILLS PER THOUSAND DOLLARS OF TAXABLE ASSESSED PROPERTY VALUE, WHICH IS 5.66 % ABOVE THE ROLLED BACK RATE COMPUTED PURSUANT TO STATE LAW, FOR THE 2017 TAX YEAR". segs.text: Resolution C-1506, Confirming and Ratifying the Town Mayor s Declaration of a State of Emergency due to the imminent and severe threat of Hurricane Irma was read by Town Attorney Helfman. Councilperson Digiacomo moved to approve this Resolution as read. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Finance Director Roy Danziger announced that as of now the Budget Meeting is scheduled for September 12, 2017. We don t know what will happen due to Hurricane Irma. Mayor Martell announced that Heriberto Cabrera is helping the Town put up the shutters at Lakeside Retirement Park and then he will go to 8181 N.W. South River Drive. Our goal is to protect the residents and pray that the hurricane does not come this way. Mayor Martell stated that we are still waiting for the County to tell us which shelters will be open and when. He also stated that the Municipal Services Facility Building is only qualified for a category three (3) hurricane or less. Not a category 4 or category 5. Residents cannot be in this building knowing that it could be damaging. Arturo Jinete from the Medley Police Department stated that we have done this before and asked that flyers be sent out to residents advising them of where they can go for shelters. They will go out there and tell them personally and guide them the right way. We cannot do anything against mother nature. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo stated that we have been trained to follow FEMA Guidelines. Councilperson Digiacomo asked if the Town was ready for after the Hurricane. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo said yes. We need to get the building up and running in order to help the residents. Mayor Martell stated we have items, and that if everything in the Town is secure, he will make the decision as to whether or not he will be closing Thursday and Friday. As of now, no final decision has been made. Since there was no further business to be considered, Councilperson Digiacomo moved to adjourn. segs.text: MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA APRIL 2, 2018 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on April 2, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by Josue Hernandez and Maikol Ortega from the Medley Police Explorers Post 67,the Town Council and Audience. The Minutes of the Regular Meeting of March 5, 2018 7:00 P.M. were discussed and approved. Presentation by Fire Chief Dave Downey on the Miami-Dade Fire Rescue (MDFR)2017 Service Delivery Report. Mr. Downey gave a brief presentation and informed the Mayor and Council on what they provide to our community. Mr. Downey stated that the Miami-Dade Fire Rescue originated as a single unit fire patrol in 1935 and it has since grown into the largest Fire Rescue Department in the Southeast United States and one of the top ten in the nation. It has a response territory of 1,899 square miles and a resident population of more than 1.9 million. MDFR responds to more than 260,000 calls for assistance annually making it one of the busiest Departments in the Nation. It has more than 2000 Firefighters, 143 units in service throughout 69 fire rescue stations and several administrative facilities serving residents, businesses and visitors 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. It is a strong Department and continues to grow. He thanked everyone for giving him the opportunity to speak at the meeting and to work with the Town. The Mayor and Council thanked him for his services. The appointment of four(4) Part-Time employees for the After School/Summer Camp Program in the Social Services Department was the next item on the Agenda. Supervisor Lizmari Valido stated that she recommends the hiring of Yenny Lorenzo, Claudia Oliver, Yessica Medina and Suanly Ascunce. They all have met the qualifications required for the position. If approved by the Town Council they can fulfil their positions on Tuesday,April 3, 2018. segs.text: The Minutes of the LPA and Regular Council Meeting of October 1, 2018 and the November 5, 2018 Regular Council Meeting were discussed and approved. segs.text: Ordinance C-433, Amending Chapter 62 Zoning by amending Article I In General Section 62-1 Definitions to provide Definitions related to Marijuana Uses; and by amending Article III District Regulations , Section 62-86 Restrictions in General , to prohibit Marijuana Dispensaries in all Zoning Districts was read by Town Attorney Arango. Attorney Arango stated that her co-worker Kathryn Mehaffey from Weiss Serota Helfman Cole & Bierman, P.L. was present to answer any specific questions on the Ordinance or on the regulations of Marijuana. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that when she read the Ordinance completely and saw that the Ordinance bans all of the Marijuana Dispensaries completely from the whole Town, she spoke to Attorney Arango and asked that someone come and explain all of the options to all of us because the reality is that this is the future and this is coming, and the Dispensaries if they are not in Medley, they will be in Hialeah or other Cities close to us and all over the County. She does not want those revenues that at one point can come to Medley to go to other Cities. The Town can place regulations and restrictions, but the way it reads now we are banning Dispensaries Page 3 December 3, 2018 completely. Kathryn Mehaffey stated that the State Legislature in 2016 the Constitutional Amendment was approved permitting Medical Marijuana usage within the State. The State Legislature adopted a Bill which regulates how Local Governments can control the Medical Marijuana. There are basically two (2) options. One is to prohibit and the second is to regulate it the same way as you regulate Pharmacies within your jurisdiction. Within Medley s jurisdiction Pharmacies are permitted in a large part of the Town and there are no restrictions. You can choose to prohibit, which is the Ordinance in front of you or you can choose to regulate. Right now, if you allow it, it would be permitted pretty much throughout the Town with no restrictions and no limits. Your choice, if you wish to allow, it is to either permit it totally unrestricted or impose regulations as long as you are willing to impose those same restrictions on Pharmacies. Councilperson Digiacomo asked if we regulate it, do we have to put the same restrictions on all pharmacies? Ms. Mehaffey said yes. All Pharmacies and Dispensaries must be treated in the same way. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked if tonight we approve this Ordinance prohibiting the Marijuana Dispensaries and then in the future, we want to chang

segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA FEBRUARY 21, 2018 ______________________________________________________________________________ A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on February 21, 2018 at 2:00 p.m.
votes: Vice-Mayor Pacheco moved as follows: TO INCREASE THE MONTHLY PENSION BENEFIT FOR PART TIME EMPLOYEES BY $30.00 A MONTH ON TOP OF COUNCILPERSON DIGIACOMO S REQUEST AS FOLLOWS: Age Years of Service Monthly Benefit 65 20 $270.00 65 25 $290.00 70 15 $250.00 70 20 $310.00 70 25 $330.00 Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA FEBRUARY 21, 2018 ______________________________________________________________________________ A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on February 21, 2018 at 2:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA SPECIAL COUNSEL: ALISON SMITH The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Mayor Martell announced that the purpose of this special meeting was to have a discussion and action on the Part-Time Employees Pension Benefit. Mayor Martell then asked Councilperson Digiacomo to present her request. She stated that she wanted to increase the monthly pension benefit for the Part Time Employees. She submitted a proposal, and Finance Director Roy Danziger also submitted a proposal. She wanted to know if anyone had any comments on her request. At this time no one spoke. She went ahead and explained her proposal as follows: Age Years of Service Monthly Benefit 65 20 $240.00 65 25 $260.00 70 15 $220.00 70 20 $280.00 70 25 $300.00 After reviewing the proposal Mayor Martell suggested a $10.00 a month increase on top of Councilpersons Digiacomo s request. Vice-Mayor Pacheco then suggested a $30.00 a month increase on top of Councilperson Digiacomo s request. After a brief discussion Vice-Mayor Pacheco moved as follows: TO INCREASE THE MONTHLY PENSION BENEFIT FOR PART TIME EMPLOYEES BY $30.00 A MONTH ON TOP OF COUNCILPERSON DIGIACOMO S REQUEST AS FOLLOWS: Age Years of Service Monthly Benefit 65 20 $270.00 65 25 $290.00 70 15 $250.00 70 20 $310.00 70 25 $330.00 Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Finance Director Roy Danziger stated that an Impact Statement needs to be done which is required by the State.
votes: Councilperson Digiacomo moved to adjourn. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Finance Director Roy Danziger stated that an Impact Statement needs to be done which is required by the State. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that once he comes back with the Impact Statement we can meet again and prepare an Ordinance. Mayor Martell thanked the Council and all the Employees. Vice-Mayor Pacheco then also thanked Councilperson Digiacomo for bring this up and for caring for the Employees. Councilperson Digiacomo wanted to thank Ms. Carmen Pelaez for bringing the idea to her. Since there was no further business to be considered Councilperson Digiacomo moved to adjourn. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 2:06 p.m. on February 21, 2018.

segs.head: The request by Councilperson Digiacomo for discussion and action on Parental Leave Policy was then discussed.
votes: Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO PREPARE A RESOLUTION FOR THE PAID PARENTAL LEAVE POLICY WITH FOUR (4) WEEKS OF FULL PAY . Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The request by Councilperson Digiacomo for discussion and action on Parental Leave Policy was then discussed. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that this policy will help new parents stay at home longer and receive full pay. Mayor Martell recommended to her to base the leave on years of service for example: 0 to 1 year of service will receive 0 weeks of pay; 1 year and 1 day to 4 years of service will receive 2 weeks of pay; 4 years and | day to 8 years of service will receive 4 weeks of pay; and 8 years and 1 day and up will receive 6 weeks of pay. Page 6 February 5, 2018 Councilperson Digiacomo stated she would prefer to offer 4 weeks of pay instead of 6 weeks of pay and that way it will benefit everyone who needs it. Special Counsel Alison Smith stated that the employee must first apply for short-term disability and once the short-term disability has finished then then the employee can apply for the 4 weeks of full pay. Councilperson Ayala stated that it was a good thing for mothers and their babies but not for the fathers. Special Counsel Alison Smith stated that the law does not discriminate, it is equal to both the mother and father. She stated that FMLA allows up to 12 weeks for both. After a brief discussion Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO PREPARE A RESOLUTION FOR THE PAID PARENTAL LEAVE POLICY WITH FOUR (4) WEEKS OF FULL PAY . Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

votes: Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO APPROVE THE TOWN OF MEDLEY FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR YEAR ENDING SEPTEMBER 30, 2017, PREPARED BY WITHUM SMITH+BROWN, PC. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The next item was a presentation by Ray Bastin, CPA from Withum Smith + Brown PC for discussion and approval of the September 30, 2017 Financial Statements. Mr. Bastin stated that he appreciated being here tonight and thanked the Town of Medley staff for working with him and his staff on obtaining all the information needed to prepare the financials. He presented the Mayor and Council with a Financial Report dated September 30, 2017 and then started explaining the Financials as follows: The assets of the Town exceeded its liabilities at the close of the most recent fiscal year by $178,823,515 (net position). Of this amount $16,448,366.00 (unrestricted net position) may be used to meet the government s ongoing obligations to residents and creditors. During the fiscal year, the Town s total net position decreased by $452,986.00 or by 0.3%. This is comprised of a decrease of $1,531,417.00 in governmental activities and an increase of $1,078,431.00 in business type activities. The decrease in governmental activities was attributable to expenses being greater than revenues. Compare to last year, when there was an increase in net position of $115,237.00, current year s decrease in net position was $1,531,417.00. Total revenues decreased by $963,318.00 primarily due to decreases in other general taxes, permit fees, fines and charges for services. Total governmental expenditures increased from 2016 by $683,336.00 primarily due to increases in general government, public safety and human services expenses. The increase in business type activities was attributable to revenues being greater than expenses. Compared to last year, when there was an increase in net position of $567,172.00, current year s increase in net position was $1,078,431.00. Revenues decreasing include user charges and service and hook-up charges by $43,390.00 and grants by $205,121.00. Operating expenses decreased by $772,804.00, primarily due to a decrease in sewer treatment costs. As of the close of the current fiscal year, the Town s governmental funds reported combined ending fund equity of $14,118,520.00, a decrease of $1,644,738.00 in comparison with the prior year. Of this amount, $12,201,590.00 is available for spending at the government s discretion (assigned or unassigned fund balance) of which $9,200,000.00 has been assigned for future projects and expenditures consisting of $2,000,000.00 for pensions, $5,000,000.00 for working capital, $900,000.00 for debt service and $1,300,000.00 for

segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 18, 2018 A workshop meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 18, 2018 at 6:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO (ABSENT) JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience.. Mayor Martell announced that the purpose of this special meeting was to have a discussion on the proposed Budget for the fiscal year October 1, 2018 through September 30, 2019; and to discuss and establish the proposed tentative millage rate based upon the Certification of Taxable Value of real and personal property within the Town of Medley for the fiscal year October 1, 2018 through September 30, 2019. Proper notice had been given. Mayor Martell then asked Finance Director Roy Danziger to proceed with the Budget. Roy submitted Budget worksheets with the Actual and Projected Budget to the Mayor and Council for discussion tonight. He stated that tonight the goal is to set the tentative millage rate. The current millage rate is 5.4000 mills with a rolled back rate of 5.0260. What we want to propose is a millage rate of 6.3000 mills, which is approximately 25% increase in taxes, we can always go lower. He then started explaining the Budget worksheets page by page. He stated that he is predicting a projected deficit of $2,480,113.00. We cannot go into reserves every year. If reserves are too low the Town needs to borrow money and it might have to borrow at a higher interest rate. Roy stated that the proposed budget includes a 3% salary increase for all FPE Union employees and PBA employees. He then asked about salary increases for all non-union employees and part timers. Vice-Mayor Pacheco asked to hold off on the decision at this time. Roy continued explaining the Budget. He is projecting a 10% increase in medical insurance and requested reduction in office supplies. He continued as follows: General Fund - General Administration Department: No changes. General Fund - Building and Zoning Department: No changes. General Fund - Public Safety No changes. General Fund - Code Compliance No changes. General Fund - Physical Environment (Public Works) No changes. General Fund - Capital Improvement and Economic Development No changes. Gene

segs.text: MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 4, 2018 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on June 4, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO (ABSENT) COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by Clifford Gurdian and Maikol Ortega from the Medley Police Explorers Post 67,the Town Council and Audience. segs.head: MINUTES OF A WORKSHOP MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MAY 10, 2018 9:10 A.M. A Sexual Harassment Workshop was called to order on May 10, 2018 at 9:10 a.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A WORKSHOP MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MAY 10, 2018 9:10 A.M. A Sexual Harassment Workshop was called to order on May 10, 2018 at 9:10 a.m. The following were present: Roberto Martell, Mayor Ivan Pacheco, Vice-Mayor Griselia Digiacomo, Councilperson Herlina Taboada, Town Clerk Victoria Martinez, Assistant Town Clerk/Legal Assistant Roy Danziger, Town of Medley Finance Director Alison Smith, Esq., Town Attorney Special Labor Counsel Alison Smith opened the meeting by giving different scenarios of Sexual Harassment cases. She explained each case one by one and helped everyone understand the difference between cases and why some were considered sexual harassment and why others were not. She explained that in order for a sexual harassment case to go to court the case must be severe. If there is a pattern you can get sued. You need to be very careful in what you say, in what you do and how you act. If there is inappropriate behavior and you don't tell that person, or that person does not mind then it is not considered Sexual Harassment. Whether you are on the clock or off the clock nothing changes. If you see or hear something you need to bring it forward even if it is not directly with you. A person can be fired even if the incident occurred years ago. Harassment in the workplace is a form of discrimination. Harassment must be tied to a protected category. If you fail to report harassment even if you did not participate in the harassment you are subject to disciplinary action. If comments are not welcomed,then it is sexual harassment. There are two forms of sexual harassment Quid Pro- Quo and Hostile Environment. Sixteen (16)% of lawsuits for sexual harassment are filed by men and eighty-four (84)% are filed by women. Harassment can happen anywhere: In the workplace, outside the workplace, business trip, business meeting, business related social events, holiday parties, after holiday parties, after hour meetings, facebook, twitter, blog, testing, you tube, e-mail, and other forms of electronic forms of social media. Words that can be considered harassment: honey, baby, sweetie, girl, boy, stud, bimbo, hunk, etc. Comments on clothing, body language, behavior of the person's body, looking up and down, kissing, hugging, personal gift, etc. Special Counsel Smith stated that no matter where you are at, you must be very careful in what you say, what you do, how you act, etc. because if it is not liked by the other person you can get in trouble.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA OCTOBER 1, 2018 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on October 1, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO JACK MORROW TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Morrow Councilperson Morrow and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Town Council and Audience. The Minutes of the Regular Council Meeting of September 4, 2018, the Special Meetings of September 11, 2018 and September 24, 2018 were discussed and approved. Mayor Martell announced that there was an add-on item on the Agenda which was a Presentation by Bob Reynolds on insurance renewals. Councilperson Digiacomo moved to approve this add-on. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Councilperson Ayala congratulated Herlina Taboada for her 38 years of service to the Town and congratulated Jose Guasch for his 25 years of service to the Town.
votes: Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO APPOINT ANGEL HERNANDEZ TO THE POSITION OF METER READER LOCATOR IN THE UTILITIES DEPARTMENT TO BE EFFECTIVE OCTOBER 2, 2018. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Councilperson Ayala congratulated Herlina Taboada for her 38 years of service to the Town and congratulated Jose Guasch for his 25 years of service to the Town. The Mayor and Council congratulated both. Mayor Martell asked if anyone in the audience wanted to speak on any item on the Agenda to please come forward. No one came forward. Mayor Martell announced that today we have one of our Special Officers Arturo Jinete. He went to the FBI Academy in Virginia and passed the Academy with Honors. Mayor Martell stated that it was a great Honor to present him with a plaque for his dedication and service. Arturo Jinete then thanked the Mayor for giving him the opportunity to go there. He also thanked the Council, Co-workers, Residents and Businesses for all their support. Chief Said stated that should could not be any prouder of him for what he represents to Medley and for all of us. Finance Director Roy Danziger then introduced Christopher Kittleson from Preferred Government Insurance Trust. He is from our Workers Compensation Insurance Provider and is the Town s safety coordinator. Mr. Kittleson then gave a brief presentation on the safety program and presented the Town with a $5,000.00 ceremonial check to the Town. He then asked for a group picture with the Council. Finance Director Roy Danziger also introduced Andrew Woodcock and Diana Santander from Tetra Tech and stated that they have prepared a Water/Sewer Rate Study which basically compares our Water and Sewer rates to what other Water Utilities charge and what we should be charging. Andrew Woodcock presented a brochure which explains the purpose for the study, the existing commercial rates, revenue sufficiency analysis, rate adjustments, calculated rates for water showing existing and calculated rates, calculated rates for sewer also showing existing and calculated rates, changes to the monthly bill combined water and sewer, comparison with other Cities, and recommendations as to what the Town can do. Mayor Martell stated that he will speak to Utilities Director Jorge Soto to see what he recommends. Councilperson Ayala believes we need to go forward with this. Finance Director Roy Danziger stated that he will do a detail study based on their recommendation to see how it will affect our customers. Mayor then asked Roy and Soto to give him the numbers. Councilperson Digiacomo then asked if this was for informational purposes only. She was informed that yes, for informational purposes only, no decision will

segs.text: The next item was also the appointment of one (1) Laborer Position for the Utilities Department. Jorge Soto recommends the appointment of Michael Guasch. After a brief discussion Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO APPOINT MICHAEL GUASCH TO THE POSITION OF LABORER IN THE UTILITIES DEPARTMENT. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Jorge Soto stated that originally the Town advertised for two (2) positions, but at this time he could only appoint one (1) due to the amount of responses received and the need for a High School Diploma or a GED. He then stated that we need to re-advertise for one more position in the future.

segs.head: Page 2 October 1, 2018 The next item was the presentation by Bob Reynolds from Morris & Reynolds regarding the renewal of the Town s Business Insurance on November 1, 2018.
votes: Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO RENEW THE TOWN S BUSINESS INSURANCE WITH THE TRAVELERS AND MAINTAIN THE 3% WIND STORM DEDUCTIBLE; AND FOLLOW BOB REYNOLDS S RECOMMENDATION AS HE SUGGESTED IN THE OUTLINE SUBMITTED FOR OTHER CHANGES TO THE POLICY. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Page 2 October 1, 2018 The next item was the presentation by Bob Reynolds from Morris & Reynolds regarding the renewal of the Town s Business Insurance on November 1, 2018. He submitted a brochure with all of the Town s options. The first is Property Insurance which is currently with The Travelers. Bob Reynolds gave a brief presentation on the property insurance and reminded the Mayor and Council that the Town currently has a 3% wind storm deductible. If the Town wishes, it could increase the deductible to 5%, it would save the Town $6,215.00 but would expose the Town to $307,786.00. The savings is not worth an added claim if we were to have a claim. He suggested that it was not a good idea. Mayor Martell suggested that the Town keep the 3% wind storm deductible. After a brief presentation Councilperson Digiacomo moved as follows: TO RENEW THE TOWN S BUSINESS INSURANCE WITH THE TRAVELERS AND MAINTAIN THE 3% WIND STORM DEDUCTIBLE; AND FOLLOW BOB REYNOLDS S RECOMMENDATION AS HE SUGGESTED IN THE OUTLINE SUBMITTED FOR OTHER CHANGES TO THE POLICY. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Bob Reynolds then discussed several other insurances.
votes: Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO APPROVE THE STANDARD FOR THE TOWN S LIFE INSURANCE AND PRUDENTIAL FOR THE TOWN S DISABILITY INSURANCE TO BE EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2019. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Bob Reynolds then discussed several other insurances. He stated that for the Life and Disability Insurance we are under a contract until January 1, 2020, but we are not obligated to keep them. That coverage is with the Hartford Life. The Town s options are to keep the current company and make no changes, or the second option would be in his opinion to change and consolidate that coverage with The Standard. The Standard handles all of the Town s Retirement Plans and they specialize in Municipalities and they would do the Life and Disability if we wanted them too. The Standard would save the Town approximately $7,292.40. Councilperson Digiacomo asked if we would go with the change when would that be effective? Bob stated it would be effective 1-1-19 and would take all of our employees without evidence of insurability, no individual applications. She asked including employees with disabilities? He said yes, and the third option is to use The Standard for the Life Insurance and Prudential for the Disability Insurance and the combination of the two would save the Town approximately $20,784.12. After a brief discussion Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO APPROVE THE STANDARD FOR THE TOWN S LIFE INSURANCE AND PRUDENTIAL FOR THE TOWN S DISABILITY INSURANCE TO BE EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2019. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The Dental Insurance also renews January 1, 2019 and it is currently with Cigna. Cigna has raised the HMO 4% and no change to the PPO. Bob Reynolds recommends that the Town renew

segs.head: and retain Cigna for the dental.
votes: Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO RENEW AND RETAIN CIGNA FOR THE TOWN S DENTAL INSURANCE TO BE EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2019. Page 3 October 1, 2018 Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: and retain Cigna for the dental. After a brief discussion Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO RENEW AND RETAIN CIGNA FOR THE TOWN S DENTAL INSURANCE TO BE EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2019. Page 3 October 1, 2018 Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: The Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Insurance renews January 1, 2019.
votes: Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: TO MAINTAIN THE PLAN THROUGH ALL STATE AND EXTEND IT TO ALL PART TIME EMPLOYEES WHO QUALIFY. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Insurance renews January 1, 2019. We do not have the rates yet, they will not publish them until around November and he expects the cost for that plan to be within 1% or 2% above the current cost if it changes at all. The Town should maintain the current plan. The last plan is a volunteer plan and it covers illness, hospital indemnity, accident etc., and the plan is with All State and it also renews January 1, 2019. There is no change in the cost. He was asked as part of the research to confirm whether that voluntary program could be offered to part time employees and the answer is yes, if the Town decided to do that, it would only be for employees who work 17 1/2 hours or more weekly. This insurance is optional, and employees decide what they want and if they want it or not. After a brief discussion Councilperson Morrow moved as follows: TO MAINTAIN THE PLAN THROUGH ALL STATE AND EXTEND IT TO ALL PART TIME EMPLOYEES WHO QUALIFY. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Report by Vice-Mayor Pacheco on Waste Management Trash Carts for Residents was the next item to be discussed.
segs.text: Report by Vice-Mayor Pacheco on Waste Management Trash Carts for Residents was the next item to be discussed. Vice-Mayor Pacheco stated that before he got elected he had no doubt in his mind that we had to upgrade the way garbage for the residents was being picked up. After he got elected he approached Mary Taylor and she rapidly scheduled a meeting with Mr. Sori and Mr. Gonzalez from Waste Management and he presented the idea to them. Mr. Sori and Mr. Gonzalez were very happy about his concern and started the process of obtaining the carts at a zero cost to the Town of Medley and zero cost to the Residents. Vice-Mayor Pacheco then thanked Mr. Sori for his dedication and long hours spent with this process to make this happen, Mayor Martell for helping in the distribution of the carts, Mary Taylor for her scheduling of the meetings and her suggestions, Councilperson Digiacomo for helping in the distribution of the carts, Mr. Heriberto Cabrera and his group of employees for coordinating the logistics and the distribution of the carts Town-wide. Mayor Martell also thanked him, Waste Management and the rest of the crew who worked on this project.

segs.head: Ordinance C-429, Amending Chapter 62, Zoning by amending Article III District Regulations , Section 62-87(d)-(e), to amend regulations related to Setbacks for One-Family Districts applicable to properties located between N.W.
segs.text: Ordinance C-429, Amending Chapter 62, Zoning by amending Article III District Regulations , Section 62-87(d)-(e), to amend regulations related to Setbacks for One-Family Districts applicable to properties located between N.W. South River Drive and the Miami (C-6) Page 5 October 1, 2018 Canal was read by Town Attorney Arango. Resident Lily Stefano wanted to know why are the only properties affected on the Canal and not the rest of Medley? Town Engineer Jorge Corzo stated that the reason we are addressing that now is because the Town just completed N.W. South River Drive between N.W. 72 Avenue and N.W. 74 Street and we are also planning to continue N.W. South River Drive east of Palmetto Expressway to N.W. 72 Avenue. Those lots are very irregular, and we are focusing on that segment because if we leave it the way it is, having 20 feet of setback basically leaves nothing because of the canal on the back. This is the first step because as we speaking we are working on that design. We need to improve that road and place side walks and improve the area. Ms. Stefano said that the Town already did a part of N.W. South River Drive and the setback was not changed. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo stated that this will cover both sides. She wanted to know if we had some type of paperwork stating that the Town will continue with the rest of Medley especially the residential areas. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo that she had his word. She said that we need to get it in writing. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo stated that we are constantly looking for ways to work with the residents. After a lengthily discussion Attorney Arango wanted to clarify that the motion is to approve the Ordinance with the highlighted change to Section 62-87(d). Councilperson Digiacomo moved to approve this Ordinance with the change on second reading. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and the following votes were cast:

segs.head: Vice-Mayor Pacheco: Yes Councilperson Digiacomo: Yes Councilperson Ayala: Yes Councilperson Morrow: Abstained Mayor Martell: Yes The motion was carried by majority vote.

It applies to members of advisory and non-advisory bodies who are presented with a voting conflict of interest under Section 112.3143, Florida Statutes. Your responsibilities under the law when faced with voting on a measure in which you have a conflict of interest will vary greatly depending on whether you hold an elective or appointive position. For this reason, please pay close attention to the instructions on this form before completing and filing the form. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 112.3143, FLORIDA STATUTES A person holding elective or appointive county, municipal, or other local public office MUST ABSTAIN from voting on a measure which would inure to his or her special private gain or loss. Each elected or appointed local officer also MUST ABSTAIN from knowingly voting on a measure which would inure to the special gain or loss of a principal (other than a government agency) by whom he or she is retained (including the parent, subsidiary, or sibling organization of a principal by which he or she is retained); to the special private gain or loss of a relative; or to the special private gain or loss of a business associate. Commissioners of community redevelopment agencies (CRAs) under Sec. 163.356 or 163.357, F.S., and officers of independent special tax districts elected on a one-acre, one-vote basis are not prohibited from voting in that capacity. For purposes of this law, a relative includes only the officer's father, mother, son, daughter, husband, wife, brother, sister, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law, and daughter-in-law. segs.text: (1) Road Repairs, Repairs to Entrance and Repairs to Seawall. Roy stated that salary benefits by Department have decreased by working with less employees and others have retired. Town Attorney Arango stated that she wanted to publicly announce that she has not heard of any changes or amendments to the Proposed Budget or the Proposed Millage Rate and should publicly announce that the proposed Millage Rate of 6.3000 Mills exceeds or increases the Rolled back rate of 5.0260 Mills by 25.35 % this is the percentage increase on property taxes. votes: Mayor Martell moved as follows: Page 3 September 4, 2018 TO APPROVE THAT ALL PART TIME EMPLOYEES BE PAID FOR ALL TOWN OF MEDLEY RECOGNIZED HOLIDAYS AND THAT NO SERVICES BE PROVIDED ON THOSE DAYS, TO BE EFFECTIVE OCTOBER 1, 2018. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The request by Councilperson Digiacomo for Discussion and Action on Part-Time Employees Holiday Pay was then held. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that part-time employees work on certain Holidays depending on their schedule and get paid double time. She is proposing that all part-timers be given the thirteen (13) Town of Medley recognized Holidays off, the same way full-time employees take the time off. If the part-time employee is scheduled to work on the day of the recognized holiday, they will then take the day off and be paid, at regular time, for the same number of hours scheduled to work on that day. Thus, the Town will not provide any services on any of the recognized holidays with the exception of the After-School program that opens on certain holidays like Columbus Day in which the public schools remain open. Councilperson Digiacomo specified that the Holiday Pay proposal is in addition to the current floating days benefit that part-time employees already receive. After a brief discussion Mayor Martell moved as follows: Page 3 September 4, 2018 TO APPROVE THAT ALL PART TIME EMPLOYEES BE PAID FOR ALL TOWN OF MEDLEY RECOGNIZED HOLIDAYS AND THAT NO SERVICES BE PROVIDED ON THOSE DAYS, TO BE EFFECTIVE OCTOBER 1, 2018. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA APRIL 1, 2019 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on April 1, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: EDGAR AYALA COUNCIL MEMBERS: GRISELIA DIGIACOMO IVAN PACHECO LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA ASST. TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Town Council and audience. The Minutes of the Regular Meeting of March 4, 2019 and the Special Meetings of March 11 and March 21, 2019 were discussed and approved. Mayor Martell stated that he wanted to move some items forward on the Agenda. The first item was a discussion and action on the appointment of one (1) Laborer Position for the Public Works Department. Public Works Director Heriberto Cabrera stated that the position for a new Laborer Position Full Time was posted. Applications were received and after careful review he recommends Ivan Gonzalez for the position, he is the one that is most qualified for the job and with the Council s approval he will start working on April 2, 2019. TO APPROVE THE HIRING OF IVAN GONZALEZ AS LABORER ON A FULL TIME BASIS FOR THE PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT EFFECTIVE APRIL 2, 2019. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Ivan Gonzalez then thanked the Mayor and Council.

segs.head: The request by Miami Springs Chief Armando Guzman to address the Town Council was the next item.
segs.text: The request by Miami Springs Chief Armando Guzman to address the Town Council was the next item. Chief Guzman thanked the Mayor and Council for giving him the opportunity to make this brief presentation. He stated that he was appointed Chief for the City of Miami Springs in January 2015 and one of the first people he met at that time was Chief Said-Jinete. She was very graceful in offering assistance, help and cooperation and that has been going on through the years. He stated that recently they were able to acquire a very expensive software for dispatching and report writing at a very discounted price through the assistance and cooperation of Chief Said-Jinete. He thought it was important for the Mayor and Council to know about the extent of their professional relationship and the extent of being close friends. Chief Said-Jinete gets along very well with his wife and he also gets along with Arturo. He is here tonight to present Chief Said-Jinete with a Certificate of Appreciation from himself and members of the Miami Springs Police Department. Mayor Martell thanked him for coming over and stated that the Town s Chief is amazing, she works hard and is very committed to our Town. He stated that we don t get too many people like that now a days. We are all very proud of having Staff and Department Heads like her. She is superb. Artie Jinete then announced that last night was the first time in many years that they could get the Police Department and Public Works Department together to play a fun game of softball, the teams were led by Mr. Cabrera. We were able to unite both departments and played at the Miami Springs Field. Everyone came out to support us, its something we should do like we did in the past, but we are already planning on doing it again. He thanked Mr. Cabrera for putting the event together and having them there. Arturo Jinete also stated that last week was the Explorers yearly competition. It was a three (3) day event and our kids participated as volunteers as role players and he wanted to thank Edgar, Lily for helping with donating candy. He said Ivan was there but was not sure about Griselia. He stated that without that kind of support this does not happen. He wanted to thank everyone for showing up to all of these events and supporting them. Mayor Martell stated that they are doing a great job, keeping the kids in doing a wonderful job and representing our City. Mayor Martell then asked Town Attorney Arango to continue with the meeting. It applies to members of advisory and non-advisory bodies who are presented with a voting conflict of interest under Section 112.3143, Florida Statutes. Your responsibilities under the law when faced with voting on a measure in which you have a conflict of interest will vary greatly depending on whether you hold an elective or appointive position. For this reason, please pay close attention to the instructions on this form before completing and filing the form. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 112.3143, FLORIDA STATUTES A person holding elective or appointive county, municipal, or other local public office MUST ABSTAIN from voting on a measure which would inure to his or her special private gain or loss. Each elected or appointed local officer also MUST ABSTAIN from knowingly voting on a measure which would inure to the special gain or loss of a principal (other than a government agency) by whom he or she is retained (including the parent, subsidiary, or sibling organization of a principal by which he or she is retained); to the special private gain or loss of a relative; or to the special private gain or loss of a business associate. Commissioners of community redevelopment agencies (CRAs) under Sec. 163.356 or 163.357, F.S., and officers of independent special tax districts elected on a one-acre, one-vote basis are not prohibited from voting in that capacity. segs.head: Special Council Meeting of April 30, 2019 The next and last item was agenda item A which was a presentation by Patricia Romeu, Chief of the Miami-Dade County Department of Cultural Affairs/Arts in Public Places Program.
votes: Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO APPROVE THE ARTWORK/SCULPTURE AS PRESENTED AND SELECTED BY THE MIAMI-DADE COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF CULTURFAL AFFAIRS/ART IN PUBLIC PLACES PROGRAM Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Special Council Meeting of April 30, 2019 The next and last item was agenda item A which was a presentation by Patricia Romeu, Chief of the Miami-Dade County Department of Cultural Affairs/Arts in Public Places Program. Ms. Romeu informed the Town Council that she had been working closely with the Mayor, Town Engineer Jorge Corzo and Executive Assistant Susana Guasch and at this point was happy to present a model of the selected and proposed sculpture to the Council. She informed the Town that the committee selected artist Carlos Enrique Prado, a well renowned artist. The chosen artist was among six (6) who submitted their vision and concept under specific directions including what the vision of the city was. Ms. Romeu also explained that the funds allocated for the monument are funds that were appropriated through the Arts in Public Places Program that was approved when the Town of Medley Municipal Services Facility was built. The selected artwork is a fourteen (14) feet high metal sculpture that incorporates the Town s map engraved in. The artwork is titled Rising Above the Horizon which reflects a creative approach showing the vision of the City. The sculpture will reflect the current map of the Town in the inner face and the other side will be polished reflective metal. The sculpture will be the focal point of the plaza located in front of the Town of Medley Municipal Services Facility. The implementation time is approximately twelve (12) months. The artist is looking to engage with local businesses and local metal fabricators. Ms. Romeu then moved to inform the Town Council that The Miami-Dade County Art in Public Places Trust is meeting in two (2) weeks and a consensus from the Town is needed before they move forward with implementation. After a brief discussion Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO APPROVE THE ARTWORK/SCULPTURE AS PRESENTED AND SELECTED BY THE MIAMI-DADE COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF CULTURFAL AFFAIRS/ART IN PUBLIC PLACES PROGRAM Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion it was carried unanimously. segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA AUGUST 20, 2019 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on August 20, 2019 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: EDGAR AYALA COUNCIL MEMBERS: GRISELIA DIGIACOMO IVAN PACHECO LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and The Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited. Councilperson DiGiacomo moved to place a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and the agenda was adopted by a unanimous vote.

segs.head: Item A of the agenda to discuss the proposed staffing request of the Department of Capital Improvement Projects and Economic Development was held.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows: TO CREATE AND ALLOCATE BUDGET FUNDING FOR AN ASSISTANT DIRECTOR OF THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. Special Council Meeting of August 20, 2019 Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Item A of the agenda to discuss the proposed staffing request of the Department of Capital Improvement Projects and Economic Development was held. Director Jorge Corzo distributed a department s operational organizational chart to be reviewed along with the rest of the item s documentation. The documentation as provided to the Council for consideration and approval reflected a list of five (5) positions including a Capital Improvement Projects and Economic Development Assistant Director. The recommendation as presented for this position included the recommendation for appointment of Manny Perez, a current employee of Snubbs Consulting Inc. Director Corzo further stated that said position, because of the requirements of certain existing Town programs, require an engineering license. Thus, having these duties performed by a full- time employee instead of having them outsourced to the consultant present significant savings to the Town. Vice-Mayor Ayala and Councilperson DiGiacomo both addressed Director Corzo to clarify and confirm that upon the approval of his recommendation of creating the position and appointing Manny Perez, a replacement for his current position and/or job duties will not be requested by the Town nor provided by Snubbs Consulting Services Inc. After a brief discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows: TO CREATE AND ALLOCATE BUDGET FUNDING FOR AN ASSISTANT DIRECTOR OF THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. Special Council Meeting of August 20, 2019 Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: The next position to be discussed was the Procurement Specialist position.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows: TO CREATE AND ALLOCATE BUDGET FUNDING FOR A PROCUREMENT SPECIALIST FOR THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried by majority of vote.
segs.text: The next position to be discussed was the Procurement Specialist position. Councilperson Stefano addressed Director Corzo to clarify whether this position was to carry out the duties of procurement solely for his department or for the Town in general. Mayor Martell then added that the position is to perform said duties for the Capital Improvements department only. However, depending on the performance, said position could be considered to be extended to perform the same duties for the entire Town organization. Councilperson DiGiacomo added that in the case the Mayor s plan is considered and brought back to Council, a whole department were to be created. After no further discussion was held, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows: TO CREATE AND ALLOCATE BUDGET FUNDING FOR A PROCUREMENT SPECIALIST FOR THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried by majority of vote.

segs.head: The other position next to be discussed was the engineering technician position.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows: TO CREATE AND ALLOCATE BUDGET FUNDING FOR A CIVIL ENGINERING TECHICIAN/PROJECT COORDINATOR FOR THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The other position next to be discussed was the engineering technician position. This position includes administrative work and is also to perform inspections of Town projects. A discussion on the amount of positions requested for the department was held to which Director Corzo clarified and confirmed his request of a total of five (5) positions. The Council, although two (2) Engineering Technician positions were requested, only agreed to approve of one (1). After no further discussion was held on this issue, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows: TO CREATE AND ALLOCATE BUDGET FUNDING FOR A CIVIL ENGINERING TECHICIAN/PROJECT COORDINATOR FOR THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: The next item to be discussed was item B of the agenda which was a discussion and action on the proposed budget for FY 2019-2020.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion to adopt it with the recommendations as reported herein. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Before the meeting was closed, Councilperson DiGiacomo asked permission to discuss the usage of Town issued credit cards.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion, Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Before the meeting was closed, Councilperson DiGiacomo asked permission to discuss the usage of Town issued credit cards. She stated that currently there were only two (2) Town issued credit cards available and it was being used for all Town needs. Councilperson DiGiacomo further requested for all directors to have a Town issued credit card of their own to be solely used for the needs of their respective department. In addition, it was agreed upon that no credit card should be shared, and each department director s issued Town credit card should have a limit of $ 5000. It was also mentioned that the limit on the credit cards previously issued to the Chief of Police Said-Jinete and Town Clerk Victoria Martinez to be left at the current credit limit as they are both used during events of emergency in nature. However, in the case where a department s director has the need for the available to be increased, instructions to the Town Clerk were given to approve the increase without having to bring the request before the Town Council for approval. After a brief discussion on the matter, Mayor Martell placed a motion, Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
