segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC INFORMATIONAL MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA AUGUST 29, 2019 11:00 A.M A public informational and emergency operations meeting was called to order on August 29, 2019 at 11:00 A.M. The following were present: Mayor Roberto Martell Public Works Director Heriberto Cabrera Vice Mayor Edgar Ayala Utilities Director Jorge Soto Councilperson Griselia Digiacomo Building & Zoning Director Richard McConachie Councilperson Ivan Pacheco Social Services Director Lizmari Valido Councilperson Lily Stefano Code Compliance Director Jose Guasch Town Clerk Victoria Martinez Finance Director Roy Danziger Police Chief Jeanette Said Jinete Custodial & Janitorial Services Director Omar Sanchez Meal Program Director Fatima Fuentes Police Chief Jeanette Said-Jinete, as part of the Town s unified command, opened the meeting informing how the Town through its emergency operations plan was getting ready for hurricane Dorian. She advised that the next briefing with the Miami-Dade County Operations Center would take place at 1:45 pm but circumstances up to this point were uncertain and to plan and prepare was strongly encouraged. She also shared that no evacuation orders had been announced at this point in time for Miami-Dade County, thus shelters had not been assigned. Once and if an evacuation order is issued for Miami-Dade County, the Town will automatically notify the residents through all social media platforms and through its Code Red notification system. Police Chief Said-Jinete then went around for all directors and/or Emergency Plan Section Chiefs to inform the public the status of their preparation orders. Building & Zoning Official Richard McConachie together with Code Compliance Director Jose Guasch informed that both departments staff were ready to initiate any damage assessments needed after the storm. Code Compliance director also mentioned that his department had started to reach out to businesses and residents to encourage them to eliminate any outside storage on premises to minimize any potential projectiles. Social Services Director Lizmari Valido and Utilities Director Jorge Soto informed that pictures of Town facilities and Town infrastructure had been taken to document any possible impact and property damage. segs.head: Resolution C-1751 Approving the Purchase and Installation of Novatime Web-Based Time and Attendance System, Pursuant to the Proposal of Andrews Technology HMS, Inc.

segs.text: Resolution C-1751 Approving the Purchase and Installation of Novatime Web-Based Time and Attendance System, Pursuant to the Proposal of Andrews Technology HMS, Inc. Attached as Exhibit A . Councilperson DiGiacomo brought up some question about the new proposed time clock system. Assistant Finance Director Isabel Hughes approached the podium to explain that this new system is to replace the current Kronos time program purchased three (3) years ago. Assistant Finance Director Hughes further explained that Novatime offers a better integration with the BS&A finance and payroll system. Vice-Mayor Ayala raised the question that given the proposal is for a three (3) year commitment, if the staff was prepared to take action if the software wouldn t work as expected. Finance Director Roy Danziger explained that Novatime was highly recommended by BS&A representatives and other cities that have it already in place. In addition, Mr. Danziger explained that the current Kronos time clock software will expire in early 2020. Thus, the proposal, if approved by Council, would replace the existing Kronos software for a fully integrational option. Vice-Mayor Ayala moved to place a motion to adopt Resolution C-1751, Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that he had been thinking for a whole year about the Town Charter.
segs.text: Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that he had been thinking for a whole year about the Town Charter. He stated that he believes that the Town needs to make a review of the current Charter. He said that there will be Elections in two (2) years and his main concern is the one (1) year residency requirement. He believes that the residency requirement is a very short time, that it should be changed for future candidates running for office. He also has other minor changes that he would like to propose. Town Attorney Arango stated that it is a Statutory and County issue. We must comply with both, we need to schedule with the County and there are deadlines to get it on the ballot. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that the only way we can change it is through elections. Councilperson Stefano stated that the Town should do a complete Charter review, not just for the Page 2 February 4, 2019 residency requirement. The Town Charter is not very clear, and this would be the opportunity to review the whole Charter, since it must go through a voting process. Town Attorney Arango stated that she will come back to the March 2019 meeting with the exact procedure to follow for both processes.

Mayor Martell moved to approve this Resolution, Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Resolution C-1713 approving the purchase and installation of a license plate recognition system from Vetted Solutions, LLC was read into the record by Town Attorney Lillian Arango.
votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo moved to approve this Resolution, Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Resolution C-1713 approving the purchase and installation of a license plate recognition system from Vetted Solutions, LLC was read into the record by Town Attorney Lillian Arango. Finance Director Roy Danziger and Chief of Police Jeanette Said-Jinete addressed the Council to confirm that the purchase, as previously mentioned, was being funded through forfeiture funds. Councilperson DiGiacomo moved to approve this Resolution, Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Discussion and Action on the Appointment of two (2) laborer positions for the Utilities Department was then held.
segs.text: Discussion and Action on the Appointment of two (2) laborer positions for the Utilities Department was then held. Supervisor Jorge Soto approached the Council and recommended Kevin Perez and Enrique Martinez III for the two (2) Laborer positions. Vice-Mayor Ayala July 1, 2019 Regular Council Meeting moved to approve the recommendation and appointment of Kevin Perez for the laborer position. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the second recommendation and appointment of Enrique Martinez III for the utility s laborer position.
votes: Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the second recommendation and appointment of Enrique Martinez III for the utility s laborer position. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the second recommendation and appointment of Enrique Martinez III for the utility s laborer position. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Discussion and action on the appointment of one (1) Part-Time After School/Summer Camp Program Certified Teacher position was then held.
votes: Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the recommendation and appointment of Leslie Vazquez. Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Discussion and action on the appointment of one (1) Part-Time After School/Summer Camp Program Certified Teacher position was then held. Director Lizmari Valido informed the Town Council of the recommendation of Leslie Vazquez. She also stated that Ms. Vazquez is a current teacher of the Miami Springs Middle School and has been actively volunteering with her son in the Medley Youth Social Club. Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the recommendation and appointment of Leslie Vazquez. Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Discussion and action on the appointment of three (3) part-time after school/summer camp counselors for the Social Services and Park and Recreations Department was held.
votes: Councilperson Ivan Pacheco moved to approve the appointment of the three (3) part-time positions as recommended by director Valido. Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Discussion and action on the appointment of three (3) part-time after school/summer camp counselors for the Social Services and Park and Recreations Department was held. Eivys Amador, Angelique Rodriguez and Jessica Diaz were introduced by Social Services and Parks and Recreations Department Lizmari Valido, which stated that all three (3) successful applicants had completed the childcare training requirement. Councilperson Ivan Pacheco moved to approve the appointment of the three (3) part-time positions as recommended by director Valido. Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Resolution C-1714 approving the emergency purchase and installation of two (2) roof top A/C units and plan service agreement for the Medley Municipal Services Facility was read into the record by Town Attorney Arango.
votes: Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve Resolution C-1714, Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Resolution C-1714 approving the emergency purchase and installation of two (2) roof top A/C units and plan service agreement for the Medley Municipal Services Facility was read into the record by Town Attorney Arango. Richard McConachie, Director of the Building and Zoning Department explained to the Town Council that because of the proprietary software that controls the A/C units which is licensed and operated by Johnson Controls, the Town can treat the proposal as a sole source proposal since the Town s A/C system was designed to be operated and controlled by said computer software. After a brief discussion, Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve Resolution C-1714, Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: The next item discussed was the recommendations submitted for the Social Services Programs and Operations.
segs.text: The next item discussed was the recommendations submitted for the Social Services Programs and Operations. Director Valido explained how the recommendations as included for Council approval, were the same recommendations that were discussed on the Council Workshop held on June 5, 2019 with the exception of one additional change made to the MYSC program in which the starting age of 13 or older was added in the final recommendation memorandum. The council entered into a brief debate and concluded to approve the recommendations as proposed by Director Valido and the following additions. - All Town of Medley events will have an entrance fee of five dollars ($5) for all non- resident guests. Vendors, Police explorers, Medley Chamber of Commerce Executive Board and non-resident MYSC members will be allowed to bring one (1) guest each and both, members and their guest will be exempt from said entrance fee. In addition, music night events will be open to both, residents and non-residents, with the exceptions of special events that could be held during music night events that would be treated as special events and not as the regular music night program. July 1, 2019 Regular Council Meeting Mayor Martell carried a motion to approve the recommendations as presented and additions. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: In continuance, a discussion on a proposed full-time Social Services Clerk position was held.
votes: Mayor Roberto Martell then moved to approve the position, Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: In continuance, a discussion on a proposed full-time Social Services Clerk position was held. Director Valido moved to explain how the proposed position will carry out the supervisory duties of the After School/Summer Camp Program as well as assisting the department. It was also explained how the position, given that it is a full-time position, would have to be submitted to the Federation of Public Employees (FPE) for approval and then posted as required by the FPE agreement. Mayor Roberto Martell then moved to approve the position, Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: The following item to be discussed was the canceling of the August Regular Council Meeting.
votes: Councilperson Digiacomo moved to cancel the August Regular Council Meeting, Councilperson Lily Stefano seconded, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The following item to be discussed was the canceling of the August Regular Council Meeting. Councilperson Digiacomo moved to cancel the August Regular Council Meeting, Councilperson Lily Stefano seconded, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Director Jorge Soto then approached the Council to inform them of a need for consideration and approval of a change order to the contract for construction for the NW 74 Avenue project.
votes: Councilperson Ivan Pacheco moved to approve the total of nine (9) full-time positions as proposed by Councilperson DiGiacomo, Mayor Roberto Martell seconded, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Director Jorge Soto then approached the Council to inform them of a need for consideration and approval of a change order to the contract for construction for the NW 74 Avenue project. He asked the Council to, if possible, schedule a Special Meeting to consider an item that would address issues found after constructions was initiated. After a brief discussion, it was agreed by Council and staff to hold a Special Meeting of the Town Council on Wednesday July 17, 2019 at 5:15pm. The next item on the agenda was the request by Councilperson DiGiacomo to consider the conversion of some part-time positions of the Meal Program Department to be full-time positions. In addition, Councilperson DiGiacomo explained how the proposed positions, with the approval of the Council, would be submitted to the FPE for approval and would be subject to all the guidelines and requirements as stipulated by the FPE agreement. Councilperson DiGiacomo also explained how the proposal includes one (1) full-time meal program coordinator positions and eight (8) full-time Meal Program Drivers/Helpers/Attendant positions. After a brief discussion Councilperson Ivan Pacheco moved to approve the total of nine (9) full-time positions as proposed by Councilperson DiGiacomo, Mayor Roberto Martell seconded, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: A brief recess was taken.
votes: Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the recommendation and appoint Victoria Martinez as the new Town Clerk. Councilperson Ivan Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: A brief recess was taken. Meeting reconvened as follows: In continuance, the next item to be discussed was add-on item (1) to approve and appoint Victoria Martinez as the Town Clerk in light of the recent retirement announcement of Town Clerk Herlina Taboada. Mayor Martell explained how after almost Thirty-Nine (39) years of employment, Town Clerk Herlina Taboada announced her retirement dated of July 11, 2019. Town Clerk Herlina Taboada thanked the Mayor and Council for the good retirement wishes and explained her recommendation for succession. She explained how now Assistant Town Clerk Victoria Martinez, has been working with the Clerk s Office since she was fist employed by the Town. After a brief discussion, Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the recommendation and appoint Victoria Martinez as the new Town Clerk. Councilperson Ivan Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: July 1, 2019 Regular Council Meeting Next item was add-on item (2) to approve and appoint Jenny L.
votes: Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the recommendation and appoint Jenny L. DiGiacomo as the new Assistant Town Clerk. Councilperson Ivan Pacheco seconded the motion, Councilperson Griselia DiGiacomo abstained, and the motion was carried by majority of vote.
segs.text: July 1, 2019 Regular Council Meeting Next item was add-on item (2) to approve and appoint Jenny L. DiGiacomo as Assistant Town Clerk. Town Clerk Herlina Taboada explained how Ms. DiGiacomo has been working closely with the Clerk s office in the retention, preservation and management of the Town s records for the last several years. Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the recommendation and appoint Jenny L. DiGiacomo as the new Assistant Town Clerk. Councilperson Ivan Pacheco seconded the motion, Councilperson Griselia DiGiacomo abstained, and the motion was carried by majority of vote.

segs.head: Next item to be discussed was add-on item (3) to discuss the proposal of three (3) full-time positions for the Custodial and Janitorial Services Department.
votes: Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the three (3) full-time positions for the Custodial and Janitorial Services Department. Councilperson Ivan Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Next item to be discussed was add-on item (3) to discuss the proposal of three (3) full-time positions for the Custodial and Janitorial Services Department. Custodial and Janitorial Services Director Omar Sanchez explained to the Town Council the proposal to convert three of the existing part-time positions to full-time positions. Mayor Roberto Martell moved to approve the three (3) full-time positions for the Custodial and Janitorial Services Department. Councilperson Ivan Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Since there was no further business to be considered Mayor Roberto Martell moved to adjourn.
votes: Mayor Roberto Martell moved to adjourn. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Since there was no further business to be considered Mayor Roberto Martell moved to adjourn. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 8:02 P.M. on July 1, 2019.

votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo moved to place a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was adopted unanimously.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUEYe TT 2019 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 17, 2019 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: EDGAR AYALA COUNCIL MEMBERS: GRISELIA DIGIACOMO IVAN PACHECO LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ ASST. TOWN CLERK: JENNY L. DIGIACOMO TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and The Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited. Councilperson DiGiacomo moved to place a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was adopted unanimously.

segs.head: Mayor Martell started and addressed the first item of the agenda which was the discussion of the proposed budget for the Fiscal Year starting October 1, 2019 through and until September 30, 2020.
votes: Mayor Roberto Martell moved to place a motion to approve the tentative operating millage rate for FY 2019-2020 of 5.8075 mills as proposed. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried by a unanimous vote.
segs.text: Mayor Martell started and addressed the first item of the agenda which was the discussion of the proposed budget for the Fiscal Year starting October 1, 2019 through and until September 30, 2020. Finance Director Roy Danziger then approached the podium and referred everyone to the documentation included with the agenda item which included the Certification of Taxable Value Form DR-420. Finance Director explained the information as listed on said form which reflects assessed property values before adjustments for the 2019-2020 fiscal year are calculated. He also stated that the goal of the meeting was to set the tentative millage rate so that the Town can submit it by August 4, 2019. Director Danziger also stated the current millage rate of 6.3 mills and the proposed estimate millage rate of 5.8075 mills. In addition, he stated that if the Town chooses to use the same roll-back rate, the Town would have a zero percent (0%) tax increase while receiving the same revenues. He then started explaining the Proposed Budget Worksheet page by page. Budget Highlights as of 7-19-2019- Projections as shown. Budget for this department is to include a total of three (3) full time and three (3) part-time employees. In addition, finance director and police Chief to research and evaluate the cost and benefit comparison of purchasing the police motorcycles instead of the leasing program. Finance director and code compliance director to research and evaluate the cost of a full-time code compliance officer instead of an outsourced contractor. segs.head: Special Council Meeting of July 17, 2019 Water and Sewer Utilities - Operations Proposal of ERU changes to commercial rates to be included for Council discussion and action at the September regular council meeting.
votes: Mayor Roberto Martell made a motion to approve the salary increase of Twelve Thousand dollars ($ 12,000) a year as proposed. Vice- Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: Special Council Meeting of July 17, 2019 Water and Sewer Utilities - Operations Proposal of ERU changes to commercial rates to be included for Council discussion and action at the September regular council meeting. Water and Sewer Utilities No changes Water and Sewer Utilities Capital Expenditures - No Changes Stormwater Utilities Operations Details as presented will be discussed in detail at the Public Meeting/Council Workshop requested by the department s director. Stormwater Utilities Capital Expenditures Details as presented will be discussed in detail at the Public Meeting/Council Workshop previously scheduled for July 23, 2019. Lakeside Retirement Park Operations Includes funds allocated for seawall and road repairs. No other changes but deficit continues. Police Gun Range Operations Reflects funds received from insurance claim. Facility continues to show operating at a loss. Finance director together with Police Chief to look into the revenues generated by the facility including the financial impact of the newly increased rates to be in effect and report back to the Town Council for further discussion and decision. Finance director then moved to address the notice of rate increase received from consultants Kimley-Horn and Associates. Capital Improvement Director, Jorge Corzo explained that said increase as notified by the consultant is not acceptable under the master service agreement the Town and said consultant have in effect. Finance Director Roy Danziger then approached the Town Council to request a salary increase of twelve thousand dollars ($ 12,000) a year. He explained that in 2011 he received a salary reduction of Fifteen Thousand Five Hundred dollars ($ 15,500) and would like to be compensated as a senior management professional. Mayor Roberto Martell made a motion to approve the salary increase of Twelve Thousand dollars ($ 12,000) a year as proposed. Vice- Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: Finance Director Danziger brought up as a budget item for discussion, the overtime rule for salaried employees.
votes: Councilperson Ivan Pacheco made a motion to approve the extended overtime benefit for salaried employees as discussed and agreed upon. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Finance Director Danziger brought up as a budget item for discussion, the overtime rule for salaried employees. After a discussion between councilmembers and Town staff, the Council agreed as follows: - All salaried employees who have worked six (6) or more hours on a scheduled day off are entitled to take a full day of work within thirty (30) days of the day worked. In addition, hours worked for events of emergency in nature after a full day of work, department heads shall have the discretion to approve future time off in accordance with the standards of this benefit. Councilperson Ivan Pacheco made a motion to approve the extended overtime benefit for salaried employees as discussed and agreed upon. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Special Council Meeting of July 17, 2019 In continuance, Mayor Martell requested to move the receptionist position under the Town Clerk s department of the General Administration effective immediately for purposes of the Town s organizational chart.
segs.text: Special Council Meeting of July 17, 2019 In continuance, Mayor Martell requested to move the receptionist position under the Town Clerk s department of the General Administration effective immediately for purposes of the Town s organizational chart. He then moved to make a motion approving said position change on the Town s organizational chart which will be brought back for Council review at the next scheduled budget meeting. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.

segs.text: The next item addressed was Resolution C-1714 approving change order No. | to the contract for construction with E&M Equipment, Corp to include additional water services improvements, labor and equipment to complete the original scope of work for the NW 74" avenue drainage improvement project. segs.text: * Bermello Ajamil & Partners (AOR) Danny 4 Meehan f 2 | Recreational ae ot ES The proposed Medley Community Pool, scheduled to be completed in late 4 2020, will be a state-of-the-art facility meeting all current Building Code and American Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements for the safe use of all the Medley residents for many years to come. The facility, when completed, will allow the Town to continue the long-established youth swimming programs that for so many years have provided a healthy and fun time for all. The project, to be developed at an estimated cost of 3 million dollars, consist of a 4-lap pool, approximately 30 feet by 60 feet, which will include a personal lift for those with difficulties in walking or desiring to conduct therapeutically exercises, and lounge chairs for tanning and relaxing. One of the most important components of the project is the construction of a Restroom facility annex that will always serve both the pool visitors as well as the visitors to the Medley Community Center, thus providing much needed code compliant facilities. In addition to the new pool facilities, the project will provide a Picnic area with 3 shelters and barbeque grills for the enjoyment of the community. The area will be enclosed with an ornamental fences and privacy screening on all public view sides. A public parking area will be constructed on the east side of the site, to reduce the noise impact on adjacent residential areas to the east, with an 8-foot-wide walkway along the proposed canal side bulkhead wall that Concept Plan will interconnect the parking, picnic area, and pool area to the new Restroom building and the Medley Community Center. segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 24, 2019 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 24, 2019 at 5:15 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 24, 2019 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 24, 2019 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: EDGAR AYALA COUNCIL MEMBERS: GRISELIA DIGIACOMO IVAN PACHECO LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ (ABSENT) ASST. TOWN CLERK: JENNY L. DIGIACOMO TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and The Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited. Councilperson DiGiacomo moved to place a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and the agenda was adopted by a unanimous vote.

segs.head: Item A of the agenda, Resolution C-1715 approving an LED Lighting Agreement with Florida Power & Light Company (FPL) for installation and modification of lighting facilities along South River Drive was then read into the record by Town Attorney Lillian Arango.
votes: Councilperson Griselia DiGiacomo placed a motion to adopt Resolution C-1715 as read, Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Item A of the agenda, Resolution C-1715 approving an LED Lighting Agreement with Florida Power & Light Company (FPL) for installation and modification of lighting facilities along South River Drive was then read into the record by Town Attorney Lillian Arango. Capital Improvements Director and Town Engineer Jorge Corzo approached the podium to discuss the item and its association with the existing construction project in detail. In addition, Town Attorney Lillian Arango pointed out that with the approval of the agreement, the Town agrees to purchase the electrical service for these facilities at FPL s current lighting rate schedule. After a brief discussion about the ongoing construction project, Councilperson Griselia DiGiacomo placed a motion to adopt Resolution C-1715 as read, Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Director Jorge Corzo then initiated discussion on the designation of parking spaces along the South side of the NW South River Drive corridor included on the SR826 to 72 Avenue construction project.
votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo moved to adjourn. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Director Jorge Corzo then initiated discussion on the designation of parking spaces along the South side of the NW South River Drive corridor included on the SR826 to 72 Avenue construction project. He circulated a worksheet for reference (see attached). This issue, as stated by Director Corzo, necessitates Right-of-Way donations. He also stated that it would be beneficial to both, the commercial and residential community, to mark said parking spaces as Special Council Meeting of July 24, 2019 such. The plan is to have the commercial properties contribute a significant amount through a Special District funding mechanism to provide for this portion and scope of the project. Mr. Corzo also mentioned that although positive conversations have been had with the property owner, no requests are being presented to the Town Council as of yet. Police Chief Said-Jinete also commented on the issue and said that if and when said parking spaces are marked so that they are used for both commercial and residential uses, to make sure the hours for commercial use are clearly reflected. Since there was no further business to be considered Councilperson DiGiacomo moved to adjourn. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 5:39 P.M. on July 24, 2019.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 3, 2019 A regular meeting of the Town Council was called to order on June 3, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: EDGAR AYALA COUNCIL MEMBERS: GRISELIA DIGIACOMO IVAN PACHECO LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: HERLINA TABOADA (ABSENT) ASST. TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO (ABSENT) The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and Mayor Martell then asked for prayers for one of our officers who is in surgery at this moment. Hopes that everything goes well for Jose Rodriguez. The Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by Josue Hernandez and Kevin Cabrera from the Medley Police Explorers Post 67, the Town Council and Audience. The Minutes of the Regular Meeting of May 6, 2019 and the Special Meeting of May 28, 2019 were discussed and approved. In continuance, a motion for the adoption of the meeting s agenda, including Councilperson s DiGiacomo two (2) add-on items, was then carried by Mayor Martell and seconded by Councilperson DiGiacomo.

segs.head: The first item on the Agenda was a Presentation by Javier Betancourt of Citizens Independent Trust to provide status of the PTP and SMART Plan.
segs.text: The first item on the Agenda was a Presentation by Javier Betancourt of Citizens Independent Trust to provide status of the PTP and SMART Plan. Mr. Betancourt thanked everyone for the hospitality. He then along with Nestor Toledo made a brief presentation, he stated that on November 2002, Miami-Dade County voters approved a half-penny surtax to implement the People s Transportation Plan (PTP). That money goes to expanding transit and incorporating roadways on a long-term basis. Along with that the voters also voted on a Citizens Independent Transportation Trust which is an independent organization comprised of Citizens who serve as volunteers with a mission to oversee expenditure of surtax revenue. The trust is composed of fifteen (15) members who are volunteer Citizens appointed by each one of the District Commissioners. All projects are listed in the five (5) year plan in order to use the money. All of the information is on their website. Surtax funds are Audited in every Municipality. He stated that the Town of Medley has been very good in using its Surtax Funds appropriately. He thanked the Finance Department for having all the documentation in order. Mayor Martell then Jume 3, 2019 Regular Council Meeting stated that the Town of Medley needs busses and trolley to move people from one City to another. Mayor Martell then thanked him for all his help to the Town. Mayor Martell then opened the public comment section and asked if anyone in the audience wanted to speak on any item of the agenda. No one came forward.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A WORKSHOP MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA June 5, 2019 9:00 A.M A workshop of the Town Council was called to order on June 5, 2019 at 9:21 a.m. The following were present: Mayor Roberto Martell Vice Mayor Edgar Ayala- Came in at 10:12 am Councilperson Griselia Digiacomo Councilperson Ivan Pacheco Councilperson Lily Stefano Assistant Town Clerk Victoria Martinez Social Services & Parks and Recreations Director Lizmari Valido Executive Assistant/Social Services & Parks and Recreations Coordinator Susana Guasch Police Chief, Jeanette Said- Jinete- Came in at 9:58 am Director Valido made sure everyone had received the memorandum reflecting all the existing program requirements along with the proposed changes she had emailed (see the attached) the day before. Thus, she started the workshop addressing the hours of operations. Director Valido explained that she would like to close the Tobie Wilson Park and Danny Meehan field at 8:00 pm like it used to be and different hours of operations for Sundays. Councilperson Digiacomo mentioned that other public parks close at sundown. Director Valido explained that closing at sundown creates a difficulty for the scheduling of personnel since some employees are schedule to work in different facilities and they would all close at the same time. A discussion of the rental of the Tobie Wilson Park in which Director Valido informed the Council that an increase of the rental of this facility had been seen in the past year and it has been rented almost every weekend. She then explained the proposal of closing the park on Sundays. If this facility closes, however, the Tobie Recreation Center should mirror the operations of the Gym and field. Mayor Martell then proposed the following hours of operations and the rest of the Council agreed: Tobie Wilson Park Monday through Friday: 2 pm through 8 pm Saturday 12pm- 8 pm Sunday 12pm 5 pm Council Workshop of June 5, 2019 Danny Meehan Recreational Field Monday through Saturday: 8:00 am- 8:00 pm Sunday: 12:00 5:00 pm The discussion then moved onto the verification and approval process and methods used by the Town for social services programs and/or benefits. The Council then discussed how using the Miami-Dade County property appraisers office s information is not a fair method. Director Valido explained how the information of the Miami- Dade County property appraisers office is used to recognize whether the applicant is the property owner or a tenant

segs.text: The First Reading of Ordinance C-436, Amending Chapter 44 Personnel of the Town Code by Codifying Departments Previously Created by Resolution, by Creating a Finance Department and Hot Meal Program Department, and by Renaming The Parks & Recreation Department to Social Services and Parks and Recreation Department; Providing for Conflicts, Providing for Severability; and Providing for an Effective Date was read by Town Attorney Arango. She stated that the Ordinance is codifying what was previously adopted as Departments in the Town, there were some Departments already listed in this Ordinance and are adding the Departments that were previously added by Resolution just to clarify and codify them in this Ordinance and also creating two (2) new Departments. segs.text: MINUTES OF A WORKSHOP MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MARCH 26, 2019 A workshop meeting of the Town Council was called to order on March 26, 2019 at 10:00 a.m. The following were present: Special Counsel Alison Smith, Town Clerk Herlina Taboada, Assistant Town Clerk Victoria Martinez, Vice-Mayor Ayala, Councilperson Pacheco, Councilperson Digiacomo, Susana Guasch and Mary Taylor. The purpose of this workshop was for: Discussion and General Overview of the Proposed Town of Medley Employee Manual. Copies of the handbook were given to everyone present and was reviewed on a page by page basis. Discussions were held among those present and numerous ideas, concerns and questions were brought up for clarification by the Attorney. Victoria Martinez stated that in the Charter the Utilities Department is named Water Department, but the name was changed to Utilities and Stormwater Department by Ordinance. It needs to be changed in the handbook. The issue of hiring employees was up for discussion. Councilperson Pacheco stated that he does not want to be involved in the hiring process because new hires are approved by the Town Council. He stated that he has nothing against Department Heads, but things should be done right and there should be advance notice of any hiring. Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that we need transparency. Victoria suggested that maybe the Town Council could go through Human Resources for information. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that she does not want to be involved in the hiring process. She wants to rely on the Department Head but would like to be notified and informed of who is being hired. Councilperson Stefano would also like to be informed of who is being hired. Mary Taylor then asked what are you asking for? She stated information of who is being recommended. Councilperson Digiacomo stated also the same thing, information of the person who is being hired. She stated that there was a time when a person was brought before the Town Council for the approval of their hiring and the Council felt she was not the correct person. Councilperson Ayala wants to be part of the interview process. Another change as part of the handbook is to change the name of Town Clerk to Human Resources Department. He then invited everyone present to a Paella event on the second floor terrace of the Medley Municipal Services Facility after the Council Meeting. Presentation by Patricia Romeu, Chief of Miami-Dade County Arts in Public Places Program (MDC-APP) on the Town s Participation in the Program. She thanked everyone for the Town s participation in the program and for the implementation of a wonderful work of art in the exterior of the Town Hall. A few years ago, through the GOB program from Miami-Dade County the construction of this building was supposed to have generated 1.50% of the actual project towards the implementation of a work of art by a professional artist. The collaboration was not done at that time and decided to hold the process until now. They have been working with Town Staff to do an invitation of artists through the program and have invited six (6) local artists to prepare a proposal for a monument at the entrance of the Town Hall. An initial meeting has already been done with the Advisory Committee and six (6) local artists were recommended and they are in the process of developing proposals which are going to be brought to a committee for presentation and selection. She advised that next month she will be coming back to the Town Council with the two (2) finalist that were recommended for implementation. After selection they will provide a one (1) year time for the completion of the monument. segs.text: Discussion and action on Charter Amendment and Residency Duration for Qualification of Elected Officials was the next item to be discussed. Town Attorney Arango stated that at the February 4, 2019 Regular Council Meeting she was directed to research possible Amendment to the Town Charter which would increase the duration of residency requirement for the Mayor and Council Candidates from one (1) year. Currently the Town Charter provides for a one (1) year residency requirement prior to the qualification period. There was some discussion of a three (3) to five (5) year requirement. The conclusion is that adoption of a residency requirement in excess of one (1) year would raise significant constitutional concerns and should not be pursued or implemented. There are some Florida cases that dealt specifically with this issue, one case is County vs. Gustavson from Sarasota and in that case the Florida District Court of Appeals struck down Sarasota s County two (2) year residency requirement for Elected Officials. They held that the two (2) year residency requirement was unreasonable and prohibited the movements of Candidates between Municipalities. She stated that the consensus with the Courts is that more than one (1) year is not supportable from the Constitutional perspective. Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that sometimes it is very hard to determine how long the resident has lived in Town. He wanted to know if anything could be added to the existing policy because it is not completely clear. Mayor Martell suggested to leave the Charter residency requirement as is and we must do everything within the law. Town Attorney Arango stated that the next item was some direction on General Process for a Charter Amendment in the Town of Medley. She stated that at the February 4, 2019 Regular Page 4 March 4, 2019 Council Meeting, she was directed to do some research on what that process would be. Article 10, Section 10 of the Town Charter currently provides that Amendments to the Charter shall be enacted in the manner provided by the Miami-Dade County Charter. There are no other provisions in the Town Charter or Code that addresses the process for that Amendment. In other words, there is no such thing as a mandatory charter review every certain number of years, there is no requirement for a Committee to be appointed to review the Charter. The Town is bound by the County Charter and the applicable provision is 6.03 of that Charter which provides for Amendments for Municipal Chart

segs.text: Resolution C-1700, Relating to the Creation of the Medley 77S-79A Infrastructure Improvement Area; Modifying the initial Assessment Resolution as Provided herein; Establishing the maximum amount of the Assessment for each Assessment Unit and Providing for the Levy of the Assessments against the Benefitted Properties; Approving the Preliminary Assessment Roll; Establishing the Method of Collection; Establishing other terms and conditions of the Assessments; and Providing for an Effective Date. She stated that this is the second public hearing titled Final Assessment Resolution for this Proposed Infrastructure Improvement Area and staff has a recommendation not to move forward with the Assessment Program at this time. To postpone it and Town Engineer Jorge Corzo may have an update for you as well. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo then explained that they have made a request to come back with this item and the basis of doing that is that it is a good possibility that we can actually lower the Assessment on the properties because one of the projects in the benefited area really extends beyond the boundaries of the Assessment Area. There might be additional contributions or participations made by other entities. As we speak, we are beginning to get a lot of interest on the redevelopment of the Metro Rail Station, the possibility of doing some private and public partnerships by adjacent property owners. By doing so the 79S connector project out of the equation we should be able to lower the Assessment significantly by almost one (1) million dollars or more. If we include the project in the Assessment, then we are committed to do it and the timeline for doing that is really difficult to assess in view that there might be a redevelopment in this area. He would like to remind the Mayor and Council that this is the first project that the Town does, we consider this a pilot project, we have learned a lot like setting up the Districts, Evaluations, the Methodology and we now have a firm grasp on what can work and what cannot work. By reducing the Assessment from 4 to possibly 3 or less would be good news for the property owners and for the Town. Mayor Martell then asked if anyone had any questions. Councilperson Digiacomo then said yes, she asked Town Engineer Jorge Corzo how come we have that issue now and we were excited about this pilot project to move forward two (2) or three (3) weeks ago when it was brought up to the Council ? Mr. Corzo stated that we are still excited

segs.text: Mayor Martell brought up the issue of the closing times of Tobie Wilson Park and the Gym. He wanted to know the Council s opinion on closing both at 7:00 p.m. instead of the scheduled 8:00 p.m. due to safety issues. He stated that the employees who are working will not loose any hours. Lizmari stated that right now the Park closes at 8:00 p.m. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked what was the reason for the change? The Mayor replied for security reasons. Lizmari stated that the Mayor is proposing to close both Tobie Wilson Park and the Gym at 7:00 p.m. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that most of the Parks close at sundown and she does not have a problem with it. Residents need to be notified by way of flyer. Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that during the summer the sun is out until 8:00 -8:30 p.m. he just wanted to know if we had any complaints. He has not heard about any accidents or any incidents. Chief Said-Jinete stated that the only concern she had before was due to the lighting in the field because there was none. Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that he could agree but for the summer months it could be left until 8:00 p.m. Lizmari stated that it would be difficult due to schedules. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that if it is not broken don t try to fix it and leave it the way it is. Mayor Martell agreed let s leave it the way it is. Since there was no further business to be considered Mayor Martell moved to adjourn. Vice- Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. segs.text: Ordinance C-442 of The Town Of Medley, Florida, Repealing Chapter 14, Article 3 Mobile Catering , in its Entirety, of The Town s Code Of Ordinances; Amending Chapter 62, Article Il, Supplementary Regulations of The Town s Code Of Ordinances to Create Section 62-66 Food Trucks , to Create Definitions, to Prohibit Food Truck Sales in the Public Rights-of-Way, to Authorize the Operation of Food Trucks in the M-1 And M-3 Industrial Districts , to Require that all Food Truck Operators Obtain a Business Tax Receipt, and to Provide Additional Regulations; Providing for Severability; and Providing for an Effective Date. Town Attorney Arango explained how the item, sponsored by Councilperson Stefano, addressed and amended article 3 of chapter 14 Mobile Catering in its entirety replacing it with the regulations set forth in Ordinance C-442. Town Attorney Arango also explained how the definitions and regulations of this new Ordinance contain restrictions and parameters like the requirement of a business tax receipt and the prohibition of overnight parking among others. In addition, these regulations as stated on Article II also include restrictions on permitted locations, parking, and waste collection regulations. The Council then discussed the requirements and directed the following changes: e To add restriction of 1000 feet from restaurants. e Not close to residential areas. e Special events permit required for private properties/events. e Exempt Town facilities/events of all regulations except the license and insurance requirements. e No BTR required for Town events. e Removal of sentence i of paragraph (e) of Food Truck Gatherings section and to eliminate the limitations for days and hours of operations as reflected. e Exclude lunch trucks and ice cream trucks from the definition section of the Ordinance. Councilperson Stefano moved to place a motion to adopt Ordinance C-441 on first reading as directed and amended, Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The next item held was the discussion and action on the appointment of one (1) Licensing Permit Clerk II for the Building and Zoning Department. Building and Zoning Director Richard McConachie mentioned the years of experience of successful candidate Scarlet Molina Urrego and expressed how Ms. Molina Urrego would be an asset to his department and the Town. Mayor Martell then moved as follows: TO APPOINT SCARLETT MOLINA URREGO TO FULFILL A FULL-TIME BUILDING LICENSING CLERK II

A motion to adopt the agenda including add-on item D as requested by Mayor Martell was then carried by Councilperson DiGiacomo, seconded Councilperson Stefano and carried by majority vote. Mayor Martell then announced Special Presentation Item A, which was the recognition and presentation by Ruban Roberts, Chairman of the Miami-Dade Branch of National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP). Although Mr. Roberts was not present, Mayor Martell instructed Town Attorney Lillian Arango to address the item. Attorney Arango then confirmed that Mr. Ruban Roberts was in fact not able to attend but the Town could address the matter related to the recognition and presentation item at a later time during the council meeting. Mayor Martell then moved to open the public comment section of the meeting to which no public comments were made but Councilperson Stefano took the opportunity to express her support towards Mayor Martell and the Town of Medley in general for the difficult time the Mayor, as representative of the Town of Medley, had to endure the last few days. The Mayor thanked Councilperson Stefano for her kind words. Mayor Martell then moved to the next presentation and recognition item which was the presentation of a ceremonial check to the Town of Medley for the NW South River Drive Drainage and Mobility Improvements in the amount of $ 500,000.00 by Senator Manny Diaz Jr. and State Representative Ana Maria Rodriguez. David Marin, assistant to the office of senator Manny Diaz Jr., approached and congratulated the Council on the achievement. State Representative Ana Maria Rodriguez also congratulated the Town Council for their efforts to secure funding for the Town in conjunction with the Town s Lobbyist Nelson Diaz from The Southern Group of Florida, Inc. The Mayor and the Town Council thanked both elected officials and took the time to take pictures along with the ceremonial check. Following the second presentation item, the Mayor then asked Town Attorney Arango to address item 7 of the Resolutions section of the agenda. Councilperson DiGiacomo placed a motion to move and address Resolutions- Item 7, Councilperson Stefano seconded, and the motion was carried majority vote. The title of Resolution C-1736 was then read into the record by Attorney Arango.

Alina Garcia from Commissioner Bovo s office then approached the Town Council to inform them of the importance of the upcoming 2020 Census and how the invitation and any documentation would be communicated to the residents. Ms. Garcia also emphasized the importance of being counted in order to receive federal funding. Mayor Martell asked Ms. Garcia if a workshop could be scheduled so that the Town could get informed and facilitate the process for all Town of Medley residents, including the senior population. Ms. Garcia agreed with the scheduling of the Workshop which would be arranged and scheduled at a future date. The last presentation item of the agenda was up next. segs.text: Resolution C-1737 Approving Work Order with Calvin, Giordano & Associates, Inc. for General Planning and Zoning Services for Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Vice- Mayor Ayala brought up some question regarding the service fees provided by Calvin, Giordano & Associates, Inc. Town Attorney Arango also informed the Town Council that Calvin, Giordano and Associates, Inc was working under a master agreement that provided for all kinds of engineering services, including planning services. Robert Collins, representative of the firm, confirmed the information and addressed the invoicing questions Vice-Mayor Ayala had brought up. In addition, Richard McConachie, Building Official and Director of The Building and Zoning Department also added that the work order presented with this resolution, was strictly for services provided to the Building and Zoning Department. Also, Mr. McConachie informed the Town Council that because building and zoning workload cannot be predicted, if services exceed the amount presented with this resolution, an additional purchase order and Council approval would be requested. He stated that the PPO dental coverage portion of the health benefit was once again staying the same and without the potential 5 % increase he had infirmed the Town last month. Thus, the PPO dental coverage effective January 1, 2020 was staying the same as the last 3 years. segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA SEPTEMBER 10, 2019 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on September 10, 2019 at 5:15 p.m.
votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo moved to place a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and the agenda was adopted unanimously.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA SEPTEMBER 10, 2019 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on September 10, 2019 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA GRISELIA DIGIACOMO LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: ALISON SMITH The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Councilperson DiGiacomo moved to place a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and the agenda was adopted unanimously.

segs.head: Mayor Martell instructed Town Attorney Alison Smith to address the agenda items whom then announced that the purpose of the Special Meeting was to discuss and establish the proposed tentative millage rate by Resolution based upon the Certification of Taxable Value of real and personal property within the Town of Medley for the fiscal year October 1, 2019 through September 30, 2020; discussion and establishment of a proposed tentative budget for fiscal year October 1, 2019 through September 30, 2020; and first reading of Ordinance C-440 adopting Budget for fiscal year 2019-2020.
votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE RESOLUTION C-1729, ADOPTING THE PROPOSED TOWN OF MEDLEY AD VALOREM TAX OPERATING MILLAGE LEVY RATE AT 5.0500 MILLS. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded it and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Mayor Martell instructed Town Attorney Alison Smith to address the agenda items whom then announced that the purpose of the Special Meeting was to discuss and establish the proposed tentative millage rate by Resolution based upon the Certification of Taxable Value of real and personal property within the Town of Medley for the fiscal year October 1, 2019 through September 30, 2020; discussion and establishment of a proposed tentative budget for fiscal year October 1, 2019 through September 30, 2020; and first reading of Ordinance C-440 adopting Budget for fiscal year 2019-2020. Ms. Smith also stated that meeting was the First Public Hearing as required by State Law, therefore proper notice had been given. In continuance, she announced the Proposed Town of Medley Ad Valorem Tax Operating Millage Levy Rate of 5.0500 Mills per thousand dollars of taxable assessed property value, which is 13% below the rolled back rate computed pursuant to State Law for the 2019 Tax Year. Councilperson DiGiacomo placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE RESOLUTION C-1729, ADOPTING THE PROPOSED TOWN OF MEDLEY AD VALOREM TAX OPERATING MILLAGE LEVY RATE AT 5.0500 MILLS. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded it and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Assistant Finance Director Isabel Hughes then approached the podium and informed the Council of some details regarding the appropriations for the Police gun range.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE PROPOSED TENTATIVE BUDGET WITH THE CHANGES AS PRESENTED FOR THE FISCAL YEAR OF OCTOBER 1, 2019 THROUGH SEPTEMBER 30, 2020. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Assistant Finance Director Isabel Hughes then approached the podium and informed the Council of some details regarding the appropriations for the Police gun range. She notified the Town Council that the budget appropriations for the Medley Police gun range, as requested at the last regular council meeting of September 3, 2019, was going to be part of the General Administration budget and thus, will not reflect salaries and depreciation values. After a brief presentation by Assistant Finance Director Hughes, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE PROPOSED TENTATIVE BUDGET WITH THE CHANGES AS PRESENTED FOR THE FISCAL YEAR OF OCTOBER 1, 2019 THROUGH SEPTEMBER 30, 2020. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: The next item was the first reading of Ordinance C-440, Adopting and Approving the Budget of the Town of Medley for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2019 and ending September 30, 2020.
votes: Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO ADOPT ON FIRST READING ORDINANCE C-440, ADOPTING AND APPROVING THE BUDGET FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY FOR THE FISCAL YEAR BEGINNING OCTOBER 1, 2019 AND ENDING SEPTEMBER 30, 2020. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The next item was the first reading of Ordinance C-440, Adopting and Approving the Budget of the Town of Medley for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2019 and ending September 30, 2020. Town Attorney Alison Smith read the title of the Ordinance into the record. Mayor Martell moved as follows: TO ADOPT ON FIRST READING ORDINANCE C-440, ADOPTING AND APPROVING THE BUDGET FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY FOR THE FISCAL YEAR BEGINNING OCTOBER 1, 2019 AND ENDING SEPTEMBER 30, 2020. Councilperson Digiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Since there was no further business to be considered Mayor Martell moved to adjourn.

segs.text: - The Mayor has a Facebook page which he utilizes exclusively to communicate about Town business. The Mayor has decided to run for re-election and would like to use the same Facebook page for city activities and campaign activities. Is the Mayor permitted to use his Facebook page for both purposes? 15 A Councilmember has a private Facebook page and posts a comment about an item currently before the Council. Among his Facebook friends are other members of the Council and they receive his post. One of the Councilmembers indicates that he likes the post. Does pressing the like button violate the Sunshine Law? 16 One of the City s board is considered a controversial item. A member of the Council wishes to attend the meeting and offer his perspective to the board before the board takes action. Other members of the Council are also planning to attend, but will not speak. Must this meeting be noticed by the Council? What if a second Councilmember speaks? i7 During the course of a regularly- scheduled Council meeting, an item is brought up by one of the Council and a lengthy discussion ensues. This item was not listed on the agenda. Does this discussion violate the Sunshine Law? Can the Council vote on the unscheduled item? 18 e After a spirited Council meeting, several of the members of the Council go out for dinner and limit their discussion of town business to those items receiving final approval at the meeting. Would engaging in these discussions violate the Sunshine Law? 13 FS 286.011(1) Applicability All city board or committee meetings at which official acts are to be taken; even if authority is limited to making recommendations Board business Must comply when an item is currently before the council or could foreseeably come before the council. General notice of meeting necessary not specific agenda items 23 MINUTES verbatim account of everything that has been said is not necessary; summarize discussion and if vote taken identify how each member voted; if meeting recorded or televised, must be made available to public if requested. VOTING required to vote unless board member has a real or perceived conflict of interest. Some votes require roll call; others allow voice votes or by paper ballots. Paper ballots would have to state the name of member and his/her vote and would be a public record. 24 PARTICIPATION The Sunshine Law does not require that members of the public be permitted to speak at public meetings. In 2013 the Legislature passed Section 286.0114, Florida Statutes, which requires boards, subject to limited exceptions, to give members of the public a reasonable opportunity to be heard on issues before them 25 PARTICIPATION Opportunity to be heard need not occur at same meeting in which council take official action, provided is it during the decision-making process and within reasonable proximity in time before council take official action. Opportunity to be heard does not apply to the following situations: 1) emergencies if compliance would cause an unreasonable delay in the ability of the board to act; 2) a ministerial act (approving minutes/issuing proclamations; 3) shade meeting; 4) when acting in quasi-judicial capacity 26 PARTICIPATION

segs.text: - A City Councilmember lives two blocks away from an intersection where the City will be installing a traffic light. In addition, to reduce speeding in the neighbor, the City will be installing traffic calming devices as well. Does the elected official have a _ voting conflict if he votes to approve funding for these projects? 62 VOTING CONFLICT -- BUSINESS RELATIONSHIP An elected official owns a business and retains a consultant to design a website for the business. The consultant s business is located in the city and wishes to expand. Before it can expand, the business needs a variance from the Council. Is the elected official who is _ utilizing the consultant barred from participating in this matter because the two parties have a business relationship? 63 VOTING CONFLICT -- BIAS While campaigning for office, the candidate (who was elected) campaigned under the platform of a moratorium on high-rise development (residential/commercial). After the election, an application is submitted by a developer whose project would exceed the height limitation proposed by the official when he was a candidate. The City will hear the application in its quasi-judicial capacity. Does the official have a bias barring him from hearing this application? 64 VOTING CONFLICT -- BIAS A local restaurant is requesting a variance from the City to expand its parking lot. A City Commissioner is the former business partner of the applicant, the two had a falling out and their partnership ended badly. Does the official have a_ voting conflict? VOTING CONFLICTS -- PERCEPTION A municipal official votes an item in which the applicant is represented by the official s former aw partner. Some of the residents are outraged because they believe the official at a minimum nad an appearance of a voting conflict and should have abstained. Is the elected official required to abstain? If the official fails to abstain, can the Florida Commission on Ethics sanction the official? 66 VOTING CONFLICTS State standard: Special private gain or loss economic benefit or harm that would inure to an official, a relative, business associate or principal unless the measure affects a class that includes the official, a relative, business associate or principal considering the following factors 1) size of the class affected; 2) the nature of the interests involved; 3) the degree to which the interests of all members of the class are affected by the vote; 4) whether official would receive a greater benefit or burden

Provides criteria that must be met for employment to be accepted: position already in existence or was created by employer w/o knowledge that elected official was interested in position; was publicly advertised; official was subjected to same application and hiring process as others; official meets or exceeds required qualifications 92 DUAL EMPLOYMENT Continued employment: A current elected official or a candidate may continue public sector employment as long as_ any promotion, advancement, additional compensation or any of value connected to the employment is not given as a result of elected or position. 93 UNAUTHORIZED COMPENSATION?

Is there a prohibited conflict for the county commissioner? 96 DOING BUSINESS WITH AGENCY Yes. Section 112.313(3) consists of two parts. Part 1 requires an elected official to have a material interest in order to create a conflict and he has no such interest. segs.head: The next item was the discussion and action of the Town of Medley business insurance policy renewal also presented by Robert Reynolds from Morris and Reynolds Insurance.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve the health portion of the insurance coverage and to also keep the negotiations for the PPO dental plan portion of the policy, Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: The next item was the discussion and action of the Town of Medley business insurance policy renewal also presented by Robert Reynolds from Morris and Reynolds Insurance. Mr. Reynolds stated that although the item was listed for action, he was only giving updated information as he continued to research for coverage and pricing offers. Therefore, he would like to bring the item back for formal action at the October council meeting, providing the research is completed. The council agreed and moved to the next item. The next item was the discussion and action of the Town of Medley medical insurance policy renewal starting on January 1, 2020. Mr. Reynolds stated that Cigna had approached him with various price increase offers during the last few months, to which none of the received offers were acceptable in his opinion. However, Cigna came back with a reasonable offer that may be of interest to the Town. That offer has now been submitted in writing and includes a 3% increase over the current rate and may be the best offer received thus far. In addition, Cigna has also notified of a price increase of 3% for the PPO dental plan. Mr. Reynolds suggested the Town to take action on the health coverage portion of the offer and to allow him to keep negotiating the PPO dental plan increase offer. Mayor Martell thanked Mr. Reynolds for the extraordinary job Robert Reynolds from Morris and Reynolds Insurance has done for the Town of Medley throughout the years. Thus, since no further discussion was held, Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve the health portion of the insurance coverage and to also keep the negotiations for the PPO dental plan portion of the policy, Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.

segs.text: Resolution C-1724 approving agreement for performance and completion of contract and release of bond between the Town of Medley, FCCI Insurance Company ( Surety ), and PT Suppliers LLC ( Completing Contractor ) for the design-build services to the medley firearms training facility. This item was related and linked to the item listed under Town of Medley items as discussion and action on the Town of Medley police firearms range operations. Police chief Jeanette Said-Jinete and Finance Director Roy Danziger addressed the podium to review and explain the financial analysis of the facility. Police Chief Said-Jinete explained how she did not agree with the way the operations funds were being allocated. Finance Director Roy Danziger explained how the facility being reported as an enterprise fund, reflects a loss when audited. Therefore, he recommended to incorporate the financial operations of the range into the general funds section of the Town s budget to financially maintain the operations of the facility. This change would be reflected as a separate department under the general funds section of the Town s budget but operated by the Medley Police Department effective October 1, 2019. Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows: TO KEEP THE OPERATIONS OF THE MEDLEY FIREARMS TRAINING FACILITY, ALSO KNOWN AS THE GUN RANGE OPEN, AND FOR THE FINANCIAL OPERATIONS TO BE INCORPORATED INTO THE GENERAL FUNDS SECTION OF THE TOWN S BUDGET. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: The next item on the agenda was an item requested by Councilperson DiGiacomo.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion as follows: FOR FLOATING DAYS AFFORDED TO PART-TIME EMPLOYEES TO COVER THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF HOURS OF THE SCHEDULED WORKDAY. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The next item on the agenda was an item requested by Councilperson DiGiacomo. She stated that since there are very few part-time employees left, perhaps the floating days benefit could be extended. Currently part-time employees are entitled to receive an amount of up to six (6) hours per floating day. However, they would like to receive the total amount of hours scheduled to work on each of the floating day taken. votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo placed a motion as follows: TO ADOPT RESOLUTION C-1797 APPROVING THE FAMILIES FIRST CORONAVIRUS RESPONSE ACT EMERGENCY POLICY WITH AMENDMENTS AS AGREED UPON BY COUNCIL. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Resolution C-1797 Approving and Adopting The Families First Coronavirus Response Act Emergency Administrative Policy in Connection with the Covid-19 Health Emergency; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Vice Mayor Ayala began the discussion by asking the Mayor to explain his intent with the authority given through the proposed resolution. Councilwoman DiGiacomo asked the Mayor, Council and Labor attorney Lindsey Ryder about the procedure the Town would implement moving forward with employees who are 65 years and older given the Council has authorized the employees under that criteria to stay home with a 100% compensation of their salaries. Legal counsel Ryder explained that those employees do not need to be addressed in The Families First Coronavirus Response Act Emergency Administrative Policy because the governors emergency orders address that concern and allows said employees whom qualify to apply for the Emergency Paid Sick Leave where they will receive 80 hours of compensated sick leave. Legal counsel Ryder further explained that The Families First Coronavirus Response Act Emergency Policy is already in effect and the Town has already been enforcing this policy. Thus, employees may apply pursuant to the act, and the resolution before Council is a mechanism to protect the Town from liability. It was also stated it is not mandatory to exclude first responders and the resolution will allow the Mayor to exercise authority to do so once the policy is adopted and will identify those individuals that are classified as first responders. The Mayor asked the Council for their input about employees who have been EEE SS at home not working with 100 % compensation, employees telecommuting, and the employees placed on a rotation schedule. Councilwoman DiGiacomo explained that the act and proposed administrative policy authorizes the Mayor to exclude first responders if necessary. Human Resources Director Olga Quin also explained that hurricane season is upcoming, and it would not be in the Town s best interest to be shorthanded with first responders. Legal counsel Ryder clarified that the Council s decision at this time is to decide what will the Town do with the employees that are at home and cannot perform their duties from home. The Mayor and Council agree to amend The Families First Coronavirus Response Act Emergency Policy to exclude Police Department personnel as they are classified as emergency responders and to allow employees

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Councilperson Pacheco s proposal to Grant Reduction to the Residential Utility Fee for the three (3) month Billing Cycle of April, May and June. Therefore, he proposed a 50% reduction to the residential utility fee for the three (3) month billing cycle of April, May and June. Utilities director Jorge Soto stated that the proposed reduction was possible but it would be a manual effort and each reduction would be entered by his staff one by one on each account so it may take several days. segs.text: - Add-On Item # 1- Discussion and Action on Councilperson Stefano s Proposal for a legal review on pending capital improvement contracts and projects in order to postpone start dates due to the impact of COVID-19. Councilperson Pacheco addressed Ms. Stefano s proposed item and placed a motion for the Council to table this item to be discussed at a later time in the form of a council workshop. Councilwomen Stefano emphasized that her request to address the item was in light of the impacts of COVID-19 and needed to be addressed as soon as possible. Mayor Martell seconded the motion to table the item to be discussed at a later date. Vice- Mayor Ayala stated that the item should be discussed out of respect for Councilwoman Stefano. Councilperson DiGiacomo explained that it would be unfair to not allow a member of the Council to discuss a proposed and requested item. Mayor Martell agreed and continued to withdraw his motion, and the discussion of the matter continued. Councilwoman Stefano stated her concerns with the continued expenditure on capital improvements projects that have yet to begin and stated that the Town needed to review and prioritize projects to lessen the financial hardship caused to the Town by COVID-19. Town engineer Jorge Corzo expressed his willingness to respond to whatever financial plan or monetary restrictions the Town considered prudent. After a brief discussion it was decided to schedule a Council workshop to review pending capital improvement contracts and projects in order to potentially postpone start dates due to the impact of COVID-19. The Mayor instructed staff to attend in person, if possible, and the Council to participate virtually as well as the public. Councilwoman Stefano also wanted to notify that she will be sponsoring a food truck once a week, one in Lakeside and one located at the 8181 Riverstone mobile home park and thus she would like to extend the invitation to the Mayor and Council to join her. The Mayor then instructed Councilwoman Stefano to advise the Clerk s office so the information could be circulated to the Council. Since there was no further business to discuss Councilwoman DiGiacomo made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and the meeting was adjourned at 7:49 pm on April 20, 2020. 9 ae Victoria ia z, FRP, CMC, Town Clerk R artell, Mayor

The motion was seconded by Councilperson Lizelh Ayala and the votes were cast as follows: Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- No Councilperson Edgar Ayala- Yes Councilperson Yesenia Martinez- Yes Councilperson Lizelh Ayala- Yes Mayor Roberto Martell- No In continuance, a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda, including the requested add-on item was placed by Vice-Mayor Pacheco, seconded by Councilperson Ayala and carried unanimously. votes: Councilman Edgar Ayala placed a motion to approve the Chief s recommendation. Councilwoman Lizelh Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Introduction and Ratification of One (1) New Police Officer for the Medley Police Department. Chief of Police Jeanette Said gave a brief introductory information about the proposed candidate and continued to recommend officer Yoel Guerra for the position of Medley police officer. Councilman Edgar Ayala placed a motion to approve the Chief s recommendation. Councilwoman Lizelh Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously. Officer Yoel Guerra was congratulated by the Medley Town Council and so he thanked in return. Mayor Martell then opened the public comment section of the meeting where resident Odalys Torres, residing at 8181 NW South River Drive Lot B-138 Medley Florida 33166 took the opportunity to publicly share an incident that took place with Councilperson Edgar Ayala. Ms. Torres shared the details of the incident including but not limited to stating that Councilperson Ayala had on November 29, 2020 stopped her to question her activities on that day that supported Mayor Roberto Martell. Ms. Torres s comments were translated into the English language for the audience which included words of encouragement for everyone, including the Town Council, to respect one s rights to their personal opinions and political preferences. Councilperson Ayala suggested to follow the Robert s Rules of Order parliamentary procedures to not engage with public comments presented during the public comment section of the meeting. Councilmembers followed. No other public comments were made. In continuance with the agenda, Mayor Martell instructed Town Attorney Lillian Arango to address the resolution reflected on the consent agenda section. Said Resolution was then read into the record as follows:
