votes: Mayor Pacheco made a motion to adopt Resolution C-1868, Councilman Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Resolution Approving the Proposal of Four Seasons Painting for Sealing and Painting of the Town of Medley Municipal Building; Waiving Formal Competitive Procurement Per Section 2-131(D) of the Town Code; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Enter Into any Necessary Agreements for the Work; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Councilman Ayala addressed Richard McConachie, Director of Building and Zoning to clarify why the Town should allow waiving the procurement process. Director McConachie explained that he discussed the matter with the Mayor and due to the time sensitive aspect, nature of the scope of work necessary, and the knowledge of the anticipated cost of repair it was then determined that it would be in the best interest of the Town to waive the competitive process and choose a vendor. Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the Council on the matter and agreed that choosing a vendor would allow the Town to save the expenses associated with the competitive bidding process. Councilman Ayala reiterated that although he was agreement with this resolution the Town needs to continue to follow the regulations set by the procurement ordinance. Without further discussion, Vice Mayor Pacheco made a motion to adopt Resolution C-1868, Councilman Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Hiring Process.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Hiring Process. Councilman Ayala began his discussion by explaining that because politics have implicated employees and the Council, he added the item because prior to elections job positions were opened and brought to light flaws in the hiring process, beginning with the posting of positions. Councilman Ayala further explained that the Council needs to be involved in the hiring process before the recommendations are brought at public meetings for final approval and appointment. Councilman Ayala continued to explain that the Social Services and Parks and Recreation director Lizmari Valido did share information of the qualifications of each interviewed applicant for the positions that are currently posted, and so it was the first time that initiative was taken. Therefore, he believes the hiring process should always be inclusive to presenting all the documentation to the council individually prior to the council meeting. Mayor Martell explained that prior to his tenure there was no process and most of the hires were not even brought before Council for approval, thus he helped establish a structure in the hiring process. Mayor Martell also stated that he agreed with Council involvement, however none have voiced any opinion or concerned toward this matter in the past. Councilwoman Ayala expressed how she has heard from the residents that although positions are open, they are already intended for and she has seen how that has caused residents to complain about favoritism within the Town. Councilwoman Martinez asked that perhaps position s requirements could be shared with the Council prior to the job postings for input if possible. Councilman Ayala explained that positions should come before council prior to posting to determine the necessity of those positions and approval for employment by Council before notice is put out. Mayor Martell explained that positions recently available are not specific replacements to previous personnel. He then further explained that the positions posted for the social services were intended to assist both Park and Recreations and the Afterschool Program to improve the productivity and qualifications of the staff. Councilman Ayala continued to explain that he agreed with the process of staff meeting with each council members individually to brief them on the decision made by the hiring committee for any positions open at the Town. segs.text: Resolution C-1773 Finding that Acquisition through Negotiated Conveyance or the Use of Eminent Domain of Private Property Designated as Parcels 124-1, 124-2, 124-3, 124-4, and 124-5 (Fee Parcels) and 124-11, 124-12, 124-13, 124-14, 124-15, 124-16, 124-17, 124-18, and 124-19 (Permanent Easements) for Road Improvement Project Serves a Public Purpose and are Necessary for Road and Related Improvements Project on NW South River Drive from State Road 826 to NW 72 Avenue and from NW 74 Avenue to NW 82 Street to NW South River Drive. Councilperson Stefano raised a question on the cost, if any, of the negotiation of the parcels. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo approached the podium and explained that this resolution is associated with current ongoing road improvement projects in the Town. Mr. Corzo further explained that the parcels as reflected in Resolution C-1773 are associated and needed for projects such as the ongoing NW South River Drive roadway improvement project for which parcels are required to address the need of additional parking , as well as utilities that were already in place but were not located on an existing easement , and additionally the Town is acquiring Right-of- Way easements to install light poles. Mr. Corzo also explained that the project funding has been previously approved by the Council, however acquiring the easements of these parcels would require additional approval of the Town Council. Vice Mayor Ayala stated that he had previously spoken to Mr. Corzo about the preparedness at the beginning stages of the NW South River Drive road improvement project and additional parking was not addressed at that point. To confirm the purpose of the resolution in question, Councilperson Digiacomo asked for clarification and confirmed that the approval at this point is for the authorization to begin negotiations with the property owners for the parcels listed under resolution C-1773. Building and Zoning Director Richard McConachie approached the podium and explained that the Town has already collected a permit fee of $186,300.00 which recovers the cost of the work order presented under resolution C-1775 which incorporates the work of the consultants overseeing the project. Mayor Martell moved to place a motion to adopt Resolution C-1775, Vice Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. The next item to be addressed was Resolution C-1776 Approving and Establishing a Residential Water Assistance Program. Councilperson Pacheco who sponsored this item wanted to clarify and amend the name of the program. His proposal as it read referred to Pacheco s Water Assistance Program and the resolution read Residential Water Assistance Program . He then began to discuss his revised proposal of the residential program which referred to a program based on water consumption. Therefore, households using 0 2,500 gallons would not be charged for water and sewer which is similar to the practice the Town holds for the residents of the Lakeside Retirement Park. He also stated that if approved, the water department will be charging the general funds account as a benefit to its residents as a water assistance program. In addition, households consuming 2,500 and up to 5,000 gallons monthly will be charged a fee of $14.99 a month, and households consuming water greater than 5,000 gallons per month will see no change in their monthly billing. Councilperson Pacheco also stated that another benefit of the program is to encourage water conservation. To conclude, his final proposal includes a change in the residential water billing cycle from monthly to quarterly. He stated that if approved, the quarter billing will save the Town the expenses of mailing, staffing, as well as residential processing charges. Councilperson Digiacomo questioned Councilperson Pacheco s proposal stating that the new proposal does not coincide with the Resolution as it was instructed to be drafted and it no longer represented an income-based program as the Council had previously discussed. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Waiving Admission Fee for the Hermanamiento y Evento Cultural con Colombia of July 11, 2020. Mayor Martell informed the Town Council that on July 11, 2020 the Town will be hosting a cultural exchange event with Colombia. Therefore, he would like to waive the admission fee since diplomats and other non-resident individuals will be attending the event. segs.head: - Discussion on Councilperson Ivan Pacheco s Proposed Household Water Assistance Program.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion to approve a contribution of $ 500.00 to Teleton U.S.A. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion on Councilperson Ivan Pacheco s Proposed Household Water Assistance Program. Councilperson Pacheco presented his proposal for a water assistance and conservation program he has been working on with the input from staff including Finance and Utilities departments. The proposal is based in a chart that includes brackets depending on the household water consumption. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked if any requirements were going to be put in place for this program. Social Services Director Lizmari Valido approached the Council to elaborate on Councilperson Pacheco s proposal and effort to help seniors with their water utility expenses. Councilperson DiGiacomo expressed that if the goal is to help seniors or households the program should be based on a low- income basis. Therefore, income should be verified and be part of the qualification process for this program. Councilperson DiGiacomo also circulated a draft of an application generated by the finance director reflecting some suggested language for the program. Said proposed language included a minimum of 65 years of age and a minimum of income of $ 23,000 for one person or a maximum of $ 27,000 per household if said household includes more than one person. Councilperson Stefano suggested to apply the United States low income standards to the program. After further discussion Council directed as follows: TO BRING BACK A RESOLUTION AT THE FEBRUARY 3, 2020 REGULAR COUNCIL MEETING CREATING A WATER ASSISTANCE PROGRAM WITH A STRUCTURE BASED ON INCOME USING THE UNITED STATES LOW INCOME STANDARDS, REQUIRING AN INCOME VERIFICATION PROCESS AND YEARLY RENEWALS. IN ADDITION, WATER ACCOUNTS MUST REFLECT AT LEAST OF ONE OF THE RESIDENTS RESIDING IN THE HOUSEHOLD. The next and final item to be addressed was the discussion and action on donation to Teleton U.S.A foundation to support children with disabilities. Mayor Martell made a motion to approve a contribution of $ 500.00 to Teleton U.S.A. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. name: July 21, 2020 Special Virtual Council Meeting - Budget

segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL VIRTUAL MEETING (BUDGET WORKSHOP) OF THE TOWN COUNCIL TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 21, 2020 A special virtual meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 21, 2020 at 5:15p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL VIRTUAL MEETING (BUDGET WORKSHOP) OF THE TOWN COUNCIL TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 21, 2020 A special virtual meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 21, 2020 at 5:15p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: EDGAR AYALA COUNCIL MEMBERS: GRISELIA DIGIACOMO IVAN PACHECO LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and The Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited. A motion to adopt the meeting s agenda, was placed by Councilperson DiGiacomo, seconded by Vice Mayor Ayala and carried unanimously.

segs.head: In continuance Mayor Martell opened the meeting for public comment in which Town Clerk Victoria Martinez noted that no public comments were received or spoken at the time.
votes: Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows. TO SET THE PROPOSED TOWN OF MEDLEY AD VALOREM TAX OPERATING MILLAGE LEVY RATE AT 4.8 MILLS. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: In continuance Mayor Martell opened the meeting for public comment in which Town Clerk Victoria Martinez noted that no public comments were received or spoken at the time. Mayor Martell then instructed Town Clerk Victoria Martinez to read item A as reflected on the agenda. The item was read into the record and discussed as follows: - Discussion on the Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2020 through September 30, 2021. Finance Director Roy Danziger began his discussion on the proposed budget for the Fiscal Year beginning October 1, 2020 through September 30, 2021. Director Danziger then referred everyone to the documentation included with the agenda item which included the Certification of Taxable Value Form DR-420. Finance Director explained the information as listed on said form which reflected assessed property values before adjustments for the 2020-2021 fiscal year are calculated. He also stated that the goal of the meeting was to set the tentative millage rate in order for the Town to submit such by its deadline. Director Danziger also stated the current millage rate of 5.05 mills and further stated for the record the proposed estimate millage rate of 5.51 mills. In addition, Mr. Danziger explained that if the Town would have to assess a mills rate of 4.5494 to have a zero percent (0%) tax increase while receiving the same revenues. Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows. TO SET THE PROPOSED TOWN OF MEDLEY AD VALOREM TAX OPERATING MILLAGE LEVY RATE AT 4.8 MILLS. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Finance Director Danziger then continued to explain the proposed budget as provided to the Council and staff page by page.
votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo placed a motion as follows, TO INCREASE THE SALARY FOR ALL BARGAINING, EXEMPT, PART-TIME AND POLICE DEPARTMENT COMMAND EMPLOYEES BY 3%, EXCLUDING POLICE OFFICERS THAT ARE MEMBERS OF THE POLICE BENEVOLENT ASSOCIATION BARGAINING AGREEMENT Mayor Martell seconded and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Finance Director Danziger then continued to explain the proposed budget as provided to the Council and staff page by page. It was discussed as follows General Fund- Budget Summary- As reflected. There Town will have a $16,508,456 deficit of our 25,000,000.00 million-dollar reserves. General Fund- Revenues- As reflected and discussed. Anticipated $350,000 in less value adjustment. Discussed that sales tax saw a substantial reduction, but the Town does not count on that revenue. Franchise fees and utility taxes, down from last year but by a small margin. Business Tax Receipt are also lower, but numbers will be accurate once renewal billing goes out. Building Permits have a smaller projected for the remainder of the year. Displayed revenues received from grants and the Police revenue. One of the property owners impacted by the special assessments Director Danziger discussed the projected employee salaries and explained that the Council could make a motion to, as practice, continue to give a 3% increase to all bargaining, non-bargaining employees as well as command staff. Without further discussion Councilperson DiGiacomo placed a motion as follows, TO INCREASE THE SALARY FOR ALL BARGAINING, EXEMPT, PART-TIME AND POLICE DEPARTMENT COMMAND EMPLOYEES BY 3%, EXCLUDING POLICE OFFICERS THAT ARE MEMBERS OF THE POLICE BENEVOLENT ASSOCIATION BARGAINING AGREEMENT Mayor Martell seconded and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.head: In addition, finance director Danziger addressed the issuance of the employee holiday bonus as it was allocated and included in the proposed budget.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO INSTRUCT THE FINANCE DIRECTOR, THE TOWN ENGINEER AND THE TOWN ATTORNEY TO LOOK INTO APPLYING FOR A SRF LOAN Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: In addition, finance director Danziger addressed the issuance of the employee holiday bonus as it was allocated and included in the proposed budget. He continued to state that he would bring this matter before the Council for a final decision in the month of November. He further continued to address the proposed budget as follows: General Fund - General Administration Department: As reflected General Fund - Building and Zoning Department: Proposed budget as reflected, will receive the 3% increase, and professional fees are high. General Fund - Public Safety Proposed budget to include the command staff receiving the 3%. Off duty is estimated as presented. General Fund - Code Compliance (3) Employees and professional fees are high but expenses are anticipated to go down. General Fund - Physical Environment (Public Works) Proposed budget as reflected. Discussed that a new vehicle is required. The department has gone over their vehicle budget solely on repairs and maintenance of older existing vehicles. General Fund - Capital Improvement and Economic Development discussed as reflected General Fund Senior Social Services Includes the meal and medical transportation program as well as house cleaning. Budget as presented. Discussed that social services need an additional vehicle. General Fund - Culture and Recreation (Social Services) Includes Town annual events and other social service programs. Each expense will be projected back to the usual expenses. The budget anticipates that COVID-19 pandemic only affected the current year s budget. General Fund Debt Service Proposed as reflected. No changes. General Fund Capital Expenditures As reflected some items need further discussion with the capital improvement department. Expenses to be used for MMSF repairs and roof repairs. Water and Sewer Utilities No changes Water and Sewer Utilities Capital Expenditures No Changes It was determined that the Mayor and Director Danziger would sit and discuss the purchase of vehicles for several departments in need. Also, a social services vehicle will be budgeted based on county requirements for the vehicle. Stormwater Utilities Capital Expenditures Director Danziger proposed for the Town to attempt to reduce the anticipated 16-million-dollar deficit from the reserves. He explained that by taking CWSRF loans for three projects presented on this worksheet the Town could substantially reduce the projected deficit. He explained that the interest rate fora CWSRF loan is currently 2.

segs.head: It was noted that the Town had not been negatively impacted by the COVID-19 global pandemic.
segs.text: It was noted that the Town had not been negatively impacted by the COVID-19 global pandemic. Director Danziger foresees that the only effect may come next year when property owners are required to pay their property taxes and there could be a greater reduction in the assessed property values. Since there was no further business to discuss Vice Mayor Ayala made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and the meeting was adjourned at 7:06pm on July 21, 2020.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Proposals Submitted for the Compensation and Pay Equity Study Previously Approved by Council. Town Attorney Lillian Arango stated that as previously instructed by the Council, two proposals from firms Evergreen Solutions LLC and Gallagher to perform compensatory and pay equity studies were submitted for the Town Council s consideration. Councilperson DiGiacomo and Mayor Martell voiced their agreement to retain Evergreen Solutions LLC. Vice Mayor Ayala expressed his concerns with the public records request No. 2020PRRTC-15 and stated that a decision be made to begin an investigation to find out who the requester was. Town Attorney Lillian Arango and Councilperson DiGiacomo explained that is legal for the requester to remain anonymous and further explained that there was no unlawfulness to these requests as presented to the Town. Town Attorney Arango also explained that the request for public record under Florida Statute Chapter 119 allows individuals to request any records from the Town and the Town is responsible to provide them. Councilwoman DiGiacomo stated that she believed there was validity to the claims submitted by the individual and that the Town should address and attempt to create a structure to determine and set the wages for the employees. Mayor Martell agreed with Councilperson DiGiacomo s statement and to conduct the study. Councilperson Stefano stated that she agreed with investigating on the basis that the individual also crossed the line by discussing employee s processes and employee s matters. Councilwoman Stefano continued to state that the Town has no structure on any employee processes of, hiring, terminating, and determining wages. Councilwoman DiGiacomo responded to Councilperson Stefano and continued to state that the Town has a recently adopted employee handbook that underlines a process for hiring that has been in place with the adoption of Ordinance C-280 and has been practiced ever since as well as a disciplinary and termination process. However, the Town lacks a process to determine and establish wages for employees. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO RETAIN EVERGREEN SOLUTIONS, LLC TO PERFORM A COMPENSATORY STUDY TO INCLUDE A GENDER ANALYSIS Councilwoman DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. *Recessed 6:37pm* *Returned 6:47PM* Town Attorney continued the discussion by explaining that the Town may choose to perform an investigation on the

segs.head: - Councilperson Pacheco s Request for Discussion and Action on Lucelly Arena s Termination of Employment.
segs.text: - Councilperson Pacheco s Request for Discussion and Action on Lucelly Arena s Termination of Employment. Councilperson Pacheco began his discussion by stating that he promised himself when beginning office that he would act diligently and morally. Councilperson Pacheco then commended Janitorial Director Omar Sanchez for his hard work and clarified that the discussion is not based on his work performance but based on how he allegedly directs his staff, which resulted in the termination of Lucelly Arena. Councilperson Pacheco stated that he believed that she was wrongly terminated with no credible evidence that reflected she was not performing her duties. Councilperson Pacheco continued to explain that he did not receive sufficient evidence from the human resources department and stated that the screenshots he received are not a form of acceptable evidence because there is no video to attest to the screenshots. He emphasized that there have not been any negative work performance evaluations for the employee in question and he questioned the human resources director for not divulging supporting documents of the interviews held with the employees of the janitorial department. In conclusion, he stated that there was not enough evidence for the termination and the believed decision was made because she approached human resources to complain about her supervisor. Director Sanchez approached the Council and stated that he had discussed his concerns about the employee with Councilperson Pacheco and had shown him sufficient evidence to support his decision. Director Sanchez also stated that he has evidence supporting that her claims against him are false and he has been dealing with her work performance for months, since she was hired. Human Resources Director Olga Quin also approached the Council and began by explaining the timeline in which she provided information and evidence to Councilperson Pacheco in regard to the investigation that was initially held to determine if Director Sanchez was acting unfairly towards his employees. Director Quin explained that on July 16, 2020 she spoke with Councilperson Pacheco and went through in detail the evidence of the case explaining each document. She then stated that on July 22, 2020 she provided the photos that he claimed he did | not receive and provided to him, both by email and by physical copies that were given to him in | person. Ms. Ryder explained that from a legal perspective Ms. Arenas needed to apply and qualify for the position she is being proposed to be appointed, and for a better legal opinion and understanding , the Town needed to provide more information on the intent towards this employee. Attorney Ryder continued to present the Council with two options, the first was to reinstate the employee to her previous position and the second was for the Council to agree to approve her employment going through the proper hiring process if a vacancy was available and if she was qualified for and come to a settlement agreement to allow for the proposed back pay. To this legal advice, Vice Mayor Ayala expressed his agreement with the first option of reinstating her to her previous position because the Town has in the past switched employees from departments. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on Councilperson DiGiacomo s Request to Address Findings of Public Records Request No. 2020PRRTC-15.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO SOLICIT PROPOSALS TO HIRE AN INDEPENDENT FIRM TO PERFORM A COMPENSATION STUDY OF ALL DEPARTMENT HEADS, ASSISTANT DEPARTMENT HEADS, THE MAYOR S ASSISTANT, THE CHIEF OF POLICE AND THE POLICE DEPARTMENT S COMMAND STAFF Councilwoman DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Councilperson DiGiacomo s Request to Address Findings of Public Records Request No. 2020PRRTC-15. Councilwoman DiGiacomo began discussion on the item as requested that referenced Public Records request No. 2020PRRTC-15 as it was received and processed by the Office of the Town Clerk. Councilperson DiGiacomo further stated that the email along with all the information provided by the request for records was then forwarded to members of the Council by the requester and the email questioned the Town s methods to determine salaries for individuals that fall under the same professional and educational classifications. Councilwoman DiGiacomo also stated that the email in question provided and addressed differences in salary between male and female employees in their administrative positions and claimed a large marginal salary difference between the male and female employees, also highlighting and claiming male employees to receive higher compensation. Councilwoman DiGiacomo explained that once she received this email with said allegations, she sent it to the Town attorney for review and a legal recommendation. Councilperson DiGiacomo further stated that although these practices have been in place much prior to the current administration, once it is been brought to light, it is the Town s responsibility to take action and establish fair practices, therefore the Town s attorneys recommended to retain a company to perform a salary study including the comparison of salaries, and most importantly addressing employees that have the same credentials and education but are not making similar wages. Town Attorney Lillian Arango joined the discussion and reiterated that the legal recommendation is to hire an independent firm to perform a compensation study so the Town can establish if there are any validity to these allegations, and if so, correct them accordingly. Mayor Martell agreed with the legal recommendation and suggested that the study include all department heads, assistant department heads, the Mayor s assistant, the chief of Police and command staff. Without further discussion Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO SOLICIT PROPOSALS TO HIRE AN INDEPENDENT FIRM TO PERFORM A COMPENSATION STUDY OF ALL DEPARTMENT HEADS, ASSISTANT DEPARTMENT HEADS, THE MAYOR S ASSISTANT, THE CHIEF OF POLICE AND THE POLICE DEPARTMENT S COMMAND STAFF Councilwoman DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: Resolution C-1809 Approving and Accepting an Agreement to Convey Parcels with Riverstone Communities, LLC, for Conveyance of Parcels 123-01-1425 (Fee Parcel), 123-11-1425, 123-12-1426, 123-13-1426 (Permanent Easements), and 123-31 (Temporary Easement) in Connection with the Road Improvement Project on NW South River Drive from State Road 826 to NW 72nd Avenue To NW 82nd Street to NW South River Drive. Councilwoman DiGiacomo asked for some clarification as to why some parcels require permanent easements and others temporary easements. Town legal Counsel Pete Waldman explained that acquiring permanent easements are typically for projects that require drainage work, or possibly sidewalk construction where as temporary easements are acquired for harmonizing the road and in those cases the Town only needs to acquire the easement on a temporary basis to finish construction. Town engineer Jorge Corzo also explained that when the Town constructs a new road or side walk it is required to obtain and purchase the right of way, but if the Town is working on a driveway connection and after it is constructed there is need to own that property, therefore a temporary easement is only necessary. Without further discussion, Councilperson Pacheco made a motion to adopt Resolution C-1809, Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: Resolution C-1814 Amending and Restating in its Entirety Resolution C-1689 Adopted on April 30, 2019 Entitled A Resolution of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida, Relating to the Medley 77S-79A Infrastructure Improvement Area Project ; Describing the Property to be Included Within the Proposed Medley 77S-79A Infrastructure Improvement Area and the Local Improvements to be Provided Therein; Determining the Estimated Capital Cost of the Medley 77S-79A Infrastructure Improvement Area Project; Establishing the Method of Assessing the Project Cost Against the Properties that Will Be Benefitted Thereby; Establishing Other Terms and Conditions of the Assessments. Vice Mayor wanted to be provided a brief explanation of the Resolution and what the Town is hoping to accomplish. Town legal Counsel Lori Smith-Lalla explained that this is the first district the Town has established which will impact only two property owners. Ms. Smith-Lalla further explained that the assessment will only apply to those two individuals and the funds determined will be collected through their tax roll. The Town will soon commence traffic and roadway improvements. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo also explained that the Town has recognized the lack of funds necessary to apply all the required improvements. Therefore, it was decided to include participation from property owners in the form of a special assessment. He continued to explain that one project has already been completed and the two property owners Gamma Delta and Prologis as well as the major tenant in Prologis Seaboard Marine have been involved in this initial assessment and are well aware of the improvements needed. It has been a pilot project and the Town is now better informed and well-practiced in the process of imposing a special assessment. Without further discussion, Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion to adopt Resolution C-1814 and Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on Mayor Martell s Proposal to Provide Rental Assistance for Town of Medley Residents due to Hardship Caused by the COVID-19 Pandemic.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Mayor Martell s Proposal to Provide Rental Assistance for Town of Medley Residents due to Hardship Caused by the COVID-19 Pandemic. Mayor Martell began to discuss his proposed item stating that the purpose was to utilize Town of Medley Foundation funds to help residents that have been experiencing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The mayor stated the following proposals for the guidelines and structure of the program, by the recommendation of Finance Director Roy Danziger. The Mayor further stated that a total budget of $60,000 was to be used from the Town of Medley Foundation, and would also like to wait till after the end of the qualification period so the Town could determine how many applicants are approved, therefore allowing for a distribution amount to be determined. Ms. Arango provided the council information on similar neighboring cities programs and requirements that can be used for consideration in this housing assistance program. Councilwoman DiGiacomo stated that she had been researching the topic along with Town Attorney Arango to get a better understanding of what documentation would be required for submittal and qualification. Councilperson Pacheco suggested the distribution of the $60,000 equally amongst all of the households within the town, but it was determined that it would not serve the purpose of attempting to get funds to households affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and in deer need of financial assistance. Councilwoman DiGiacomo suggested that the Office of the Town Clerk distribute the recommended guidelines from other cities to the Mayor and Council for their input on the program s qualification and criteria subject to final approval of those conditions provided any changes the Council may wish to impose. Councilwoman Stefano stated that she is aware of many residents who have been impacted and would like to include individuals who have also experienced loss of work hours not solely employment. Councilwoman DiGiacomo also suggested having this program handled by the office of the Town Clerk. Without further discussion Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO ESTABLISH A COVID-19 HOUSING ASSISTANCE PROGRAM FOR TOWN OF MEDLEY RESIDENTS, BOTH TENANTS AND HOMEOWNERS, WHO HAVE LOST EMPLOYMENT OR HAVE RECEIVED A TEMPORARY REDUCTION IN HOURS CAUSED BY THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Re-Opening of Town of Medley Public Facilities and Operations.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO OPEN THE MEDLEY MUNICIPAL SERVICES FACILITY TO THE PUBLIC FROM THE HOURS OF 7:30AM TO 12:00PM MONDAY THROUGH THURSDAY EFFECTIVE JUNE 2, 2020 FOR ESSENTIAL MUNICIPAL SERVICES ONLY. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Re-Opening of Town of Medley Public Facilities and Operations. Human resources director Olga Quin explained the processes as described in the return to work policy and procedure handbook. Councilperson DiGiacomo asked if the Town will continue to allow employees who have children and are able to perform from home to telecommute. The mayor explained that the utilities department had a recent emergency and they were short staffed therefore determining that the utilities department and public works department must return to full work because they cannot fulfill their duties from home and will no longer rotate or telework. The Mayor also stated that the remaining employees will continue to telecommute or rotate as determined by each department s director and each departmental need. Director Quin explained that the Medley Municipal Services Facility will slowly begin to open to the public with limited access and reduced hours to the public. Ms. Quin continued explaining that the recommendation is to only allow two individuals of the public to enter the facility at the time, it is suggested that the Town be open only from 7:30am to 12:00pm. There will be proper signage following the guidelines provided by Miami Dade County for the public, screening for entering the building and the Town will be taking proper sanitary measures. The Mayor proposed for the re-opening to be effective the next day June 2,2020. A public comment was received regarding the plans for the Town of Medley 2020 Summer Camp where Ms. Quin explained that there is course of action at this time for the Town of Medley Summer Camp Program. The Mayor continued to explain that the Town is waiting on information and direction from Miami Dade County before discussing and taking action on the procedure to open the summer camp. Without further discussion Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO OPEN THE MEDLEY MUNICIPAL SERVICES FACILITY TO THE PUBLIC FROM THE HOURS OF 7:30AM TO 12:00PM MONDAY THROUGH THURSDAY EFFECTIVE JUNE 2, 2020 FOR ESSENTIAL MUNICIPAL SERVICES ONLY. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Town Clerk Martinez noted a comment received from the public asking if temperatures will be taken at the door at which time, she responded yes and further explained that any individuals entering will have body temperature taken and be provided gloves by the Town. Also, facial coverings will continue to be mandated and required

segs.head: MINUTES OF A VIRTUAL SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 15, 2020 A special virtual meeting of the Town Council was called to order on June 15, 2020 at 5:15 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A VIRTUAL SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 15, 2020 A special virtual meeting of the Town Council was called to order on June 15, 2020 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: EDGAR AYALA COUNCIL MEMBERS: GRISELIA DIGIACOMO IVAN PACHECO LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and The Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited. In continuance, A motion to adopt the meeting s agenda was placed by Councilperson DiGiacomo, seconded by Councilperson Pacheco and carried unanimously. Mayor Martell then opened the meeting for public comment to which it was noted that no comments were made nor received by the Town Clerk.

segs.head: The Mayor then moved on to address the items on the agenda.
votes: Vice Mayor Ayala made a motion as follows: TO OPEN THE TOWN OF MEDLEY SUMMER CAMP FOR THE 2020 YEAR AS RECOMMENDED BY DIRECTOR VALIDO INCLUDING THE CONTROLLED PICK UP AND DROP OFF OPTION , FOLLOWING THE CDC GUIDELINES AND A COVID-19 WAIVER TO BE SIGNED BY THE PARTICIPANT S PARENTS. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: The Mayor then moved on to address the items on the agenda. They were discussed and acted upon as follows. - Discussion and Action on the Opening and Operations of the Town of Medley 2020 Summer Camp Program. Social Services and Parks and Recreations Director Lizmari Valido explained that given the restrictions and new regulations imposed by Miami-Dade County and health organizations for the COVID-19 pandemic, the Town of Medley summer camp program, if opening, would be obligated to limit the capacity. With that said, a total amount of 16 children would be allowed to attend the program and priority will be given to residents. This total amount would be divided between 2 facilities in order to accommodate the regulations imposed. Director Valido wanted to note that she also has limited staff and by opening the Summer Camp they will no longer be available to be assigned other duties. Director Valido further explained that the Town is required to inform the parents of the steps the town is taking for the safety of their children as well as placing signage at the program s facilities. Director Valido also explained that given the restrictions and limited capacity, it was her recommendation to open the enrollment to children whose both parents are working, subject to employment verification, in an effort to prioritize parents who would have a necessity for the program. In addition, as part of the enrollment process a doctor release would be required in addition to the Town of Medley standard verification process. Director Valido also mentioned than in case an excess of the 16 applications are received, a lottery system would then take place by parent s name to ensure all children to be selected if more than sibling is applied for. If the amount of applications received do not exceed the total amount of the limited capacity, the enrollment opportunity will be then open to employees and the final date for registration would be June 26, 2020. In addition to the limited capacity of the program and in order to ensure the safety of all program participants, Director Valido recommended the pickup and drop off to be in a controlled manner which would include to restrict the hours of operations of the Town of Medley resident GYM to minimize the exposure of both children and staff. After a brief discussion, it was determined that Director Valido s recommendation to establish a carline drop off restricting arrival between the hours of 8:00AM -10:00AM would be implemented

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Re-Opening and Operations of the Town of Medley Residential Gym Facility.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion as follows: TO OPEN THE RESIDENT GYM FACILITY AND TOBIE WILSON PARK WITH THE HOURS OF OPERATIONS FROM 1:00 PM TO 8:00PM MONDAY TO SATURDAY AND SUNDAY FROM 12:00PM TO 5:00PM EFFECTIVE JUNE 22, 2020. INDIVIDUALS SELECTING TO USE THE GYM FACILITY WILL BE REQUIRED TO COMPLETE A DISCLAIMER WAIVER SPECIFIC TO THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Re-Opening and Operations of the Town of Medley Residential Gym Facility. Social Services and Parks and Recreations Director Lizmari Valido then continued to explain the proposed hours of operations for said Town of Medley facility. Director Valido reiterated the restrictions imposed by Miami-Dade County and went on to also highlight the location s relations with the new logistics and operations previously discussed for the 2020 Summer Camp Program. Thus, possible hours of operations were discussed in order to still provide the benefit to Medley residents. Councilperson DiGiacomo stated that although the facility had to be restricted in the hours of the morning perhaps the Town could keep the current 8:00 PM closing hours including for the weekends. Director Valido also mentioned the proposal of restricting the facility to Medley residents only, therefore not allowing guests or companions. Director Valido also recommended to restrict the amount of time an individual will use the gym so other residents can use the gym without an extended wait time. Councilwoman DiGiacomo stated that the Tobie Wilson Park should be opened on the weekends for residential use since residents have been at home now for extended period of time and allowing them to use the park would provide relief in this stressful time. The Mayor suggested extending the hours of the park for the public from 1:00pm-8:00pm Monday through Saturday and Sunday from 12:00pm-5:00pm. Without further discussion Mayor Martell made a motion as follows: TO OPEN THE RESIDENT GYM FACILITY AND TOBIE WILSON PARK WITH THE HOURS OF OPERATIONS FROM 1:00 PM TO 8:00PM MONDAY TO SATURDAY AND SUNDAY FROM 12:00PM TO 5:00PM EFFECTIVE JUNE 22, 2020. INDIVIDUALS SELECTING TO USE THE GYM FACILITY WILL BE REQUIRED TO COMPLETE A DISCLAIMER WAIVER SPECIFIC TO THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously. The third and last item of the agenda to be addressed was discussed and acted upon as follows.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Proposal of a Modified School Bus Route to begin 2020- 2021 School Year.
votes: Vice-Mayor Ayala made a motion as follows: TO ADD THE PROPOSED SCHOOL BUS ROUTE TO AIE CHARTER SCHOOL AND BEFORE SCHOOL CARE/DROP OFF AT TOBIE WILSON PARK BEGINNING ON THE 2020-2021 SCHOOL YEAR. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Proposal of a Modified School Bus Route to begin 2020- 2021 School Year. Social Services and Parks and Recreations Director Lizmari Valido continued to present the new proposed school bus route for the 2020-2021 school year that included the Academy International of Education Charter School (AIE). Director Valido stated that a total of eighteen (18) medley children are currently enrolled, and several others are in the waiting list for future enrollment. Director Valido, in addition to the new route, proposed a new drop-off/before care option at Tobie Wilson Park to incorporate the new proposed route with the existing and current school bus routes and to avoid the outdoor conditions that a bus stop would bring. Without further discussion Vice-Mayor Ayala made a motion as follows: TO ADD THE PROPOSED SCHOOL BUS ROUTE TO AIE CHARTER SCHOOL AND BEFORE SCHOOL CARE/DROP OFF AT TOBIE WILSON PARK BEGINNING ON THE 2020-2021 SCHOOL YEAR. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Since there was no further discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion to adjourn the meeting.

segs.head: MINUTES OF A VIRTUAL SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 18, 2020 A special virtual meeting of the Town Council was called to order on June 15, 2020 at 5:15 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A VIRTUAL SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 18, 2020 A special virtual meeting of the Town Council was called to order on June 15, 2020 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: EDGAR AYALA COUNCIL MEMBERS: GRISELIA DIGIACOMO IVAN PACHECO LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and The Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited. In continuance, A motion to adopt the meeting s agenda was placed by Councilperson Stefano, seconded by Councilperson DiGiacomo and carried unanimously. Mayor Martell then opened the meeting for public comment to which it was noted that no comments were made nor received by the Town Clerk.

segs.head: The Mayor then moved on to address the item on the agenda as it was requested by Councilperson Stefano.
segs.text: The Mayor then moved on to address the item on the agenda as it was requested by Councilperson Stefano. The item was discussed and acted upon as follows. - Discussion and Action on the Guidelines and Requirements of Town of Medley COVID-19 Housing Assistance Program. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez stated that as reflected on the documentation provided to the Town Council, there were a total of thirty-nine (39) applications received and the information provided also reflected the status and documentation provided by each applicant thus far. Councilperson Stefano then addressed her request by stating that after the COVID-19 Housing Assistance Program was created, some self-employed residents had approached her with some concerns as it would be difficult to provide the documentation required by the program. Therefore, making it difficult for said individuals to quality and receive the assistance. In addition, Councilperson Stefano mentioned that retirees, which in many cases continue to be employed because of financial hardships, were also restricted from the assistance. Councilperson DiGiacomo joined the discussion and stated that the assistance program was created with the goal to provide a one-time assistance to those residents who by losing their employment would automatically lose their source of income. Councilperson DiGiacomo further stated that compared to most of the Medley residents, retirees have a fixed and guaranteed monthly income, thus that was the reason why the assistance program did not include them. Vice-Mayor Ayala joined the discussion and explained how self-employed individuals were also affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, thus it would be fair to consider their source of income and employment as well. Vice-Mayor Ayala further explained and recommended for these individuals to provide a letter reflecting their source of employment with a minimum of three (3) sources/individuals to whom services were provided for verification in addition to a legal affidavit in support to said employment information. Mayor Roberto Martell addressed Town Attorney Lillian Arango for legal advice and recommendation. Town Attorney Arango stated that said affidavit could be drafted to document the applicant s eligibility to the program and to confirm the loss of employment or partial income. Without further discussion Vice-Mayor Ayala made a motion as follows: TO ALLOW FOR AN AFFIDAVIT AND LETTER WITH A MINIMUM OF THREE (3) SOURCES OF EMPLOYEMENT IN LIEU OF THE F

segs.head: The Council then moved to discuss the awarded amount to each applicant as an amount had not been decided upon.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion as follows, TO AWARD AN AMOUNT OF $ 1200 PER APPLICANT SHALL THE NUMBER OF APPLICATIONS RECEIVED NOT EXCEED FIFTY. HOWEVER, IF 50 APPLICATIONS OR MORE ARE RECEIVED, THEN THE AMOUNT AWARDED SHALL BE THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF THE FUNDS EQUALLY DIVIDED BY THE NUMBER OF APPLICANTS. Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The Council then moved to discuss the awarded amount to each applicant as an amount had not been decided upon. Mayor Martell stated that the total amount of funds for this program was previously set at sixty thousand ($ 60,000) dollars. Therefore, given the number of applicants and possible additional applicants an amount of $ 1000 to $ 1200 per applicant should be considered. After a small discussion about the reasonable amount, Mayor Martell made a motion as follows, TO AWARD AN AMOUNT OF $ 1200 PER APPLICANT SHALL THE NUMBER OF APPLICATIONS RECEIVED NOT EXCEED FIFTY. HOWEVER, IF 50 APPLICATIONS OR MORE ARE RECEIVED, THEN THE AMOUNT AWARDED SHALL BE THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF THE FUNDS EQUALLY DIVIDED BY THE NUMBER OF APPLICANTS. Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Since there was no further discussion, Councilperson Pacheco made a motion to adjourn the

segs.head: meeting.
segs.text: meeting. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and the meeting was adjourned at 7:06 pm on June 18, 2020.

segs.head: Resolution C-1788 Declaring the Town of Medley State of Emergency due to the Public Health Threat Resulting from the Spread of the Coronavirus Disease (COVID- 19).
votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion to adopt Resolution C-1788, Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Resolution C-1788 Declaring the Town of Medley State of Emergency due to the Public Health Threat Resulting from the Spread of the Coronavirus Disease (COVID- 19). Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion to adopt Resolution C-1788, Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: The next item to be discussed and as reflected on the agenda was the following Town of Medley item: Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Operations and Town of Medley Events in Preparation for the Continued Monitoring of the Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19).
votes: Councilperson Digiacomo made a motion as follows: TO CANCEL ALL TOWN EVENTS FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE MONTH OF MARCH WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE CHILDREN S EASTER PARTY Councilperson Stefano seconded, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: The next item to be discussed and as reflected on the agenda was the following Town of Medley item: Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Operations and Town of Medley Events in Preparation for the Continued Monitoring of the Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19). The Mayor began the discussion stating his proposal, given the emergency circumstances, to cancel all major Town events, but would like to exclude the cancelation of the Town s weekly music night celebration held at Lakeside Retirement Recreational Center. He stated that with the Council s consideration he would also like to continue the meal program, cold lunch program, and afterschool program unless the situation progresses. He further explained that at this point would initiate level 2 operations. Councilperson DiGiacomo stated that most of the Town s residential population is elderly, and it has been confirmed that the senior demographic is affected at a higher risk of contracting the Coronavirus (COVID-19) disease. Thus, because the Senior music night event congregates individuals she did not agree with the continuance of this event. The Mayor then addressed Social Services director Lizmari Valido and suggested that she mentioned each program and event allowing the Mayor and Council to put the cancellation of each of these items to vote. She began to state the events in which the Mayor confirmed the cancellation of the monthly residential birthday celebration. After a brief discussion it was said that any major event held in March be cancelled or postponed for a later date. Ms. Valido addressed the children s Easter party and it was determined that the event may still be held but only during afterschool hours for the afterschool children not as a public town event. Director Valido also mentioned the previously schedule event with the Department of Motors Vehicles (DMV) to which the Council agreed to reschedule it to a later date. Next director Valido explained that she had spoken to Meal Program director Fatima Fuentes regarding the weekend cold lunch distribution held at Tobie Wilson Park. They further explained that the process in which the distribution takes place puts both the residents and staff at risk of exposure. Therefore, director Valido suggested that for the duration of the State of Emergency the weekend cold lunch be distributed through the kitchen window not permitting residents into the Tobie Wilson Park facility. The Mayor and Council agreed with the recommendation, adding that an

segs.head: Next director Valido informed the council that Latin America Grill, our vendor for the hot meal program, had informed the Town of safety measures and health protocol implemented on their end.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion as follows: ALL TOWN PROGRAMS WILL CONTINUE TO OPERATE AS IS WITH THE EXCEPTION OF COLD LUNCH DISTRIBUTION IN WHICH THE OPERATIONS WILL BE CHANGED TO ACCOMMODATE DISTRIBUTION THROUGH TOBIE WILSON PARK WINDOW AND THE ASSIGNMENT OF AN OFFICER TO BE STATIONED FOR THE DURATION OF THE PROGRAM Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Next director Valido informed the council that Latin America Grill, our vendor for the hot meal program, had informed the Town of safety measures and health protocol implemented on their end. Director Valido further explained that she had reached out to both, Advancare and Senior Care Services vendors that provide services to our elderly residential community, but they have yet responded. Without further discussion or questions on Town s programs, Mayor Martell made a motion as follows: ALL TOWN PROGRAMS WILL CONTINUE TO OPERATE AS IS WITH THE EXCEPTION OF COLD LUNCH DISTRIBUTION IN WHICH THE OPERATIONS WILL BE CHANGED TO ACCOMMODATE DISTRIBUTION THROUGH TOBIE WILSON PARK WINDOW AND THE ASSIGNMENT OF AN OFFICER TO BE STATIONED FOR THE DURATION OF THE PROGRAM Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: The discussion continued to address employee protocol for sickness and the Town s plan for preventative measures including discussion on daily operations and essential personnel.
segs.text: The discussion continued to address employee protocol for sickness and the Town s plan for preventative measures including discussion on daily operations and essential personnel. Ms. Valido addressed the concern that on Tuesday March 17, 2020 elections will be held and the Municipal Facility is a polling place. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez explained that the Miami- Dade Elections Department has not informed the Town of cancellations. However, they are taking sanitary measures for the polling area and for their staff. Vice Mayor Ayala initiated a discussion about his concerns with employee sick leave and the determination of sickness. The Mayor explained that the Town has taken initiative, considering the recommendations of health professionals, to take action if an employee is unwell. If that is the case the Town encourages employees to go home and follow any instruction given by their physician. The Mayor further explained that If employees under these circumstances are scheduled to return to work but still feeling unwell, at that point and time, the Town encourages employees to take additional time until fully recovered. Humans resources director Olga Quin approached the podium to provide clarification in regard to employee-health protocol. She stated that the existing Town s policy requires employees to submit a physician s note once they have taken three or more days of sick leave. She also stated that the Town has already implemented preventative measures by sending employees who feel or look ill home. Director Quin further asked for instructions as to whether the Town Council would like to implement a paid administrative leave for employees who show signs or have flu-like symptoms. Ms. Quin further explained that according to the Department of Health and Human Services (CDC), self-quarantine has been determined to be fourteen (14) days. Therefore, direction from the Town Council is needed to make that determination and implement said administrative time and whether the administrative pay leave would be implemented after the three (3) day sick leave policy. Town attorney Lilliana Arango addressed the questions to state that the CDC has reported that an employee who exhibits symptoms of influenza during a pandemic should leave the workplace, and may be asked to go home, thus the Town has the authority to send an employee under these circumstances home. Councilperson DiGiacomo intervened and expressed that the Town should compensate employees sent home

segs.head: Mayor Martell suggested a rotation schedule that would allow employees within a department to alternate their attendance to establish some social distancing from other staff members and members of the public.
votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion as follows: EFFECTIVE MONDAY MARCH 16, 2020 DIRECTORS AND ASSISTANT DIRECTORS WILL ENTER INTO A ROTATION SCHEDULE Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Mayor Martell suggested a rotation schedule that would allow employees within a department to alternate their attendance to establish some social distancing from other staff members and members of the public. Mayor Martell further explained that administrative personnel should start the rotation schedule on Monday March 16, 2020. Mayor Martell made it clear that he will allow department heads to determine their staff s rotation schedule and employees must understand that they are being compensated to work from home so they must stay home and be on call as well as perform the duties that they are capable of doing. Concerns were addressed about meal program staff, utility department and public works personnel. Town Clerk Martinez explained that from an IT perspective, because the needs of every department are different, it was necessary to determine the essential personnel and those who, depending on their duties, could perform remotely to then provide the necessary equipment to satisfy those needs. Without further discussion Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion as follows: EFFECTIVE MONDAY MARCH 16, 2020 DIRECTORS AND ASSISTANT DIRECTORS WILL ENTER INTO A ROTATION SCHEDULE Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: In continuance with the employee s discussion, director Valido asked the Mayor and the Council to determine/approve a practice to address employees that may potentially be forced off work during the closure of Town programs and facilities.
segs.text: In continuance with the employee s discussion, director Valido asked the Mayor and the Council to determine/approve a practice to address employees that may potentially be forced off work during the closure of Town programs and facilities. Mayor Martell stated that at this time he would like to keep both locations open but if and once Miami-Dade County Public Schools announces closure of the public schools the Town can then make the decision to close the afterschool program and those employees be forced-off will be compensated. Councilperson Pacheco agreed with the decision to close the afterschool program. On the other hand, Vice Mayor Ayala expressed concern for the parents who have to work and cannot keep their children at home. Thus, he would like for the program to stay open to help the residential community. Director Valido explained that the purpose of closing the afterschool programs is to reduce the possibility of contamination amongst the children, as well as the exposure to the staff of the municipality, and our first responder s who are located in the same building. The purpose is to create social distancing to reduce the chances of contracting Coronavirus disease (COVID-19). Without further discussion on the matter, Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion as follows: THE TOWN OF MEDLEY AFTERSCHOOL PROGRAM WILL FOLLOW THE MIAMI-DADE COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOLS SCHEDULE. IF AND WHEN MIAMI -DADE COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOLS ANNOUNCES CLOSURE THEN AT THAT TIME THE TOWN WILL CLOSE THE AFTERSCHOOL PROGRAM. IN ADDITION, THE TOWN AUTHORIZES PAID ADMINISTRATIVE LEAVE TO EMPLOYEES FORCED-OFF OF WORK UNDER THESE EMERGENCY CIRCUMSTANCES Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: After a brief discussion between the Mayor and Council about the Town of Medley facilities, it was Clarified that the Lakeside Retirement Park Recreational Center, Tobie Wilson Park and Danny Meehan Recreational field including the residential gym will remain open.
votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion as follows: THE TOWN AUTHORIZES THE MAYOR TO IMPLEMENT AND ENFORCE AN EMPLOYEE RECALL PROCESS IF NEEDED Councilperson Pacheco Seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: After a brief discussion between the Mayor and Council about the Town of Medley facilities, it was Clarified that the Lakeside Retirement Park Recreational Center, Tobie Wilson Park and Danny Meehan Recreational field including the residential gym will remain open. However, as the circumstances related to the coronavirus (COVID-19) progresses, the Mayor can exercise the authority given by the Council under the Declaration of Emergency previously adopted to take the decision to close the facilities as he deems necessary. In regards to the employee rotation schedule, Councilperson DiGiacomo addressed the department heads and suggested they make it clear to their staff that although they were being compensated for being at home during the rotation schedule, staff must remain at home and on call. Therefore, staff is not allowed to use the time for recreational activities. In addition, she addresses the Mayor and stated that the County implemented an employee recall order. Thus, she asked the Council if the Town will be enforcing a similar policy in which employees must cancel their scheduled vacation time that falls within the next thirty (30) days. She explained that the Town needs all personnel available in case staff members become sick or diagnosed with (COVID- 19). Lieutenant Jinete suggests the Town implement the policy for future vacation requests but not remove the vacation time from employees who already received prior approval for time off. Councilperson DiGiacomo explained that as the Miami-Dade County recall policy states and given the circumstances she would like to make it clear to employees who choose to travel knowing the risk of contracting the Coronavirus (COVID-19), that if they return and test positive for the disease the Town will then enforce the fourteen (14) day quarantine at the expense of the employee. Thus, the Town will not compensate employees based on their negligent behavior and personal liability. The Mayor was in agreement and can use his authority under the emergency declarations to implement and enforce an employee recall process if needed. After a brief recess, the meeting resumed and Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion as follows: THE TOWN AUTHORIZES THE MAYOR TO IMPLEMENT AND ENFORCE AN EMPLOYEE RECALL PROCESS IF NEEDED Councilperson Pacheco Seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Public works director Heriberto Cabrera addressed the Council and explained that although the directors and assistant directors have been instructed to go into a rotation schedule, allowing the rest of the staff to work all at once puts them are at risk of someone getting infected and having to quarantine the whole crew.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion to amend the previous action taken on this matter. Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion and the decision to amend the previous motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Public works director Heriberto Cabrera addressed the Council and explained that although the directors and assistant directors have been instructed to go into a rotation schedule, allowing the rest of the staff to work all at once puts them are at risk of someone getting infected and having to quarantine the whole crew. If that were to happen, director Cabrera further explained, that at that point the assistant director Camilo Martin and himself could not perform the duties of their department and Public Works would not be able to operate. He suggested for his department as well as the Utilities department to also follow the rotation schedule so they may dispatch their crew members on a weekly rotation basis allowing for backup in case one crew becomes exposed and that way minimizing the chances of closing their departments. Director Soto confirmed that those employees on rotation would also be subject to the on-call process. Because a previous motion was unanimously carried to only include directors and assistant directors for the rotation schedule, Mayor Martell made a motion to amend the previous action taken on this matter. Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion and the decision to amend the previous motion was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Councilperson DiGiacomo then placed a motion to amend the previous motion as follows: TO CREATE AND IMPLEMENT A ROTATION SCHEDULE EFFECTIVE MARCH 16, 2020 FOR ALL DEPARTMENTS INCLUDING DIRECTORS, ASSISTANT DIRECTORS AND STAFF CONSIDERATING EACH OF THEIR DEPARTMENT NEEDS Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: Assistant finance director Isabel Hughes approached the podium and requested all department heads to properly document and note each employee s timesheets especially if employees are part of rotation schedules so that all actions are documented and accounted for. Councilperson DiGiacomo explained her concerns with the meal program especially if an employee gets sick when preparing the food for our elderly residents. Meal Program director Fatima Fuentes agreed on putting her staff on rotation but will need The Town to send notification to the recipients of the meal program that deliveries may occur later than the usual time. The Mayor then state that he would like all department heads to evaluate their operations and to submit their rotation schedules to the human resources and assistant finance director. Lh ee Discussion on the operations of the facilities was then held as Councilperson DiGiacomo asked the Mayor whether the Town would keep the Lakeside Retirement Recreational Center open in the evenings. Her concern was that although the Town has cancelled the events at the facility, seniors could continue to gather in the evenings to play dominoes putting themselves and others at risk. Councilperson Stefano asked is there was a way to limit visitation to the Rec Center, Director Fuentes suggested closing the facility once the meal program has finished its operations for the day. Councilperson Pacheco stated that the residents take precautionary measures by sanitizing their hands when entering, but Councilperson Stefano expressed that the issue to resolve is whether the Town should be limiting outside visitation. The Mayor stated that he would like notification sent out to the residents advising them that no visitors will be permitting at the facilities. The Mayor and Council then decided to keep the Lakeside Retirement Recreational Center, Tobie Wilson Park and the Danny Meehan Recreational field including the residential gym open to all residents but will not allow visitors to enter facilities until further notice. The Mayor then directed the human resources director Olga Quin to distribute a memorandum to all department heads so that staff is aware of the decision made at the special meeting. segs.head: Ordinance C-443 of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida Approving and Adopting a New Employee Handbook; Providing for Implementation; Providing for Severability; Providing for Repealer of Ordinances, Resolutions and Policies Inconsistent with the Employee Handbook; and Providing for an Effective Date.
segs.text: Ordinance C-443 of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida Approving and Adopting a New Employee Handbook; Providing for Implementation; Providing for Severability; Providing for Repealer of Ordinances, Resolutions and Policies Inconsistent with the Employee Handbook; and Providing for an Effective Date. Councilperson DiGiacomo initiated the discussion in the matter stating that in September 2019 she brought before Council and was approved to change the holiday leave for part time employees to be the amount of hours scheduled to work on that day off requested but when reviewing the new proposed employee handbook she found that on page 69 where the section addressing the part-time employee s leave benefits is located, the language did not reflect the approved benefit. In addition, Councilperson DiGiacomo stated the approved change of September 2019 may not had included all time off/leave benefits like bereavement. Therefore, Councilperson DiGiacomo proposed to extend the same hour coverage benefit to all other leave benefits for part-time employees that may had not been included then in the new proposed employee handbook. The comment was noted, and staff was instructed to review the language in question and make the necessary revisions for final approval at the second reading of the Ordinance. Without further comments or questions, Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion to adopt

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Proposal from Intertek-PSI for Roof Condition Survey and Exterior Wall Thermography Services for the Town of Medley Municipal Services Facility (MMSF). Richard McConachie, Building and Zoning Director, approached the podium to explain the scope of work, pricing and other details associated with the proposal. He further explained that the proposal included an assessment of the roof of the Medley Municipal Services Facility (MMSF). Councilperson DiGiacomo expressed the need to include the need for a general assessment of the entire MMSF facility in the scope of work. Building and zoning director McConachie stated that if a general assessment was added to the scope of the work of the agreement, the amount would then change to reflect the addition of the work requested. Mayor Martell agreed with the comment made by Councilperson DiGiacomo and agreed to expand the scope of work to include a general assessment of the MMSF. Town Attorney Arango requested for the Mayor and Council to instruct her to review and revise attached agreement as needed and to add standard legal language requiring insurance. Finance Director asked if the three-quote protocol was necessary, whereas the Mayor responded advising that this was being treated as an emergency situation because of the increase of water damage to the building and the Council agreed to waive the three-quote requirement as stipulated by the Town s procurement policy . Without further discussion Mayor Martell made a motion as follows, TO WAIVE THE REQUIREMENTS UNDER THE TOWN S PROCUREMENT ORDINANCE AND APPROVING PROPOSAL FROM INTERTEK-PSI FOR ROOF CONDITION SURVEY AND EXTERIOR WALL THERMOGRAPHY SERVICES FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY MUNICIPAL SERVICES FACILITY (MMSF). Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on Mayor Martell s Proposal to Increase Compensation to the Musicians of the Music Night Event.
votes: Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion as follows: APPROVING AN INCREASE OF $30.00 PER MUSICIAN PER MUSIC NIGHT EVENT AND CONTRACTING MIREYA RIVERO AT A RATE OF $83.00 PER MUSIC NIGHT EVENT Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Mayor Martell s Proposal to Increase Compensation to the Musicians of the Music Night Event. Mayor Martell called Director Danziger to the podium to obtain information on the current salary of the musicians. The Mayor explained his proposal to increase by $30.00 per Musician per music event. Councilperson Stefano explained that there are members of Lakeside who do take part in the practices and play a big hand in the event itself. Councilperson DiGiacomo stated that resident Mireya does not even receive any compensation, and both councilperson DiGiacomo and Stefano stated that she should be included as an employee and receive a compensation as well as the increase being proposed. Social Services Director Lizmari Valido stated that each musician is afforded $53.00 dollars per person per night and adding $30.00 would make their new salary $83.00 per night. Mayor Martell agreed and stated that he would like this amount to be applied to the proposed new employee Lakeside resident Mireya Rivero as well. Mireya Rivero approached the podium to thank the Mayor and Council. Ms. Valido addressed the Council to confirm if the Town would still apply the previous practice where when a musician is absent from an event and the remaining employees split that employee s salary amongst them equally. The Council agreed that the practice shall remain in place. Musician Orlando Hurtado also addressed the Council to give his gratitude for the Council s action. Without further discussion Councilperson DiGiacomo made a motion as follows: APPROVING AN INCREASE OF $30.00 PER MUSICIAN PER MUSIC NIGHT EVENT AND CONTRACTING MIREYA RIVERO AT A RATE OF $83.00 PER MUSIC NIGHT EVENT Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Add-On Item # 1- Discussion and Action on Councilperson Pacheco s Proposal regarding Senior Resident Birthday Parties. The Mayor addressed Councilperson Pacheco for him to initiate discussion on his proposed agenda item regarding Senior Residential Birthday parties. Councilperson Pacheco explained that the Town had the prior practice of holding a monthly birthday event for all residents and although his item stated senior residents he would like to propose to bring back the birthday events to celebrate and include all residents in general. He further explained his concern of the attendance of non-residents and questioned whether the Town will continue to impose a fee for non-residents attending the event. He suggested to hold the birthday celebrations in the middle of every month so it would not conflict with the current monthly dominoes event. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked if all residents will be invited and would like to know where the proposed location for the event will be. Councilperson Pacheco confirmed that the event would include all residents and the event would alternate on a month to month basis between Tobie Wilson Park and the Lakeside Recreational Center. Councilperson DiGiacomo explained that the Town previously suspended celebrating the children s birthday parties at those locations because there were larger amounts of non-residential adults attending so the Town changed the celebration to take place within the Afterschool Program to celebrate only the residential children s birthdays. Mayor Martell asked about the type of music and meals being proposed to be served at these events, and what time will the events be held. After a brief discussion councilperson Pacheco stated that the food can be whatever the Council proposes and he foresees an estimated attendance of no more than 100 residents at the first event, and would like for the event to take place Saturdays from 3 pm 7 pm. Councilperson Pacheco also addressed Town transportation and stated that as long as he is available he would be willing to transport residents to the events, but would like for Town transportation to be assigned in the event that he may not be available to do so. The Mayor agreed to provide transportation. segs.head: Mayor Martell then read into the record Town of Medley new business item B as follows, - Discussion and Action On Future Operations Of The Medley Municipal Services Facility (MMSF) During The Remaining Of The Coronavirus State Of Emergency.
segs.text: Mayor Martell then read into the record Town of Medley new business item B as follows, - Discussion and Action On Future Operations Of The Medley Municipal Services Facility (MMSF) During The Remaining Of The Coronavirus State Of Emergency. Mayor Martell opened the item for discussion addressing Councilperson DiGiacomo to initiate the discussion as the item was requested by her. Councilperson DiGiacomo clarified her intention in requesting the discussion of the topic and stated that the closure of the Town hall and operations was not her intention. However, she did believe that it was time to take additional measures for the safety of the Town, staff, and visitors. Councilperson DiGiacomo informed the Mayor and Council of the recent occurrence at Miami-Dade County where several of their Building and Zoning inspectors tested positive for virus causing them to close all operations. Furthermore, she expressed a concern about contracted personnel coming into the facility for both Building and Zoning and Code Compliance departments after working in other municipalities. Mayor Martell then explained that he had already discussed with the Building and Zoning Director Richard McConachie and stated that director McConachie had a course of action ready to be implemented so that operations may continue. Mayor Martell also voiced his concern for the wellbeing of his staff and informed the Council that he is authorizing sick personnel to stay home in an attempt to keep everyone in the facility healthy and safe, and gave his gratitude to Councilperson DiGiacomo for addressing this issue with the rest of the Council. Mayor Martell was in accordance to close the MMSF to the public and placing a drop box outside of the entrance so that customers may drop off items for business of any department, a water payment drop off box is already located outside of the building. Mayor Martell then addressed Councilperson Stefano welcoming her to express her opinion and address any concerns she may have on the matter. Councilperson Stefano then addressed Town Attorney Lillian Arango asking if the Town will receive funding to compensate for employee salaries as part of the stimulus legislation passed by Congress. The Mayor stated no. Continuing with the topic, Director McConachie asked the Mayor and Council for his staff members to come in on Friday to settle their departmental needs so that the new procedures were followed beginning that Monday. The Mayor approved his request. Social S
