Chief Said- Jinete explained that the Police Department had already taken these measures and ordered the work permits, thus she will share the information with both director Quin and town clerk Martinez. Since there was no further discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and the meeting was adjourned at 6:02 pm on March 26, 2020.

segs.head: Ordinance C-444 of The Town of Medley, Florida, Amending Chapter 62 Zoning By Amending Section 62-44 (A) And (C) Fences or Walls To Change the Maximum Allowable Height of Fences and Walls; Providing for Severability; And Providing for An Effective Date.
segs.text: Ordinance C-444 of The Town of Medley, Florida, Amending Chapter 62 Zoning By Amending Section 62-44 (A) And (C) Fences or Walls To Change the Maximum Allowable Height of Fences and Walls; Providing for Severability; And Providing for An Effective Date. Mayor Martell then opened the public comment for the second reading of Ordinance C-444 to which no comments were made nor received by the Town Clerk. Director of Building and Zoning Richard McConachie addressed Councilperson Stefano s concern about the height language and informed her that he had reviewed the Miami-Dade County Ordinance 33-11 that addressed Fences and Walls and found that verbiage for this Ordinance was found in compliance with the County s regulations. Without further discussion, Councilwoman DiGiacomo made a motion to adopt

segs.head: Ordinance C-444, Vice Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Ordinance C-444, Vice Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Next for discussion and/or approval was the Resolution item as reflected on the agenda. It was read into the record and carried as follows:

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on Councilperson DiGiacomo s Request to Revise Social Services Benefits for Town of Medley Senior Citizens.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion as follows, TO AMEND THE HOTMEALS PROGRAM QUALIFICATION AGE TO 60 YEARS OLD OR ABOVE. THE REMAINING SOCIAL SERVICES PROGRAMS ARE TO STAY THE SAME. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Councilperson DiGiacomo s Request to Revise Social Services Benefits for Town of Medley Senior Citizens. Councilwoman DiGiacomo initiated the discussion to explain that many residents have contacted her because they were unaware that the eligible age to participate in the hot meal program had changed. Councilperson DiGiacomo stated that she had the understanding that the change adopted previously grandfathered residents that had already been living in Medley but were not of age yet into the initial age of the program which was 55 years of age or older, and could apply once they reached 55, but the existing program criteria only accepts new applications starting at the age of 65 years or older. Councilwoman DiGiacomo stated that she has spoken to the Meal Program Director Fatima Fuentes and after reviewing the documentation provided by both the Social Services and the Finance Department they agreed that two additional employees were not necessary at the moment and although they might be short staffed the meal program can still accommodate for the additional meals that may be approved by Councilwoman s proposal to lower the age requirement for the meal program. A discussion was held on how many additional meals and supplies may be required. Vice Mayor Ayala expressed how he is not in agreement with the proposal and how he opposed to the provider being Latin American Grill. Vice Mayor also stated that residents often discard the meals and he does not agree with increasing the number of meals distributed given that he believes that people are unrightfully giving away the meals provided to them which was not the intent of the program. Vice Mayor apologized to the hot meal program personnel but ultimately, he believes it is a waste of food and it is an unfair use of the Town of Medley benefits. Councilwoman DiGiacomo appreciates Vice Mayors feedback but disagreed with his comments of the use of the program s meals. Councilwoman Stefano joined the discussion and suggested changing the qualification age to 60 years of age and older. Councilperson Pacheco also commented and did not agree with the timing of the request. Director Fuentes stated that her job is to serve the residents who apply and qualify for the program. Councilwoman DiGiacomo further clarified that although Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that the Town is acting wrongly providing these meals she disagrees and believes that there is hardship amongst the residents whom are at home a

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on Councilperson DiGiacomo s Proposal to add Two (2) More Days for a Total of Five (5) Days to the Part-Time Employees Bereavement Leave Benefit.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion as follows, TO INCREASE THE PART-TIME EMPLOYEE BEREAVEMENT LEAVE BENEFIT TO A TOTAL OF FIVE (5) DAYS. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Councilperson DiGiacomo s Proposal to add Two (2) More Days for a Total of Five (5) Days to the Part-Time Employees Bereavement Leave Benefit. Councilwoman DiGiacomo explained that the practice of applying (5) days Bereavement Leave for part time employees has already been in place but has not been approved by Council. Therefore, the proposal is to formally approve the practice. Without questions or further discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion as follows, TO INCREASE THE PART-TIME EMPLOYEE BEREAVEMENT LEAVE BENEFIT TO A TOTAL OF FIVE (5) DAYS. Councilperson DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. In continuance, the following item was addressed.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Approval of Job Descriptions for Several Department Directors.

Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Approval of Job Descriptions for Several Department Directors. Human resources director Olga Quin briefly explained that the Town is working on completing job descriptions for exempt employees as well employees who may not be on salary but do not fall under the union umbrella. At this time, the job description brought forward for Council approval include the Town Clerk, Assistant Town Clerk, Human Resources Director, and Social Services Director. Director Quin informed the Mayor and Council that several other descriptions will follow every month until they are all approved. After a brief discussion Councilwoman Digiacomo made a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE JOB DESCRIPTIONS AS PRESENTED FOR THE POSITIONS OF TOWN CLERK, ASSISTANT TOWN CLERK, HUMAN RESOURCES DIRECTOR AND SOCIAL SERVICES AND PARKS AND RECREATIONS DIRECTOR. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on Mayor Martell s Proposal to Mandate Facial Coverings in the Community.
votes: Councilwoman DiGiacomo made a motion as follows, TO ISSUE AN EMERGENCY ORDER MANDATING FACIAL COVERINGS OUTSIDE THE BOUNDARIES OF A PERSON S PROPERTY AS WELL AS ALL TOWN OF MEDLEY PUBLIC FACILITIES. ENFORCEMENTS MAY BE IMPOSED IN THE FORM OF WARNINGS AND TO ADHERE TO MIAMI DADE COUNTY S EXEMPTIONS FOR FACIAL COVERINGS Councilwoman Stefano seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Mayor Martell s Proposal to Mandate Facial Coverings in the Community. The Mayor began by addressing the Council for their input on the matter. Vice-Mayor Ayala and the rest of the Council were in agreement with the Mayor s proposal to impose facial coverings in the community. Mayor Martell further explained that Miami-Dade County Emergency Order 19- 20 encourages persons outside their home to wear face masks and the other Miami-Dade County Emergency Order 20-20 makes it mandatory within the description in the order. Town Attorney Lillian Arango explained that the Town has the right to enforce as they deem necessary. Councilwoman DiGiacomo asked if the Town can empower the Police Department to enforce this order. Town Attorney Arango stated that the Town may issue an emergency order which would allow for enforcement and consequences for failure to adhere to the order. She continued to explain that the county also included exemptions to these orders such as for children two years of age and younger and individuals with respiratory medical conditions. Ms. Arango explained to the Chief of Police Said-Jinete that the Police Department may enforce face masks in residential areas even if private property, and the Town may also include additional restrictions to include the requirement of facial masks at Town of Medley public facilities. It was discussed that a warning would be a sufficient form of enforcement by the Police Department to the public. Without questions or further discussion, Councilwoman DiGiacomo made a motion as follows, TO ISSUE AN EMERGENCY ORDER MANDATING FACIAL COVERINGS OUTSIDE THE BOUNDARIES OF A PERSON S PROPERTY AS WELL AS ALL TOWN OF MEDLEY PUBLIC FACILITIES. ENFORCEMENTS MAY BE IMPOSED IN THE FORM OF WARNINGS AND TO ADHERE TO MIAMI DADE COUNTY S EXEMPTIONS FOR FACIAL COVERINGS Councilwoman Stefano seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Since there was no further business to discuss Councilwoman Stefano made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Councilwoman DiGiacomo seconded the motion and the meeting was adjourned at 8:22 pm on May 4, 2020. Victoria artinez, F ae C, Town Clerk i da acti

segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA NOVEMBER 30, 2020 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on November 30, 2020 at 5:15 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA NOVEMBER 30, 2020 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on November 30, 2020 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA YESENIA MARTINEZ TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and The Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited. In continuance, a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda was placed by Vice Mayor Pacheco, seconded by Mayor Martell and carried unanimously.

segs.head: The Mayor continued by addressing Town s special legal counsel Tony Recio who began by announcing and explaining the two intents for the meeting.
segs.text: The Mayor continued by addressing Town s special legal counsel Tony Recio who began by announcing and explaining the two intents for the meeting. Mr. Recio further explained that the Town is to consider both items on the agenda which are in connection with the development of the property located at 7400 NW 79" Avenue as a last-mile logistics and retail distribution center for probably the biggest and most recognized online retailer in the world, Amazon. In addition, Mr. Recio explained that said facility has been designated as a contaminated site also known as a Brownfield Area. Thus, the approval of the first item would allow for incentives that will not cost the Town anything but will allow funds to be made available to the developers so they may rehabilitate the site in question. Town special counsel Recio continued to explain that the second item is to consider amending the Town s code to allow for the specific use of a last-mile logistics and retail distribution and because there is no current use in the Town s zoning code that allows that specific use, staff, and legal counsel have put together the proposed Ordinance to provide for that use in that zoning area. Furthermore, the Ordinance at the same time requires a very thorough review by staff of traffic and operations through the site plan approval process which would allow the development of the land with the intent of developing an Amazon logistics facility. Mayor Martell then opened the public comment section of the meeting to which no comments were made. In continuance with the agenda, Mayor Martell instructed Town Attorney Lillian Arango to address the resolution reflected on the quasi-judicial public hearing section of the agenda. It was then read into the record as follows: -

segs.head: Resolution C-1866 A Resolution of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida; Providing Findings; Designating a Brownfield Area Within the Town for Real Property Located At 7400 NW 79" Avenue, Medley, Florida, as Depicted On Exhibit A and Legally Described on Exhibit B , for the Purposes of Environmental Rehabilitation, Job Creation, And Economic Development; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Implement this Resolution; Providing for Severability; and Providing for an Effective Date.
segs.text: Resolution C-1866 A Resolution of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida; Providing Findings; Designating a Brownfield Area Within the Town for Real Property Located At 7400 NW 79" Avenue, Medley, Florida, as Depicted On Exhibit A and Legally Described on Exhibit B , for the Purposes of Environmental Rehabilitation, Job Creation, And Economic Development; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Implement this Resolution; Providing for Severability; and Providing for an Effective Date. Mr. Recio reiterated what he had previously explained and addressed the exhibits as provided so the Mayor and Council can understand how the applicant has agreed to meet the five criteria necessary to move forward with the designation of a Brownfield area. Mayor Martell then opened the public comment section of the meeting to which no comments were made. Councilperson Edgar Ayala then asked what agency oversees assigning this area as a Brownfield area, where the Mayor responded that the Department of Economic Resources Management (DERM) has identified and established the land as a brownfield area since it was noted that the site was a former landfill and had been contaminated. Mr. Brett Brumund with the Goldstein Environmental Law Firm, 2100 Ponce de Leon Blvd, Coral Gables, FL 33134, approached the podium and explained how there are state based incentives that allows for reimbursement for the rehabilitation of the site. He also explained that through the proposed redevelopment there will be economic productivity to the area creating many job opportunities. Mr. Brumund continued to explain some of the requirements involved in the redeveloping of the land including DERM presence and involvement throughout the entire process. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo also approached the Council and explained how Town staff had met and felt that the proposal has merit and the Town can continue with a study for a transit oriented district, but also contemplate the approval of this site as proposed. In addition, and for clarification purposes, Councilperson Edgar Ayala further inquired as to why the responsibility of designating the land would fall on the Mayor and Town Council. The Mayor responded and explained that although DERM has already determined the land is contaminated, the Town also needs to designate the land as a Brownfield area in order to allow the developer to have access to available grants and incentives associated with the cleanup and the rehabilitation of the site. segs.text: Ordinance C-447 An Ordinance of the Town Of Medley, Florida, Amending Chapter 62 Zoning by Amending Article III District Regulations , Section 62- 88(A), to Amend Regulations for Permitted Uses Within The M-1 Zoning District to Allow Last-Mile Logistics and Retail Distribution as a Permitted Use; Providing for Conflicts; Providing for Severability and Providing for an Effective Date. Mr. Recio once again explained that the proposed Ordinance is for the development of an Amazon logistics facility and it will be used as the last part of the distribution chain which will allow items to be shipped out directly from this facility to homes and businesses. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion to adopt Ordinance C-447 Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Group Medical Insurance with Cigna effective January 1, 2021. The Town insurance representative Robert Reynolds from Morris and Reynolds began the discussion on this matter by explaining that his firm had been in negotiations with Cigna and their initial proposal included a 10% increase for the current plan. However, after continued negotiations he was pleased to announce that Cigna s has now made an offer of a 3% increase for the current same exact plan and have agreed to apply a surplus through the month of July and apply it to the 2021 premium as a credit to be applied in April 2021. He continued to explain that the Town currently offers an in-network plan but there have been several employees that have inquired with Human Resources about the possibility of a point of service plan. Mr. Reynolds continued to explain that this plan would allow employees to take part in this new plan and pay the difference so they can continue to visit the physicians they have even if they are out of network. The Town would pay for the in-network plan and the employee would pay the cost differential. Mr. Reynolds then advised to renew the current Cigna in Network Plan and suggested adding a point of service plan. He further stated that the cost difference for the inclusion of the point of service plan was minimal and if the Town chooses, may be placed in the responsibility of the employee and choose the plan with the smaller deductible option. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO RENEW THE CURRENT TOWN OF MEDLEY GROUP MEDICAL INSURANCE PLAN WITH CIGNA, EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2021 AND TO INCLUDE AND EXTEND A POINT OF SERVICE PLAN AS AN OPTION FOR EMPLOYEES Councilwoman DiGiacomo seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously. Mr. Reynolds continued to discuss and explained that his firm has compared Allstate rates and benefits for the additional policies and coverages provided by the Town and would suggest changing the provider to Colonial Life. Employees will be given the option to remain with Allstate, but they will not longer be deducted through payroll and will be responsible to pay their own dues if not chosen to transfer to the new provider. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO CHANGE THE BENEFITS PROVIDED BY ALLSTATE TO THE COLONIAL LIFE PLAN Vice Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA APRIL 14, 2021 COUNCIL WORKSHOP A Special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on April 14, 2021 at 2:00 pm. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Mayor began his discussion by addressing Mr. Christian Infante and Mr. Alexander Carulo both representing SFM Security Services Inc. (SFM) located at 9700 NW 79 Avenue, Hialeah Gardens, Florida 33016 who presented a new hiring process that would be implemented moving forward for the security post located at the Town of Medley Lakeside Retirement Park. Mr. Infante stated when SFM was initially retained, all security officers were, as requested by the Town, Medley residents. However, with time vacancies had occurred and it was difficult to maintain an all-Medley resident post as the Town preferred. In addition, Mr. Infante explained that although SFM has tried to keep the Medley resident preference, vacancies needed to be filled and thus positions were filled along the way with interested and qualified applicants. Nonetheless, a new hire policy (attached) was presented to the Town Council and was said to be in place for any vacancies at the post moving forward. Mr. Infante distributed along with the proposed policy a draft of a Job Posting (attached) that reflected a summary of the position description to show the Town Council how both, the Town, and the post, will be notified of any future job availability. Furthermore, it was confirmed that said job availability would be open to Medley residents and posted on the site for seven (7) days before any vacancies are afforded and opened to non-Medley residents. A consensus to the new hiring policy and notification steps was had. The discussion was then moved to the review of the contract for services as previously instructed. Town attorney Lillian Arango clarified the directives of the Town council during the March 18, 2021 special council meeting and the directives to amend the existing and current contract was confirmed. votes: Vice Mayor Pacheco placed a motion as follows, TO AMEND THE TOWN OF MEDLEY GENERAL PENSION PLAN TO ALLOW ALL FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES TO RECEIVE ALL PENSION CREDIT INCLUDING WHILE ON SHORT TERM DISABILITY BENEFIT, AND TO CREDIT BACK PENSION DUES TO ALL FULL TIME EMPLOYEES WHO HAVE TAKEN SHORT TERM DISABILITY BENEFITS IN THE PAST Councilwoman Stefano seconded, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Pension Benefits for Employees While on Short-Term Disability. Finance Director Roy Danziger explained that the Town s general pension plan currently reads that full-time employees who have received short term disability within a year for reasons such as maternity leave and/or other eligible medical reasons are not currently eligible for a full year of pension benefit for said year, thus they do not receive pensionable credit for the time they are on said leave. However, director Danziger stated that it was his understanding that said practice may not be the intention of the Council. Town s Pension Attorney Pedro Herrera further explained the details as the plan currently mandates which confirmed the information previously stated by director Danziger. In addition, director Danziger further recommended to the Town Council to amend the plan to allow for the employees to receive their full pension benefits although they may receive short term disability benefits. Without further discussion on the matter, Vice Mayor Pacheco placed a motion as follows, TO AMEND THE TOWN OF MEDLEY GENERAL PENSION PLAN TO ALLOW ALL FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES TO RECEIVE ALL PENSION CREDIT INCLUDING WHILE ON SHORT TERM DISABILITY BENEFIT, AND TO CREDIT BACK PENSION DUES TO ALL FULL TIME EMPLOYEES WHO HAVE TAKEN SHORT TERM DISABILITY BENEFITS IN THE PAST Councilwoman Stefano seconded, and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion on Town of Medley Employee Salaries and Pension Benefits.
segs.text: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion on Town of Medley Employee Salaries and Pension Benefits. Director Danziger began his discussion by clarifying that there are approximately (43) Forty-Three employees that have worked part time and after some time, were transitioned to full time status. Councilwoman Ayala explained that she wanted to work on this matter and be provided with the information as to how many employees have gone from part time to full time status but also to have the information as to how much time each employee spent with a part time employment status. After a brief explanation Mr. Danziger was instructed to provide Councilwoman Ayala with calculations as to how much pension benefit current part time employees are entitled to based on the years of service under the Town s general pension plan. Also, Councilwoman Ayala stated that she would like to know if it is possible to apply years of part time service to an employee s pensionable years of service. Pedro Herrera, pension attorney for the Ton of Medley General Pension Plan clarified that amendments as approved by the Town Council can be done, but there will be a financial impact for the Town. Councilwoman Stefano then instructed Roy to provide a list of all part time employees and the cost to increase their pension benefit. Mr. Danziger was also instructed to have an actuary study to determine the cost of giving employees who have gone from part time to full time status pensionable credit. A motion was placed by Councilwoman Ayala as follows, TO CONDUCT AN ACTUARY STUDY AND PROVIDE THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL COSTS TO APPLY PENSIONABLE CREDIT TO EMPLOYEES WHO HAVE GONE FROM PART TIME TO FULL TIME EMPLOYMENT STATUS. IN ADDITION, TO PROVIDE A LIST OF ALL PART TIME EMPLOYEES INCLUSIVE OF THEIR YEARS OF SERVICE AND THE COST TO INCREASE THEIR PENSION BENEFIT Councilperson Ayala seconded, and it carried unanimously. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Investigative Report Prepared by Emplar Consultants LLC on the Gender Discrimination and Retaliation Allegations filed by Lizmari Valido Regarding Councilperson Edgar Ayala. Sharon P. Kelley from Emplar Consultants LLC located at 19571 Havensway Court, Boca Raton, Florida 33498 approached the podium and addressed any comments or concerns from the Town Council and explained the recommendations as reflected on the report. Ms. Kelly further stated that the basis of her investigation was to conclude whether the concerns brought up by Director Valido violated the statute, whether or not they were outside her protected status and ultimately a violation of the law. Therefore, the recommendations as listed on the report were merely a good starting point, for both, the Council and employees, to learn what the duties and responsibilities are but could be expanded to include any other recommendations the Town Attorneys may find beneficial. Councilwoman Stefano expressed her agreement with the outcome and findings reflected on the report. Councilperson Ayala thanked Ms. Kelly for conducting the investigation and took a moment to express that although he was unfairly accused, he understood that being a councilperson would place him in such positions. Councilperson Ayala further stated that he looked forward to moving on and starting over, therefore he agreed with the findings of the investigation. Councilwoman Ayala commented that their jobs as elected officials included, at times, questions as Councilmembers have a job to do which is to do what is best for the community. Town Attorney Lillian Arango advised the Town Council of a fifteen (15) day period from the day the report was delivered to the Town council for both parties to submit responses. If responses are received, Ms. Kelly would then address said comments and a final report would then come back to Council with a final report incorporating said submitted responses and final comments. Without further discussion on the matter, Councilperson Ayala made a motion as follows: TO ACCEPT THE INVESTIGATIVE REPORT, FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS SUBMITTED BY EMPLAR CONSULTANTS, LLC Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously. segs.text: - Resolution Approving Amendment to the Public Transportation Grant Agreement Between the State of Florida, Department of Transportation, and the Town of Medley for the Town of Medley Central Commuter Route. Jorge Corzo Director of the CPED department approached the podium and explained that the Town of Medley Central Commuter Route program has yet been implemented due to the Covid-19 pandemic. He continued to explain that the services proposed have been modified and are now similar to how Uber operates which can be considered a user-friendly mode of transportation within the Town. The Town would contract a vendor that Miami Dade County Transit uses, and they then provide the service. Riders could access the service through an app that will be at no cost to the individual for said transportation within the Town. Although the original contract had been previously executed, it was clarified that the Town has not made any payments and no payments will be made until services are rendered. segs.text: MINUTES OF A MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA AUGUST 23, 2021, COUNCIL WORKSHOP A public meeting of the Town Council was called to order on August 23, 2021, at 3:00 pm. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ Town Clerk Victoria Martinez opened the public meeting and read into the record the item of business which was the discussion on the Town of Medley Hot meal Program. Renier Gonzalez from Latin America Grill approached the Town Council and explained how there is a nationwide inflation of prices and in the thirteen years he has worked for the Town, Latin America has never requested a price increase. However, because the cost of products has skyrocketed and the cost of doing business has increased exponentially,he would like to request an increase from the current cost of$5.05 a meal to $7.95 a meal. Councilwoman Stefano expressed how steep the increase requested is and Mr. Gonzalez began to detail the difference of prices from 2019 to present of some of the necessary supplies which have increased in price by double and some even triple their initial cost. Councilwoman Stefano emphasized that quality is what is most important to her, and it is important for Latin America to stay on top of market quality with awareness that some choices may not appease everyone. Mrs. Stefano continued to commend Latin America and the service being provided and understood that the market is not allowing for much negotiation on the price increase proposal, nonetheless she would like the Town to have an opportunity to renegotiate the extent of the increase if there is a drop in market prices. Councilperson Ayala also understood the reasons of the increase but reiterated that the $2.90 increase per meal is an aggressive proposal that will cost the Town an additional $300,000.00 a year on the meal program. Councilperson Ayala and the Mayor both request a lower offer. Mr. Gonzalez stated that he would have a counteroffer if in the past there have been requests for increases, but thirteen years have passed without any requests and in that time, the cost of living has increased, the cost of doing business has increased, and the cost of products has skyrocketed due to the market inflation. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Salary Study and Gender Analysis for the Town of Medley Prepared by Evergreen Solutions, LLC. Special Labor Counsel Lyndsey Rider approached the Council and gave a brief introduction of the services performed by Nancy Berkley with Evergreen Solutions, LLC located at 2878 Remington Green Circle Tallahassee, Florida 32308. It was also stated that services provided by Evergreen Solutions, LLC had been requested and approved by Council to conduct a salary survey and gender analysis in response to anonymous complaints of pay inequality between male and female department directors received in 2020. Nancy Berkley addressed the Town Council and discussed a power point presentation that included a report of the study process, positions reviewed, current conditions, classification review, equity review, compensation review, identified proposed pay ranges and slotting and salary adjustment implementation. Ms. Berkely further explained that the process included collection of the data the Town provided which included position descriptions and employee data files along with Town s pay practices. In addition, it was also explained that clear definitions of the job duties and minimum qualifications specifically were asked from the Town since they were not immediately identified when data was received the first time. Tenure, qualifications, and related experience information for each incumbent was also requested as well as any other qualifications and/or related experience incumbents processed beyond the minimum qualifications. Once updated position descriptions and incumbents qualifications were reviewed, the incumbents qualifications specifically regarding the minimum qualification specified in the position descriptions were analyzed. Ms. Berkley further stated that a gender equity analysis was conducted as well as an external analysis by surveying peer organizations to determine salary ranges for the same types of positions. Thus, based on the data provided, recommended pay ranges were provided for the identified 19 reviewed positions. It was stated that it was determined that a clear practice or formal pay plan for determining salaries as well as defined job description and minimum qualifications for the positions was not had and that until the day, she had no confidence that the job descriptions were well defined. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of an Interim and Successor Building Official for the Town of Medley Building and Zoning Department. Building and Zoning Director Richard McConachie approached the Council and informed them that as previously informed, he will be retiring effective December 31, 2021. Therefore, and taking into consideration the qualifications and experience he recommended William Guillermo Diaz to undertake the duties and responsibilities of the Director of Building and Zoning/Building Official. Director McConachie further stated that Mr. Diaz has helped oversee the Town s permitting and violation process as well as has worked with the staff to improve all aspects of the department for the past 8 years. In addition, director McConachie stated that it was proposed for Mr. Diaz to begin in an interim status effective October 1, 2021 and in full capacity effective January 1, 2022 having full authority of the operations in his absence. Director McConachie thanked the Town and all the staff for all the years shared. Vice-Mayor Pacheco then asked about the base salary that would be assigned to Mr. Diaz considering the Town s recently provided compensation study information to which the Mayor responded that the salary had already been discussed and agreed upon. Therefore, it was stated the annual salary would be $125,000 a year which was the starting salary previously assigned to the prior Building and Zoning/Building Official. Director McConachie also stated that the salary assigned will not be part of the Town s general funds since the building department operates from an enterprise account and thus, all departmental expenses are managed as such. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion as follows, TO APPOINT WILLIAM GUILLERMO DIAZ AS THE DIRECTOR OF BUILDING AND ZONING DEPARTMENT /BUILDING OFFICIAL POSITION IN AN INTERIM BASIS EFFECTIVE OCTOBER 1, 2021 AND APPOINTED IN FULL CAPACITY EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2022 HAVING FULL AUTHORITY OF THE DEPARTMENT IN THE ABSENCE OF FORMER DIRECTOR MACCONACHIE UNTIL FULL CAPACITY TAKES PLACE Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Interior Improvements of the Multiuse Training Room & Kitchen Renovations of Medley Municipal Services Facility (MMSF).
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Interior Improvements of the Multiuse Training Room & Kitchen Renovations of Medley Municipal Services Facility (MMSF). Capital Improvement and Economic Development director Jorge Corzo approached the podium to address the item and explained that bids were received for the project, and they were higher than expected he would like to re-bid the project including a more direct solicitation process. Mr. Corzo further stated that although the project was initiated as an internal upgrade/repair project he was asked to help since there was an insurance claim involved. In addition, Mr. Corzo explained the historical need on which the project was initiated which included a most robust kitchen to support the Town s Emergency Operations. However, because the needs of the Town for a more robust kitchen, compliance with certain construction codes would be required that included stainless steel appliances, the need for a grease trap amongst others elevating the cost of the project in the process. Mr. Corzo also stated that the increase of building supplies has not helped the overall cost of the bids received for the project. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez reminded the Town Engineer that the space and room in question serves as the designated area for the Miami-Dade County Elections Department and the Town s department elections process. Thus, the Town should keep that in mind in case any long-term construction is considered especially since the area must be in full use condition before the next elections of November 2022 take place. Councilperson Ayala then asked if any other solution could be taken into consideration and asked if perhaps the repairs could be performed by Town personnel. Social Services and Parks and Recreations Director Lizmari Valido remined the Council that the kitchen used to be on the first floor and was moved to the area in question because of the amounts of events that the Town was holding. Thus, it made it easier for the Hot Meal director Fatima Fuentes to supply the events from that room. Building and Zoning director McConachie explained that in order to accommodate the already purchased appliances that included a range and fryer, a more robust approach was needed to meet compliance including electrical and plumbing licensed work. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Request to Waive Early Retirement Penalty for the Town of Medley General Pension Plan.
votes: Councilwoman Stefano made a motion as follows, TO OPEN AN EARLY 90 DAY RETIREMENT WINDOW AND WAIVE THE EARLY RETITREMENT PENALTY FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY GENERAL PENSION PLAN SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF FEDERATION OF PUBLIC EMPLOYEES (FPE) BARGAINIGN UNIT. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Request to Waive Early Retirement Penalty for the Town of Medley General Pension Plan. Finance Director Roy Danziger addressed the item and stated that the Town has in the past applied the same benefit to the police pension plan and has allowed employees to retire early. Thus, he would like to also extend the same to employees who have at least 24 years of full-time service. Mayor Roberto Martell then stated that a 90-day window has been extended to the police department and so he would like to do the same, to be consistent, to participants of the Town s pension plan. Director Danziger then informed the Town Council that if proposal is approved, there would be 2 potential qualifying participants of the general pension plan. Town s special labor counsel Lindsey Ryder joined the discussion and stated that if the Council approved said benefit, it would have to be presented to the FPE barraging unit for consideration and approval since one of the 2 qualifying individuals is a member of the bargaining unit. In addition, special labor Counsel Ryder confirmed that 90-day window is what has been presented to the other bargaining unit in the past. Finance Director Roy Danziger further stated that if approved, the October regular meeting would be the target day to bring back a resolution to formalize the action. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Stefano made a motion as follows, TO OPEN AN EARLY 90 DAY RETIREMENT WINDOW AND WAIVE THE EARLY RETITREMENT PENALTY FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY GENERAL PENSION PLAN SUBJECT TO THE APPROVAL OF FEDERATION OF PUBLIC EMPLOYEES (FPE) BARGAINIGN UNIT. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

Social Services and Parks and Recreations Director Lizmari Valido inquired whether the flexibility of the event s timing was to coordinate for any of the Councilmembers to perform the transportation to the event in question. Councilwoman Stefano confirmed director Valido s question and further stated that in the case of the Arts & Crafts event, the change the timing of the event only would be used to coordinate the transportation of said event being performed by the Council. Director Valido further stated that if in the case of a change, the rest of the Town Council would be consulted to make sure the new time would be agreed upon. Councilwoman Stefano then stated that perhaps every month was not necessary but at least quarterly meetings were appropriate to discuss Town events since there are several events that require planning in advance like the Thanksgiving, Halloween, and Christmas events and since the councilmembers are also allowed to do events on their own. The Council agreed in a consensus manner that quarterly events would best fit the Council after the workshop scheduled for September 7, 2021 takes place. Councilwoman Ayala took the opportunity to clarify and address individual council events since the Council has been allotted an annual amount with the purpose to conduct activities like such. Councilwoman Ayala further stated that as it was previously approved by Council, and as consulted with the Town Attorney, councilmembers have the authority to conduct individual events with initiatives important to them. Thus, she further stated that individual councilmember events are not considered Town events. In addition, director Valido further stated that since the individual event conducted by Councilperson Ayala involved information requested by the after-school program, that she would like to be notified as such especially when staff is involved. segs.text: MINUTES OF A MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA DECEMBER 6, 2021 COUNCIL WORKSHOP A public meeting of the Town Council was called to order on December 6, 2021 at 2:00 pm. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley COVID-19 Emergency Sick Leave.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley COVID-19 Emergency Sick Leave. Mayor Martell referred the presentation of the item to Human Resources Director Olga Quin. Ms. Quin explained how the policy in place, supported by the Cares Act, had expired at the end of 2020. Thus, the Town needed direction on how to process the matter moving forward for 2021. The recommendation was to continue to allow and cover a total of (10) days of sick leave for any employee who has tested positive for COVID-19 and to have employees present a negative PCR test result prior to returning to work. Also, it was presented and recommended to require employees to submit negative PCR test results after traveling outside of the state. However, Council s input and direction is required. Councilwoman Ayala agreed with requiring a negative PCR test result before returning to work as well as a negative PCR test result after having traveled outside of the state of Florida and before returning to work. Mayor Martell and Vice-Mayor Pacheco both agreed to apply the negative test result requirement before returning to work when domestic and/or international travel has occurred. Mayor Martell recommended that the maximum paid sick time be a total of two (2) work weeks, however it would apply to both, full-time and part-time employees work week schedule for only one occurrence of contracting Covid-19 effective January 1, 2021 and until further notice. Without further discussion, Vice Mayor Pacheco placed a motion as follows, EFFECTIVE RETROACTIVE TO JANUARY 1, 2021, THE TOWN WILL PROVIDE A MAXIMUM OF TWO (2) WORK WEEK SCHEDULE OF PAID SICK LEAVE TO ALL FULL TIME OR PART TIME EMPLOYEES AFTER CONTRACTING COVID-19. THIS WILL ONLY BE APPLICABLE FOR ONE

segs.head: (1) OCCURANCE AND EMPLOYEES WILL BE REQUIRED TO PRESENT A NEGATIVE PCR TEST RESULT BEFORE RETURN TO WORK. IN ADDITION, IF AN EMPLOYEE IS TRAVELING OUT OF STATE DOMESTICALLY OR INTERNATIONALLY A NEGATIVE PCR TEST RESULT WILL BE REQUIRED BEFORE RETURN TO WORK.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Allegations of Gender Discrimination Made by Town of Medley Social Services and Parks and Recreation Director Lizmari Valido Against Councilperson Edgar Ayala. Human Resources director Olga Quin approached the Council and explained that at the last council meeting allegations had been made towards an elected official and although the Town has a discrimination policy in place, the involvement of an elected official does not fall within her capacity as a Human Resources Director and equal employment officer of the Town. Director Quin further stated that because of the circumstances of the complaint in question, she would require Council direction to move forward with the allegation and initiate an investigation. Director Quin s recommendation was to allow the authority of the Mayor and herself to hire an outside consultant to conduct the investigation. Councilwoman Ayala before casting her vote, took the opportunity to note on record that she can attest to the character of Councilman Ayala on a personal level and as a colleague. Councilwoman Ayala further stated that she believed in transparency, thus she had confidence in her vote. Councilman Ayala also joined the discussion and took a moment to thank the residents and employees present in support of him and his position on the matter. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion as follows: TO HIRE AN INDEPENDANT CONSULTANT TO CONDUCT AN INVESTIGATION ON THE ALLEGATIONS BROUGHT FORWARD AGAINST COUNCILMAN AYALA AND FOR THE FINDINGS TO COME BACK TO COUNCIL TO PRESENT WHETHER OR NOT THE ALLEGATIONS ARE SUBSTANTIAL . Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously. segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JANUARY 20, 2021 COUNCIL WORKSHOP A Special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on January 20, 2021 at 10:30 am. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA- Joined at 10:44 am LIZELH AYALA TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO LINDSEY RYDER, LABOR COUNSEL The Mayor began his discussion by addressing Human Resources Director Olga Quin who approached the council and began discussion on the matter in question. Director Quin further explained that the CARES Act legislation had sunset on December 31, 2020 and therefore the Town needed to re-evaluate the current COVID-19 practices, including the Return-to-Work Policy moving forward. With that said, current practices were discussed, and options were proposed for the Town Council to consider, including the possibilities of affording quarantine time and amount of paid time off. Special labor counsel Lindsey Rider sated that although federal requirements applicable to the Town were no longer in place, the Town could freely decide and draft a policy if desired. Human Resources director Olga Quin mentioned that surrounding cities like City of Doral, City of Hialeah and Miami Springs do not offer employees a 100 % COVID-19 emergency sick leave benefit. In addition, director Quin stated that in accordance with the Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) guidelines, the recommended time afforded for quarantine was, at this point, a total of seven (7) days and that after ten (10) days with no symptoms an employee could potentially return to work without the need for a negative test result. Thus, one of the issues to consider for a final decision to be made was whether the time off due to COVID-19 and possibly additional time off for quarantine would be paid, if any. It was also discussed that under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), eligible employees could obtain the necessary time to care for themselves and/or certain family members. However, employees under FMLA would be required to use their own accrued time to cover said time off for up to a 12-week period. Furthermore, it was also stated that the FMLA benefit may not be applicable to part-time employees as said eligibility requires 1250 hours during a 12-month period. Special labor counsel Lindsey Rider said she was going to re-distribute the memo that explained the legal aspects,

segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL SITTING AS THE LOCAL PLANNING AGENCY OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JANUARY 7, 2021 5:15 P.M. A special virtual meeting of the Town Council sitting as the Local Planning Agency was called to order on May 4, 2020 at 6:30 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Ayala and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Town Council and audience The Mayor then instructed Town Attorney Lillian Arango to address the item on the agenda. Attorney Arango then announced that the purpose of this meeting was for the Council, sitting as the Local Planning Agency (LPA), to consider and make a recommendation on the following Ordinance which title was read into the record by Town Attorney Arango as follows: AN ORDINANCE OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA, AMENDING CHAPTER 62 ZONING BY AMENDING ARTICLE III DISTRICT REGULATIONS , SECTION 62-88(A), TO AMEND REGULATIONS FOR PERMITTED USES WITHIN THE M-1 ZONING DISTRICT TO ALLOW LAST-MILE LOGISTICS AND RETAIL DISTRIBUTION AS A PERMITTED USE; PROVIDING FOR CONFLICTS; PROVIDING FOR SEVERABILITY AND PROVIDING FOR AN EFFECTIVE DATE. After a short discussion councilperson Ayala made a motion as follows: TO RECOMMEND APPROVAL OF ORDINANCE C-447 AND FIND THAT THIS ORDINANCE IS CONSISTENT WITH THE TOWN S COMPREHENSIVE PLAN. Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

Mayor Martell then opened the public comment section of the meeting where resident from Lakeside Retirement Park Eduardo Sosa approached the podium. After stating that he had a petition signed by several residents and circulating a copy of said petition to every member of the Town Council, it was suggested to the Council to review said petition and have the item included in the February meeting for further discussion and action if so, they wished. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of one (1) Part-Time Social Services Driver Position for the Social Services and Park and Recreations Department. After a brief presentation about the applicants and position requirements, Councilman Ayala addressed director Valido about the hiring process and qualifications taken into consideration for the selection of the proposed candidate. Director Valido expressed her reasons for the selection and recommendation and after a back-and-forth discussion with Councilman Ayala, Director Valido stated the following: T always admired and respected you as an elected official and longtime neighbor but in recent months your actions and behavior have turned my admiration to disappointment. Before and throughout this process you made what, I believe, are gender biased and inappropriate comments. You asked to view the female applicants photos to put a face to the name , you asked about our forklift certifications and if you will actually be seeing me on one. Do you also ask the males if they will get on a forklift? Do you ask Richard what his relationship is with other men? Do you put them through the same scrutiny as you have to me? Your comments did not stop there, you asked us to pick your family member and friends in exchange for your support of the other candidates and protection if Lily Stefano became Mayor, even made a comment you needed us to pick Carlos Gonzalez because he helped your daughter Lizelh Ayala in her campaign. You have implied on several occasions that you knew selections were not going to be approved by the new Council. You told us to tell candidates not to come so they are not publicly humiliated when the Council does not approve them just like when Isabel from 8181 was not approved for reception. Councilman Ayala, how would you know how the other council would vote? Do you understand that speaking to council in private regarding agenda items is a violation of the sunshine law? As an elected official you hold a lot of power but sadly you are misusing this power and your position for your personal politics and agenda instead of the wellbeing of the Town. You speak about being fair but whe

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of four (4) Park Attendants for the Social Services and Park and Recreations Department.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of four (4) Park Attendants for the Social Services and Park and Recreations Department. Executive Assistant to the Mayor and Social Services Coordinator Susana Guasch approached the Council to present the item. Ms. Guasch explained that she had met and discussed the department s needs with the Council individually in which, at said point, applicant s documentation and requirements were reviewed providing answers to the questions and concerns that arose following the notice of job availability. In addition, Ms. Guasch further explained that considering the department s growth and lack of staff, employees have had to take on extra hours and duties to provide adequate coverage. Thus, it had been difficult to maintain the level of service that the Social Services Department strives for. Councilwoman Ayala then recommended to make a motion for two (2) applicants with more hours per week for each position since it could potentially provide the solution the department needed instead of the proposed four (4) since she did not feel comfortable with the total number of positions requested and that it would be healthy to revisit the matter in the future when the current vacancy for council is filled. Councilman Ayala agreed with councilwoman Ayalas s suggestion. However, no formal motion was made for this recommendation, nor was it seconded. Camilo Martin, Assistant Public Works director, who was also part of the interview and selection committee for both presented positions for the Social Services and Parks and Recreations department, approached the Town Council to support the recommendation as proposed. Mr. Martin stated that although questions were being addressed to the department s director, he had never been approached nor questioned about the selection process. Susana Guasch concluded presenting the item by stating that given all documentation was provided and all questions had been answered she believed the most qualified candidates had been selected. After a brief discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion, Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows: Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilperson Edgar Ayala- No Councilperson Lizelh Ayala- Yes Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes

votes: Vice Mayor Pacheco made a motion as follows, TO ASSIST RESIDENTS AND PROVIDE COVID-19 RELIEF BY DISTRIBUTING $75.00 GIFTCARDS PER HOUSEHOLD TOWNWIDE AND TO INCLUDE EFFICIENCIES AT THE DISCRETION OF THE MAYOR. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Vice-Mayor Pacheco s Request for the Use of Cares Act Funds Towards Residential Assistance. Vice Mayor Pacheco began his discussion by explaining that his first item was intended to be a request for a gift to the residents for Christmas but unfortunately the meeting was cancelled, and it was not possible to have a discussion prior to the holidays. Vice Mayor Pacheco continued to explain how he proposed the second item in hopes that the Mayor and Council will consider using funds reimbursed under the Cares Act to assist residents because of the hardships they have experienced and continue to experience due to the pandemic. He further explained his request to combine both of his requests and proposed an amount of Seventy-Five ($75.00) to be given per household except for the Mayor and Town Council. Councilman Ayala addressed the Mayor and asked to extend the proposed benefit to the efficiencies that are registered with the Riverstone medley mobile home park management office. Finance Director Roy Danziger had technical difficulties and could not answer concerns by the council regarding the financial impact of gifting the gift cards, but Social Services Director Lizmari Valido stated that a projected total amount, if efficiencies were to be considered, would be unknown. Mayor Martell agreed to consider households residing in efficiencies subject to the legality of distributing/recognizing efficiencies. It was discussed that the Mayor and Council will distribute to Lakeside Retirement Park but the remaining of the town will have to pick up at the Medley Municipal Services Facility. Without further discussion, Vice Mayor Pacheco made a motion as follows, TO ASSIST RESIDENTS AND PROVIDE COVID-19 RELIEF BY DISTRIBUTING $75.00 GIFTCARDS PER HOUSEHOLD TOWNWIDE AND TO INCLUDE EFFICIENCIES AT THE DISCRETION OF THE MAYOR. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and carried unanimously.

This would potentially provide $ 22,000 revenue to the proposed budget. e Increase employee medical contribution by $ 25.00 per paycheck. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 19, 2021 COUNCIL WORKSHOP A public meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 19, 2021 at 3:00 pm. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO SPECIAL COUNSEL TONY RECIO Jorge Corzo, Town Engineer and Director of the Town s Capital Projects and Economic Development opened the meeting by introducing the staff involved in this project which includes Building and Zoning Director Richard McConachie and consultant Town s planner Robert Collins and colleague James Hickey from Calvin Giordano & Associates, Inc. Mr. Corzo explained that staff previously mentioned had been working on the evaluation of the Town s zoning map for over a year now. Mr. Corzo further explained that because there is a direct connection between land use and zoning designation and economic development, he took share in the task and presentation. In addition, director Corzo took the opportunity to inform the Town council of a similar upcoming presentation specific to the metro rail station area. Robert Collins, Town s consultant planner started the presentation (see the attached) by addressing the objectives and purposes of the presentation which represents the issues found after review of the Town s current residential zoning code and residential zoning map. Mr. Collins also stated that the presentation did not include formal recommendations since additional process is required before formal action is taken on the matter. Therefore, the presentation is merely a report of the findings after a detailed investigation was performed which discovered a lack of residential zoning districts, regulations and incorrect zoning designation and incorrect future land use designation on parcels. Mr. Collins also presented the Town s current zoning map and current future land use map and further explained the differences between future land use map and zoning map terms along with the connections to the Town s comprehensive plan. In addition, and as part of the residential zoning review performed, Mr. Collins presented a recommended three-phase approach to correct the residential zoning issues found and they were explained as follows: Process for Phase 1: Quickly correct parcels with residential zoning that should be designated M-1 (light industrial zoning category) zo

segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 28, 2021 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 28, 2021 at 5:15p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 28, 2021 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 28, 2021 at 5:15p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilperson Ayala and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by everyone in attendance. In continuance Mayor Martell opened the meeting for public comment in which Town Clerk Victoria Martinez noted that no public comments were received. Mayor Martell then instructed Social Services and Park and Recreations director Lizmari Valido to address the two items on the agenda. The items were discussed and acted upon as follows: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Medical Transportation Program. Director Valido addressed the documentation provided in the agenda packages and mentioned some corrections made to the job description presented for Social Services and Parks and Recreation CDL Driver position. The changes, as stated by director Valido, included driver s license endorsement language and the non-exempt status applicable to the position. Director Valido also mentioned that the need for a social services driver has existed for a while now and because former employee Osvaldo has now retired, and the new school year is scheduled to begin August 23 the need is overgrowing. Thus, director Valido continued to address the options presented for the operations of the social services medical transportation program which included part-time and full-time position options in conjunction with the arts and crafts, CITT shopping route and music night events schedule. Director Valido and the Town Council discussed of options 1, 3 and 4 in detail, explaining how the Uber Health program is structured and how it is proposed to work with the Town s medical transportation program, along with the pros and cons of both, a full-time and part- time position were had. In addition, director Valido discussed the participation of the medical transportation program for the last three (3) months and analyzed the participation it in detail with the recommended options. After a brief discussion, Councilperson Stefano made a motion as follows, TO APPROVE OPTION NUMBER 1 INCLUDING THE PART-TIME SOCIAL SERVICES AND PARKS AND RECREATIONS CDL DRIVER POSITION WITH THE U

segs.head: Arrangements for the posting of the position were discussed and it was concluded that the effective date for the notice of availability for said position was to take effect Monday August 2, 2021. - Discussion and Action on the Request for Job Availability of One (1) or More Social Services and Parks and Recreation CDL Driver Position.
votes: Councilwoman Stefano made a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE REQUEST FOR ONE (1) PART-TIME PARKS AND RECREATION SOCIAL SERVICES CDL DRIVER POSITION FOR THE SOCIAL SERVICES AND PARKS AND RECREATIONS DEPARTMENT. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Arrangements for the posting of the position were discussed and it was concluded that the effective date for the notice of availability for said position was to take effect Monday August 2, 2021. - Discussion and Action on the Request for Job Availability of One (1) or More Social Services and Parks and Recreation CDL Driver Position. Having discussed the options proposed for the social services medical transportation program, it was decided to approve and make available a part-time social services and parks and recreation CD driver position. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Stefano made a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE REQUEST FOR ONE (1) PART-TIME PARKS AND RECREATION SOCIAL SERVICES CDL DRIVER POSITION FOR THE SOCIAL SERVICES AND PARKS AND RECREATIONS DEPARTMENT. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Town Clerk Victoria Martinez took a moment to announce that the first Town of Medley budget public hearing was scheduled to take place on Wednesday September 8, 2021 at 5:15 pm.
segs.text: Town Clerk Victoria Martinez took a moment to announce that the first Town of Medley budget public hearing was scheduled to take place on Wednesday September 8, 2021 at 5:15 pm. It was also announced that the second and final Town of Medley budget public hearing was scheduled to take place on Tuesday September 21, 2021 at 5:15 pm. Councilperson Ayala also took a moment to recognize Lieutenant Arturo Jinete for his 30 years of service to the Town. Councilperson Ayala also asked Town staff to prepare a small gathering to celebrate such a tenure that perhaps could take place after the next scheduled council meeting and to also include utilities director Jorge Soto who had recently reached 35 years of service. Lieutenant Jinete thanked the Town Council for the recognition and expressed his gratitude. Mayor Martel then gave the Town Council a brief update of the construction of the concrete all along NW 107 Avenue in the Lakeside Retirement Park. He explained that it was just discovered that a concrete floor runs along the area and a change order was needed to be assigned to another contractor to cut the concrete in order to install the concrete posts for the wall. Mayor Martell further explained that several contractors are being approached for an assessment of the work to be performed and estimates and a minimum of three (3) quotes will be presented to the Town Council for approval. Chief Said-Jinete also approached the Town Council to inform them that the Medley Police Department will be planting a tree in honor and memory of former officer Dan Garcia who passed away a year ago. Mayor Martell and Council were happy and supported the initiative and thanked Chief Said-Jinete for it. Since there was no further business to discuss Mayor Martell made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Councilwoman Stefano seconded the motion, and the meeting was adjourned at 5:55pm on July 28, 2021.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JULY 6, 2021 COUNCIL WORKSHOP A public meeting of the Town Council was called to order on July 6, 2021 at 2:00 pm. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ Social Services and Parks and Recreations Director Lizmari Valido began the meeting by addressing the projected expense details for the July 4 Independence party (attached) that although the event was cancelled due to hurricane Elsa, services were scheduled, and some paid for. The DJ services were discussed, and Director Valido stated that it was very difficult and expensive to engage vendors for services the day of the celebrated Holiday. Vice-Mayor Pacheco inquired about the cost charged by former DJ vendor Banana Entertainment for past events, and it was informed that their price was $ 100.00 per hour. Thus, it was determined that perhaps it was cost efficient to get an estimate and engage Banana Entertainment for the monthly birthday celebrations until other options are considered and approved. In continuance and when large events were discussed, it was mentioned by Councilwoman Stefano that standard annual events should be planed in advance and should take place as closer to the celebrated holiday as possible. Director Valido explained that most events, especially the large celebrations do get coordinated ahead of time and dates and times are set with plenty of time for that same purpose. Director Valido further explained that small events like the recent vaccination events are not always coordinated with the preferred time notice as they involve other organizations. However, the Council is notified as soon as possible. Councilwoman Ayala mentioned that she would prefer a minimum of three (3) days notice for events like distributions including but not limited to food distributions, as the rest of the Council should and would like to participate in such community targeted events. Mayor Martell then explained that food distribution planning is sometimes difficult since perishable goods require immediate distribution. Therefore, when these types of items are received, he schedules distribution right away but will try his best to adjust the preparations to accommodate the Council s preference when possible. segs.head: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC INFORMATIONAL MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 17, 2021 A Public Informational Meeting of the Town of Medley took place on June 17, 2021, at 3:00p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC INFORMATIONAL MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 17, 2021 A Public Informational Meeting of the Town of Medley took place on June 17, 2021, at 3:00p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO Mayor Martell opened the meeting explaining the purpose of the public informational meeting. Mayor Martell continued to explain how the Town Council had, at the May regular meeting, approved the construction of a concrete wall along NW 107 Avenue that takes place directly behind the lots of the 700 block of the Lakeside Retirement Park. Mayor Martell further announced that during the preparation of the construction, it was discovered that eight (8) lots were encroaching in the proposed construction area. Live footage of the area in question along with descriptive images of the encroachment and structures were displayed for everyone to see. Guillermo Diaz, Town of Medley Building Chief inspector addressed the public and explained that structures blocking the area were found illegal and not controlled by the Florida Building code. In addition, Mr. Diaz addressed the existing fence which conditions were found to be unsafe. Councilwoman Stefano addressed the Mayor and Town staff to inquire the construction time for the proposed wall to be completed. It was clarified that once all obstructions were cleared and permitting process was completed, the installation of the concrete wall would not take long since the wall is mostly constructed of pre-manufactured panels. It was also explained by chief inspector Diaz that since a commercial company was selected, the footing process of the construction would normally advance at about 500 linear square footage per day. Affected residents specifically asked about the encroachment circumstances for each of the eight (8) lots and specific details and discussion was held for each of the lots mentioned. Discussion was then followed by a consensus, with the assistance from the Town, to continue the construction of the proposed concrete wall given the benefits it provided the park considering the future NW 107 Avenue expansion. In specific the following residents spoke on the matter. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC INFORMATIONAL MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 21, 2021 A Public Informational Meeting of the Town of Medley took place on June 21, 2021, at 3:00p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO Mayor Martell opened the meeting explaining the purpose of the public informational meeting. Mayor Martell continued to explain how the property, also known as Parcel B was acquired by the Town and the steps and action taken by Town to further to develop the property. In addition, Mayor Martell stated that because a large number of Medley residents are seniors, the idea was to lease the land and have investors clean up the site and develop the specific use determined by the Town for the property. Therefore, Mayor Martell further stated that back in 2012 the Council had determined and voted to draft and release a Request for Proposal (RFP) to solicit potential candidates and/or developers for a senior care facility at no cost to the Town until the recent action presented and taken by the Council to adjust the concept to a passive park concept along with the cleanup of the site. Councilperson Ayala addressed the public and informed that discussion for the site in question had already taken place at a previously council workshop and was followed by formal action at a council meeting in which the passive park concept was decided on. Councilperson Ayala further stated that ever since 2012 he has done everything possible to clean up the site because he has received many complaints, since then, about wild animals trespassing and encroaching into living areas of the park. Councilperson Ayala also stated that since 2012, although the Council has had many discussions about the site, the Council has failed to unanimously agree to move forward. Therefore, the passive park concept was moved forward in an attempt to clean-up the site. A recap of the master plan concept for the site in question and how the idea first initiated in 2012 was told by both Mayor Martell and Councilperson Ayala and it was concluded that both, the senior care facility, and passive park concept were discussed during the very beginning where the usage of the property was first mentioned and acted upon. segs.text: - Special Presentation by Vice-Mayor Pacheco to Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava and the Florida Department of Health in Miami-Dade County for the Outstanding COVID-19 Vaccine Outreach Events in the Town of Medley. Miami Dade County Mayor Daniella Cava approached the podium and thanked the Mayor and Vice Mayor for their invitation. She then continued to explain how she is taking the time to visit all the cities in the county to help build a relationship of partnership between the County and the cities. Mayor Cava explained how she fought hard by spearheading efforts in getting availability of the COVID-19 vaccine out into the communities. Mayor Martell then, on behalf of the Medley Council, congratulated Mayor Cava on her initiatives and then presented her with a key of the city. Vice Mayor also thanked Mayor Cava and recognized her and her team for their response time when vaccines were scarce, but most needed in the community, and he also thanked Commissioner Jose Pepe Diaz for his behind-the-scenes efforts in assisting in acquiring vaccines for the Town of Medley. Vice-Mayor Pacheco then presented Ms. Cava with a recognition from the citizens, the Medley Town Council, and the Medley Police Department. Vice Mayor Pacheco continued to also express the Town s gratitude to the Florida Department of Health in Miami Dade County for the outstanding COVID-19 vaccine outreach events held in the Town. The following Health department personnel were recognized for their efforts: Administration: | Dr. Reynald Jean, Irima Gonzalez RN, Carlos Cuevas, Daniela Garcia, and Paola Menoscal. Clerical Staff: Karel Vidal, Karim Velasquez, Laude Addison, Marianela Sanchez, Malange Joseph, Angel Camacho, Mary Gonzalez, Chiara Spinzi, Oreimy Suarez, Yaritza Madrigal, Isali Bouret, Mercedes Rodriguez, Connie Soto, and David Hong, RN Nursing Staff: Ana Camejo RN, Marisol Diaz RN, Felipe Garcia RN, Isabel RuizRN, Daydene Palacios RN, Mileidis Perez RN, Yesica Cruz RN, Chenice Orga RN, Sandra Moreno RN, Yusely Martinez RN, Julio C. Pelaez RN. Moreover, Carlos Cuevas from the Florida Department of Health approached the podium and thanked the Town, and the Town s staff for helping in the vaccination initiative and acknowledged director Lizmari Valido and Susana Guasch for their assistance and hard work. Lastly, Vice Mayor Pacheco also presented recognition to Town personnel involved whom assisted in the vaccine outreach. They were as follows: Jennifer Perez, Eyvis Amador, Angeli

segs.text: - Request by the Social Services and Parks and Recreations Department for Discussion and Action on the COVID-19 Baum Research Community Outreach Project Conducted by Florida International University (FIU). David Brown, from the Florida International University (FIU) college of medicine, requested to utilize Town facilities to conduct a study based on COVID-19 responses. The proposal as presented is based on studies that would involve COVID-19 testing to document community responses to the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as conducting surveys, responses on exposure to COVID-19 and community sentiment on vaccinations. The study would also include June 7, 2021 Regular Council Meeting Minutes COVID-19 testing, and bloodwork on site.
