segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Social Services Program s Rules and Regulations.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Social Services Program s Rules and Regulations. Social Services and Parks and Recreation Director Lizmari Valido approached the Council and addressed the documentation provided for said item that included proposed changes as previously discussed during the May 6, 2021 Council workshop. Proposed changes as provided addressed existing rules and regulations to programs administered by the Social Services department. In addition, director Valido specifically addressed the Start-Up Grant program and recommended not to penalize students for the circumstances and outcomes because of the global pandemic of 2020. Director Valido continued to recommend not to take grades into consideration for the 2020 school year so that a Start-Up applicant would not be affected. Councilwoman Ayala expressed agreement with the recommendations. Councilwoman Stefano then addressed the Hot Meal program and inquired about a particular case of a resident that applied for the meal program and issues were found. Hot Meal program director Fatima Fuentes approached the podium and began to explain that an application was received from an individual who has a physical debilitation. However, the rules and regulations in existence do not address nor allows for exceptions to be made. Director Fuentes then asked that if the Council wished to consider said circumstances, the authorization to take applicants on a case-by-case basis was then required. Without further discussion Councilwoman Stefano placed a motion as follows, "TO APPROVE CHANGES TO THE RULES AND REGULATIONS OF THE June 7, 2021 Regular Council Meeting Minutes SOCIAL SERVICES PROGRAMS AS PROPOSED, AND TO AUTHORIZE THE DEPARTMENT DIRECTORS TO MAKE EXCEPTIONS ON APPLICATIONS RECEIVED FOR THE HOT MEAL, MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION AND BATHING PROGRAM TO CONSIDER APPROVAL ON A _ CASE-BY-CASE BASIS OF APPLICANTS WITH PHYSICAL IMPEDIMENTS. " Councilwoman Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion, Action and Ratification on the Appointment of the Assistant to the Council Position.
segs.text: - Discussion, Action and Ratification on the Appointment of the Assistant to the Council Position. Town Attorney Lilian Arango addressed the matter by stating that the job description had been presented for Council review and approval as instructed in the Council workshop of May 25, 2021. Ms. Arango reiterated that after further research it was determined that the position was clerical in nature and did not meet the exempt status. Vice Mayor Pacheco stated that he was not in agreement with the position s compensation matching the Councilmember s salary and he suggested for the council to wait on the pending gender study to determine the proper salary for this position. Human Resources Director Olga addressed the Council and clarified that she had previously misspoken regarding the current wage that Rosa Palau was making. Director Quin also urged the Council to set a starting wage rate at this time with the tentative effective date of June 15 while also taking into consideration the current wage rate of individuals currently fulfilling the same position having higher education, qualifications, tenure and experience. Councilperson Ayala stated that he believed a starting wage of $24.00 was reasonable. After a brief discussion it was determined to set a starting wage to $23.00 dollars an hour. segs.text: - Update by Town Clerk on the Translation Services and Audio-Visual Improvements Previously Requested for Public Meetings. segs.head: - Monthly Update by Town Staff on Current Town Projects and Related Finances.
segs.text: - Monthly Update by Town Staff on Current Town Projects and Related Finances. Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the Council and distributed a 2021 assessment from the Property Appraisers and explained that the Town experienced a 6.7% increase from last year s initial assessment of $2,648,409,814.00, and although the Town does not have the final assessment, this is a positive review. Finance Director Roy Danziger circulated a second piece of documentation which reflected the amount of funds distributed to cities under the CARES Act and suggested using the funds for water infrastructure improvements. It was also discussed and announced that the office of the Town clerk is working with the finance department to schedule budget workshops and necessary public meetings for the Town s budget for the June 7, 2021 Regular Council Meeting Minutes 2021-2022 fiscal year. Assistant Utilities Director Osmanny Larzabal approached the Council and stated that the Town experienced an unusually high bill for Stormwater in the month of May. Mr. Larzabal further stated that the Town s assumptions are that the issue may be an error with Miami Dade County s readings to which Director Soto is already inquiring and addressing as such. Director Jorge Corzo also approached the Council and gave a brief update on some ongoing projects. It was mentioned that the Town was awarded about 1.4 million dollars from the State for partial funding of three ongoing projects. In addition, Mr. Corzo stated that NW 97 Ave extension near the Sea Vee boats property, about $500,000.00 was awarded for the road project. Also, for the project of 89 Avenue, the widening into three lanes of the segment of 87" Ave and the FEC railroad were presently repairing some roads and with the funds we may be able to extend the design to three lanes to match the previous work done by the Town in front of the waste management building. It was also noted that the Town is receiving partial funding for NW 99" Terrace, which is a new road connecting NW SRD to 87" Ave to allow for northwest bound traffic to go over the proposed flyover ramp that FDOT is proposing as part of the improvements out west to Okeechobee Road. Director Corzo then went over some highlights and explained that the progress of the community pool has been accomplished as scheduled, but it has been the underground unforeseen work, that delayed the work, but it now was ongoing and completed in the next couple of months. segs.text: * The City Manager alone is responsible for managing City employees (including the City Clerk) and their salaries. The City Council has no direct authority to increase the salary of the City Clerk position. The City Manager will be requesting a measure from the City Council to appropriate a $10,000 salary increase for the City Clerk not connected to any increase or change in the Clerk s responsibility. One of the City Councilmembers is married to the City Clerk. Would a city councilmember be in violation of Florida's anti-nepotism statute were the city council to approve an appropriation to the city manager's budget and direct the city manager to use the appropriation to increase the salary of the city clerk, who is the councilmember's wife?

segs.head: * Under the circumstances presented, a city councilmember will not violate the anti-nepotism statute were the city council to approve a budgetary appropriation and direct it to be used to increase the salary of the city clerk, so long as the pay increase does not exceed the salary range authorized for that position 97 99 ANTI-NEPOTISM SOCIAL MEDIA GENERAL CONCERNS

segs.text: - Resolution Adopting the SW-0113 NW 96 Street Stormwater Facilities Plan (Plan) and Authorizing the Town Mayor and Town Officials to Seek Funding or Financing of the Plan through the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) State Revolving Loan Fund (SRLF) Program. Mayor Martell then opened the item for public comment. No public comments were made on the matter. Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the podium and explained that the state has an infrastructure program that allows cities to borrow funds and repay the loans within twenty (20) years with an interest rate of .02 percent. His recommendation was to approve the application for the loan for this project. Director Danziger also suggested that the application for this loan be approved for other projects the Town may have or pursue. Rodney Carrero-Santana from Snubbs Consulting approached the Council and reiterated that this project allows for great opportunity within the town by creating many job opportunities and development to the Town. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion to adopt Resolution C-1888, Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously. segs.text: - Resolution Selecting and Awarding an Agreement to CBRE Inc. for Real Estate and Broker Services for the Sale of Previously Declared Town Surplus Property Located at 10701 NW 122 Street, Medley Florida 33178. Councilman Ayala addressed his concerns on the matter and the Mayor began to explain that the intent to sell this property is to utilize the revenue to build the public works and utilities department a new building. Councilman Ayala expressed understanding that a discussion was held between the Mayor and the directors, but also expressed that the council had not received ample time to review or discuss this proposal to act on it. It was explained by Director Corzo that this parcel was acquired by the Town twenty years ago so that the Town can install an elevated water tank, but the pressure system improved over time with the involvement of Miami Dade County Water and there was no need or use for the original purpose of the parcel. Director Corzo continued to explain that the proposed resolution is solely for the approval awarding the agreement to a real estate broker. Councilman Ayala stated that in his opinion, the asset should not be sold and be allowed to continue to grow in value. It was also explained that there is an additional intent to relocate the police department to the current public works department so they may have a central home base. Chief of Police Jeanette Said reaffirmed the approved discussion to move the police department and explained that there are forfeiture funds to be allocated for this project, but she does not have an estimated time when the forfeiture funds will be received. Utilities Director Jorge Soto also explained that it was also discussed that the new facility would be designated as a category 5 hurricane safe building which provides relief to the emergency operations personnel as well as a possible shelter for the residents. Director Danziger reiterated that selling the parcel would allow for the property to go from a non- revenue producing property to a revenue producing property. The property will provide tax revenue. Councilwoman Ayala joined the discussion and agreed that the police department needs their own facility and Public Works/Utilities need their own or an upgraded building as well. She continued to explain that she needs additional time to review the documentation to decide on this matter. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on add on item discussion and action on the vaccination site agreement (COVID-19) for closed point of administration memorandum of agreement between the state of Florida, Department of Health, Miami-Dade County Health Department and the Town of Medley. Town Attorney Arango explained that this item would allow the Town to enter into a Closed Point of Administration agreement with Miami Dade County that would allow the Town to hold a vaccination program for employees and the families of employees. It is not open for the public such as resident. However, if the Town would opt to enter into an Open Point of Administration Agreement, the Town would be required to have refrigeration to house the vaccine and a licensed medical provider available to administer the vaccines. It was explained that the logistics of implementing the programs have yet to be determined. Mayor Martell then suggested to leave both options of the agreements open for the Town to enter into to maximize the resources to both, employees and residents. Without further discussion Councilman Ayala made a motion as follows, TO AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO ENTER INTO BOTH, OPEN AND CLOSED POINT OF ADMINISTRATION (COVID-19) VACCINATION SITE AGREEMENTS WITH MIAMI DADE COUNTY SUBJECT TO AVAILIBILITY. Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously. Since there was no further business to consider Mayor Martell made a motion to adjourn the meeting, it carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 8:00 pm on March 1, 2021. segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MARCH 18, 2021- 7:00 P.M. A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on March 18, 2021 at 7:00 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO ASSISTANT TOWN CLERK: JENNY DIGIACOMO TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Councilwoman Ayala and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited. It was noted that Councilwoman Stefano distributed supporting documentation to the Mayor and Council in support of her items as reflected in the night s agenda. In continuance, a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda was placed by Councilperson Stefano, seconded by Councilman Ayala and carried unanimously.

segs.head: Mayor Martell then addressed Councilwoman Stefano to begin with her requested New Business Items section of the agenda.
segs.text: Mayor Martell then addressed Councilwoman Stefano to begin with her requested New Business Items section of the agenda. Said items were addressed and acted upon as follows: - Councilperson Stefano s request for Discussion and Action on the procedures held by SFM Security Services, Inc. for Lakeside Retirement Park. Councilperson Stefano began discussion on the matter and called representatives from SFM Security Services, Inc to the podium. Christian Infante owner of SMF Services, Inc as well as Director of Security Alex Carulo were present. Councilperson Stefano began the discussion by explaining that an employee who had been with the company for 11 years was given a warning notice and then relieved from his Lakeside Retirement Park Post. Thus, she asked for clarification on the company s decision to have the individual removed from that security post. Mr. Alex Carulo explained that it was brought to the company s attention that the employee had left the gate open and when asked about the incident the individual admitted to leaving said security gate open. Mr. Carulo further explained that it is company policy to have cameras within the guard shack and said individual would turn the cameras off or obstruct the vision of the cameras even after being instructed not to do so. Therefor he was addressed for violating the post rules. In addition, Mr. Carulo made it clear that although it was his decision to remove the individual from the lakeside post, the employee in question would not lose his job and was given an increase. Councilwoman Stefano began explaining that in 2019 the Town had approved an hourly wage increase for SMF on the basis that SFM Security Services would pass down said increase to the employees. Mr. Carulo confirmed that an increase was given to said employees. SFM Security Services owner Christian Infante joined the discussion and clarified that the increase approved by the Town council in 2019 had been the first requested and granted price increase to the company since beginning to work for the Town in 2011 and that the company increases the wages of their employees on a yearly basis. Councilman Ayala wanted clarification on the source of the complaint given to SMF about the security guard on duty and Mayor Martell explained that he was present when the gate was left open by the security guard and that he reported the incident to SMF because the Town is receiving a service that should be performed properly for the safety of the residents of

segs.head: Next for discussion was New Business item B.
segs.text: Next for discussion was New Business item B. It was discussed and acted upon as follows, - Councilperson Stefano s Request for Information, Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Capital Improvement Projects Councilwoman Stefano addressed Town Engineer Jorge Corzo and requested an update on the progress of capital improvement projects in the Town. Mr. Corzo approached the Council and began to explain how the council approved a capital program which has continually been followed with the instructions approved by the council as it relates to capital projects and the budgets that were approved. Councilwoman Stefano directed Mr. Corzo s attention to a Lakeside fact sheet she held and began to explain that a year ago she had taken Assistant Director Manny Perez to Lakeside Retirement Park while the sea wall was being built. Councilwoman Stefano stated that she showed Mr. Perez a residential home that was experiencing flooding because of the construction. She stated that it has been a year and a half, and the Town has not taken the initiative to correct the flooding although it was said that the Town would draw plans and come before council with a solution, but it has yet to be done. Councilwoman Stefano once again expressed that the Lakeside Fact sheet reflected that the design for said project would begin in June of 2021 and that it is unacceptable for it to commence almost two years later. Director Corzo explained that lot 743 is not the only location where the flooding occurs and that every process has steps such as permitting which requires proper planning and budgeting. Director Corzo also explained that a plan has been put in place, but if there are priorities within the council then they must be instructed to him. Councilman Ayala explained that he feels there has not been good faith from Director Corzo s part to follow the Council s instructions. Director Corzo expressed his commitment to both the residents and businesses evenly. Mayor Martell joined the discussion and explained that he was unaware of the request by Councilwoman Stefano, and if a workshop had been held to discuss these matters, they would have been addressed properly. Councilwoman Ayala asked for clarification on the Lakeside driveways and Public Works Director Heriberto Cabrera approached the council and offered the clarification as requested. Further, director Cabrera explained that he was instructed to oversee the repairs of lakeside driveways which would be done in parts. The i

segs.head: Utilities Director Jorge Soto approached the Council and explained that the State of Florida allows for maintenance procurement of Three-Hundred Thousand ($300,000) dollars or less to be done without three (3) bids.
segs.text: Utilities Director Jorge Soto approached the Council and explained that the State of Florida allows for maintenance procurement of Three-Hundred Thousand ($300,000) dollars or less to be done without three (3) bids. Director Soto suggested including said language and allow for these terms when amending the procurement ordinance only for maintenance such as pump repairs, watermain breaks and related maintenance. Director Soto also explained that many of these occurrences are for emergency services that require immediate attention. Town Attorney Lillian Arango clarified that although state law provides for exemption, the best practices is to solicit three (3)quotes. Mayor Martell stated that the Town should continue the process of soliciting the three quotes and bidding process as stated under the Town s Procurement Ordinance. Director Cabrera approached the Council to inform them that the hiring process for the public works position vacancy was going very well. Since there was no further business to consider, Councilwoman Stefano made a motion to adjourn the meeting and the meeting was adjourned unanimously at 9:15 pm on March 18, 2021. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MARCH 4, 2021 A Council Swearing-In ceremony of the Town of Medley, Florida was held on March 4, 2021 at 5:30 pm. The following were present, Mayor Roberto Martell Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco Councilmember Edgar Ayala Councilmember Lizelh Ayala Councilmember Elect: Lily Stefano Certification of the official results of the Town of Medley Special Municipal Election of March 2, 2021 was read into the record and announced for everyone in attendance as follows, Councilmember-Vote for 1 (at Large) Lily Stefano 255 Votes Karina Pacheco 160 Votes Griselia Digiacomo 51 Votes Oath of Office was administered to Council-Elect Lily Stefano by the Honorable Milena Abreu, Miami-Dade County Judge. segs.head: MINUTES OF A MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MAY 25, 2021 COUNCIL WORKSHOP A public meeting of the Town Council was called to order on May 25, 2021 at 1:00 pm.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MAY 25, 2021 COUNCIL WORKSHOP A public meeting of the Town Council was called to order on May 25, 2021 at 1:00 pm. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL (ABSENT) VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO LINDSEY RIDER, SPECIAL LABOR COUNSEL Town s special labor counsel Lindsey Rider opened the meeting circulating a draft of the proposed job description (attached) for the Executive Assistant to the Council position for the Council to review. In addition. Ms. Rider stated that the purpose of the workshop was to have a clear understanding of the Council s needs to incorporate all duties and responsibilities set by Council. After the proposed job description was reviewed, questions about the non-exempt proposed status were raised to which special labor counsel Rider clarified that because the duties and responsibilities as shown in addition to the required skills and minimum education required, the position would not qualify to be an exempt position under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA). Ms. Rider further stated that because the individual filling the position would not carrying out duties of a department head or those a professional position although the duties include confidentiality nature, it was not enough to qualify under the FLSA criteria and standards. Councilwoman Ayala asked for a status of the gender pay study being that has been conducted since it was approved in 2020. Human resources director Olga Quin gave a brief explanation of the status of the study including some challenges encountered since most department heads did not have job descriptions on file so that proper comparisons could be performed as instructed. In addition, labor counsel Lindsey Rider further explained issues faced with several department heads challenging the job descriptions as drafted and providing comments about the same. Human resources Quin also stated that another challenge was finding similar positions in other cities to use as comparable for positions like the hot meal program since these positions were unique to the Town. Councilwoman Ayala and Councilwoman Stefano expressed that since the job descriptions were being drafted according to the needs of the Town, department heads should not have a say nor input in the matter. Special labor counsel Rider agreed with the Council s feedback

segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MAY 25, 2021 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on May 25, 2021 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL (ABSENT) VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO Before the meeting opened Town Clerk Victoria Martinez announced that Mayor Martell was absent. Therefore, Town Clerk Martinez further stated that in accordance with the Town of Medley council meeting procedures, the Vice-Mayor, in the absence of the Mayor, becomes the presider officer of said council meeting. Thus, Vice-Mayor Pacheco presided the meeting accordingly. The Invocation was given by Councilwoman Ayala and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited. A motion to approve the meeting s agenda was made by Councilperson Ayala, seconded by Councilwoman Ayala, and carried unanimously. The meeting was then opened for public comments to which it was noted that no comments were made.

segs.head: In continuance, Vice-Mayor addressed the next order of business which were the Town of Medley Items.
votes: Councilwoman Ayala made a motion as follows, TO APPROVE AND TO HOLD A TOWN OF MEDLEY KARAOKE NIGHT EVENT TO TAKE PLACE AT THE LAKESIDE RETIREMENT PARK RECREATIONAL CENTER ON FRIDAY MAY 28, 2021 FROM 6:00 PM TO 9:00 PM Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: In continuance, Vice-Mayor addressed the next order of business which were the Town of Medley Items. They were discussed and acted upon as follows: - Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Lakeside Event Sponsored by Councilperson Stefano. Councilperson Stefano addressed the rest of the Town Council and audience present and stated that at the May 3, 2021 Regular Council meeting, the Council had discussed and agreed to hold monthly workshops to discuss all Town of Medley events moving forward. However, she had proposed to hold an event on Friday May 28, 2021 to which the Mayor expressed a different interpretation of the Council final decision. Therefore, Councilwoman Stefano was then asking the Town Council for support to her proposed Karaoke Night event to take place on Friday May 28, 2021 from 6-9 pm. It was also inquired by Councilperson Ayala whether the proposed event would be sponsored by herself or if it would be a Town event on behalf of the entire Town Council. Councilperson Stefano expressed that although she proposed the event she would be pleased to hold and celebrate said event as a Town of Medley event with the entire Town of Medley Council. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Ayala made a motion as follows, TO APPROVE AND TO HOLD A TOWN OF MEDLEY KARAOKE NIGHT EVENT TO TAKE PLACE AT THE LAKESIDE RETIREMENT PARK RECREATIONAL CENTER ON FRIDAY MAY 28, 2021 FROM 6:00 PM TO 9:00 PM Councilperson Stefano seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Request by Councilperson Stefano for the Discussion and Action on the Cancellation of the Town of Medley Food Distribution Event Sponsored by Mayor Martell.
votes: Councilperson Stefano made a motion as follows, TO REQUEST ENOUGH DONATIONS, IN AN EFFORT TO ELIMINATE ANY POSSIBLE LIABILITY TO THE TOWN, FOR MEDLEY RESIDENTS ONLY AND REMOVING DISTRIBUTION OF SUPPLIES TO OTHERS THAN MEDLEY RESIDENTS. TO ALSO HOLD THE FOOD DITRIBUTION TWICE PER MONTH CARRYING IT HOUSE TO HOUSE. Councilwoman Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Request by Councilperson Stefano for the Discussion and Action on the Cancellation of the Town of Medley Food Distribution Event Sponsored by Mayor Martell. Councilperson Stefano began the discussion by stating that she had no wishes to cancel the food distribution currently leaded by Mayor Martell. However, she wanted to adjust the way the distribution and its operations were taking place since she has had the opportunity to observe how the Town carries a liability allowing third parties, such as religious entities and their representatives, being part of the logistics of the receiving aspects in addition to already receiving some of the donations given to the Town. In addition, Councilperson Stefano stated the arrangements for the additional distribution to these organizations place additional workload to the Town of Medley employees whom some have already complained of the conditions in which they are working during the distribution days considering the significant number of pallets being loaded and carried. Executive Assistant to the Mayor Susana Guasch approached the Council and explained that donations received for the food distributions were received through Freedom Fresh, a local Medley business and a registered partner of USDA. Ms. Guasch also further explained that the Town s participation and request to successfully carry out the distribution is a total of ten (10) pallets. However, in certain occasions Freedom Fresh has supplied more than requested and the Town provides it to these religious organizations to not let the excess go to waste. Vice-Mayor Pacheco joined the discussion and stated that the Town does not pay for the donations or any of the resources used during the distributions including the truck used etc. and although some residents may look like they are carrying more than the one (1) box provided by the Town, some of these residents are helping others in taking the boxes for them since a lot of the elderly population do not have the transportation means to come to town hall to pick up the donations themselves. Councilperson Stefano continued to express her concerns for the liability the excess of pallets and third parties represent to the Town and Councilperson Ayala addressed Town Attorney Lillian Arango for a legal perspective of the situation. Town attorney Lillian Arango stated although she did not have the opportunity to review any agreements between the Town and Freedom Fresh, clarified that the Town does not have to exten

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Request for Job Availability for the Receptionist Position.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Request for Job Availability for the Receptionist Position. Human Resources Director Olga Quin addressed the Council and explained that at the May 3, 2021 regular council meeting, employee Rosa Palau had been appointed to the Executive Assistant to the Council position, thus leaving a vacancy to fulfill. Vice-Mayor Pacheco inquired as to whether the reception position could be filled with the help of other departments and if it necessarily had to be a full-time position. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez explained that said position had always been a full time and a bargaining unit position. Town Clerk Martinez further explained that providing coverage was difficult since it was divided between the Building and the Social Services department adjusting to their operations and availability. Both HR Director and Town Clerk Martinez discussed a tentative timeline for the hiring process which resulted to tentatively schedule a special council meeting for the third week of June in order to fill said position so that employee Rosa Palau can fulfill the new duties assign to her. Without further discussion on the matter, Councilperson Stefano placed a motion to approve the posting of the notice of job availability for the receptionist position. Councilwoman Ayala seconded

segs.head: the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on the Approval of an Agreement Between the Town of Medley and CGI Communications, Inc. for a Community Video Program.
segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on the Approval of an Agreement Between the Town of Medley and CGI Communications, Inc. for a Community Video Program. Andrea Tempio with CGI Communications was present via virtual platform for discussion on the matter and explained that CGI communications is a partner with the National League of Cities and further explained that CGI Communications is a video production company producing professional content that helps communities market themselves. The service consists of a four-video series of three minutes of length each with the Town having complete control over the content. It is a completely free service, and it is performed through an agreement with a three-year term. It was discussed among the Council to add language to reflect a thirty (30) day termination clause for liability purposes and that the Town must pre-approve all content as well as what business ads will be displayed on the Town social media accounts. Councilperson Stefano asked clarification on the sponsored ads to be displayed on the Towns videos and it was explained by Ms. Tempio that there will be business ads displayed within the videos, but the Town can have complete control in approving what businesses or sponsors are part of the advertisement section on said videos. Without further discussion Councilperson Ayala then placed a motion as follows, TO APROVE AND ENTER INTO A THREE-YEAR AGREEMENT WITH CGI COMMUNICATIONS, INC FOR A COMMUNITY VIDEO PROGRAM INCORPORATING THE LANGUAGE/CHANGES AS _ DISCUSSED INCLUDING A THIRTY (30) DAY TERMINATION CLAUSE AND LANGUAGE REFLECTING THE TOWN TO PRE-APPROVE ALL CONTENT OF THE VIDEOS AS WELL AS BUSINESS SPONSORED ADS THAT WILL BE DISPLAYED ON THE VIDEOS. segs.text: - Ordinance of the Town of Medley, Florida, Amending Chapter 14 Businesses, Article II Business Tax Receipts, of the Town of Medley Code of Ordinances Relating to Business Tax Receipts and Certificates of Use; Providing for Codification; Providing for Severability; Providing for Conflicts; and Providing for an Effective Date. Town Attorney Lillian Arango explained that said amendments are primarily because the provisions were outdated and the Town needed to clarify and update some of these provisions including home occupations requiring a BTR, shifting existing enforcement duties from the legal department to the Town s Building and Zoning department, and Code Compliance Department to reflect what is in practice, and to provide for revocation of a BTR when a business violates certain laws while conducting its business activities. Councilperson Stefano requested clarification on the section that included language regarding nonprofit organizations being exempt from requiring a BTR and it was confirmed by Ms. Arango that said exemption was permissible under Florida law. Ms. Arango began explaining that Section 2-130 was amended to include language requiring expenditures above 25,000 thousand dollars to come before council for approval. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Early Retirement Penalty for the Town of Medley General Pension Plan.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Early Retirement Penalty for the Town of Medley General Pension Plan. Financial Director Roy Danziger explained that the proposal is to offer employees which fall under the criteria of the age of 55 or older or have 25 years of service with the Town to retire early waiving the early retirement penalty. Thus, the Town would provide a ninety (90) day window for the qualifying employees. Director Danziger further explained that qualified employee still would be required to meet eligibility for medical insurance and said employees would not qualify for the drop benefit. Director Danziger then presented the Mayor and Council with a list of employees that would fall under the qualifying terms. Councilperson Ayala asked to know which employee requested this benefit and wanted to make it clear that although this benefit could be approved it is not guaranteed that the employees will take advantage of the opportunity to participate. Mayor Martell clarified that it would benefit several employees and he was approached by more than one. Mayor Martell also informed the council that the benefit had been provided to the police department in the past. Councilperson Ayala did not agree with the proposal and stated that it was not fair to extend this benefit to an individual who has not taken accountability for his actions in the Town. Councilperson Stefano joined the discussion and requested to table the item. Councilperson Ayala agreed to table the item but for it to be brought back in two (2) weeks at a special meeting to be re-discussed and acted upon. Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO AMEND THE GENERAL ADMINISRATION PENSION PLAN TO WAIVE THE EARLY RETIREMENT PENALTY FOR EMPLOEES WITH (25) YEARS OF SERVICE AND OVER THE AGE OF (55) FIFTY-FIVE. EMPLOYEES STILL WOULD BE REQUIRED TO QUALIFY FOR MEDICAL INSURANCE AND WILL NOT QUALIFY FOR THE DROP BENEFIT. AMENDMENT TO BE SUBJECT TO BARGAINING UNIT REQUIREMENTS, ACTUARIAL AND IMPACT STUDY. Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilwoman Lily Stefano- No Councilperson Edgar Ayala- No Councilwoman Lizelh Ayala- No Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes The motion as carried did not pass by majority of vote. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on Lakeside Parcel B, CIP Project No. 0238-2.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Lakeside Parcel B, CIP Project No. 0238-2. Director Corzo began the discussion by following up on the ideas that were discussed and decided upon during the Council workshop. Mr. Corzo furthed stated that he has since the workshop sent the Mayor and Council preliminary plans of a passive park that can still be adjusted to the Council s preference. Mr. Corzo reiterated that the previous discussion with the Council included instructions to have parking, bathrooms, and as Councilperson Ayala instructed to also include a tree field. Director Corzo explained that he already requested the proposal to modify the permit, but needed further instructions and input from the Council to proceed with the proposal for the next step in the project. Mayor Martell explained that he recommended using parcel B as both a passive park and building a property on the land. Councilperson Ayala disagreed and reiterated that what the Mayor proposed was not what the Council had agreed upon at the Council workshop. Therefore, he would like to proceed with the preferences chosen by the Council. Vice Mayor Pacheco translated the discussion for the lakeside residents that were in attendance and stated how the project previously approved included to build a senior care facility, but unfortunately there has been no investors interested in the parcel and the Town is now moving forward with clearing and filling the land for the benefit of the residents, but he is not in agreement with the park concept. Councilperson Stefano joined the discussion and recalled several occasions where parcel B had been proposed for many uses but that now was the time to move forward and begin the Project so the residents could use the park and enjoy it for the time being. Councilwoman Stefano added that the Town could still allow the option to remain open for the opportunity of future development for uses such as the senior care facility as the Mayor proposed. Director Corzo expressed how he needed clear direction from the Council to move forward with a plan, and that he has dedicated his personal time in the creation of a plan based on the council s concensus at the workshop and therefore he followed up and submitted a recommendation for approval. Councilwoman Ayala then placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE ADJUSTMENT OF THE PERMIT AND TO MOVE FORWARD WITH THE CLEANING OF LAKESIDE PARCEL B SITE FOR THE CREATION OF A PASSIVE PARK, INCLUSIVE OF PARKING, AND BATHROOMS. segs.text: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion and Action on a Health and Wellness Program Initiative. Councilperson Lizelh Ayala began stating that she had presented her vision for her health and wellness initiative at the last Council meeting and afterwards researched other municipalities which indicated that these projects are usually spearheaded by a Parks and Recreation Director that has education in public health and for her program to take off she explained it was important to have personnel with the experience needed. Councilwoman Ayala also stated that although the Social Services and Park and Recreations department were combined in 2019 her proposal was to separate the two departments, but not change the title, scope of work, pay, or staff of the current director as she would continue to oversee all social services operations, but operations under the park and recreation will be separated to allow her initiative to reach its potential. Social Services and Parks and recreation Director Lizmari Valido addressed Councilperson Lizelh Ayala and explained that she had not been asked to provide her qualifications or certifications which include those needed to conduct the parks and recreations operations. Director Valido further explained that she feels that she has not been given the opportunity to be presented with working on the initiative. Councilwoman Ayala reiterated that her research and advice she has received has indicated that her initiative would do well under a director in public health. Councilperson Ayala joined the discussion and stated that the item should be tabled because of the processes established under the hiring policy that needed to first be addressed. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez also explained that Town Ordinance would need to be amended as well because it included the codification of departments created such as Social Services and Park and Recreations Department as one. Director Valido stated her current job duties and explained that if her job performance has been excellent and she has not complained about the work assigned, then there should not be a need to split and restructure her department. Director Valido also explained that based on the current gender study being conducted, removing the park and recreation operations could potential take away the opportunity for compensation since her position as is would constitute a higher rate of pay in most municipalities. segs.head: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion and Action on the Start-Up Grant Program.
segs.text: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion and Action on the Start-Up Grant Program. Councilwoman Lizelh Ayala stated that she had reviewed the criteria for the startup grant program and proposed changes before the council to update the program in a way that would most benefit the current generation of residential students as well as extending the benefit and promoting higher education. After presenting the proposed changes, Councilwoman Ayala placed a motion as follows, TO AMEND THE START-UP GRANT PROGRAM TO BE MADE INTO SOLELY A GRANT PROGRAM; TO INCREASE THE CAP PER STUDENT TO EIGHT THOUSAND FOUR HUNDRED ($8,400); TO ALLOW A GAP IN BETWEEN SEMESTERS ONLY UNDER UNFORESEEN CIRCUMSTANCES FOR NO MORE THAN TWO (2) SEMESTERS/TERMS UP TO (12) MONTHS; TO BEGIN DOCUMENTATION OF ALUMNI DEGREES, SUCH AS SUCCESS AND CAREER GOALS; TO CREATE A SUBDIVISION TO THE MEDLEY FOUNDATION DEDICATED TO THE GRANT PROGRAM; TO EXTEND THE BENEFIT TO INCLUDE HIGHER EDUCATION SUCH AS A MASTER S DEGREE SUBJECT TO THE SAME CAP IN FUNDS; TO MAKE CHANGES EFFECTIVE MOVING FORWARD BUT TO ALSO ACCEPT APPLICANTS THAT HAD REACHED THE STIPULATED CAP AMOUNT SINCE JANUARY 2020 TO RE-APPLY FOR THE GRANT UNTIL THEY EXCEED THE NEW CAP AMOUNT. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion and Action on the Request for Donation to PATH in Support and Solidarity with India due to COVID-19. segs.head: - Request by Councilwoman Stefano for Discussion and Action on the Request for an Assistant to the Council Position.
segs.text: - Request by Councilwoman Stefano for Discussion and Action on the Request for an Assistant to the Council Position. Councilwoman Stefano began by stating that the Council s Assistant position has been vacant and would like to propose to the Council that Rosa Palau, the Town of Medley s current receptionist fill the vacancy. Each Councilperson expressed their agreement with her appointment. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez addressed the Council and informed the need for a job description, wage rage, and requested that these items be formalized prior to the effective date. Rosa Palau approached the podium to thank the council and expressed her acceptance of the position and gratitude for the consideration. Councilperson Stefano proposed for Ms. Palau to begin her new position immediately while also filling the receptionist position until a job availability is made open to fill her vacancy. It was discussed that sunshine law and ethics training would be required, and Ms. Palau would need to attest that she is bound to sunshine law guidelines and therefore, she would not be a conduit for communication between the Council. Councilperson Stefano also proposed Mrs. Palau to oversee the future receptionist and be a part of the hiring process for that individual. Councilwoman Stefano informed staff that she will come up with a draft for the job description for the Town s review and consideration. Human resources director Olga Quin explained that although the position will be subject to union bargaining requirements, the Town would also follow the recently established hiring policy and the requirements of the hiring process of any employee to a new position which would include job classification, detailed job description, and established wages. Councilwoman Ayala stated that other municipalities have similar positions and read into the record some of the duties and responsibilities which are similar to the duties and responsibilities asked of the position being discussed. Human Director Quin asked as to what minimum qualifications and education requirements were to be asked for the position in question since similar positions in other municipalities were to include certain education and qualification requirements. Councilperson Ayala then asked town attorney Lillian Arango for clarification given the Council s desire and Town Attorney Arango stated that under the Town s charter, the council has the authority to hire employees. However, the Council self-imposed a hiring

segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MAY 4, 2021 COUNCIL WORKSHOP A Special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on May 4, 2021 at 1:00 pm.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MAY 4, 2021 COUNCIL WORKSHOP A Special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on May 4, 2021 at 1:00 pm. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA LILY STEFANO TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO Councilwoman Stefano opened the meeting by circulating a survey that she had performed about the Town s Hot Meal Program. Councilwoman Stefano further explained that the survey had been done anonymously and was circulated through the 8181 mobile home park and other areas of the Town with the purpose to obtain a better understanding of the nature of the complaints and/or comments about the meal program in general but not related to the staff. In addition, councilwoman Stefano referred about a specific complain that was received about the contents of a meal that included chicken and that it really stood out in a negative way. In general, councilwoman Stefano addressed the quality of the food that was being provided through the program and stated that it needed to improve. Hot Meal Program Director Fatima Fuentes addressed Councilwoman Stefano s comments and the complaints mentioned and stated that all food received is inspected meticulously on a daily basis by several of the hot meal program personnel including herself as she is the very first person, immediately upon receipt, who inspects and reports any and all issues directly to the provider Latin American Grill, if any. In addition, director Fuentes expressed how the number of complaints received throughout the years, in comparison with the 378 meals served daily, are minimal. Councilwoman Stefano also pointed out that the packaging in which the meals are being delivered and as discussed previously in other occasions, had a lot to do with the quality of the food being received by the residents. Rainier Gonzalez, president of Latin American Grill, who was also in attendance, apologized for the complaints received and inconvenience caused to the Town. Mr. Gonzalez then moved to address both comments made by councilwoman Stefano and director Fuentes and addressed the packaging issue confirming councilwoman Stefano s comments about the impact of the packaging to the final product being received, including but not limited to lack of moisture in certain items. segs.head: - Further Discussion on the Proposed Services Agreement with River North Transit,LLC For On-Demand Commuter Transit Circulator Services in the Town of Medley.
segs.text: - Further Discussion on the Proposed Services Agreement with River North Transit,LLC For On-Demand Commuter Transit Circulator Services in the Town of Medley. Jorge Corzo, Director of the Capital Improvements and Economic Development department gave an overview of the items presented for discussion. In continuance, Stuart Robinson from Kimley- Horn&Associates carried out a presentation about the Multimodal Transportation plan adopted by the Town in 2017 which addressed bicycle and transportation methods that included circulators. It was stated that the Town had received a grant from the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) for the eastern corridor to the community that included a 30-minute loop running transportation route. Thus, said services could be advantageous for the NW 79 Place,North of NW 74 street and East of the intersection of NW 74 Avenue and West 12 Street. In continuance Olivia Blahut from River North Transit,LLC went over a presentation(see attached) that included a video of current transportation services provided in the city of Arlington Texas that included case studies, benefits to riders and communities as well as the necessary steps to follow. The presentation included the explanation of Micro Transit services that are currently in service in Miami-Dade County, Broward County, Fort-Lauderdale, City of Gainesville, Orlando and many more along with the overview of Go Connect transportation services that are also in existence in Miami-Dade County. A detailed explanation of the functions of the services was provided as well as a detailed explanation of the call-in request service phone application available to riders for efficiency. In addition,the operations of the proposed transportation services were also discussed in detail, and it was stated that the hours of operations could be adjusted if desired. Director Corzo stated that an independent contract is to be negotiated and depending on the funding, the hours of operations and fees, if any, could be adjusted leaving it up to the Town and how the Town would decide to structure the circulator program.Mr.Corzo further stated that FDOT funding and the Town were approved and committed to for 3 years and that the Town has already secured funding for 2 years,but additional funding could be requested for further participation if desired. segs.head: - Claims Management (Worker s Compensation Perspective) Mr.
segs.text: - Claims Management (Worker s Compensation Perspective) Mr. Kittleson further stated that the goal of establishing a program is reduce the amount of workers compensations claims, thus liability and impact to the policy. Mr. Kittleson also mentioned he was happy to share templates to facilitate the Town s process in adopting a safety rider program within a comprehensive safety program. Mr. Reynolds took the opportunity and explained the reason why the safety meetings are taking place and gave an overview of the Town s claim history highlighting that the Town had amazing claim results over the years. However, in just the 2020/2021 year eleven (11) claims were reported potentially costing the Town over one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) in losses which prompted a need to involve the administration to ultimately set a goal to reduce this cost and injuries in the workplace. The claims and payout amounts were discussed and explained as follows for each fiscal year. 2020-2021 -11 Claims -Potentially and Expected to have $ 700,000.00 payout in Worker s Compensation Claims -Goal is to reduce cost. 2019/2020 -8 Claims -5 Closed Claims totaling to $ 173,000.00 payouts to date. $27,000.00 remaining in reserve. 2018/2019 -16 Claims -15 Closed with $500,000.00 payout and $90,000 in reserve 2017/2018 -15 Claims -14 Closed $158,000.00 Payout. $300,000.00 in reserve. 2016/2015 -6 Claims

segs.head: - Payout of $220,000.00 Mr.
segs.text: - Payout of $220,000.00 Mr. Reynolds continued to explain that the Town should focus on safety and continued training as increased expenses continue to create an impact. It was encouraged to practice safety approaches, such as groups whenever lifting is expected to avoid injuries and protocols should be put in place to change the mindset of employees so that caution is exercised when taking on tasks to ensure safety and prevent accidents. It was also stated that establishing preventable measures require the involvement of the directors so they may disseminate the information down to employees. Mr. Reynolds then continued with the discussion and reflected on the problem areas of the previous five (5) years. Mr. Reynold further discussed the reported fifty-four (54) claims reported and submitted over the five (5) years spam which 12 had been slip and fall claims given the amount, had been the most common nature of claims which could be prevented by adjusting safety gear such as shoes. In addition, Mr. Reynolds addressed the 9 strain claims reported as they most likely were associated with lifting tasks that could be easily prevented by educating and adjusting employee s mentality to waiting until there is assistance from others. Hit claims were also discussed as a total of thirteen (13) claims had been reported and the usage of proper gear like gloves could potentially reduce incidents. Lastly, automobile claims were also address as a total of four (4) claims resulted in physical injuries, and overall represented the most financial impact to the Town s policy. It was concluded that it was important to determine the issues the Town can have control over and that it was emphasized that it was imperative to act on the areas that lack focus. In addition, it was recommended to implement safety trainings but also establish a progressive disciplinary policy to address preventable claims that could result in modified behavior for operating procedures. It was also noted that the police department has policies in place that could be considered to set a starting point for the general use. In conclusion, Mr. Reynolds addressed the department heads and asked them to think of ideas that could be discussed to prevent claims and promote safety in their own departments. Therefore, he would like to readdress the question and consider any ideas and/or input on the matter at the next safety committee meeting. segs.text: MINUTES OF A MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA OCTOBER 20, 2021, COUNCIL WORKSHOP A public meeting of the Town Council was called to order on October 20, 2021, at 4:00pm. Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the Council and began by stating that only part-time employees and residents should apply for the Start-Up grant program and that a resident who is also a full-time employee, should abide by the FPE bargaining agreement and should only be permitted to apply as such. Town attorney Lillian Arango stated that it was confirmed that language provided for the benefit is also included in the employee s handbook. Councilwoman Ayala asked about the education reimbursement ordinance and when it was last amended, and it was clarified that the ordinance had not been amended to reflect current policy. However, the employee manual, which through its adoption, included language superseding said ordinance and repealed any conflicting language that may arise on the matter. The tuition reimbursement practices were also explained including but not limited to, the requirement of courses to be pre-approved by the department head after determining their association with the employee s cope of work and duties. Human Resources Director Olga Quin further explained that in the past employees were directed to their directors because the courses needed to fall within the job duties of those individuals, but it s been determined that a lot of positions, especially those that don t afford a lot of growth, difficulted and challenged the courses approval process in general. Therefore, the pre-approval process of said courses cause a confusion because some degrees require courses such as electives, that in most cases, do not fall under the scope of work of any individual in any classification. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Business Insurance Policy.
votes: councilperson Ayala placed a motion as follows, TO RENEW THE TOWN OF MEDLEY BUSINESS INSURANCE POLICY AS RECOMMENDED EFFECTIVE 11/01/2021. Mayor Martell seconded, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Business Insurance Policy. Bob Reynolds from Morris and Reynolds Insurance addressed the Mayor and Council and began to discuss his recommendation for the renewal of the Town s business insurance policy. He also gave an update on the Town s medical insurance upcoming policy renewal and announced that there will be zero increase in the Cigna healthcare plan for 2022. However, Mr. Reynolds also stated that competitive rates from other insurance companies had been received and hopes to negotiate a reduction for the Town. Mr. Reynolds further informed the Town of the increase in the cyber security liability portion of the policy driven by claim severity and frequency of the market for this matter. Thus, it was recommended to renew with Axis as they continue to be the most competitive in terms of pricing and broad coverage. It was also instructed that all department heads review the list of vehicles under the Town s general auto and insurance liability policy and advise if any are not in use so they may be sold and removed from the policy. Without further discussion councilperson Ayala placed a motion as follows, TO RENEW THE TOWN OF MEDLEY BUSINESS INSURANCE POLICY AS RECOMMENDED EFFECTIVE 11/01/2021. Mayor Martell seconded, and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on New Proposed Commercial Water and Sewer Rates and Results of the Water and Sewer Study Performed by Tetra Tech.
votes: Vice Mayor Pacheco then placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE PROPOSED COMMERCIAL WATER AND SEWER RATE INCREASE AND TO BRING BACK THE MATTER FOR FINAL APPROVAL BEFORE COUNCIL IN DECEMBER TO IMPLEMENT SAID INCREASE IN THE JANUARY 2022 BILLING CYCLE. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on New Proposed Commercial Water and Sewer Rates and Results of the Water and Sewer Study Performed by Tetra Tech. Finance Director Roy Danziger began addressing the matter by discussing the handout included in the agenda package which was previously circulated for the council and went over his recommendations from the water and sewer rates study as highlighted. Director Danziger further stated that the recommendation for the water is to raise the rate to $9.34 for every 1000 gallons over the 5000 gallons consumption with a base rate of $53.80, and the sewer recommendation is to raise the rate to $6.76 per every 1000 over the 5000 gallons consumption. Director Danziger also stated that the average bill increase will be 9% and that the water rates would basically remain as and reflecting said change in the base rate according to meter size. It was also stated that changes as proposed would generate an estimated revenue of $300,000 a year but the increase would not be burden on the minimal and average users but on the heavier consumers. Finance Director Danziger continued and stated that the recommendation is to have the increase effective by the January billing thus bringing it before council in the December regular meeting for final review and approval. Utilities Director Jorge Soto joined the discussion and explained that luckily the infiltration of rain has been recently low but there are many necessary and ongoing repairs to the sewer system. Vice Mayor Pacheco then placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE PROPOSED COMMERCIAL WATER AND SEWER RATE INCREASE AND TO BRING BACK THE MATTER FOR FINAL APPROVAL BEFORE COUNCIL IN DECEMBER TO IMPLEMENT SAID INCREASE IN THE JANUARY 2022 BILLING CYCLE. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Start-Up Grant Program and Education Finance Director Roy Danziger recommended that only part time resident employees apply for the startup grant. Thus, full-time employees would follow the FPE collective bargaining agreement and apply for the education reimbursement benefit. It was also discussed and determined that the pre-approval process of classes would not be limited to the employee s scope of work and classes would to be analyzed as it is the opinion of the Town that any education improves and enhances job positions. It was also noted that approval based on the educational institution is to be revised to include non-conventional organizations and other educational institutions. However, it was also agreed that said proposal and recommendation is not to be presented to the FPE for bargaining until the 2022 bargaining session. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Ayala placed a motion as follows, TO ALLOW ONLY PART TIME EMPLOYEES TO APPLY AND QUALIFY FOR THE START UP GRANT PROGRAM AND ALL FULL TIME EMPLOYEES TO ONLY BE AFFORDED THE OPTION OF THE EDUCATION REIMBURSEMENT BENEFIT AS STIPULATED BY THE FPE COLLECTIVE BARGAINING GREEMENT. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on Town of Medley and Elected Officials Sponsored Events.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Town of Medley and Elected Officials Sponsored Events. Social Services and Parks and Recreation Director Lizmari Valido approached the Town Council and requested clarification and distinction between Town of Medley events and events that are sponsored and/or led by Councilmembers. Director Valido further stated that clarification on the language to be used for notices for both said types of events was also in need of clarification. Director Valido continued and stated that it was unclear to her when an event should be classified as hosted by, led by, or sponsored by an elected official, and when it is okay for her to follow instructions from an elected official to properly advertise and notify the public of such events. Councilwoman Ayala stated that events held by the council using their allocated funds should be considered hosted and all other Town paid events should be solely Town of Medley events. Vice Mayor Pacheco announced that next month the COVID- 19 booster vaccine will be made available for residents at Tobie Wilson Park that will not be an event but a public health issue. Thus, he requested the same assistance previously provided by Lizmari and as he believes, because it is a public safety issue, should be everyone s responsibility to do their part. Thus. He recommended Lizmari and Susana to assist him once again alongside the council s assistant Rosa Palau. Councilperson Ayala explained how he has felt impacted by the practice of other elected officials announcing on code red events sponsored by or hosted by but would not question Director Valido because he is aware that she is only acting as she is instructed. Councilwoman Stefano suggested that all Town of Medley events should not be hosted or sponsored by, they should simply state that all residents are invited by the Town of Medley. After a brief discussion Councilwoman Stefano placed a motion as follows, TO HAVE ANY EVENT LED BY THE MAYOR AND/OR COUNCILMEMBER USING THEIR ALLOCATED FUNDS TO BE CONSIDERED HOSTED BY THAT INDIVIDUAL AND ALL ARRANGEMENTS ARE TO BE MADE BY THEIR ASSISTANT WHO WILL COMMUNICATE WITH DIRECTOR VALIDO FOR COORDINATION PURPOSES AND IF STAFF IS NEEDED THE MAYOR IS TO BE ASKED DIRECTLY. ALL TOWN OF MEDLEY EVENTS WILL NO LONGER REFER TO THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL BUT WILL INSTEAD BE AN INVITATION FROM THE TOWN OF MEDLEY. Councilwoman Ayala seconded and it carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Duties and Supervision of a Janitorial and Custodial Services Employee. Director Valido began the discussion of the matter by reiterating that this item was not being presented because she has had any issues with the individual as an employee, but because it was suggested that the employee be assigned additional duties in other departments. She continued to explain that she does not have the time to go to other areas and supervise an employee that performs job duties that are not in line with her department. Director Valido continued to address comments made at the regular council meeting and stated that she deserved an apology as well as Lucelly Arena for comments made from a previous incident that are not relevant with the current issue. Lucelly Arenas then approached the podium and assistant utilities director Osmanny Larzabal assisted in translating her statement. It was brought to her attention that her name had been brought up in a public forum as subject matter. Director Valido then continued to translate Mrs. Arenas statement. Mrs. Arenas stated that what began as just another job had turned into an obstacle. She explained that her previous supervisor Omar Sanchez fired her maliciously and then the Mayor and Vice mayor reinstated her. And then Ms. Valido became her supervisor but legally she was still under the janitorial department. Ms. Arenas addressed questions to the Town Attorney to which she was responded that the presentation was to the Town and not employees and thus, it was incorrect for an employee to go before the council to ask legal questions against the Town. Ms. Arena continued to express that she should not be working under the supervision of Director Sanchez and would like to continue under the supervision of Ms. Valido. She then respectfully requested that she not be spoken about without her knowledge at any meeting or gatherings of the Town Council. Director Sanchez then approached the Mayor and Council and stated that as he had explained before, he had given Ms. Arenas multiple opportunities to do her job correctly, but she continued to not perform her duties adequately. Thus, he had made the decision to terminate her. Vice Mayor Pacheco joined the discussion and stated that the Council needed to be held accountable for allowing things to happen. He then suggested that Director Valido continue to be Ms. Arenas supervisor and for her to be completely removed from the Custodial and Janitorial Service

segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY APRIL12, 2022 SAFETY COMMITEE MEETING A public meeting of the Town of Medley was called to order on January 11, 2022 at 10:00 am. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ Department heads were also in attendance and a sign-in sheet was provided. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez opened the meeting giving a general overview of the topics of discussion as well as the goal of the safety committee in general. She continued to state that the Town has continued to provide and assign effective trainings with the goal to ensure safety and safe work areas. Bob Reynolds from Morris and Reynolds Insurance began the discussion by stating that continued quarterly meetings are wise in ensuring workplace safety awareness. In continuance, he began to give a claim s overview for the current and recent fiscal years. 2021-2022 A favorable trend for the year to date -7 workers comp claims, 4 settled, 3 ongoing. Claims totaling to $6,500.00 payout with $4,000 remaining in reserves. 2020-2021- Terrible year in claims -11 Claims, 7 closed, 4 ongoing. Estimated $700,000 loss with the majority specific to one incident. To date $205,000 has been paid, and an estimated 433,000 pending to be paid for ongoing medical expenses, disabilities, and employee wages. In addition, to emphasize the impact only one claim can have he states the exact expenses to date for 20/21 totaling to $697,000 in losses, with $639,000 expenses being for that one claim. 2019/2020 Fair/Below average results year -8 Claims -7 Closed Claims totaling to $ 183,000.00 payouts to date. To conclude, Mr. Reynolds encouraged Town directors to find ways to reduce incidents, and explained that high claims equal high premiums, therefore limiting insurance availability. Mr. Reynolds reiterated that it is the actions taken by the directors to prioritize safety that allows for improvement. In continuance with the agenda, a discussion was held on the Town safety program trainings. It was stated that vector program trainings have continued to be completed and additional outsourced trainings have been performed by Public Works and the Utilities department such as driving safety, hand and power tool, and confined space entry trainings. Once again, it was discussed how imperative it is for the directors to disseminate the right resources, information and trainings to the employees to ensure safety and reduce exposure to hazards in the workplace. segs.text: - Resolution Approving and Adopting the Town of Medley Town Center Visioning Master Plan (February 2022) for Transit Oriented Development; Authorizing the Town Mayor and Town Officials to Take all Action Necessary to Implement the Visioning Plan, Including Amendments to the Comprehensive Plan and Zoning Code. Councilwoman Ayala asked Director Corzo for clarification on the item. Capital projects and economic development director Jorge Corzo approached the podium and explained that the plan presented would allow the Town to have some input on what types of development will be permitted and attracted in the area. He explained that the timing is ideal because Miami is now becoming the hub for technology, and many investors are looking to develop in Medley, thus the goal is to allow the zoning and the development to line up with potential investments. Councilwoman Ayala briefly defined gentrification as the process whereby the character of a poor urban area is changed by wealthier people moving in, improving housing, and attracting new businesses, typically displacing current inhabitants in the process. In addition, she explained that the current resident s average income is thirty thousand a year and they would not benefit from this project. Director Corzo stated that the plan has zero effect on gentrification because there are no residential components in the plan as the proposal goes hand and hand with economic growth and employment opportunities. Director Corzo continued to explain that his office has received entities interested in development the area in question and with council approval the Town will have input in what kind of development will be permitted, making the proposed plan a vision for the next thirty to fifty years. In addition, director Corzo explained that without setting conditions and guidelines the Town would be allowing for all kind of industrial development including but not limited to gas and chemical companies. Councilperson Ayala joined the discussion and stated that although the purpose of the plan is for the Town to prosper, he does not see any benefit for the residents. Director Corzo explained that the Town periodically receives donated funds from Waste Management which aids in funding several Town social services programs, but the Waste Management landfill will eventually cease operations and will no longer generate the tax base. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW BOARD APRIL 28, 2022 A public meeting of the administrative review board in accordance with Florida Statute 286.011 was called to order on April 28, 2022, at 3:00 p.m. The following were present: MEMBER-ELECT MICHAEL PIZZI, JR. MEMBER-ELECT MARY Y. TAYLOR TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY LILLIAN ARANGO Town Clerk Victoria Martinez opened the meeting and stated that the purpose is for the administrative review board members-elect, Mr. Michael Pizzi, Jr. and Ms. Mary Y. Taylor, to discuss, select and appoint the third member to the administrative review board regarding Ms. Olga Quin. Member-elect Mary Y. Taylor began the discussion by seeking clarification of any potential conflict of interest since she was a former employee of the Town of Medley and more precisely,the previous human resources director and had personally recommended Ms. Quin as her successor. Ms.Taylor further stated that Mr. Michael Pizzi had also served as Town attorney and has, in addition, represented Mayor Martell in a civil suit, as well as Town businesses, Town employees and most recently, elected officials of the Town. Mr. Pizzi responded that he is no longer representing any of the individuals mentioned and that conflict of interests is up to his discretion. Therefore, not an issue. Town Attorney Lillian Arango agreed and confirmed that whether a conflict of interest exists, is a decision of Mr. Pizzi's. Mr. Michael Pizzi also stated that he had no objections to Ms. Taylor's appointment to the board. In continuance, both members announced their appointees as follows, Michael Pizzi's Nominations: Richard Rand: North Miami Beach Police Chief with 30 years of experience and knowledge. Joe Geller: Has served as city attorney for Bay Harbour Island, El Portal, North Bay Village and many others. Member of the Florida Bar for over 40 years. Jose Smith: Served as city commissioner for Miami Beach for 10-20 years and serves as the city attorney for North Miami Beach. Joanna Flores: Serves as the city clerk for Opa Locka and has years of experience with personnel matters. Pamela Latimore: Serves as the president of the Florida Association of City Clerks. Ben Kuehne: Attorney for 40 years and serves as the president of the Dade-County Bar Association.

segs.text: - Resolution Approving the Work Order and Proposal with Snubbs Consulting, Inc. to Provide Professional Engineering Services for the NW 118th Way (FEC-SRD) Roadway and Drainage Improvements Project Design-Built Criteria Package. Councilperson Ayala asked Mr. Tommy Ruiz to approach the council for clarification as to the relationship between him and director Jorge Corzo. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Administrative Review Board (Board) Procedure and Appointment of Council Appointee/Member to Board (Olga Quin Termination).
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Administrative Review Board (Board) Procedure and Appointment of Council Appointee/Member to Board (Olga Quin Termination). Town Attorney Lillian Arango began the discussion by stating that at this time the Council should appoint their member for the administrative review board. Special labor counsel Caroline Saiz added that once the Town has selected their appointee, Ms. Quin would be notified, and she would have ten days to make her selection for the board. Councilperson Ayala asked to know why the Town is now initiating the administrative board process as it was his understanding that the process was to be conducted prior to the termination. Legal counsel Caroline Saiz explained that the Mayor has the authority as it relates to department heads to issue any disciplinary action or termination. Councilperson Ayala asked for additional clarification on the matter and how the Mayor can exercise his authority, whether on his own or through the Council. Mrs. Saiz explained that a decision was made by council on February 24, 2022, to terminate Ms. Quin in which the Mayor seconded the vote and then a letter was sent to Ms. Quin s attorney on March 29, 2022 where the Mayor affirmed the decision for the termination. Councilperson Ayala stated that the process will result in the same outcome if it comes before the Council for approval. Legal counsel Saiz further stated that the two chosen members would have thirty days to appoint the third member of the Administrative Review Board. Mr. Alberto Naranjo, Esq. from AN Law Firm, P.A located at 7900 Oak Lane Suite 400 Miami Lakes, Florida 33016, and legal counsel for Olga Quin, approached the Council and stated that Town Charter supersedes the employee handbook, specifically Article VII Section 1. B. which he read into the record as follows, No administrative department head shall be disciplined, demoted or dismissed until he or she has been accorded a hearing before the Administrative Review Board in accordance with such procedures as shall be adopted by ordinance. Mr. Naranjo continued to explain that the procedure is being conducted backwards. In addition, he also stated that the employee handbook on page 35 it also reiterates the process reflected in the Town charter, and requests that the Town s appointee not be subject to any conflict of interest. Councilperson Ayala then requested to see the Town Charter and the referenced article to which the Town Clerk provided a copy. Vice-Mayor
