segs.head: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC INFORMATIONAL MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA AUGUST 25, 2022 A Public Informational Meeting of the Town of Medley took place on August 25, 2022, at 6:00 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC INFORMATIONAL MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA AUGUST 25, 2022 A Public Informational Meeting of the Town of Medley took place on August 25, 2022, at 6:00 p.m. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi opened the public informational meeting at 6:00 and announced that meeting would begin at 6:10 pm to provide additional time for public arrival. Meeting resumed at 6:10 pm and Town Clerk Victoria Martinez continued to read the code of conduct for all in attendance. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi further stated that the purpose of the informational meeting,as stated in the notice mailed to each property owner, was to present and discuss the 07-Curtis Capital Assessment Area. In addition, Town attorney Pizzi gave a brief introduction explaining the legal background of the creation of an assessment district and how it provides for improvements to infrastructure and how these improvements have proven to be successful in providing benefits to business owners. Mr. Pizzi introduced Town staff as follows: Tommy Ruiz, Interim Town Engineer Roy Danziger Finance Director Victoria Martinez, Town Clerk Keidy Guzman, Project Engineer Snubbs Consulting Inc. Interim Town Engineer Tommy Ruiz discussed in detail the presentation which addressed the special assessment information as provided to everyone in attendance (see attached) for the 07- Curtis district. Mr. Ruiz explained in detail the funding methodology, project details and the assessment and funding methodology including but not limited to how a non-Ad valorem assessment is not based on the value of the property, how a special benefit must be assessed, and the fair and reasonable distribution of the costs amongst all property owners depending on the direct benefit, and the Town. Town Attorney Pizzi also announced that everyone present was welcomed to speak, address their concerns, and ask questions. It was also stated that property owners could also schedule meetings with staff, or approach staff members privately after the meeting should they wished. After the presentation ended,the meeting was then opened for public comment and participation. It was noted that Town staff would provide answers at the end of the public comments. Mr. Gary Bonacci representative of The Eastern Management Group (Parcel 07-37) approached the podium and asked how the funding methodology was determined and how the Town justifies the assessment as his property is one with the highest assessed. Yanays del Busto,owner of La Rosa&Son'

segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA AUGUST 3, 2022 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on August 3, 2022, at 6:00p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA KARINA PACHECO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: MICHAEL A. PIZZI The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Pacheco and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by everyone in attendance. A motion to adopt the meeting's agenda was placed by Councilperson Ayala. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and the agenda for the night's meeting was adopted unanimously. In continuance Mayor Martell opened the meeting for public comment and no comments were made. Mayor Martell then instructed Town Attorney Michael A. Pizzi to read item A as reflected on the agenda. The item was read into the record and discussed as follows: - Discussion and Action on the Appeal of the Administrative Review Board Regarding Ms. Olga Quin. The Mayor then began the discussion by stating his intent to affirm the employment termination of Ms. Olga Quin and to reverse the administrative review board's recommendation. Councilperson Ayala then asked for clarification on the Administrative Review Boards decision. Therefore, Town Attorney Michael Pizzi presented the transcript which stated that the Administrative Review Board Hearing findings resulted in a 2/1 vote from the appointee members, whereas the majority recommended for the Town to reverse their termination of Ms. Olga Quin. Mr. Pizzi continued to state that the Mayor's intent is to appeal that recommendation and to affirm the termination of said employee. It was also noted that the Mayor was to abstain unless the vote is tied.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action to Waive the Procurement Process for Architectural Services for the New Construction of the Town of Medley Recreational Facility (Adjacent to the Danny Meehan Recreational Field). Mayor Martell then stated that his intent is to place a motion to waive the competitive process and instruct staff to use expeditious legal process to effectuate the above mentioned projects. Councilperson Ayala then clarified for the public that the three items presented include the Lakeside Recreation Center modifications, the construction of a new public works facility and a building to be located by the Danny Meehan Park. Interim Town Engineer Tommy Ruiz approached the podium and explained that the proposal will still follow state processes but would allow expedition by saving the Town sixty(60)days. Mr. Ruiz further stated that a selection committee consisting of the Town engineer, the Town attorney and a third professional party who will then present their recommendation for selection to the Council for formal approval. Mr. Ruiz also explained that the cause for which the Town has decided to pursue an expedited process is because a grant has been awarded to the Town with a deadline for completion of October 2023. For further clarification Mr. Ruiz explained the process as follows, -The Town compiles a package of requirements, a Request for Proposal (RFP); -Professionals will then submit required documents to the Town; -The Committee will review, select, and bring forth recommendation to the Town Council for final approval. It was also clarified that the grant received was only for the Lakeside Improvement project in the amount of$200,000. Councilperson Ayala asked for clarification on the reasons for the proposal for the three projects when the deadline only applies to the Lakeside Improvements project. Councilman Ayala further stated his disagreement with allowing the Mayor to make the decision on which contractor to perform the job when the community pool project has not been completed since 2014. Councilwoman Ayala stated that she has no documentation supporting staff's statement and that the agenda does not reflect what staff is proposing. Additionally, Councilwoman Ayala stated that she supports any Town improvements and can be lenient with the Lakeside project but believes that government loses its integrity when they bypass processes, thus she will not support bypassing procurement processes. Utilities director Jorge Soto approached the podium

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Sale of Parcel B to include a Deed Restriction to Only Allow for the Construction and Operation of a Long-Term, Short-Term, Rehab, and Medical Facility. Mayor Martell stated that his proposal is to sell the property with deed restrictions. Maritza Jimenez resident of the Lakeside Retirement Park located at 10601 NW 105 Way Lot 669, expressed the want, and need for a senior facility for the residents. Vice-Mayor Pacheco explained that he disagrees with selling Parcel B but wants to remain with the ideal of that land becoming a senior care facility. He discussed the prior intent to lease the land for the construction of a senior care facility but does not foresee the likelihood that investors will lease or buy the land to build a senior center. Hector Hidalgo resident of the Lakeside Retirement Pak located at 10601 NW 105 Way Lot 740, once more expressed that the residents need a senior care facility,but unfortunately no one has come to lease the property and without Council agreement nothing will get done. Maria Aleman, again approached the podium and urged the Council to support the Mayor and his proposal and ideals for parcel B. Mayor Martell reiterated that the attempt to sell the property is to allow for the development of a senior care facility, and the Town would impose a condition to the buyer where they must agree to the Towns terms. Councilperson Ayala proposed that if parcel B is not sold, the Town could commit to develop an assisted living facility(ALF)on the property for the residents. Town attorney Michael Pizzi was then addressed and asked if the Town could restrict an ALF to only Town residents. Mr. Pizzi then stated that although he did not have a definitive answer at the moment it is unlikely that the State would allow restricting an ALF to only Medley residents. Mr. Pizzi continued to explain that the Mayor's proposal would include a clause where the sale of the property can be reverted if the terms imposed are not met. After a brief discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO SELL PARCEL B WITH DEED RESTRICTIONS AND A REVERTER CLAUSE TO INCLUDE CONDITIONS FOR THE BUYER TO DEVELOP AND OPERATE A LONGTERM, SHORT-TERM REHABILITATION AND MEDICAL FACILITY." segs.text: - Introduction of Newly Elected Miami-Dade County Commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez for Miami-Dade Board of Commissioners, District 12. Newly Elected Commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez approached the podium and thanked the community as well as the Mayor and Council for their support in his election. segs.text: Resolution C-2053 Approving Work Order and Proposal with Snubbs Consulting Inc. to Provide Professional Engineering Services for 2023 Consent Decree Compliance Continuing Services. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi explained that the County is under a consent decree where the state and federal government require them to clean up the sewer system and take steps to fix the sewer system | back up. Mr. Pizzi further explained that the Town of Medley, as part of Miami-Dade County and part of that system, is required to also comply with the consent decree and Snubbs Consulting currently has an agreement with the Water and Sewer Department. Town Attorney Pizzi agreed that a periodic RFQ s can be performed to comply with the Town s Procurement Ordinance. Mayor Martell then placed a motion to adopt Resolution C-2053 as presented. segs.head: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on the Sale of Parcel B to include a Deed Restriction to only allow for the Construction and Operation of a Long-Term, Short- Term, Rehab, and Medical Facility.
segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on the Sale of Parcel B to include a Deed Restriction to only allow for the Construction and Operation of a Long-Term, Short- Term, Rehab, and Medical Facility. Mayor Martell began the discussion by proposing to sell parcel B with deed restrictions to only allow for the operation of a long-term, short-term, rehabilitation and medical facility. Vice- Mayor Ayala instructed Town attorney Pizzi to read section 135 and further explained that the resolution details the surplus property as a property with no value to the community, when he believes that the property can serve beneficial purposes to the residents but not with the use presented by the Mayor. Vice-Mayor Ayala continued to state that he met with a federal representative from Housing Urban Development (HUD) which explained that if the Town uses the property to create a housing location, the Town then can receive funds in the millions of dollars from the federal government to develop a housing living space for the residents. In addition, Vice-Mayor Ayala urged the Council to decide on keeping Parcel B for the opportunity to later develop a beneficial housing community for the residents and further stated that selling the property with a deed restriction and the required criteria will result in a very low sale price. Councilperson Pacheco joined the discussion and reminded the Council that this land was donated to the Town and that he had previously opposed to the sale of Parcel B. Councilperson Pacheco further expressed his concerns with whether the sale will bring a benefit to the Town, and that the opportunity has been public and there has yet to be an investor interested in building a senior care facility. Councilperson Pacheco then reiterated that a rehabilitation center would be beneficial for the community, and that he is now ready to support the item with the following conditions to be included in the motion,

segs.head: - That the sale of parcel B be solely for the benefit of the residents;
segs.text: - That the sale of parcel B be solely for the benefit of the residents;

segs.head: - To instruct the Town Attorney to come back with language detailing the fair bid process and include language that the purchaser must use the property for a rehab medical facility to benefit the residents;
segs.text: - To instruct the Town Attorney to come back with language detailing the fair bid process and include language that the purchaser must use the property for a rehab medical facility to benefit the residents;

segs.head: - To bring for Council approval the approval for the bid process and sale process;
segs.text: - To bring for Council approval the approval for the bid process and sale process;

segs.head: - To allocate funds from sale of parcel B to go towards the Lakeside Retirement Park conceptual plan. A discussion was then held to determine the duration for the deed restriction and Town Attorney Pizzi explained that a deed restriction covenant would be recorded to allow for the restriction to carry on with the land forever, and to also include a reverter clause that would clearly define that if the land is not used for the purpose specified, and the agreement is violated, then the property would automatically revert back to the Town of Medley.
segs.text: - To allocate funds from sale of parcel B to go towards the Lakeside Retirement Park conceptual plan. A discussion was then held to determine the duration for the deed restriction and Town Attorney Pizzi explained that a deed restriction covenant would be recorded to allow for the restriction to carry on with the land forever, and to also include a reverter clause that would clearly define that if the land is not used for the purpose specified, and the agreement is violated, then the property would automatically revert back to the Town of Medley. Councilwoman Ayala expressed that the proposed conditions were anecdotal and that there was not a clear understanding of the health care system. Councilwoman Ayala further stated that no investor will want to invest in a sale with these myriads of conditions being placed. Additionally, Councilwoman Ayala stated that the Town cannot guarantee that residents will be seen at this health care facility. Mayor Martell then added for the Town to retain the same realtor firm which assisted in the sale or the previous surplus property. Without Further discussion Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO SELL PARCEL B WITH DEED RESTRICTIONS TO ONLY ALLOW FOR THE CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION OF A LONG-TERM, SHORT-TERM REHABILITATION AND MEDICAL FACILITY AND TO INSTRUCT THE TOWN ATTORNEY TO BRING BACK TO COUNCIL THE LANGUAGE FOR THE SALE OF THE PROPERTY. IN ADDITION, THAT THE PURCHASER MUST ALLOW PROPERTY TO BE USED AS A REHABILITATION FACILITY FOR THE RESIDENTS OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, AND FOR THE TOWN COUNCIL TO VOTE ON THE SELECTION OF THE FAIR BID PROCESS. ALSO, TO ALLOCATE FUNDS FROM THE SALE OF THE PROPERTY TO BE USED FOR THE LAKESIDE CONCEPTUAL MASTER PLAN AND FOR THE SALE TO INCLUDE A RECORDED DEED RESTRICTION CONVENANT AND A REVERTER CLAUSE. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Edgar Ayala- No Councilmember Lizelh Ayala- No Councilmember Karina Pacheco- Yes Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes The motion was carried by majority of votes.

segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Waiving the Procurement Process for the Fabrication and Installation of an Aluminum Structure to be Located at the Entrance of the Lakeside Retirement Park. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Reassignment and Reclassification of the Executive Assistant to the Council.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Reassignment and Reclassification of the Executive Assistant to the Council. votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 8:54pm.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Design Phase II Lakeside Community Center Renovations. Mayor Martell then addressed Town Engineer Tommy Ruiz to provide an update on ongoing Town projects. Mr. Ruiz began his discussion with the Town s Community Pool project and stated that the Department of Health detected a safety flaw, therefore the Town decided to have the contractor fix it and has since caused the involvement of both party s legal teams. Mr. Ruiz further explained that there is a lap lane divider placed along the wall, and the Department of Health felt that the lap lane could potentially block the ladders, therefore the lanes are being removed, and structurally the pool is fine. Additionally, Mr. Ruiz explained that the Town cannot go into the property and begin performing repairs or make changes until the construction is deemed finaled because the contractor can contend that they have alleviated their obligation to finish the project. In addition, they are being assessed liquidated damages by the Town. Mr. Ruiz continued to explain that the Town is tentatively pushing for a completion date in January, and to then schedule a workshop with the Council to discuss the opening of the pool. Mr. Ruiz then continued to state that the project on 74" street has been postponed by FDOT due to utility concerns. Also, the projects located at NW 116 and NW 122 are running behind schedule due to delays and are both now pushed back to about March and April. In addition, Mr. Ruiz continued to explain that the South River Dr project between NW 72 and NW 74 has had a slow progression and they are pending to mark out the bike lanes. Lastly, Mr. Ruiz stated that for the Lakeside Improvements, the Town received a bid which is being evaluated and will bring back a conclusion to the Council with recommendations on the matter. Since there was no other business to address, Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 8:54pm. Xi. Victorid MartineZ, FRP, CMC, Town berfo/Vfartefl, Mayor

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley 2020 Annexation Application with Miami- Dade County.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley 2020 Annexation Application with Miami- Dade County. Town Attorney Pizzi explained that the County Mayor had vetoed the annexation applications presented by the Town of Medley and the Town of Virginia Gardens due to the contention of the mitigation payments. Attorney Pizzi further stated that the items were rescheduled for consideration before the board of commissioners for January 2023 and explained that the Miami-Dade County board of commissioners include 6 new commissioners who may not be familiar with the Town of Medley annexation application history. Thus, the application would be in front of the commissioners for reconsideration requiring a total of 9 votes for passage, otherwise the Town could face a redo of the annexation application process and start all over again. Attorney Pizzi explained the current options given the circumstances which include the following,

segs.head: - Ifthe vetoed decision is overridden by the Board of commissioners, The Town of Medley application moves forward with no issues to be concerned.
segs.text: - Ifthe vetoed decision is overridden by the Board of commissioners, The Town of Medley application moves forward with no issues to be concerned.

segs.head: - Ifthe vetoed decision is not overridden, the Town of Medley annexation application goes back to square one and the Town would have to decide on whether move forward with the annexation and a new Ordinance to presented accepting mitigation payments and have that considered and potentially passed on two readings with an interlocal agreement.
segs.text: - Ifthe vetoed decision is not overridden, the Town of Medley annexation application goes back to square one and the Town would have to decide on whether move forward with the annexation and a new Ordinance to presented accepting mitigation payments and have that considered and potentially passed on two readings with an interlocal agreement. Process could take a few months and current proposed mitigation payments $517000 a year for 7 years.

segs.head: - Consideration of Senator s Garcia motion to reconsider the item which supersedes the vote on the vetoed decision and includes the option to have the commissioners re-vote on the November 15, 2022 Town of Medley approval.
segs.text: - Consideration of Senator s Garcia motion to reconsider the item which supersedes the vote on the vetoed decision and includes the option to have the commissioners re-vote on the November 15, 2022 Town of Medley approval. Senator Garcia s proposal includes mitigation payments for four years Town attorney Pizzi explained that if a decision is made on the County Mayor s vetoed decision and the Town of Medley does not get the 9 votes of support, the approval of the Town of Medley annexation application does not take place and the application submitted is at that point dead. However, Mr. Pizzi further stated that if the motion to reconsider presented by Senator Garcia is heard and acted upon before the vetoed decision is discussed, the Town can between now and then negotiate and work on proposed language including amounts and methodology. In addition, the Town can argue that because the number one cause is police assistance, the county is saving millions of dollars and the fact that the Town is already providing police service to the areas in question. Attorney Pizzi also stated that it is possible that between now and then, the County hold their position as it is possible that changes happen regarding the mitigation payment amounts, time and calculations. He also stated that there is also something else to consider now that mitigation payments are back for discussion, and it is what would the mitigation payment entails as mitigation payment is determined by a methodology composed of revenue loss. Thus, the Town can argue that funds are necessary to improve the area in question and the County is not losing revenue as the financial burden would pass to the Town and the Medley and the Town is already providing police service which is a financial responsibility already absorbed by the Town which is the number one financial component of the mitigation payment argument. Attorney Pizzi further explained that when the January Board of Commissioners meeting takes place, the county could act on the motion to reconsider as proposed and the Town s negotiations can take effect. Thus, if so the case, there are two things the Town need to discuss and make a decision at a future Town Council meeting to whether or not accept the County s decision and language imposed, the amount of the mitigation payments and/or whether or not the Town wants to accept or, although it is not a good idea at the moment since a decision has not been made yet, litigate the County s decision as ot

segs.head: MINUTES OF A MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA FEBRUARY 16, 2022, COUNCIL WORKSHOP A public meeting of the Town Council was called to order on February 16, 2022, at 1:00 PM.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA FEBRUARY 16, 2022, COUNCIL WORKSHOP A public meeting of the Town Council was called to order on February 16, 2022, at 1:00 PM. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA-Joined at 1:07 pm LIZELH AYALA KARINA PACHECO TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ Town Clerk Victoria Martinez opened the public meeting and read into the record the items to be presented and discussed. - Discussion on the Future Operations of the Town of Medley Community Pool. Social Services and Parks and Recreation Director Lizmari Valido circulated a memorandum (see attached) listing the Town facilities, including the community pool. All the facilities and their respective hours of operations were discussed as well as new fee proposals. They were discussed as follows, Tobie Wilson Park: Hours of Operations as stated and in effect. Rental fee proposed to be $ 50.00 and$ 100.00 security deposit.Rental for employees and residents only. Additional Hours proposed to be $ 25.00 per hour. Facility not available for rentals for events/gatherings of 100 people or more.Rental hours to remain the same. Danny Meehan Recreational Field: Hours of operations to remain the same. Rental fee proposed to be$ 50.00 and$ 100.00 security deposit.Rental for employees and residents only. Additional Hours proposed to be$ 25.00 per hour. Facility not available for rentals for events/gatherings of 100 people or more.Rental hours to remain the same. Resident Gym: Hours of Operations to remain the same. Participation open to employees and residents. Participants must be 16 years of age or older (minors must have parent/guardian sign registration and waiver form). Each registered resident/employee is allowed one (1) guest. Residents/employees must be present for guest to use facility. Lakeside Retirement Center: Hours of Operations remain the same. Rental fee proposed to be $ 50.00 and $ 100.00 security deposit for residents and current elected officials. $ 100.00 rental fee for candidates, including incumbents. segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA FEBRUARY 24, 2022 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on February 24, 2022, at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH AYALA KARINA PACHECO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO SPECIAL LABOR COUNSEL LYNDSEY RIDER CAROLINE SAIZ The Invocation was given by Councilperson Ayala and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Mayor Martell then moved to place a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and the agenda for the night s meeting was adopted unanimously.

segs.head: Mayor Martell then opened the meeting for public comment and no comments were made.
segs.text: Mayor Martell then opened the meeting for public comment and no comments were made. Mayor Martell then addressed Vice-Mayor Pacheco to address the agenda item. The following matter was then discussed and acted upon as follows, - Discussion and Action on Personnel Administration Matters and Human Resources. Vice-Mayor Pacheco began his discussion by stating that the Town has been experiencing issues with employee morale, lack of professionalism, and leadership from the administration which has created many problems. In addition, Vice-Mayor Pacheco stated that budgets have been exploited to create departments that he believes were unnecessary, thus he proposed that it would be cost efficient for each department head to handle their own departmental employee matters with the assistance of the mayor s office and to terminate the employment of Human Resources Director Olga Quin. Councilwoman Ayala expressed that the decision to not have a human resources department is unheard of in an organization of the Town s capacity. Therefore, she disagreed with the actions and the Vice- Mayor s proposal and continued to not support the matter. Councilperson Ayala encouraged newly elected councilwoman Pacheco to not support the item for lack of understanding and knowledge of the details of the matter. In addition, Councilperson Ayala expressed his wish to hear Director Olga Quin s thoughts on the matter at hand and stated that he was aware that Ms. Quin had submitted a claim against Vice-Mayor Pacheco. Councilperson Ayala also stated that claims were made against him by a director thus initiating an investigation against him, and that he is aware that director Quin has also submitted a claim against Vice-Mayor but is not being afforded the same opportunity as the other director to initiate an investigation on the matter. In addition, he mentioned that the Vice-Mayor on other occasions has made accusations towards director Quin and questioned her job performance. He emphasized that he believes the Town should perform the same process as what was recently done. Mayor Martell then addressed director Quin who approached the council and explained that in accordance with the Town charter, an administrative board is supposed to be called for any directors to be demoted or dismissed. Director Quin also reiterated that she has filed a complaint against Vice-Mayor Pacheco and continued to explain how she attempted to meet with Vice-Mayor Pacheco on numerous occasions but unfortunate

segs.text: - Resolution Rescinding Resolution C-1885, which Adopted a Town of Medley Policy Establishing a Process for the Recruitment and Hiring of Town Employees. Mayor Martell began the discussion by explaining that the purpose to rescind Resolution C-1885 is to revert the process to how it was prior to the adoption of the hiring policy. The prior practice involved Directors expressing to the Mayor their need to hire employees for their department. Thus, if the Mayor approves the request, then directors may move along and conduct the hiring process. Once the hiring process is concluded, directors would then present their recommendation for hire before the Mayor and Council for formal approval. Councilperson Ayala stated that the policy was created after concerns from the Vice Mayor for not being a part of the hiring process and the Town wanting to establish an efficient policy when hiring employees. He continued to address the directors present and requested that any director who may want to speak on the matter approach the podium. Director Corzo stood and explained that the hiring process for his department was excessively long and strenuous. Vice Mayor interjected to explain that he was pursuing transparency in the process but did not agree with making the directors feel uncomfortable in their choice of hire or to instruct them whom to choose for their department. It was noted that the process is longer for the police department, but not strenuous. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve resolution C-1981. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follow, Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Edgar Ayala- No Councilmember Lizelh Ayala- No Councilmember Karina Pacheco - Yes Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes The motion passed by majority of vote. Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, ALL TOWN COUNCIL EVENTS AND FIELDTRIPS TO BE APPROVED BY THE MAYOR AND SCHEDULED BY THE MAYOR S OFFICE IN ADDITION TO ALL EVENT WORKSHOPS THAT WILL ALSO NEED TO BE SCHEDULED BY THE MAYOR S OFFICE. segs.head: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Lakeside Parcel B Project.
segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Lakeside Parcel B Project. Mayor Martell proposed to revert to his initial intention for the property which was to allow the construction of a short term, long term, and extended care facility for the elderly residents. He then instructed Town Clerk Victoria Martinez to translate the discussion into the Spanish language for the audience present. Councilperson Ayala wanted clarification on how the mayor expects to accomplish this goal. The Mayor explained that a Request for Information is to be put out to the public to solicit an investor for the leasing of the property and construction of a senior care facility. The proposal would be to acquire a business that would provide short-term care, long term care, extended care, and medical care facility including a medical clinic and the Town would decide the best company and the terms. Councilperson Ayala reiterated that he would like to know how the Mayor plans to guarantee the qualification of every resident that seeks these services. Mr. Lowell Dunn, owner of the property in which Lakeside Retirement Park is located, approached the Council and agreed with the proposal of a senior services facility but suggested processing in a master plan format. In addition, Mr. Dunn stated that he would like to be informed on the ongoing process and offered his assistance in the matter. Mayor Martell interjected and confirmed that the intent is to lease the land to whomever wins the contract, and the Town will establish all facility rules with the leasee. Councilperson Ayala further explained his disagreement with the proposal to sell the surplus property. He continued to express his concern for the residents living at the 8181 mobile home park and explained that the residents can be displaced at any moment and there will be no placement for the families. Councilperson Ayala stated that if that would occur the Town will could seek assistance from Mr. Dunn but if the Town would have an available S-acre property then the property can be resurfaced to create housing for the residents, but if the intent is to construct on the property, then the Town will no longer have a contingency plan if the residents from the 8181 mobile home park are forced to leave their mobile homes. Vice Mayor Pacheco addressed the lakeside residents informing them of the back-and-forth journey that deciding what to do with parcel B has been. Vice-Mayor Pacheco continued and stated that the intent

Mayor Martell addressed the item and proposed for the Council to return the credit cards assigned through the previously approved allocated funds, effective immediately. Councilperson Ayala stated that he was never in agreement with being given public funds for Council use and has never used nor charged the card since it was given. Councilwoman Ayala also wanted to note that an annual stipend of seven thousand dollars ($ 7,000) had been previously approved and in that time, she has used two thousand three hundred dollars ($2,300) to promote science, technology, engineering, and mathematic programs (STEM), for the children of the after-school program. In continuance, Councilwoman Ayala reiterated that she used the funds as they were meant to be utilized. Vice Mayor Pacheco also stated that he did not need a credit card with public funds. Councilperson Ayala stated that although the intent of the funds was to allow for all members of the Council to have the opportunity to sponsor events for the residents, the intent now is for the Council to work together for the sake of Town and residents. Councilwoman Ayala then explained that a financial report should be properly documented and submitted, and that the lack there of, has led to the Town receiving repeated audit findings that are unethical. Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, TO CANCEL THE PREVIOUS COUNCIL FUND ALLOCATION Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Issued Credit Cards.
votes: Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, TO REMOVE ALL PREVIOUS TOWN ISSUED CREDIT CARDS FROM ALL DEPARTMENT HEADS WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE MAYOR, THE CHIEF OF POLICE, THE TOWN ENGINEER, AND THE TOWN CLERK Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Issued Credit Cards. Mayor Martell addressed the item and proposed that all Town of Medley issued credit cards be removed. He continued to state that only the following individuals cards would remain, his office, Chief of Police, Engineering, and the Office of the Town Clerk. Finance Director Roy Danziger explained that accountants do not like the usage of credit cards. Councilwoman Ayala stated that this is an ongoing issue since 2019 with continued audit findings and it stems from the Town not having a centralized purchasing system, and departments buying their own supplies goes against the Town Ordinance and the Town was provided until April for compliance. In addition, she addressed the mayor and asked how the Town plans to address the purchasing system. Director Danziger explained that the Town is not told what practices to implement but given recommendations from the State. He continued to emphasize that the procurement policy is not followed at most times when items are approved by council. Town Attorney Arango joined the discussion and explained that many processes can be implemented to take steps towards centralized purchasing. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, TO REMOVE ALL PREVIOUS TOWN ISSUED CREDIT CARDS FROM ALL DEPARTMENT HEADS WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE MAYOR, THE CHIEF OF POLICE, THE TOWN ENGINEER, AND THE TOWN CLERK Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA January 25, 2022 6:00 PM A Public meeting was called to order at 6:01 pm on January 25, 2022 at the Miami-Dade County Elections Department located at 2700 NW 87 Avenue, Miami Florida 33172. name: July 21, 2022 Special Council Meeting- Budget Workshop

segs.head: First Reading of Ordinance C-462 of the Town of Medley Amending the Budget for the Fiscal Year Beginning October 1, 2021 and Ending September 30, 2022.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion to adopt Ordinance C-462. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and the first reading of the ordinance was approved unanimously.
segs.text: First Reading of Ordinance C-462 of the Town of Medley Amending the Budget for the Fiscal Year Beginning October 1, 2021 and Ending September 30, 2022. Finance Director Roy Danziger addressed the Town Council and explained the factors that required a budget amendment such as loan consolidation payments, the sale of the surplus property in the amount of 5.7 million dollars, and the special assessment district created to start collecting in the 2022 tax roll and a$ 1 million dollar surplus for the Building and Zoning department. After a brief discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion to adopt Ordinance C-462. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and the first reading of the ordinance was approved unanimously. The next item of business was discussed and acted upon as follows,

segs.head: - Discussion on the Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023.
segs.text: - Discussion on the Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023. Finance Director Roy Danziger began the discussion on the proposed budget for the Fiscal Year beginning October 1, 2022, through September 30, 2023 by announcing the goal of the meeting which was to address the budget including making changes and giving instructions on certain items in addition to setting the tentative millage rate so that it is filed to the County and the state. Director Danziger continued to explain that, taken into consideration the proposed millage rate of 3.2 mills and the projected assessed property value,there would be a projected revenue shortage of$695,000 dollars for FY 2022-2023. Mr. Danziger continued to address a list of items for discussion and possible action including a presentation (see the attached) of the budget report for said fiscal year. Director Danziger also stated that the assessed property value had increase by fifteen percent according to the DR-420 form. The budget items proposed as presented and discussed as follows:

segs.head: - Sale of Parcel B Property.
segs.text: - Sale of Parcel B Property. The proposed budget reflected the sale of a portion of the Parcel B property leaving the attached parcel of land for future Town projects. Vice-Mayor Pacheco expressed his disagreement and stated that after discussing potential uses for the property, it was never intended for the land to be sold. Mayor Martell explained that after having not received interested developers for the intended senior care facility, he believes it is a better strategy to sell the property with the condition that the respective buyer develops a senior care facility committing a portion of the facility to Medley residents.

segs.head: - No raises for non-union employees.
segs.text: - No raises for non-union employees. Vice-Mayor Pacheco expressed his disagreement and circulated a proposed estimate that included the following financial options. . Option 1- 3% increase for all employees except police officers totaling $ 315,000. . Option 2-3%increase for all employees except police officers and salaried employees totaling $ 224,000. Director Roy Danziger stated that a final decision could be made at the first budget public hearing. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez took a moment and announced that the first budget public hearing is scheduled to be held on Monday September 12, 2022 at 5:15 pm and the second and last public hearing is scheduled for Wednesday September 21 also at 5:15 pm.

segs.head: - New Special Revenue Fund.
segs.text: - New Special Revenue Fund. Director Danziger continued the presentation on the proposed budget for FY22-23 and discussed the creation of a new special revenue fund for the building department that created a venue to keep the department's revenues and expenses separately.

segs.head: - Water Budget.
segs.text: - Water Budget. Director Danziger explained that sewer costs have been significantly reduced which have provided savings to the estimated budgeted amounts. Director Danziger further stated that improvements to the sewer system have also provided for reductions in the sewer repairs and if improvements continue, reduction of sewer rates may be feasible in the future.

segs.head: - Stormwater Budget Director Danziger explained that user fees are collected by Miami-Dade County through the tax roll which provides for a substantial reduction in the professional fees previously paid for this matter.
segs.text: - Stormwater Budget Director Danziger explained that user fees are collected by Miami-Dade County through the tax roll which provides for a substantial reduction in the professional fees previously paid for this matter. The next order of business was discussed and acted upon as follows,

segs.head: - Discussion on the Proposed Tentative Millage Rate Based Upon the Certification of Taxable Value of Real and Personal Property Within the Town of Medley for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2022,through September 30, 2023. A brief discussion was held on setting the tentative millage rate emphasizing the pledge to Miami- Dade County to lower the millage rate for the annexation application process.
votes: Vice-Mayor Pacheco made a motion as follows, "TO SET THE PROPOSED TOWN OF MEDLEY AD VALOREM TAX OPERATING MILLAGE LEVY RATE AT 3.200 MILLS FOR FY 2022- 2023." Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion on the Proposed Tentative Millage Rate Based Upon the Certification of Taxable Value of Real and Personal Property Within the Town of Medley for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2022,through September 30, 2023. A brief discussion was held on setting the tentative millage rate emphasizing the pledge to Miami- Dade County to lower the millage rate for the annexation application process. Vice-Mayor Pacheco made a motion as follows, "TO SET THE PROPOSED TOWN OF MEDLEY AD VALOREM TAX OPERATING MILLAGE LEVY RATE AT 3.200 MILLS FOR FY 2022- 2023." Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously. Since there was no further business to discuss Mayor Martell made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and the meeting was adjourned at 7:17 pm on July 21, 2022. Victoria ine RP, CMC, Town Clerk oberto artell, Mayor

segs.head: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW BOARD JULY 25, 2022 A public meeting of the administrative review board in accordance with Florida Statute 286.011 was called to order on July 25, 2022, at 6:00 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW BOARD JULY 25, 2022 A public meeting of the administrative review board in accordance with Florida Statute 286.011 was called to order on July 25, 2022, at 6:00 p.m. The following were present: MEMBER-ELECT MICHAEL PIZZI JR. MEMBER-ELECT MARY Y. TAYLOR MEMBER-ELECT VALERIE KIFFIN LEWIS TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY DAVID REINER II, ESQ. SAMUEL REINER, ESQ. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez opened the meeting stating rules of conduct and further stated that the purpose for the administrative review board members, Mr. Michael Pizzi, Jr., Ms. Mary Y. Taylor, and Ms. Valerie Kiffin Lewis to discuss the termination of former employee Olga Quin. Attorney Alberto Naranjo,representing Ms. Olga Quin was first to present his case and he stated that the Town was in violation of the Town Charter by terminating Ms. Quin with no unpaid leave or discipline process. Mr. Naranjo further stated that the due process was taking place backwards although he had placed the Town on notice the day the Council decided to terminate his client. Mr. Naranjo continued to state that the Town,to this date,has not provided reasons for the decision that was made. Thus,his client seeks retroactive pay. In addition, Mr. Naranjo stated that although the Town of Medley Employee Handbook provides for a list of violations, his client was terminated without notice. Mr. Naranjo continued that his client is blamed for high attorney bills, and the Town fails to recognize that the instructed and ongoing equal pay investigation is to blame. Mr. Naranjo continued and stated that there was a male employee issue that was treated differently and was given preferred treatment causing a differential treatment. Additionally, information was leaked to a media source, and wanted to clarify that his client has nothing to gain from the information being made public. Mr. Naranjo also requested that the administrative review board members interview everyone who took part on the termination decision for accuracy. Board member Michael Pizzi stated that the EEOC is the right forum for the differential treatment claim and that the administrative review board hears the terminating of the employee. In continuance,Mr.Pizzi asked all parties to clarify whether the Town Council has the authority to create and eliminate departmental positions should they wish and whether any provisions of the Town Charter would prevent them from placing an employee on administ

Since there was no further business to be considered, Town Clerk Victoria Martinez moved to adjourn. Mayor Martell then opened the meeting for public comment and employee Niurka Castro, from the Building and Zoning Department approached the podium and addressed the Mayor and Council. Ms. Castro explained how item 13(A)4 was originally meant to be her appointment to the Building and Zoning/License Clerk III position,but she was told that she did not meet the minimum requirements for the position and was not allowed to discuss the matter further with the Mayor. Ms. Castro further explained how she had been transferred from her receptionist position to the building department without prior knowledge or consent, and since then was appointed to Building and Zoning/License Clerk II position as discussed and promised by the Mayor. She explained that she did not meet the minimum requirements at the time for the Clerk II position, but at the discretion of the Town and taking into consideration her education of a bachelor's degree she was promoted. In addition, she expressed how she has since received her master's degree and believes that the same consideration should be taken when deciding for the promotion to Building Clerk III. Furthermore, Ms. Castro explained how the Building and Zoning Director William Diaz supports her appointment to Clerk III and how she has been performing duties of the Clerk III position for some time, thus proving her capacity to fill the position. However, when she was told that the item was to be removed from the agenda, she made attempts to discuss the matter further with the Mayor as it had been prior practice, and was then told that she could not speak to him about the matter. In conclusion, Ms. Castro requested for the Mayor and Council to reconsider her promotion. Mayor Martell thanked Ms. Castro for her comment. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Cold Lunch Program. Vice-Mayor Pacheco began the discussion by explaining that he has had a myriad of residents complaining about picking up their cold lunch program sandwiches at Lakeside Retirement Park. He then proposed to move the program to the Medley Municipal Services Facilities (MMSF) and allow residents to drive up to pick up their lunches. Meal Program director Fatima Fuentes approached the Council and expressed how there was a previous attempt to do the cold lunch program at Town hall,but it did not work out for multiple reasons. Nonetheless, director Fuentes expressed that if it is the will of the council to change the location, she will do as instructed with her staff Director Fuentes also explained that there are public health safety requirements such as the refrigeration of the milk that is distributed to each household. Councilwoman Ayala agreed that the Town is required to comply with food safety regulations, or it could cause a public safety issue. A brief discussion was then held to discuss the logistics of relocating the program,and having it operated from the 2nd floor training room or from the garage as proposed by director Fuentes. Consequently, Vice-Mayor Pacheco then placed a motion as follows, "TO MOVE THE COLD LUNCH PROGRAM TO THE MEDLEY MUNICIPAL SERVICES FACILITY FOR RESIDENT PICK UP EFFECTIVE JULY 16, 2022" Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Edgar Ayala- Yes Councilmember Lizelh Ayala- Yes Councilmember Karina Pacheco - Yes Mayor Roberto Martell-No The motion was carried by majority of vote.

Therefore,he wished to discuss it at this meeting and called Mr. Corzo to the podium to discuss the matter. Mayor Martell clarified that he placed the item on the agenda to be discussed prior to the resignation effective date. He further proposed that the Town enter a contract for his services with the conditions that he work twenty-two hours a week. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW BOARD JUNE 13,2022 A public meeting of the administrative review board in accordance with Florida Statute 286.011 was called to order on June 13, 2022, at 6:00 p.m. The following were present: MEMBER-ELECT MICHAEL PIZZI, JR. MEMBER-ELECT MARY Y. TAYLOR MEMBER-ELECT VALERIE KIFFIN LEWIS TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN COUNSEL DAVID REINER II, ESQ.-joined at 6:35 PM SAM REINER, ESQ.-joined 6:35 PM Town Clerk Victoria Martinez opened the meeting with rules of conduct for the meeting and stated that the purpose is for the administrative review board members-elect, Mr. Michael Pizzi, Jr., Ms. Mary Y. Taylor, and Ms. Valerie Kiffin Lewis to discuss the termination of former employee Olga Quin. It was further stated that Ms. Quin's attorney,Alberto Naranjo,had notified the Town at around 5:08 pm of the day of, of medical issues that precluded him from attending the meeting in person,thus asking for other participation accommodations. It was also noted that Town Counsel,David Reiner was running late to the meeting. Therefore, a recess was taken at 6:16 pm to provide Mr. Reiner time to arrive. Town Clerk Martinez initiated several phone calls to Mr. Naranjo to arrange other possible accommodations as requested at no avail.Town Counsel Sam Reiner confirmed receipt of Mr.Naranjo's request to hold the meeting at a later day due to unexpected medical reasons. After a brief discussion member-elect Michael Pizzi made the following motion: "TO CONTINUE THE HEARING AT THE REQUEST OF MS. QUIN'S ATTORNEY AND INSTRUCT THE TOWN CLERK TO CONTACT ALL PARTIES AND SCHEDULE A FUTURE MEETING DATE" There were no objections by either party and the motion carried unanimously. Since there was no further business to be considered, Town Clerk Victoria Martinez moved to adjourn. The meeting was adjourned at 6:43 p.m. on June 13,2022. Victoria artinez, P, CMC, Town Clerk

OR 1 0 _'' June 21, 2022 Honorable Mayor Martell and Members of the Town Council Medley, Florida Dear Mayor Martell and Members of the Town Council: I'm pleased to present you the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) for the fiscal years 2022-2026. The CIP serves as a long-range planning tool used to help the Town match revenues with major capital needs over a 5-year period. The projects in the CIP are derived from the Town's Capital Assessment Program, Public requests, Departmental requests/recommendations,Town's Utilities Master Plans, and other economic development needs. A summary version of the CIP was provided with a recommended budget and fiscal year 2023 projects. Subsequent fiscal year projects are unfunded and presented for planning purposes only. As a result of the Town's success in recent applications for Federal and State grant opportunities, fiscal year 2023 includes a large list of projects with grant commitments. Major Factors Impacting Capital Planning Revenue: All budgets are constrained by available revenues. Capital projects are prioritized so that available funds are allocated based on need, Council priority, and their impact on service provision. Fiscal year 2023 includes funding for a variety of the Town's Capital Projects. Right-of-Way: Public Right-of-Way (R/W) acquisition is one of the biggest factors impacting most of the Town's Capital Projects. The Town has wide range of R/W deficiencies. Some common cases are existing public-maintained roads without proper R/W, encroachments of existing building into public R/W, poor R/W connectivity, and others. Environmental Considerations: Our environment is fragile and we understand the importance of environmental assessment in the very early planning stages of projects. The CIP continues to ensure our attention to compliance with Local, State, and Federal requirements. Stormwater improvements projects in our Capital Plan are required to ensure compliance with water quality requirements. In addition, Water and Sewer infrastructure improvements will enhance the reliability of the wastewater system and upgrading the size and material of the domestic water system. segs.text: ee ee en ee ee ee ere ee MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA JUNE 21, 2022 5:15 P.M. A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on June 21, 2022 at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBER: EDGAR AYALA TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: MICHAEL A. PIZZI, JR. The Invocation was given by Councilperson Ayala and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Town Council and audience. In addition, Vice Mayor addressed the council and requested to make a statement prior to the adoption of the meeting s agenda. He continued to explain the importance in discussing and acting on Item A of the agenda, which was noticed as follows, - Discussion and Action on Previously Declared Town of Medley Surplus Property Located at the NW Corner of NW 122 Street and NW 107 Avenue, Medley, Folio No. 22-2030-016-0060 and 22-2030-016-0061. Therefore, Vice Mayor Pacheco stated that he will adjourn after the discussion and action of item A. Vice | Mayor Pacheco then placed a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez asked, for clarification, if the intent was to table or withdraw item B, noticed as follows, - Discussion and Action on the Town Engineer s Proposed Professional Services Agreement. Vice Mayor Pacheco reiterated that he would adjourn and remove himself from the meeting and then asked Town Attorney Michael Pizzi to clarify further. Town attorney Pizzi explained that without Vice-Mayor Pacheco s attendance, quorum would be lost, and the Town would no longer be able to conduct the public meeting. Councilperson Ayala stated that the Council has had workshops with the previous Town attorneys and former ethics department s director Robert Meyers as well as previous Town attorney Steve Helfman where they clarified that under the Robert s Rules of Order, if a commissioner attends a meeting, they have an obligation to vote on the item and if there is a conflict then they can abstain, providing written reasoning for abstaining. Town attorney Pizzi then referred to a recent occurrence when Town s elected officials and staff attended a Miami-Dade County meeting, and several commissioners left the meeting losing quorum resulting in the meeting to end. Thus, Mr. Pizzi continued and stated that his legal opinion on the matter is that business cannot be conducted with less than three councilmembers in att

Figure 2-1: Sanderson District Limits Capital Projects & Economic Development Department Funding Methodology Report Capital Assessment District 05-Sanderson Town of Medley Within this area, NW South River Drive, NW 118th Way and NW 117th Way are Town of Medley R/Ws. The existing waterway C-6 Canal (maintained by the South Florida Water Management District) borders the northeasterly edge of the area. Following the review of the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Contamination Locator Map GIS database, no contaminated properties were observed within the study limits. However, there is an FDEP cleanup site (ID 982083115) within the limits of this District located at 10300 NW 121st Way (Duke Realty Limit Partnership). According to the FEMA Flood Zoning map, part of the Sanderson District is classified as FEMA Flood Zone AH with a base flood elevation (BFE) of 7.00 FT (NGVD). Among the R/W facilities within the District, NW 117th Way and NW 118th Way appears to be above BFE, being on FEMA Flood Zone X, which represents minimal flood hazard. On the other hand, NW South River Drive is partially located within FEMA Flood Zone AH with a BFE of 7 FT (NGVD). Ms. White proceeded to present the following findings and they were presented in detail as follows, -The study corridor limits and scope; -Existing network characteristics; -Demographic characteristics of the corridor; -Right of way limitations; -Existing and proposed typical sections; In addition, she presented other evaluated alternatives when determining the results of the assessment. | Assistant Director for the Capital Projects and Economic Development Department Manny Perez | clarified that this study is conceptual and in the planning stages to be federally funded through the FDOT LAP program. segs.text: - Resolution Amending and Approving a Revised Town of Medley Employee Handbook. Councilperson Ayala referred to the Town attorney for his legal opinion on acting or the possibility of postponing the proposed changes to the Employee handbook, since there is a pending lawsuit for the reinstatement of the former Human Resources Director Olga Quin which is directly related to the changes being proposed. Mr. Ayala also voiced concerns of conflict because Town Attorney Michael Pizzi, prior to his hire was appointed to represent the Town as a member of the Administrative Review Board. Town Attorney Michael A. Pizzi responded that after reviewing the legislative document of the employee handbook, the Town code provides for the Council to set any policy and that the Council has the legal authority to modify and amend as deemed appropriate. In addition, attorney Pizzi stated that Council had previously approved to have employees report to their department heads, thus the proposed amendments memorialize and effectuates the last direction from the Town Council. Councilperson Ayala continued to express how the Town Council had a shade meeting where legal advice had been provided to assist in cleaning up the discrepancy in the matter in which Ms. Quin was terminated. In addition, Councilmember Ayala stated that to correct Ms. Quin s wrongful termination, | the Council was advised to reinstate her to her position, with the title of absentee Human Resources Director. Mayor Martell joined the discussion and stated that he had instructed staff to include the | amendments to the employee handbook to the agenda and then proceeded to place a motion to approve | Resolution C-2008. Councilwoman Ayala asked how situations were to be mediated if employees or department heads were to have an issue with the Mayor s office and how would the Town guarantee that the employee will not experience an unfair treatment in the absence of a Human Resources Department. Attorney Pizzi responded that the action taken on this matter is entirely up to the Council and there are union positions where the collective bargaining agreement sets forth procedures, as well as an employee handbook with procedures for grievances and complaints. Attorney Pizzi further stated that employees should follow the chain of command which is to discuss the matter with their department head and if the matter does not get resolved, then it proceeds to get discussed with the Mayor s office. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Executive Assistant to the Code Compliance Chief Position for the Code Compliance Department.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Executive Assistant to the Code Compliance Chief Position for the Code Compliance Department. Jose Guasch Director or the Code Enforcement Department approached the council to recommend the hire of Ms. Suhail Rolon. Mr. Pizzi interjected to include that this individual has been doing the same duties in the City of Doral and the hiring panel was unanimous when selecting Ms. Rolon which was the only candidate fully qualified. Ms. Rolon introduced herself and explained that she began in the City of Doral as a code compliance clerk for seven years but was then promoted to the position of special master coordinator and has been performing as such for the last three years. Councilwoman Ayala requested a resume, but it was not available to be provided. Therefore, Councilwoman Ayala expressed that she could not make a conscience decision without supporting documentation. Vice Mayor Pacheco asked about the employees starting pay rate, which was noted to be twenty-six dollars an hour. Mayor included that Ms. Rolon would be on a probationary status for a duration of two (2) years to allow for the completion of continued education. Councilperson Ayala voiced his disapproval with the lack of documentation presented to Council to make a decision and then urged the Mayor to require supporting documentation when hiring matters are brought before Council. Without further discussion Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO APPOINT SUHAIL RODAN AS A FULL TIME EXECUTIVE ASSISTANT FOR THE CODE ENFORCEMENT DEPARTMENT, EFFECTIVE JUNE 7, 2022 WITH A PROBATIONARY PERIOD OF TWO (2) YEARS, AND WITH THE CONDITION THAT THE EMPLOYEE COMPLETE CONTINUED EDUCATION COURSES. ADDITIONALLY, THE EMPLOYEES RESUME IS TO BE PROVIDED TO THE COUNCIL AS SOON AS POSSIBLE Councilmember Ayala seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Edgar Ayala- Yes Councilmember Lizelh Ayala- No Councilmember Karina Pacheco - Yes Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes The motion was carried by majority of vote.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Proposed Amendment to the Town of Medley Capital Improvement Plan FY 2022-2026.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Proposed Amendment to the Town of Medley Capital Improvement Plan FY 2022-2026. Assistant Director Manny Perez approached the Council and presented the proposed amendments to the FY 2022 Capital improvement plan, and explained that a workshop will need to be scheduled to discuss the 2023 fiscal year. The proposed changes are to reduce the 14-million-dollar budget to 8.4 million dollars because some projects are not set to commence until the 2023 Fiscal Year. Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the Council and asked for clarification about whether or not the remaining 7 million dollars are anticipated to be spent within the last three months of the 2022 fiscal year. He stated that the all a a ia a ia Town is already amending the budget per the requirement for a debt refinancing, which will be presented to the Council in July, and the amendment will require to reflect what has been done throughout the year. Assistant Director Perez explained that the numbers are determined by contracts, and although the projected expenditures may not be used in the current year the department may receive bills for payment on undetermined amounts at any time. Mayor Martell instructed staff to meet and then present their proposal at a Council workshop to discuss the capital improvement plan in mid-June. In addition, Mr. Pizzi suggested that the finance department alongside the CPED department present for formal approval of the Council both the amended Capital Improvement Plan and the Budget Amendment. Councilwoman Ayala asked for clarification on the community pool. Assistant Director Perez stated that the contractor has applied for a final inspection with the building department. In addition, he explained that if the contractor received a temporary certificate of occupancy, then his department can finalize their completion of the project, otherwise they cannot consider the project substantially complete. Councilwoman also asked about an RFP issued for the Senior Healthcare center, but no status was available at the time. After a brief discussion, it was instructed that following the Council workshop, the capital improvement plan be amended at the regular July Council meeting and a subsequent special July meeting/Council workshop would be held to amend the budget.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Salary Study and Gender Analysis for the Town of Medley Prepared by Evergreen Solutions, LLC.
votes: Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, TO ACCEPT THE FINDINGS BY EVERGREEN SOLUTIONS FOR THE SALARY STUDY AND GENDER ANALYSIS, Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Salary Study and Gender Analysis for the Town of Medley Prepared by Evergreen Solutions, LLC. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi began the discussion by explaining that there are two operative points that he would like to focus on and reflected on page 28 of the study. Mr. Pizzi read the differences in salaries in this instance may be more indicative of the level of complexity of the position, role, responsibility, and salary potential of each classification. Attorney Pizzi further stated that the study also states that Based on the results of the market survey, when comparing operational level, essential skills and education/certifications, the Town offers a competitive rate of pay . Attorney Pizzi concluded that there is no evidence of any gender base discrimination in the Town of Medley salary levels according to the data. He further stated that the report states that different individuals have different levels of requirements, education, experience, and duties therefore have different salaries. Furthermore, Mr. Pizzi also concluded that Medley when comparing salaries to other cities has a competitive rate regardless of the gender. He continued to state that the study shows that there are twenty- one people with different experience levels doing entirely different unrelated positions, and the salaries are different as expected of different job titles, concluding that there is no gender discrimination. Without further discussion Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, TO ACCEPT THE FINDINGS BY EVERGREEN SOLUTIONS FOR THE SALARY STUDY AND GENDER ANALYSIS, Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded, and it carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Purchase of a Vehicle for the Building and Zoning Department in Accordance with BID FSA20-VEL28.0. Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the Council and explained that the Town received a quote for the purchase of a Chevy Silverado in the amount of $51,740.30 for the building department to be used by the Building Official. It was noted that the vehicle would not be ready until December and will be included for the 22/22 FY Budget, and said expenditure would be funded by the building department budget. Vice- Mayor Pacheco clarified that the building department budget comes from the general fund and expressed his disagreement with the purchase as well as with the money being spent and allowing the purchase of this vehicle for a probationary employee. Vice-Mayor Pacheco continued to state that he would prefer to use the funds to grant raises to other employees. Councilperson Ayala stated that after discussing the item with the building official he was informed of the Mayor s approval because the vehicle can be utilized for multiple departments as needed, and that he believes the newly appointed building official William Diaz has been doing a great job in his position. Councilwoman Pacheco joined the discussion and explained that she had been conducting town business with a Town vehicle when it suddenly broke down. Therefore, she would like to know what vehicle can best be used by the Council. Vice Mayor Pacheco also included that the Council does not have a decent vehicle for use, and there is limited availability because there are several members of the Council. Vice- Mayor Pacheco also addressed the Mayor and stated that he should not have already approved this item, because he has a twenty-five-thousand-dollar cap under the procurement process and that he does not have the authority to approve this purchase. Mayor Martell confirmed his agreement with the purchase and that he brought it before Council as required by Town code for formal approval. Mayor Martell also informed the Council that he shows no bias, as he himself uses his personal vehicle to conduct Town business. Additionally, the building official s position requires a truck to be used when performing inspections , and for some inspections some materials may be needed such as a ladder, and a truck is the best option to facilitate that use. Pursuant to ITB No.2021-034 for CIP Project No. 0121-1,NW 90th Street Stormwater Lift Station No. 2 and Retention Area; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Enter Into A Contract For Construction With the Contractor Substantially in the Form Attached Hereto as Exhibit"A". Councilwoman Ayala requested clarification on the project cost, indicated to be 2 million dollars. Town Engineer Jorge Corzo explained that the Town is responsible for 1.37 million this fiscal year with a contract totaling to 2.5 million dollars and continued to explain that he will need to present an amended five-year plan for the project, this would allow him to look at other project expenditures and relocate them if a project will not commence this year.Town Engineer Jorge Corzo also stated that the amendment will allow his department to reprogram the funds to not exceed the cap the council has approved. Councilwoman Ayala explained that his response did not satisfy her question, and then referred to the memo for recommendation detailing that the contract amount is $2,153,627.45. Councilwoman Ayala continued to ask Director Corzo to confirm the source of the funding grant given that in section 2 of the memorandum presented stated that the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) was providing for of the funding, whereas section 4 states that the Florida Department of P g $412,000.00g, P Economic opportunity was providing the grant funding. Finance Director Roy Danziger interjected and explained that due to inflation construction cost will be higher and that ATC Engineering, Inc. were the lowest costing bidder. Director Danziger continued to explain that he expected the budget this year to be accurate, but there may need to be a higher amount allocated for the following years. Councilwoman Ayala instructed to have all grant documents to be included in the exhibits for future council approved items. Mayor Martell then placed a motion to approve resolution C-1985. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Tobie Wilson Park Structural Concerns.
votes: Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, "TO DEMOLISH THE TOBIE WILSON PARK RECREATIONAL CENTER AND INSTRUCT STAFF TO PREPARE PLANS FOR A THREE-STORY BUILDING" Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Tobie Wilson Park Structural Concerns. Building and Zoning Director Diaz approached the Council stating that on February 16, 2022 he performed a visual inspection of Tobie Wilson park and then began his discussion by describing the structural damages he witnessed describing the photographs presented on the display for the council and public. In addition, Director Diaz explained that the roof was leaking, there was a metal piling with no record of permitting and that due to the rushed nature and unknown process of the installation of the metal piling he would have to declare the Tobie an unsafe structure. Director Diaz continued to state that said property has no information with the Miami-Dade County Property Appraiser, thus it was not built with permits or registered as an existing building with the County. It was noted that the building was constructed in the 1970's requiring at this time a 40-year recertification, as well as a structural study. Councilperson Ayala asked for clarification on the intent for this item and Mayor Martell proceeded to recommend that a new three-story building be built to replace the Tobie Wilson park,in compliance with the Florida Building Code to be used as a hurricane shelter. It was also stated that once a repair exceeds 25%of the structure, it is then required to bring the building's structure up to the 2022 Florida Building Code. It was clarified to Councilperson Ayala that the plans for the new facility and the repairs for the seawall will be processed simultaneously and in conjunction with one another. Vice Mayor Pacheco expressed agreement with the Mayor and stated that he would support any item that benefit the welfare of the residents. Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, "TO DEMOLISH THE TOBIE WILSON PARK RECREATIONAL CENTER AND INSTRUCT STAFF TO PREPARE PLANS FOR A THREE-STORY BUILDING" Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Request by Vice-Mayor Pacheco for Discussion and Action Regarding the Executive Assistant to the Council Position. Vice Mayor Pacheco began his discussion by explaining that he was not in agreement with the schedule of the executive assistant to the council and would like to propose that she work the same hours as the other employees of general administration. The schedule proposal would be as follows, Monday through Wednesday: 7:00 am to 5:00 pm Thursdays: 7:00 am to 4:30 pm Fridays: Off The Vice Mayor then continued explaining that when he is in need of his assistant,he sends an email and copies the other councilmembers so they are aware that she is assisting him for that day or for that moment and would like the practice implemented for everyone else so that the rest of the councilmembers can be on the same page. In continuance, he stated that no one is responsible for her daily duties, and she needs a supervisor if she is in the Town all day. Councilperson Ayala stated that Mrs. Palau is an asset to the Council. Executive assistant to the Council Rosa Palau then approached the podium and confirmed that her current schedule is Monday through Wednesday 8:00AM to 6:00PM and Thursday 8:00AM to 5:30PM. A brief discussion was held on the process for requesting Mrs. Palau's assistance, and Mrs. Palau expressed that it is difficult for her to split her assistance in events where all councilmembers are sitting apart,therefore she would like for everyone to be sitting together if she is expected to assist everyone at the same time. Additionally, she would like requests for assistance to be made two days in advance. Councilmembers agreed. Without further discussion, Vice Mayor Pacheco then placed a motion as follows, "TO CHANGE THE EXECUTIVE ASSISTANT TO THE COUNCIL SCHEDULE TO MONDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY 7:00AM TO 5:00PM AND THURSDAY 7:00AM TO 4:30PM EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY.
