segs.text: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion and Action Regarding Sponsorship of Town of Medley Resident to Attend Health Occupations Students of America (HOSA) State Competition. Ms.Liset Icaza approached the podium and thanked the Mayor and Council for allowing her to be present for the evening. She then explained that she has been a teacher for 22 years at Miami Springs Senior High School and is currently teaching in the medical academy. She has students that compete as members of the Health Occupations Students of America Club (HOSA) and at this time she would like to ask for funding assistance from the Town Council to help sponsor an upcoming competition held from April the 9th to April 12th, 2022. Accompanying her at the podium was member of the (HOSA) club and Town of Medley resident Nicole Mollinedo. Ms. Icaza further explained that unfortunately efforts to fund raise have not amounted to enough to cover for the students' accommodations, therefore she requested assistance in any amount possible from the Town of Medley. Councilwoman Ayala explained that Ms. Icaza is her former AP biology teacher and recognized that her profession matters in making a difference in the community and promoting education in young people's lives. It was clarified that the funds are to be donated directly to the school accompanied with a letter explaining that it is for the (HOSA) club so the school may allocate the funds appropriately. Ms. Icaza thanked the Mayor and Council for any support they can provide. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Ayala placed a motion as follows, "TO DONATE ONE THOUSAND DOLLARS ($1,000.00) TO MIAMI SPRINGS Ituit SENIOR HIGH SCHOOL FOR THE HEALTH OCCUPATIONS STUDENTS OF AMERICA (HOSA) CLUB." Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Pension Benefits I Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the Council to request permission to amend the Town of Medley general pension plan.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO INSTRUCT STAFF TO CONTACT THE TOWNS PENSION LEGAL COUNSEL TO DRAFT AN AMENDMENT TO THE PENSION PLAN TO CALCULATE RETIREMENT BENEFITS BASED ON THE FIVE HIGHEST EARNING YEARS IN A TEN-YEAR PERIOD." lip Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Pension Benefits I Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the Council to request permission to amend the Town of Medley general pension plan. He explained that currently the plans benefit is calculated based on the employees last five consecutive years of employment,and his proposal is to amend the policy for it to be calculated based on the employees five highest earning years in a ten-year period rather than consecutive years.The intent is to assist a long-term employee,that earned less monies one year for an injury in which workers compensation is received, and that year is being considered in the average calculation for the retirement benefit. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO INSTRUCT STAFF TO CONTACT THE TOWNS PENSION LEGAL COUNSEL TO DRAFT AN AMENDMENT TO THE PENSION PLAN TO CALCULATE RETIREMENT BENEFITS BASED ON THE FIVE HIGHEST EARNING YEARS IN A TEN-YEAR PERIOD." lip Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously. Since there were no other business to address, the meeting was adjourned at 8:30pm. c Victor artinez, FR , MC, Town Clerk obert Martell, Mayor

segs.head: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MAY 16, 2022 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on May 16, 2022, at 5:15 p.m.
votes: Vice-Mayor Pacheco then moved to place a motion to adopt the meeting's agenda. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the agenda for the night's meeting was adopted unanimously.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MAY 16, 2022 A special meeting of the Town Council was called to order on May 16, 2022, at 5:15 p.m. The following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR IVAN PACHECO COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA- ABSENT LIZELH AYALA KARINA PACHECO TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: LILLIAN ARANGO The Invocation was given by Vice-Mayor Pacheco and the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag of the United States was recited by the Council and audience. Vice-Mayor Pacheco then moved to place a motion to adopt the meeting's agenda. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the agenda for the night's meeting was adopted unanimously. Mayor Martell then opened the meeting for public comment and no comments were made. In continuance, Mayor Martell then addressed Vice-Mayor Pacheco to address the new business item on the agenda. The item was then discussed and acted upon as follows, - Review and Action to Create Greater Efficiency in Vendor Contracts and Services. Vice-Mayor Pacheco began the discussion by stating that the Town should never stop evaluating the Town's contracts and services and that the Town has, by history, been represented by local practitioners and not large firms.Vice-Mayor Pacheco continued to state that the legal bills from October 2019 through September 2020 were almost seven hundred thousand dollars and over one half million dollars from past year to date. In addition,Vice-Mayor Pacheco stated that no negative comments should be seen from his comments and the current law firm, thus his statement was merely based on policy difference. Vice-Mayor Pacheco then placed a motion as follows, "EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY UPON PASSAGE OF THE MOTION, THE TOWN TERMINATES ANY AND ALL CONTRACTS OR AGREEMENTS WITH WEISS SEROTA AND HELFMAN AND IMMEDIATELY APPOINT THE LAW FIRM OF MICHAEL PIZZI AS INTERIM ATTORNEY AND AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE AN AGREEMENT AND SPENT FUNDS UP TO A MAXIMUM OF TWENTY-FIVE THOUSAND DOLLARS A MONTH BASED ON THE URGENT NEED TO HAVE AN ATTORNEY IN PLACE FAMILIAR WITH THE TOWN."

segs.head: Mayor Martell joined the discussion and asked if the fees proposed could be negotiated to which Vice- Mayor Pacheco answered that he could negotiate the service feed and execute an agreement as such.
votes: Mayor Martell moved to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 5:23 p.
segs.text: Mayor Martell joined the discussion and asked if the fees proposed could be negotiated to which Vice- Mayor Pacheco answered that he could negotiate the service feed and execute an agreement as such. Town attorney Lillian Arango interjected and stated that a professional courtesy would have been appreciated before the public humiliation towards the firm and the offensive manner in which the termination was being conducted. Ms. Arango further stated that Weiss Serota and Helfman provided specialized services for almost 10 years, and that it was shocking to learn that the Town would be addressing the matter without a professional and frank conversation to address the Town's needs and wishes, including but not limited to financial concerns. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Edgar Ayala- Absent Councilmember Lizelh Ayala-No Councilmember Karina Pacheco - Yes Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes Councilwoman Ayala thanked attorney Lillian Arango for the services and professionalism demonstrated throughout the years and apologized for the manner in which the Council had chosen to address the matter in question. Mayor Martell also thanked Ms. Arango for the services and stated that finances are always an issue. Since there was no further business to be considered, Mayor Martell moved to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 5:23 p.m. on May 16, 2022. Victoria artinez RP, CMC, Town Clerk obe o Martell, Mayor

segs.text: - Presentation by the Medley Police Department of the Chief's Award. Chief Said-Jinete presented the first item and stated that by recommendation officer Gonzalo "Gonzo" Garcia is presented with the Officer of the Bid Award. Captain Jack Young then continued to explain that a bid is a six-month work period and that Officer Garcia is being recognized for not only his work as a supervisor, but also for the knowledge he provides when he performs training for the staff in the police department, which is above his job duties. votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-456 on first reading, Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: Ordinance C-456 of the Town of Medley, Florida,Amending Section 62-8 of the Town Code to Reference a Specific Updated Version of the Official Zoning Map of the Town; Deleting Section 62-8(c) of the Town Code Referencing C-2 Zoned Properties; Formally Adopting the Updated Zoning Map and Attaching it to the Code as an Exhibit; Providing for Severability; Providing for Inclusion in the Code; Providing for Conflicts; and Providing for an Effective Date. James "Jim" Hickey representing the Town's Zoning/Planning consultant Calvin Giordano and Associates, approached the Council and explained that the proposed Ordinance is to amend the Town code to formally adopt a zoning map of the Town. He clarified that the handouts presented to the Council shows what is called a map atlas,which helps identify and clarify the zoning uses for each folio. He also explained that the solid waste district was not previously included but is now being codified to be included in the Town's zoning map. Councilperson Ayala asked for clarification on a section of the map, and Mr. Hickey then explained that the map has different layers to identify zoning within the map. Mr. Hickey continued to explain that this first reading of the ordinance is to adopt an official map because the remaining ordinances being proposed cannot be applied to a map that had not been adopted,thus adopting the map to set a guideline. Town Attorney Lillian Arango affirmed that the zoning map needed to be adopted to move forward with the map designations, and then the map will be amended to include the changes in the remaining ordinances. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-456 on first reading, Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-455 on second reading. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - An Ordinance of the Town of Medley, Florida, Amending Section 2-86 of The Code, "Settlement; Disposition of All Collected Fines And Liens" To Read "Mitigation of Fines, Penalties and Liens"; Establishing Procedures And Guidelines For The Mitigation of Code Enforcement Fines, Penalties And Liens; Providing For Codification; Providing For Severability; Providing For Conflicts; And Providing For An Effective Date. Mayor Martell then opened the item for discussion, and Mr. Kenneth Dougal with Bilzin Sumburg with office located at 1450 Brickell Ave Miami, Florida approached the Council and explained that he was representing Florida Wood Recycling. It was noted that the public comments were limited to three minutes. Mr. Dougal explained that a letter was sent to the Mayorreflecting and Council, a recent court ordered g mandate between his client and the Town of Medley. Mr. Douglas further stated that on March 9, 2022 the court order resolved the dispute of the imposition of fines which was wiped out by the court. Mr. Dougal also stated his presence before the Town Council was to confirm that the Ordinance's adoption would not have retroactive effects on his client, explaining that doing so may cause legal ramifications. Jose Arango Town special legal counsel with offices formerly located at 2525 Ponce De Leon Boulevard, Coral Gables Florida addressed the comments made and explained that the ordinance will be effective from the moment of its adoption, and there would not be any retroactive implication with Florida Wood. Mr. Arango continued to explain that mitigation of code enforcement fines is discretionary which can only be requested when compliance is met, and although the case took an appeal from the certification hearing, and remanded it to redo the certification process, Florida Wood has not complied and has no vested right in respects to the mitigation.Town Attorney Lillian Arango concurred with the determination made by her colleague Jose Arango and further explained that Florida Wood would have the right to a meaningful second certification hearing with due process, however, that does not have to do with the mitigation of the fines which will occur down the line when compliance has been met. Mr. Dougal stated that the court did not order a remand, and in a legal perspective it looks like the attorney's view is that the new amended ordinance could be applied, but pleaded once more that Florida Wood be carved out. Mr. Brian Adler, also from law offices

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Flex Time Off for Salaried Employees.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Flex Time Off for Salaried Employees. Mayor Martell addressed the item explaining his intent which was to both remove the flex time off benefit afforded to the exempt employees and removing the punching in and out process for exempt employees. Mayor Martell further explained that after inquiring the punching in and out process of 21 cities, it was determined that no other city had salary employees punching in and out. Director Roy Danziger approached the Council and clarified for councilwoman Ayala that salary employees are paid for the job and are expected to work even outside of regularly scheduled hours,thus working on a weekend does not afford that employee to take a day off during the week. Councilwoman Ayala expressed that she was not being provided enough information to make a decision on the employee matter,and would like additional information from either legal, or labor, but unfortunately labor counsel was not present. Director Danziger then clarified that the current flex time off benefit is a policy where exempt employees working six consecutive hours on a day that is not their regularly schedule workday, would allow exempt employees to take a full day off within a thirty (30) day period and the mayor's proposal is to remove this benefit. Councilwoman Ayala explained that because there is a lack of human resources, she needed additional clarification from the finance department. Director Danziger explained that any salary employee taking a full day off would need to put in time from their bank, either from sick, or vacation for the time off. Building and Zoning Director William Diaz explained that he'll be working on Fridays and Saturdays sending emails and that it's unfortunate that he is scrutinized for being minutes late. Director Diaz continued to explain that all directors of the Town are responsible and know what their job duties are. Director Diaz expressed that he is not in agreement with punching in and out but will continue to do so if instructed. Councilwoman Ayala clarified that flex time is one item and the punching in and out policy is another. Director Diaz further stated that the flex time does not impact him because he does not work six consecutive hours on a day outside of his work schedule to take a day off.Director Diaz also expressed that those directors who perform their work and get the job done deserve the trust to not punch in and out but not all directors should be treated the same, and t

Pizzi to read the Item found in the New Business section of the agenda. The agenda item was then discussed and acted upon as follows, - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Continued and Revised 2020 Annexation Application with Miami-Dade County. Vice Mayor Pacheco began the discussion by asking for clarification on the resolutions adopted by Miami Springs and Virginia Gardens. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi explained that although resolutions had been adopted including mitigation fees, that fee would be eliminated once the ordinance went before the County commission. Mr. Pizzi continued to explain that the County initially urged the Town to adopt a resolution entering into an interlocal agreement that would require the Town of Medley to pay Miami-Dade County a mitigation fee close to $600,000 a year for seven years, and that the County after adoption would then remove the requirement for the mitigation fee. Mr. Pizzi continued to explain that he was not in agreement with adopting said resolution and after discussion with the County, it has been agreed to modify the resolution. Therefore, the Town may adopt a resolution entering into an interlocal agreement with Miami- Dade County eliminating the mitigation fee in its entirety. Mr. Pizzi explained how he compared agreements of other cities to ensure that the Town of Medley was getting a fair agreement. Mr. Pizzi continued to congratulate the Mayor and Council and further explained the process for finalizing the annexation. Minutes of October 25, 2022 Special Council Meeting In addition, Mr. Pizzi stated that the County must present to its board of Commissioners an Ordinance to be adopted by two readings, changing the boundaries of the Town of Medley. Additionally, during either reading, a Resolution will be presented entering into an interlocal agreement with the Town which would outline the governing terms for items such as zoning and utilities. Furthermore, attorney Pizzi stated that the reason for the emergency meeting is to adopt the presented Resolution so the Ordinance can be heard by the County commissioners on first reading by November 1 and second reading on November 15", therefore making the adoption and effective date for annexation midnight on November 15, 2022. Mr. Ruiz approached the Council and began to list several neighboring municipalities and their rate of hourly pay for the position of principal engineer, all of which exceeded his proposal of $165.00 an hour which explained that the rate has already been adjusted for the Town and that he has a firm stance on the hourly fee. Councilperson Ayala stated that the Town's efforts to save expenses has been noted and that the proposal is high when budgets have been cut in other departments. Mayor Martell explained that many projects have been postponed and will not be budgeted for, thus allowing expenditures for other needs. Additionally, Mayor Martell explained that he initially wanted 40 hours of service, but if the Council is not in agreement, then the Town can reduce the weekly hours from the proposal. Councilwoman Pacheco expressed that she would not like to consider Mr. Ruiz as taking advantage of the Town's urgency for an engineer, but his proposal is too expensive. Mr. Ruiz once again explained that he would not be receiving any Town benefits such as pension which would cost the Town much more in employee benefits and expressed that as a business owner,he cannot, in all fairness,take less than his value of work when he already has reduced the cost for the Town. Mr. Ruiz reiterated that he could work less hours but undoubtedly things will not get done as quickly as the Town would like. Councilwoman Ayala stated that it was unfair for the Council to now state that all the red flags were missed, such as too many projects, when residents have been used to insult the Council for their opposition to projects. segs.text: Councilperson Ayala addressed the employees in the public and asked if they had any comments on this matter. Councilwoman Ayala requested clarification for the notes given and addressed interim finance director Charmaine Parchment. Councilwoman Ayala further asked for clarification on the professional fees noted, and it was explained that set on the run rate it was then determined what fees to eliminate from the budget. Additionally, pre-employment allocations being defunded was inquired about, and it was explained that funding can be moved among the line items and if not, an amendment to the budget could be done to allocate funding from reserves if needed. Lastly Councilwoman Ayala asked to clarify the longevity pay item as listed and Ms. Parchment explained that the existing longevity pay benefit is $1,000 the first year earned, and the proposed budget reflects funding for half which would equal to $500.00 the first year earned, and $50.00 every additional year on the earned day. segs.text: Resolution C-2024 Approving a Variance Application for IAero Thrust Engine Test Center, LLC for Property Located at 9051 NW 84th Avenue Medley Florida. (Folio No. 22-3003-033-0053) James Hickey,consulting Town Planner,and Paul Hernandez representative for the applicant approached the podium. Mr. Hickey briefly explained that the applicant performs engine testing,and the Town Code currently has a limit of 80-A decimal level,but through multiple tests they have determined that they go over the decimals allowed for in the Town Code and would like to formally request a variance allowing an increase to 90-A decimals. Mr. Hernandez also explained and clarified by giving examples to sounds that would be equivalent to 90-A decimals and how it is unlikely that it would be heard by neighboring businesses or the residential area. Additionally, Mr. Hernandez noted that the Town, to date, has not received any complaints while IAero has been conducting its business. segs.head: Resolution C-2029 Approving and Amending the Town of Medley Building Fee Schedule.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve resolution C-2029. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously.
segs.text: Resolution C-2029 Approving and Amending the Town of Medley Building Fee Schedule. Town Attorney Pizzi explained that according to Florida Statue the Building Department can only generate enough revenue to pay for departmental needs and not generate a surplus,but be self-contained as surpluses cannot be transferred to general funds or used for other departments.Attorney Pizzi further stated that if funds are generated in excess of what is required,the Town must either return the funds or amend its fee schedule. In addition, Mr. Pizzi stated that after discussions with the finance director, building department director, and discussions with other cities, it was explained that if your budget shows a surplus for over five years then the consistent surplus would require an amendment to the fee schedule.Therefore Mr. Pizzi presented the following resolution proposing a ten percent(10%)decrease across the board for all building department fees, which he believes will not result in a short fall and alleviate the concerns of generating continuous surpluses. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve resolution C-2029. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Presentation and Recognition of the Police Department Officer of the Bid Award. Lieutenant German Gutierrez approached the Council and announced that officer Luis Rivera was the recipient of the Officer of the Bid Award from July through December 2022. He continued to state that in October of 2022 officer Rivera received the Life Saving Award for assisting another officer in saving the life of a wounded victim. Moreover, officer Rivera assisted the Seminole Police Department in locating a federal wanted individual. It was noted that aside from officer Rivera performing his official duties, he is also a part of the Police Department s social media unit and serves as a public information officer. Therefore, for his display of teamwork, professionalism, and utmost loyalty to the department, officer Luis Rivera was awarded with the Officer of the Bid Award. Officer Luis Rivera then approached to thank the Police Department s Command staff, his fellow officers, and the Town council for acknowledging his hard work.

segs.text: - Presentation and Recognition of the Police Department Chief's Award. Sergeant Louis Ponce was awarded the Chief s award and was recognized for his outstanding work ethics, dedication to the department s accreditation process and for his devotion to continued training efforts. Sergeant Ponce approached the Council and stated that the award was a recognition to every member of the team whose efforts helped accomplish the accreditation. Additionally, sergeant Ponce expressed his gratitude to the Chief of Police for her leadership and vision, the Mayor and Council for their unwavering support, and his colleges for their hard work towards this accomplishment.

segs.head: - Presentation and Recognition of the Police Department Officer of the Year Award.
segs.text: - Presentation and Recognition of the Police Department Officer of the Year Award. Officer Omar Galvan was awarded the Officer of the Year Award and was recognized for his exemplary performance throughout the year. It was sated that he has consistently been the most productive officer in arrests, traffic enforcements, and self-initiative activities. It was also stated that in October 2022 officer Galvan received the Life Saving Award for his immediate action in applying a tourniquet technique to a wounded victim which would have otherwise perished and on the same day, he continued to locate a fleeing armed subject that with his efforts, was detained. It was also stated that these occasions are only an example of his continued hard work and efforts, thus earning him the title of Officer of the Year. Officer Omar Galvan then approached the Council and expressed his gratitude towards all his mentors and colleagues as well as the Mayor and Council. segs.text: - Discussion and Action for the Request to Notice Two (2) Utilities Laborer Positions for the Utilities Department. Director Jorge Soto approached the Council and explained that the two requested positions were to partially fill vacancies in the department since four positions had been vacant in the recent years. Councilperson Pacheco expressed his disagreement with the request since a hiring freeze had recently been implemented and he did not wish to open said freeze. Vice Mayor asked for clarification on the filling of the vacant positions, whereas Director Soto explained that the applicants need a high school diploma or equivalent to obtain their license through the State of Florida and be qualified for the positions. Vice-Mayor Ayala also addressed the hiring freeze and asked Town Attorney Pizzi whether the hiring freeze was in effect since hirings had occurred after its adoption. Mayor Martell explained that the request was for four employees, but director Soto agreed to the hiring of two, to allow for the minimum number of hires for departmental function. Councilwoman Ayala interjected and stated that it is important to provide employees when a department is deficient because that is how the Town will continue to run efficiently and stated her support for the item. Additionally, Councilwoman Ayala also stated that the hire will help the department because working understaffed is difficult. Councilwoman Ayala also thanked director Soto for his willingness to compromise. Without further discussion Mayor Martell made a motion to approve the request for two utilities laborer position. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell - Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala - Yes Councilperson Lizelh Ayala- Yes Councilperson Ivan Pacheco- No Councilperson Karina Pacheco- Yes The motion was carried by majority of vote. segs.head: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Community Pool Operations.
segs.text: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Community Pool Operations. Councilperson Pacheco began the discussion by stating that he has received complaints for the last couple of months about the pool being closed. Councilperson Pacheco further stated that the pool has been closed since September and he had circulated cost estimates for lifeguard services to expand the current hours of operations and explained that the Town already pays monthly maintenance expenses for the heated pool. Mayor Martell explained that the expense associated with opening the community pool all year round would be 128,000 thousand dollars per year which is not cost effective for the Town and that, according to the visitor logs that were also circulated, there was not enough attendance on Fridays. Thus, Mayor Martell proposed to try and extend the current operating hours to weekends only and instructed finance director Charmain Parchment to obtain a cost estimate for lifeguard services for the proposed weekend only schedule. Councilwoman Rodriguez joined the discussion and stated that weather starts getting hot in the month of March and that whatever decision is taken, the Town needs to do a better job at informing the residents of the pool schedule. Councilwoman Rodriguez also suggested to extend the current operating schedule from the month of March through June from Fridays to Sundays and a full schedule from July to September and back to weekends on the months of October and November. Councilwoman further stated that Fridays should be considered to allow middle and high school students the opportunity to attend. Mayor Martell further stated that the suggested schedule can be tested subject to the estimate for the lifeguard services of the same, and in the case that the expenses associated with the expanded schedule is not feasible, he would bring the matter back for further discussion. Vice-Mayor Ayala suggested that police department employees and their families could use the community pool without the need for lifeguard services. After discussing the matter Councilperson Pacheco made a motion as follows, TO CHANGE THE CURRENT OPERATING SCHEDULE OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY COMMUNITY POOL, ON A TRIAL BASIS, AND SUBJECT TO COST ESTIMATES RECEIVED, AS FOLLOWS: - 18' DAY OF MARCH THROUGH THE END OF JUNE: FRIDAYS TO SUNDAYS; - 18 DAY OF JULY THROUGH END OF SEPTEMBER: MONDAYS TO SUNDAYS; - 18ST DAY OF OCTOBER THROUGH END OF NOVEMBER: FRIDAYS TO SU

Additionally, Vice-Mayor Ayala placed a motion to adopt the meeting's agenda. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion and the meeting's agenda was approved unanimously. Mayor Martell then opened the meeting for public comments. It was noted that no public comments were made. In continuance with the next order of business,Mayor Martell instructed Town Attorney Michael Pizzi to address the agenda item. The item was then discussed and acted upon as follows, - Discussion and Action on the Request for Job Availability for the Capital Improvement Projects Department. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi explained that following Council's directives from the last Council meeting that all requests for job openings be brought before Council,therefore the capital improvement projects director had requested a replacement for the position, since it had become vacant. Councilperson Pacheco inquired about the starting salary position to which Mayor Martell responded that, if allowed by the Council, he would determine the salary according to the qualifications and experience of the selected applicant, if any. Vice-Mayor Ayala addressed the minimum qualifications and scope of the proposed position and the needs of the department given that the director was the only employee in the department.Mayor Martell explained that the job description as proposed, reflected the Town's interest for an individual who has experience in the construction field as well as clerical. Mayor Martell further explained that director Cardenas would be part of the selection body that will be assessing the qualifications of every applicant.

segs.head: Councilwoman Ayala expressed her concerns with the job description as presented and further stated that the job description and the minimum requirements of the same were standardized given that the capital improvement projects department is a specialized department that could use a higher educated individual such as an engineer student.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 6:32pm.
segs.text: Councilwoman Ayala expressed her concerns with the job description as presented and further stated that the job description and the minimum requirements of the same were standardized given that the capital improvement projects department is a specialized department that could use a higher educated individual such as an engineer student. In addition, Councilwoman Ayala stated that it would be beneficial for the Town to attract a candidate interested in a long-term employment relationship with the Town and when the last employee filled the position it was required to have a bachelor's degree. Councilwoman Ayala also stated that a minimum standard education was not the best fit for the department's needs and the Town and a high school education requirement is not rigorous for the department. Councilwoman Ayala further stated that not having a wage range for the position may not attract the right candidates and will result in a waste of time, for both the Town and the applicants. Councilman Pacheco expressed his agreement with some of the statements made by Councilwoman Ayala but expressed willingness to try and see what candidates it may attract. Town Attorney Pizzi was asked for input on the mater and expressed that a firm expectation for the position and a wage range is essential for the director to select the right candidate. In addition, attorney Pizzi stated that the budget included a position at the rate of$ 18.00 per hour and it was important to establish a wage range so that the director could consider applicants from a targeted pool. Mr. Pizzi further stated that a flexibility in the salary range within the Town's budget could better help the director make a better selection within a range of applicants depending on the qualifications submitted. Director Cardenas expressed agreement with the town attorney's statement and further stated that she also considered employees from other departments that already know the inner workings of the Town. Regarding the salary wage range, director Cardenas stated that if the Town is interested in an intermediate position, the adequate salary would start at $ 35.00 per hour. Mayor Martell then recommended to initiate the posting and selection process with the position as described with a wage range of$ 18.00- $ 35.00 per hour on a trial basis and see what candidates are attracted. segs.head: - An Ordinance of the Town of Medley, Florida, Providing an Amendment to Ordinance C- 455 Amending Section 2-86 of the Code, Settlement; Disposition of All Collected Fines And Liens to Read Mitigation of Fines, Penalties and Liens ; Establishing Procedures and Guidelines for the Mitigation of Code Enforcement Fines, Penalties and Liens; Providing for Codification; Providing for Severability; Providing for Conflicts; and Providing for an Effective Date.
votes: Vice-Mayor Ayala then placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-466 on first reading amending the cap amount for fines imposed at One Hundred Thousand dollars. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - An Ordinance of the Town of Medley, Florida, Providing an Amendment to Ordinance C- 455 Amending Section 2-86 of the Code, Settlement; Disposition of All Collected Fines And Liens to Read Mitigation of Fines, Penalties and Liens ; Establishing Procedures and Guidelines for the Mitigation of Code Enforcement Fines, Penalties and Liens; Providing for Codification; Providing for Severability; Providing for Conflicts; and Providing for an Effective Date. Town Attorney Michael A. Pizzi explained that the methodology in which Code enforcement fines are assessed and how at times daily accrual of fines surpass the value of the property, thus the cost becomes exuberant and unreasonable for the property owners. Mr. Pizzi further stated that many cities have passed legislation capping fee amounts and that prior to adopting Ordinance C-455, the Town had the ability to hear a property s owner circumstances and determine if there was just cause in not curing the violation by the compliance deadline. Therefore, the ordinance presented proposes to cap the Town of Medley Code Compliance fines at the assessed amount of One Hundred and Fifty Thousand dollars. Vice-Mayor Ayala proposed to amend the proposed capped amount and to lower the cap to One Hundred Thousand dollars to which it was agreed upon. Vice-Mayor Ayala then placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-466 on first reading amending the cap amount for fines imposed at One Hundred Thousand dollars. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously. The Resolutions items were then read into the record, discussed, and acted upon as follows,

segs.head: Resolution C-2060 Appointing Mary Cardenas-Aldir as Director of the Capital Projects and Economic Development Department; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date.
votes: Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2060 naming Mary Cardenas as Director and renaming the Capital Projects and Economic Development (CPED) department to the Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) Department. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Resolution C-2060 Appointing Mary Cardenas-Aldir as Director of the Capital Projects and Economic Development Department; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Mayor Martell began the discussion by stating that Ms. Cardenas has approached her position very energetically, and that he and Town attorney have discussed the matter internally to determine her wage. Town Engineer Tommy Ruiz approached the podium to express his support for Ms. Cardenas appointment and vouched for her qualifications, experience, and work ethic. Attorney Pizzi joined the discussion and explained that under the terms of the Resolution Ms. Cardenas would be expected to come back to Council in May with a presentation of her plan for capital projects and explanation of how she will manage the departmental needs. Mr. Pizzi also explained that she is being offered a salary of One Hundred and Ten Thousand dollars ($110,000) a year and imposed a one- year probationary period. Councilperson Pacheco expressed concerns with the proposed salary. Employee Mary Cardenas residing at 625 Biltmore Way, Coral Gables Florida, approached the podium and Councilwoman Ayala asked her to explain how she will approach the position and the precedent she will establish as the Director of the department in question. Ms. Cardenas stated that she will prioritize project scheduling, pursue timelines, work towards resolving problems and continuously communicate matters with the Mayor and Council. Vice-Mayor Ayala then proposed to change the department s name to Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) Department, and the Council agreed. Without further discussion, Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2060 naming Mary Cardenas as Director and renaming the Capital Projects and Economic Development (CPED) department to the Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) Department. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Resolution C-2061 Ratifying the Non-Solicitation Rules for Lakeside Retirement Park Located at 10601 N.W. 105 Way; Directing Continued Enforcement of the Rules and Regulations of the Mobile Home Park; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date.
votes: Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2061. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Resolution C-2061 Ratifying the Non-Solicitation Rules for Lakeside Retirement Park Located at 10601 N.W. 105 Way; Directing Continued Enforcement of the Rules and Regulations of the Mobile Home Park; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. It was explained that Councilmembers raised concerns whether the Town s non solicitation rules at the Lakeside Retirement home were being imposed, and that the presented resolution does not impose any additional rules but simply reiterates and directs staff to continue enforcing the regulation. Councilwoman Ayala asked for clarification and Town attorney Pizzi explained that the non-solicitation rule was already in place and then referred to councilperson Pacheco as he placed the item for action on the agenda. After a brief discussion, Councilperson Pacheco expressed concerns with the residential peace due to unpermitted visitors such as clinics, and funeral home salespersons. Vice- Mayor Ayala asked for the Town s plan to enforce this rule. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez then explained that the removal of the security guard services had shifted the responsibility of granting entrance to Lakeside to the residents. Therefore, tenants are now responsible for whom they let in and ensuring that the person or entity has left once the visitation has concluded. It was decided that a notice be sent in both English and Spanish, to which Town Clerk Martinez confirmed that all communication directed to Lakeside residents from the Clerk s office, is always sent in both languages. Lakeside Resident Lourdes Rodriguez Lot 729 approached the podium and raised concerns about the candidates campaigning at Lakeside during election season and how often the candidates come and solicit residents. Mr. Pizzi clarified that the rules on the prospectus have always been in place and the rules need to be enforced fairly and uniformly. Without further discussion, Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2061. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.head: Resolution C-2062 Directing the Town Attorney to Initiate the Process to Amend the Town Charter to Remove Article VIII of the Town of Medley Charter; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date.
segs.text: Resolution C-2062 Directing the Town Attorney to Initiate the Process to Amend the Town Charter to Remove Article VIII of the Town of Medley Charter; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Mayor Martell opened the discussion by proposing an amendment to the entire Town of Medley charter. Town Attorney Pizzi explained that a charter review has never been done, therefore he suggested a workshop be held to discuss and recommend changes to the charter in its entirety. Councilwoman Ayala expressed concerns with how vague the current resolution was presented and stated that removing article VIII is removing a supervisor s right to have representation through a board, thus finds it troublesome. Councilwoman Ayala also stated that she is not in agreement with the removal of Article VII, further stating that employees have a right to a due process. Additionally, Councilwoman Ayala asked for the specific purpose of the item being brought up but expressed that an entire charter review would be healthy. However, the proposed resolution only addresses one section of the Town charter. Mr. Pizzi explained that members of the Council have expressed that the administrative review board process served no purpose because ultimately the matter comes back to the Town Council for a vote, and in his experience these administrative review board processes do not do anyone any favors and are useless delays because the process results in the same body of the board that decided to terminate the employee, whereas there are other forms of protection such as the whistle blower statue. Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that in 2018 he recommended a Charter review as well and was told that the process would be too strenuous to accomplish. Nonetheless he recommended eliminating the language for the removal of article VIII as an amendment to the resolution. Mayor Martell agreed for the resolution to reflect a full Town of Medley Charter review. Councilperson Pacheco joined the discussion and expressed agreement to Vice-Mayor Ayala s comments but stated that the administrative review board process did not serve a purpose and the process should not belong in the Town Charter or the employee handbook. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Usage of Miami-Dade County Special Transportation Services (STS).
votes: Mayor Martell then moved to table the item to be discussed at a Council workshop and the council agreed unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Usage of Miami-Dade County Special Transportation Services (STS). Mayor Martell addressed the item and stated that Social Services and Parks and Recreations Director Lizmari Valido would present the item. Director Valido then approached the Council and stated that she had been informed about this item only a week prior and is only aware that the Mayor proposes to remove the Uber medical services providing medical transportation through the Miami-Dade County Special Transportation Services (STS). Additionally, she explained that there are currently 62 residents receiving services through the Town s the medical transportation program. Councilwoman Ayala expressed concerns with the Council s inclination to waive fees and accommodate business needs while considering cutting expenses in residential programs. Councilwoman Ayala also explained that although STS is a program available for all Miami-Dade County residents, there are many practices such as single riding, long wait times and commute times that would drastically change, making a difficult transition for the residents. Nonetheless, Councilwoman Ayala explained that she is not against exploring alternative options if the Uber medical services are too costly. Ultimately, Councilwoman Ayala stated that if the Town can accommodate the businesses, then the Town should also accommodate the Town s elderly community. Mayor Martell joined the discussion and expressed that the Town does not have the staff necessary to move or transport residents with serious medical conditions. Town Attorney Pizzi also explained that it s not an either-or proposal, but the County does have trained medical professionals on staff, and the goal is for the residents to receive the best service. Councilperson Pacheco discussed and explained that prior to using the Uber services residents would call for medical transportation but would go to other locations instead. Councilperson Pacheco continued to state that Uber has been a pilot program as an alternative use of our employees for transportation, but the Town is spending too much money. Director Valido interjected to emphasize that medical transportation is only approved as such, and transportation has never been approved for residents to do nearby errands. However, if residents do so, it is out of the Town s control. Director Valido also stated that elected officials have called her for favors to make exceptions for residents, even having Town staff as

segs.head: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on the Creation of Policy for Limitations of Town of Medley Donations Councilperson Pacheco began by asking for clarification whether there is a policy on donation limitation.
segs.text: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on the Creation of Policy for Limitations of Town of Medley Donations Councilperson Pacheco began by asking for clarification whether there is a policy on donation limitation. Town Clerk Martinez explaining that although no formal policy exists there has always been the practice of a $500.00 dollar limitation. Vice-Mayor Ayala explained that if the Town is approached to help in a big endeavor and is limited to only donate $500.00 then the Town looks frugal and does not agree on limitations when there could be needy causes. Councilwoman Ayala included that she believed the Town can be responsible while still being generous when it comes to the residents, and explained how the Town was able to send young students to a science competition that exposes them to STEM careers and medicine, which is harder for people with minority backgrounds or low incomes to have access to these careers. She further stated that the Town was able provide access to those young residents due to the donation approved by Council. Thus, expressed disagreement with establishing a cap amount. Councilperson Pacheco then placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE A MAXIMUM LIMITATION OF $500.00 DOLLARS PER TOWN DONATION, ALLOWING FOR THE COUNCIL TO APPROVE A HIGHER DONATION AMOUNT IF ANY COUNCILMEMBER PRESENTS A CAUSE WITH NEED FOR THE SAME Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala Yes Councilperson Ivan Pacheco Yes Councilperson Lizelh Ayala No Councilperson Karina Pacheco Yes The motion was carried by majority of vote.

segs.head: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Hiring Procedures.
segs.text: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Hiring Procedures. Councilperson Pacheco explained that a Resolution was previously adopted by Council with a hiring process, and that although it has since been rescinded, he would like to reimplement the policy as provided for in said resolution with the hiring process once again. Councilperson Pacheco further stated that he wanted to adjust the step in which departments heads come before Council for approval to begin the hiring process. He then asked the Town Attorney if any of the following alternative could be used as approval to commence the hiring process. e Department heads talk directly with the Mayor; e Upon Mayor s approval, Department heads to have one-on-one meetings with each elected official; e Department heads to get approval by calling each councilperson and getting their input for the proposed hiring. Town Attorney Pizzi explained that each Councilmember would have to make their own determination but because of the sunshine law, department heads must be careful not to share the comments of the other elected officials, thus they can only brief the council member they are meeting with on their hiring process Town Clerk Victoria Martinez clarified the prior practice which established for department heads to go before council for approval to fill a vacancy for a needed position, and stated that Councilperson Pacheco is asking if department heads could pull each councilmember individually so that they can start the opening and selection process. Councilperson Pacheco agreed to the clarification of his proposal. Attorney Pizzi then clarified that any Council decision needs to be made as a body in a public forum for transparency. Thus, it is not proper for staff members to go to each councilmember and draw a straw ballot. Therefore, if the request requires Council s majority of a vote, it must be done in a public setting. Mayor Martell then proposed to allow his authority as Town manager to approve the opening of the positions to be filled and for the item to then be presented before Council as practiced currently. Councilperson Pacheco expressed disagreement with the current practice of deciding to hire a recommended applicant at the moment they are presented to the Council and expressed his intent to be informed throughout the hiring process and not at the final moment of hiring. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Pending Town of Medley Annexation Application.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Pending Town of Medley Annexation Application. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi congratulated the Town Council and Town residents and stated that after twenty years the annexation had finally been approved and further explained that the only annexation application approved was the one submitted by the Town of Medley. It was noted that a new interlocal agreement has been approved with language requiring four years of mitigation payments, and there will be a meeting with the County to confirm a start date for said payments. Mr. Pizzi also explained that police service has been provided to annexed areas since the initial approval of the annexation application. It was also clarified that the mitigation payment is set to be $517,000 dollars for the first year and increased by a percentage for a span of four years. Furthermore, after meeting with the County the Town attorney will come back to Council to report the details of the transitionary plan agreed upon for all services such as utilities, public works, etcetera.

votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 9:12 pm.
segs.text: - Capital Projects and Economic Development Report. Town engineer Tommy Ruiz approached the Council and first addressed the community pool project explaining that although the contractor has not been responsive, there should be a final inspection soon and a follow up with the health department to complete the project by the end of the month. Mr. Ruiz further stated that there are some cosmetic features that could require attention, but the Town has agreed to move forward with the contractor s completion of the project to then take on any beautification needs. Councilwoman Ayala agreed that the Town should absorb the cost of beautification to allow for this project to be completed because of its high importance to the community. In addition, Mr. Ruiz briefly gave an update on the project at NW 99 terrace which is a new road that connects south river drive and NW 87 avenue, which is 90% complete. Mr. Ruiz explained that the FDOT was going to force the Town to have the road lower than the flood plain elevation but after pushback given in the Town s defense, FDOT agreed to evenly adjust the height of the road. Vice-Mayor Ayala interjected to instruct staff to address complaints given by Lakeside residents of excessive sediment dusk. Mayor Martell stated that Code enforcement needs to go on site and issue a citation to the business causing the concerns. Director Cardenas approached the Council and provided an update for the project located at NW South River Drive between NW 72 Avenue and NW 74 Street which it was reported to be in its closeout stage. In addition, director Cardenas reported that the NW South River Drive project between NW 116 Way and NW 121 Way is on schedule and the Lakeside Phase II project is on the negotiation phase with the architect. It was also reported that the sidewalk master plan has a public meeting scheduled for March 8, 2023. Since there was no other business to address, Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 9:12 pm. hil da i by Victorid Martine#/FRP, CMC, Town Clerk / pe Mayor

segs.head: - Presentation by Councilwoman Rodriguez of an Educational Community Service Initiative Led by Resident Nicole Mollinedo.
segs.text: - Presentation by Councilwoman Rodriguez of an Educational Community Service Initiative Led by Resident Nicole Mollinedo. Councilwoman Rodriguez introduced resident Nicole Mollinedo and explained that as elected officials there is a responsibility to encourage the next generation of leaders and this initiative is an example of such. Additionally, she stated that Ms. Mollinedo had already begun an innovated community service project with the Town of Medley. Ms. Nicole Mollinedo approached the Council and explained that she has been a Medley resident for sixteen years and is entering her senior year of high school. She continued to state that she is in pursuit of receiving the Silver Knights Award,awarded by the Miami Herald.Therefore,Ms.Mollinedo decided that her student project will focus on assisting immigrant students of the summer care program with learning the English language in preparation for the upcoming school year. Attorney Pizzi also stated that Mr. Herrera was present should the Council had any questions on the matter. Ivan Herrera, resident of 23 Tahiti Beach Island Road, Coral Gables, FL approached the Council and briefly explained that his proposal focuses on assisting the Town with two issues, housing for the Town and a medical center. Councilwoman Rodriguez stated that the development proposal, as reflected, indicated a primary medical facility as well as a mix-use site and housing as opposed to the long-term health care facility that had been promised to the Medley residents. Additionally, Councilwoman Rodriguez noted that the property was appraised for 7.4 million dollars and Mr. Herrera's offer is for 5.5 million dollars. Mr. Herrera further stated that the 250 units available can be adjusted to the Town's needs whether it be public housing or for the Town's work force. Also, he briefly explained that his offer was based on the strict limitation on the property's use and further explained that by pursuing the property with the Town's requirement he would not see any form of profit until 3 years into finalized construction and the commencement of operations. segs.text: * Harassment is a form of employment discrimination that violates Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967, (ADEA), and the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, (ADA).

segs.head: * Harassment is unwelcome conduct that is based on race, color, religion, sex (including sexual orientation, gender identity, or pregnancy), national origin, older age (beginning at age 40), disability, or genetic information (including family medical history).
segs.text: * Harassment is unwelcome conduct that is based on race, color, religion, sex (including sexual orientation, gender identity, or pregnancy), national origin, older age (beginning at age 40), disability, or genetic information (including family medical history). Harassment becomes unlawful where 1) enduring the offensive conduct becomes a condition of continued employment, or 2) the conduct is severe or pervasive enough to create a work environment that a reasonable person would consider intimidating, hostile, or abusive. Offensive conduct may include, but is not limited to, offensive jokes, slurs, epithets or name calling, physical assaults or threats, intimidation, ridicule or mockery, insults or put-downs, offensive objects or pictures, and interference with work performance. Harassment can occur in a variety of circumstances, including, but not limited to, the following: The harasser can be the victim's supervisor, a supervisor in another area, an agent of the employer, a co-worker, or a non-employee. The victim does not have to be the person harassed, but can be anyone affected by the offensive conduct. Unlawful harassment may occur without economic injury to, or discharge of, the victim. The Town of Medley is committed to providing a work environment that is free from discrimination. In keeping with this commitment, the Town maintains a strict policy prohibiting any kind of unlawful harassment, discrimination and/or retaliation that is based on an individual s national origin, race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation and gender identity), age, marital status, gender identity, disability or the need to be accommodated as a result of a disability. The Town s policy against discrimination remains in effect even if the party to whom the offending conduct is directed does not evidence any displeasure at the nature of the conduct. Examples of conduct prohibited under this policy, even if the conduct does not rise to the level of discrimination, include offensive or insensitive acts (directed to, or in the presence of individuals) that relate to a person s race, color, religion (or lack thereof), national origin, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation and gender identity), marital status, age, genetic information or disability, which are in any way disparaging to any such individual or group including, but not limited to: derogatory comments, group generalizations, jokes and gestures, photographs, film, greeting cards, articl

The conduct is severe or pervasive enough to create a work environment that a reasonable person would consider intimidating, hostile, or abusive. Examples of harassment may include, but are not limited to: (1) nicknames, slurs/foul language, jokes or derogatory statements pertaining to a protected class or category defined by federal state or local laws; (2) overtly or covertly distributed materials, signs, magazines, or bulletin board notices that are offensive and pertain to any race, color, national origin, ethnicity, age, sex, disability or religion; and (3) or any other verbal or physical conduct which is offensive and objectionable to the recipient or others and where such actions are taken based on a protected class or category defined by federal state or local laws. Sexual Harassment is defined as: unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors and other verbal or physical conduct of a sexual nature, and where: Ts Submission to such conduct is made either explicitly or implicitly a term or condition of an individual's employment; 2. Submission to or rejection of such conduct by an individual is used as the basis for employment decisions affecting such individual; 3. Such conduct is sexually offensive or has the purpose or effect of substantially interfering with an individual's work performance or creating an intimidating, hostile, or offensive working environment; 4. Any other act which constitutes a violation of the Town's sexual harassment policy; and 5. Failure to comply with any directive or request to cease prohibited sexual harassment behavior. segs.head: B. DUTIES AND EXPECTATIONS: Managers and Supervisors shall be responsible for preventing acts of discrimination and harassments and utilizing this policy in the event such conduct is reported.
segs.text: B. DUTIES AND EXPECTATIONS: Managers and Supervisors shall be responsible for preventing acts of discrimination and harassments and utilizing this policy in the event such conduct is reported. These responsibilities include: 1. Expressing strong disapproval of all forms of discrimination, harassment and retaliation; 2. Monitoring the work environment on a continuous basis for signs of discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation; 3. Stopping any observed acts of possible discrimination, harassment or retaliation by taking the appropriate steps to immediately intervene in the observed behavior; 4. Immediately reporting any observed or reported acts of possible discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation to the next level supervisor or manager and/or to the Town s EO Officer; and 5. Providing immediate assistance to any Town employee who reports discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation. A manager or supervisor s failure to carry out these responsibilities shall be considered in any evaluation or promotional decision and may be grounds for discipline, up to and including termination. All Town employees shall also be responsible for adhering to this Policy and assisting in the prevention of discrimination and harassment by: 1. Refraining from participating in, or encouraging actions that could be perceived as discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation; 2. Promptly reporting acts of discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation to a supervisor (or to the next level supervisor if the supervisor is the offending party), manager and/or the EO Officer; and 3. Encouraging any employee who confides that he/she is being subjected to discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation to report those acts to a supervisor, manager and/or the EO Officer. Discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation by or against any Town employee WILL NOT BE TOLERATED. If the Town determines, after conducting an objective and good faith investigation, that an employee has violated this Policy, the Town shall take immediate and appropriate corrective action. Discipline, up to and including termination, may be imposed based on the nature and severity of the facts determined in any investigation. Cc. Harassment can also include, for example, offensive or derogatory remarks about a person's transgender status or gender transition. In Bostock vy. Clayton County, Georgia, No. 17-1618 (S. Ct. June 15, 2020),[1] the Supreme Court held that firing individuals because of their sexual orientation or transgender status violates Title VII s prohibition on discrimination because of sex. The Court reached its holding by focusing on the plain text of Title VII. As the Court explained, discrimination based on homosexuality or transgender status necessarily entails discrimination based on sex; the first cannot happen without the second. Similarly, if an employer fires an employee because that person was identified as male at birth but uses feminine pronouns and identifies as a female, the employer is taking action against the individual because of sex since the action would not have been taken but for the fact the employee was originally identified as male. (a) An agency or independent contractor shall not dismiss, discipline, or take any other adverse personnel action against an employee for disclosing information pursuant to the provisions of this section. (b) An agency or independent contractor shall not take any adverse action that affects the rights or interests of a person in retaliation for the person s disclosure of information under this section. (c) The provisions of this subsection shall not be applicable when an employee or person discloses information known by the employee or person to be false.

segs.head: (5) NATURE OF INFORMATION DISCLOSED.
segs.text: (5) NATURE OF INFORMATION DISCLOSED. The information disclosed under this section must include: (a) Any violation or suspected violation of any federal, state, or local law, rule, or regulation committed by an employee or agent of an agency or independent contractor which creates and presents a substantial and specific danger to the public s health, safety, or welfare. (b) Any act or suspected act of gross mismanagement, malfeasance, misfeasance, gross waste of public funds, suspected or actual Medicaid fraud or abuse, or gross neglect of duty committed by an employee or agent of an agency or independent contractor.

segs.head: (6) TO WHOM INFORMATION DISCLOSED.
segs.text: (6) TO WHOM INFORMATION DISCLOSED. The information disclosed under this section must be disclosed to any agency or federal government entity having the authority to investigate, police, manage, or otherwise remedy the violation or act, including, but not limited to, the Office of the Chief Inspector General, an agency inspector general or the employee designated as agency inspector general under s. 112.3189(1) or inspectors general under s. 20.055, the Florida Commission on Human Relations, and the whistle-blower s hotline created under s. 112.3189. However, for disclosures concerning a local governmental entity, including any regional, county, or municipal entity, special district, community college district, or school district or any political subdivision of any of the foregoing, the information must be disclosed to a chief executive officer as defined in s. 447.203(9) or other appropriate local official. segs.head: (7) EMPLOYEES AND PERSONS PROTECTED.
segs.text: (7) EMPLOYEES AND PERSONS PROTECTED. This section protects employees and persons who disclose information on their own initiative in a written and signed complaint; who are requested to participate in an investigation, hearing, or other inquiry conducted by any agency or federal government entity; who refuse to participate in any adverse action prohibited by this section; or who initiate a complaint through the whistle-blower s hotline or the hotline of the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit of the Department of Legal Affairs; or employees who file any written complaint to their supervisory officials or employees who submit a complaint to the Chief Inspector General in the Executive Office of the Governor, to the employee designated as agency inspector general under s. 112.3189(1), or to the Florida Commission on Human Relations. The provisions of this section may not be used by a person while he or she is under the care, custody, or control of the state correctional system or, after release from the care, custody, or control of the state correctional system, with respect to circumstances that occurred during any period of incarceration. No remedy or other protection under ss. 112.3187-112.31895 applies to any person who has committed or intentionally participated in committing the violation or suspected violation for which protection under ss. 112.3187-112.31895 is being sought.

segs.head: (8) REMEDIES. (a) Any employee of or applicant for employment with any state agency, as the term state agency is defined ins. 216.011, who is discharged, disciplined, or subjected to other adverse personnel action, or denied employment, because he or she engaged in an activity protected by this section may file a complaint, which complaint must be made in accordance with s. 112.31895.
segs.text: (8) REMEDIES. (a) Any employee of or applicant for employment with any state agency, as the term state agency is defined ins. 216.011, who is discharged, disciplined, or subjected to other adverse personnel action, or denied employment, because he or she engaged in an activity protected by this section may file a complaint, which complaint must be made in accordance with s. 112.31895. Upon receipt of notice from the Florida Commission on Human Relations of termination of the investigation, the complainant may elect to pursue the administrative remedy available under s. 1 12.31895 or bring a civil action within 180 days after receipt of the notice. (b) Within 60 days after the action prohibited by this section, any local public employee protected by this section may file a complaint with the appropriate local governmental authority, if that authority has established by ordinance an administrative procedure for handling such complaints or has contracted with the Division of Administrative Hearings under s. 120.65 to conduct hearings under this section. The administrative procedure created by ordinance must provide for the complaint to be heard by a panel of impartial persons appointed by the appropriate local governmental authority. Upon hearing the complaint, the panel must make findings of fact and conclusions of law for a final decision by the local governmental authority. Within 180 days after entry of a final decision by the local governmental authority, the public employee who filed the complaint may bring a civil action in any court of competent jurisdiction. If the local governmental authority has not established an administrative procedure by ordinance or contract, a local public employee may, within 180 days after the action prohibited by this section, bring a civil action ina court of competent jurisdiction. For the purpose of this paragraph, the term local governmental authority includes any regional, county, or municipal entity, special district, community college district, or school district or any political subdivision of any of the foregoing. (c) Any other person protected by this section may, after exhausting all available contractual or administrative remedies, bring a civil action in any court of competent jurisdiction within 180 days after the action prohibited by this section. segs.head: (9) RELIEF.
segs.text: (9) RELIEF. In any action brought under this section, the relief must include the following: (a) Reinstatement of the employee to the same position held before the adverse action was commenced, or to an equivalent position or reasonable front pay as alternative relief. (b) Reinstatement of the employee s full fringe benefits and seniority rights, as appropriate. (c) Compensation, if appropriate, for lost wages, benefits, or other lost remuneration caused by the adverse action. (d) Payment of reasonable costs, including attorney s fees, to a substantially prevailing employee, or to the prevailing employer if the employee filed a frivolous action in bad faith. (e) Issuance of an injunction, if appropriate, by a court of competent jurisdiction. (f) Temporary reinstatement to the employee s former position or to an equivalent position, pending the final outcome on the complaint, if an employee complains of being discharged in retaliation for a protected disclosure and if a court of competent jurisdiction or the Florida Commission on Human Relations, as applicable under s. 112.31895, determines that the disclosure was not made in bad faith or for a wrongful purpose or occurred after an agency s initiation of a personnel action against the employee which includes documentation of the employee s violation of a disciplinary standard or performance deficiency. segs.head: Resolution C-2093 of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida, Appointing Joseph Geller as Alternative Special Magistrate for the Code Compliance Department and System; Authorizing the Mayor to Enter Into an Engagement Agreement for the Services with the Contractor; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date.
votes: Mayor Martell then placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2092 and Resolution C-2093. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Resolution C-2093 of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida, Appointing Joseph Geller as Alternative Special Magistrate for the Code Compliance Department and System; Authorizing the Mayor to Enter Into an Engagement Agreement for the Services with the Contractor; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Mr. Pizzi explained that the proposed Resolutions provide for back up so the Town would not have to cancel any code compliance special magistrate hearings due to the current magistrate s schedule. He continued to state both Mr. Herin and Mr. Geller s qualification, their experience, and then recommend both to only serve as alternatives if the current magistrate is unavailable. Vice-Mayor Ayala briefly expressed interest in assigning an alternative Town Attorney to serve the Town if Mr. Pizzi s schedule would not allow him to be available for a Town meeting for any reason, and then recommended Mr. Joseph Geller. Mr. Pizzi explained how he has already taken measures for such occasions and has already discussed with Mr. Geller his availability in case such instance should occur. Mayor Martell then placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2092 and Resolution C-2093. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: (4) The provisions of this section shall be so construed as to secure for municipalities the broad exercise of home rule powers granted by the constitution.
segs.text: (4) The provisions of this section shall be so construed as to secure for municipalities the broad exercise of home rule powers granted by the constitution. It is the further intent of the Legislature to extend to municipalities the exercise of powers for municipal governmental, corporate, or proprietary purposes not expressly prohibited by the constitution, general or special law, or county charter and to remove any limitations, judicially imposed or otherwise, on the exercise of home rule powers other than those so expressly prohibited. However, nothing in this act shall be construed to permit any changes in a special law or municipal charter which affect the exercise of extraterritorial powers or which affect an area which includes lands within and without a municipality or any changes in a special law or municipal charter which affect the creation or existence of a municipality, the terms of elected officers and the manner of their election except for the selection of election dates and qualifying periods for candidates and for changes in terms of office necessitated by such changes in election dates, the distribution of powers among elected officers, matters prescribed by the charter relating to appointive boards, any change in the form of government, or any rights of municipal employees, without approval by referendum of the electors as provided in s. 166.031 . Any other limitation of power upon any municipality contained in any municipal charter enacted or adopted prior to July 1 , 1973, is hereby nullified and repealed. The 2022 Florida Statutes (including 2022 Special Session A and 2023 Special Session B) MUNICIPALITIES MUNICIPALITIES 166.031 Charter Amendments. (1 ) The governing body of a municipality may, by ordinance, or the electors of a municipality may, by petition signed by 10 percent of the registered electors as of the last preceding municipal general election, submit to the electors of said municipality a proposed amendment to its charter, which amendment may be to any part or to all of said charter except that part describing the boundaries of such municipality. The governing body of the municipality shall place the proposed amendment contained in the ordinance or petition to a vote of the electors at the next general election held within the municipality or at a special election called for such purpose. segs.head: A.
segs.text: A. Except as provided in Section 6.04, any municipality in the county may adopt, amend, or revoke a charter for its own government or abolish its existence in the following manner. Its governing body shall within 120 days after adopting a resolution or after the certification of a petition of ten percent of the qualified electors of the municipality, draft or have drafted by a method determined by municipal ordinance a proposed charter amendment, revocation, or abolition which shall be submitted to the electors of the municipalities. Unless an election occurs not less than 60 nor more than 120 days after the draft is submitted, the proposal shall be submitted at a special election within that time. The governing body shall make copies of the proposal available to the electors not less that 30 days before the election. Alternative proposals shall be submitted. Each proposal approved by a majority of the electors voting on such proposal shall effective at the time fixed in the proposal.
