segs.head: - Maximum of two (2) members per household for all new applicants Nora a family caregiver specialist for the Alliance for Aging, Inc, organization approached the Council and explained that the organization does not provide services but provides referrals to service agency depending on the need and the service address of the applicant.
segs.text: - Maximum of two (2) members per household for all new applicants Nora a family caregiver specialist for the Alliance for Aging, Inc, organization approached the Council and explained that the organization does not provide services but provides referrals to service agency depending on the need and the service address of the applicant. Ms. Nora further stated that services such what the Town offers are provided through state programs like Medicaid Long-Term Care program which is based on need after an initial assessment and includes both, an applicant's financial and medical information component.Ms.Nora further stated that although there is a waiting list for this type of services, services are prioritized if applicants present signs of frailty and need. It was also explained that there are other programs like the Community Care for Elderly which is not free of charge and is not as comprehensive as the Medicaid Long-Term Care program, but does not require a financial criteria nor legal status. Ms.Nora also explained that although most programs are tailored for individuals of 60 years of age and older, assistance is available for individuals as young as 18 years of age and may not require financial information but are all dependent of medical diagnosis and other conditions. Ms. Mercy provided the agency's contact information, (305) 670-4357 and encouraged everyone including participants to reach out for assistance. Councilwoman Ayala inquired about the turn around time for applicants and it was clarified by Ms. Nora that the waiting time, depending on the assistance needed, could take up to a year but services could be released as soon as possible depending on the medical conditions of the applicant,and how quickly the application is processed by the family members. Ms. Chiverton also mentioned that the application process includes submittal of medical information and that, if approved, applicants are responsible for a$3.50 per ride fee and that starting on April 1,2023 dialysis patients will be allowed to receive transportation services right away. The school bus transportation services were discussed, and the bus helper positions were debated. It was stated that although the positions were removed from the budget, the school bus helpers' positions would remain and for the Council to decide upon, if future vacancies arise. The childcare program which included the after-school care and summer camp program was also discussed, specifically the onsite supervisor position. Director Valido further stated the importance and necessity to have an onsite supervisor which is also a requirement for the Miami-Dade County lunch program grant used by the Town. In addition, director Valido mentioned her request and past discussions with Town personnel, including the Town attorney, to have an existing qualified program employee to be reclassified to fill this position.Ms.Valido explained how she was informed that,as a director,she could encompass the duties of the position being requested.Ms.Valido further stated that the Parks and Recreation Department operates seven days a week and the childcare program requires direct supervision,thus explained the need for a supervisor, director's assistant,or equivalent managerial position. The meal program was discussed next, and it was mentioned that the national poverty income guidelines could be implemented, not only to the meal program, but to all other resident programs as well except for Town's educational programs. However, it was decided that the poverty income guidelines matter would be discussed further. Since there was no further business to discuss Mayor Martell made a motion to adjourn the meeting. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One(1)Part-Time Administrative Assistant Position to the Capital Improvement Projects Department.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT MARYURY MORENO TO A PART-TIME ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT POSITION FOR THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS DEPARTMENT EFFECTIVE MARCH 27, 2023" Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One(1)Part-Time Administrative Assistant Position to the Capital Improvement Projects Department. Councilwoman Ayala requested a few minutes to review the selected applicants' documents that had only been presented to the Mayor and Council. After a few minutes the item was addressed, and Director of the Capital Improvement Projects Department Mary Cardenas approached the podium and presented her recommendation for consideration and approval. Councilperson Pacheco stated his inclination on appointing the applicant for a full-time position as opposed to part time. Mayor Martell clarified that the position was advertised as part time position, and it would be unfair to change the position at this time. Councilwoman Ayala then addressed the selected applicant and asked several questions. Applicant Maryury Moreno, residing at 6615 SW 1S` Ct. Pembroke Pines, Florida, approached the Council and clarified that although her high school diploma was not part of her education certificates,her GED was. Moreover, she stated although she is not familiar with the Town of Medley, she was eager to work as a team and help the Town grow. Director Cardenas was asked how the applicants were ranked, and she stated that the other applicants did not meet the needs of the department and others had been eliminated because the hiring was for a part-time position. After a brief discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT MARYURY MORENO TO A PART-TIME ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT POSITION FOR THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS DEPARTMENT EFFECTIVE MARCH 27, 2023" Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Future Operations of the Town of Medley of Community Pool. Director of the Social Services and Parks and Recreation Department Lizmari Valido approached the Council. Therefore, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO DIRECT PROCUREMENT TO INITIATE THE PROCESS AND RELEASE AN RFP FOR SERVICES FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY COMMUNITY POOL" Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley After School Program Educational Resources.
votes: Councilwoman Ayala placed a motion as follows, "TO APPROVE THE PURCHASE (4) IPADS FOR THE AFTERSCHOOL PROGRAM TO BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE SOFTWARE NECESSARY FOR TUTORING SERVICES" Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley After School Program Educational Resources. Councilwoman Ayala began the discussion by explaining that the Town's afterschool program has experienced an influx of immigrated students who need to learn the English language. Therefore, Bob Lebron,the afterschool program tutor has been dedicating time to help teach those students the language. Thus, the afterschool program has a demand for additional devices due to the increased number of children in the program and the need to assist both the immigrated and the students already enrolled in the program. Councilwoman Ayala then proposed for the Town to purchase four(4)IPAD's compatible with the software used for the students' learning programs,assigned homework and school assignments. The Council expressed their agreement, and affirmed the Mayor's discretion to follow the Town's protocols for the purchase. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Ayala placed a motion as follows, "TO APPROVE THE PURCHASE (4) IPADS FOR THE AFTERSCHOOL PROGRAM TO BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE SOFTWARE NECESSARY FOR TUTORING SERVICES" Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Social Services programs. A recap of the Council workshop that had taken place at 4:00 pm was discussed.After discussion,it was determined to apply the same criteria to all resident services programs except for the afterschool program, summer camp program and the start-up grant program.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Social Services programs. A recap of the Council workshop that had taken place at 4:00 pm was discussed.After discussion,it was determined to apply the same criteria to all resident services programs except for the afterschool program, summer camp program and the start-up grant program. As previously requested during the Council workshop, Finance Director Charmaine circulated the 2023 Federal Poverty Guidelines reflecting the annual income ranges for households,depending on the family size. Mayor Martell then addressed the intent to implement the federal poverty guidelines to all social services programs. Councilwoman Ayala expressed concerns with implementing these guidelines to children's programs and the Start-Up grant program,therefore she requested they be excluded from the new criteria. Additionally, it was the consensus of the Council to have annual renewals of program's registrations due to the yearly changes of the federal poverty guidelines. The Council was also in agreement to apply the annual renewal of services to the light housekeeping program and for the annual registrations of all programs to be done in March of every year. It was also agreed upon by the Town Council to grandfather all existing program participants under the former criteria. However, residents able to work and drive on the current medical transportation program are to be removed from the program immediately,unless the transportation services are requested on an emergency needed basis. After a lengthy discussion and all proposals clarified, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO APPROVE THE FOLLOWING CHANGES TO ALL SOCIAL SERVICES PROGRAMS WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE AFTER-SCHOOL PROGRAM, SUMMER CAMP PROGRAM,AND THE START-UP GRANT PROGRAM.

segs.text: - EFFECTIVE MARCH 6, 2023, THE LIGHT HOUSEKEEPING PROGRAM WILL PROVIDE A MAXIMUM OF TWO (2) HOURS OF SERVICE FOR ALL EXISTING AND NEW APPLICANTS, AND ALL PERSONS LIVING IN THE HOUSEHOLD MUST MEET ALL REQUIREMENTS FOR APPLICATION APPROVAL. NEW APPLICANTS MAY ONLY HAVE A MAXIMUM OF TWO (2) PERSONS PER HOUSEHOLD,SHALL BE SUBJECT TO THE U.S DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES POVERTY GUIDELINES, AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO RENEW THE APPLICATION FOR SERVICES IN MARCH OF EVERY YEAR." Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously. After a brief recap of the discussed changes for the medical transportation program during the Council workshop and further discussion of the same, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO MOVE ALL EXISTING PARTICIPANTS OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION PROGRAM TO THE MIAMI-DADE COUNTY SPECIAL TRANSPORTATION SERVICES PROGRAM (STS). THE TOWN WILL ASSUME FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE RIDER'S FEE ($ 3.50 EACH WAY) OF MEDLEY PARTICIPANTS ACCEPTED IN THE STS PROGRAM. IF EXISTING PARTICIPANTS ARE DENIED BY THE STS PROGRAM, PARTICIPANTS MAY AT THAT POINT, RESUME PARTICIPATION ON THE TOWN OF MEDLEY MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION PROGRAM UPON QUALIFICATION OF THE TOWN'S MEDICAL TRANSPORTATION PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS. IN ADDITION, EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY,ALL PARTICIPANTS MUST NOT DRIVE OR WORK, AND NEW APPLICANTS SHALL BE SUBJECT TO THE U.S DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES POVERTY GUIDELINES AND WILL BE REQUIRED TO RENEW THE APPLICATION FOR SERVICES IN MARCH OF EVERY YEAR" Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala Yes Councilperson Ivan Pacheco Yes Councilperson Lizelh Ayala No Councilperson Karina Pacheco Yes The motion was carried by majority of vote. segs.text: Ordinance C-467 of the Town of Medley, Florida, Amending Ordinance C-393 by Adding Section 2-146 Lobbying After Employment Extending the Two (2) Years Prohibition to Four (4) Years After Employment; Providing for Conflicts; Providing for Severability; Providing for Codification; and Providing for an Effective Date. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Fleet Services for the Town of Medley and the Medley Police Department. Daniel Pacheco, Area Manager, and Abeo Manning, Client Strategy Manager from Enterprise Fleet Management with offices at 5105 Johnson Road Coconut Creek, FL 33073 approached the Council. Mayor Martell explained that his intent is to lease the Town s vehicles to get the most out of the Town s fleet and acquire thirty new vehicles. Mayor Martell further explained that the Town auctioned four vehicles and that Ms. Charmaine Parchment, the Town s finance director, analyzed the financial data from the sale. Councilwoman Ayala asked for a brief overview of the services provided. Mr. Pacheco continued to explain that their company is a total fleet management provider that assists in acquisition, maintenance, fueling and everything related to operating the vehicles. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked for clarification on the cost for leasing the vehicles. Mr. Pacheco explained that it is considered a purchase based on an equity lease structure, a municipal lease where the Town would own the assets at the end of the term. Mr. Pacheco further explained that the expense is the same is if it were purchased and what Enterprise provides is for the Town to not to have to pay for the full cost upfront. Enterprise would also assist the Town in acquiring the vehicles in its desired cycle. Mr. Pizzi joined the discussion and directed Finance Director Parchment to approach the Council and answer any questions on the financial analysis for this proposal. It was noted that if the Council were to approve the proposal, the agreement would need to be reviewed and finalized per the Council s direction. Additionally, Mr. Pizzi explained that if the Town at any point in the agreement would like to terminate it, it could do so. Lastly, the Council asked for clarification on whether Enterprise would also maintain the current fleet or if the fleet needed to remain with the current service provider. It was clarified that the leasing program includes maintenance service at the cost of six dollars a month for the maintenance services for the fleet they assist in acquiring. Councilperson Pacheco asked Ms. Parchment to state her recommendation on this matter. Director Parchment then expressed how leasing the vehicles is financially sustainable for the Town whereas the Town could not support purchasing all the vehicles needed right out in cash. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of Two (2) Utilities Laborer Positions for the Utilities Department. Utilities Director approached the podium, and a brief recess was announced. ** A brief recess was taken at 7:47pm. Meeting resumed at 7:51pm. ** Director Soto announced that he will only be presenting the recommendation of Mr. Brian R. Jacomino for the position of Laborer because the second selected candidate no longer accepts the position. Councilwoman Pacheco interjected to state that the selection process is unfair because although the Town gives preference to Medley residents it is not advertised, therefore wasting applicant s time. Councilperson Pacheco entered the discussion and expressed his disagreement on the recommendation and explained that the Town required no experience to fill the position and believes that the Town should cease this form of hiring. Councilperson Pacheco continued to explain that if the applicant does not qualify, they should not be selected just because they are a Medley resident. Additionally, Councilperson Pacheco explained that the applicants qualifications, would be better fitted for the public works department. Mayor Martell joined the discussion and stated that checking all the applicants would be a waste of time because the selected and recommended applicant qualifies for the position. Councilperson Pacheco then voiced his disagreement with the Town funding the continued education and training of staff for their respective positions and departments. Vice-Mayor Ayala explained that eliminating the hiring process has resulted in current hiring system and he supports the Mayor s process and the director s recommendation. Councilwoman Ayala stated that no one in the Council is an expert on human resources or has the proper education required, and that the Council is not a supervisor to identify applicants issues. Councilwoman Ayala further stated that the issue is a system s issues and if the Town continues with this system there will be mistakes. Councilwoman Ayala continued to state that if the elected officials felt that the employee was unfit to perform the job, then it could have been handled, but eliminating a neutral and necessary position is a systematic issue. segs.head: - Discussion and Action of the Town of Medley Medical Bathing Services Program.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action of the Town of Medley Medical Bathing Services Program. Mayor Martell addressed the item and stated that the bathing services should be provided by medical health care providers opposed to being funded by the Town. Thus, the Mayor recommended to end the program and advise the current participants to obtain the services from their health care providers. Mayor Martell also explained that said program, in accordance with the Town attorney s legal opinion, should be funded from the Town of Medley foundation instead of the general funds and said services can be obtained from the individual s medical provider. Director Lizmari Valido joined the discussion and stated that the program currently has five participants for an estimated cost of thirteen thousand dollars per year. Additionally, she noted that the service is being provided to individuals who truly need it and are in a vulnerable state, thus changing the service provider would be difficult and uncomfortable for them. Vice Mayor Ayala expressed his disagreement with the cancellation of the program and explained that it will change the public opinion of the mayor if the proposal is approved. After a brief discussion Councilperson Pacheco made a motion as follows, TO CONTINUE WITH THE EXISTING FIVE (5) PARTICIPANTS OF THE MEDICAL BATHING PROGRAM FUNDED BY THE TOWN OF MEDLEY FOUNDATION AND TO END THE PROGRAM MOVING FORWARD FOR FUTURE APPLICANTS. Vice Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell - Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala - Yes Councilperson Lizelh Ayala- No Councilperson Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilperson Karina Pacheco- Yes Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it was carried by majority of vote.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Policy and Procedures of the Sports Contribution Program. Councilwoman Ayala addressed the item and requested for the income constraints implemented for the sports contribution program be removed. Councilwoman Ayala also stated that since the March meeting three applications had been received and rejected due to the income limitation put in effect. Additionally, she explained that the complaints she has received are a repercussion of making rushed decisions and how implemented policies at times do not work in all circumstances. Once more she proposed to have the income-based qualification for the program removed. Councilwoman Ayala further stated that the Council, as members of the Town of Medley Foundation, could meet in a quarterly basis to address and recruit funding for the foundation. Mayor Martell reiterated the Town attorney s legal opinion about funding these programs though the Town of Medley Foundation and stated the importance of reaching out to businesses for donations. It was the consensus of the Town Council to approve the recent rejected applications submitted for the sport contribution program. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Ayala made a motion as follows, TO REMOVE THE ANNUAL POVERTY INCOME GUIDELINES FROM THE SPORTS CONTRIBUTION PROGRAM AND TO FUND THE SPORTS CONTRIBUTION PROGRAM WITH TOWN OF MEDLEY FOUNDATION FUNDING. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously. The next order of business was the Town Attorney s Report/Communication section of the agenda. The items were discussed as follows,

segs.head: - Report and Update on the Enforcement of the Town of Medley Community Pool Construction Agreement.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 8:45 pm.
segs.text: - Report and Update on the Enforcement of the Town of Medley Community Pool Construction Agreement. Mr. Pizzi announced the town has taken possession of the pool, and there are two issues, one is a legal matter, and noted that at the council s direction a bid was put out for companies to apply to manage the community pool. A special meeting will be called with the recommended vendor to be awarded to manage the pool and at the meeting all pool matters can be discussed. Since there was no other business to address, Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 8:45 pm. IN Vf Jenny DiGinedmof Assistant Town Clerk / pene Mayor

segs.head: Resolution C-2078 of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida, Approving a Request to South Florida Water Management District (SF WMD) for the Sale or Exchange of Surplus Land to Assist the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) in the Completion of Traffic Improvements on Okeechobee Road and NW South River Drive Attached Hereto as Exhibit A ; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to adopt resolution C-2078, Vice Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: Resolution C-2078 of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida, Approving a Request to South Florida Water Management District (SF WMD) for the Sale or Exchange of Surplus Land to Assist the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) in the Completion of Traffic Improvements on Okeechobee Road and NW South River Drive Attached Hereto as Exhibit A ; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi addressed the Council and explained that the matter at hand was the sale of South Florida Water Management land to FDOT for the acquisition of an easement required for the completion of a current traffic improvement project, at no loss for the Town. It was noted that FDOT can waive the appraisal process for the expedition of this matter. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion to adopt resolution C-2078, Vice Mayor Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: Resolution C-2087 of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida, Selecting the Bid and Awarding Contract to Synalovski Romanik Saye, LLC for the Architectural, Structural, and Recreational Design Services for the Town of Medley Recreational Center (Safe Building) Project (CIP Project No.0500-1); Authorizing the Mayor to Enter Into a Contract for Construction Substantially in the Form Attached Hereto as Exhibit A with the Contractor; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date.
votes: Vice-Mayor Ayala placed a motion to adopt resolution C-2087. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: Resolution C-2087 of the Town Council of the Town of Medley, Florida, Selecting the Bid and Awarding Contract to Synalovski Romanik Saye, LLC for the Architectural, Structural, and Recreational Design Services for the Town of Medley Recreational Center (Safe Building) Project (CIP Project No.0500-1); Authorizing the Mayor to Enter Into a Contract for Construction Substantially in the Form Attached Hereto as Exhibit A with the Contractor; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Attorney Pizzi explained that a panel of staff members selected Synalovski Romanik Saye, LLC for the Architectural, Structural, and Recreational Design Services of the Town of Medley Recreational Center. Thus, Mr. Pizzi explained the next step is to negotiate with the vendor for the contract price. Mayor Martell reiterated the intent to build a safe building capable of withstanding winds equivalent to a Category 5 hurricane. Without further discussion, Vice-Mayor Ayala placed a motion to adopt resolution C-2087. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Community Pool Operations.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 5:20 pm.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Community Pool Operations. Town Attorney Pizzi clarified that the Town received a bid for the community pool management services, and a brief presentation had previously been given to the Council by the vendor that had been selected. Therefore, the first part presented a resolution awarding the bid to the selected contractor. Mayor Martell then explained the proposed operations for the community pool and stated the proposed hours of operation which were announced to be Fridays from 1:00pm to 7:00pm, Saturdays and Sundays from 10:00am to 7:00pm. Moreover, Mayor Martell explained that the Town hired a company for maintenance of the pool therefore the language needs to be adjusted on proposal to remove the maintenance component. Mayor Martell also announced the groundbreaking event for the community pool which was stated to be the first Saturday in June, with an opening date to the public that Friday June 2, 2023. Additionally, it was explained that the community pool open season will begin the second week of May until the second week of September. Furthermore, it was explained that hours would need to be added on the proposal to accommodate the scheduling from Social Services and Parks and Recreational director Lizmari Valido for the summer camp, and the Medley Youth Social Club (MYSC) summer activities. Director Valido approached the Council and informed them that the summer camp aged kids have activities scheduled on Mondays and Wednesdays from 10:00AM to 2:00pm and the MYSC and Police Explorer kids have Tuesdays scheduled from 10:00AM to 2:00PM. Thus, Mayor Martell instructed finance director Charmaine Parchment to add the additional hours to the weekly hours of said operations to the final proposal. After a brief discussion Vice-Mayor Ayala placed a motion to adopt resolution C-2088A as follows, TO ADOPT RESOLUTION C-2088A, SUBJECT TO THE REMOVAL OF THE MAINTENANCE COMPONENT OF THE PROPOSAL AND THE ADJUSTMENT OF THE HOURS OF OPERATIONS OF FRIDAYS FROM 1:00PM 7:00PM, SATURDAYS AND SUNDAYS FROM 10:00AM 7:00PM AND THE SOCIAL SERVICES SUMMER CAMP, MYSC, AND POLICE EXPLORERS SCHEDULED SUMMER ACTIVITIES. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it carried unanimously. Since there was no other business to address, Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 5:20 pm. [\ N Jenny DiGiacomo, Assistant Town Clerk oberto Martell, Mayor

segs.head: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA NOVEMBER 14, 2023 A public meeting of the Town of Medley was opened on November 14, 2023, at 7:00 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA NOVEMBER 14, 2023 A public meeting of the Town of Medley was opened on November 14, 2023, at 7:00 p.m. Town of Medley Capital Improvement Projects Director Mary Cardenas-Aldir opened the meeting and addressed the audience stating that the purpose of this first public meeting is to receive the public s input, address any concerns and conduct public engagement on the findings and recommendations of the Vulnerability and Resiliency Assessment and Adaptation Action Plan. Terry Garcia, Senior P.E and representative of R.J. Behar & Co., Inc conducted a presentation of the Town of Medley Vulnerability and Resiliency Assessment and Adaptation Action Plan (see attached) which included information on the project funding sources, study goals, study methodology and data collection. It was noted that the study is needed to comply with State mandate, and it is necessary for applications of funding opportunities. Furthermore, the study identifies critical infrastructural needs to be addressed, to assist in compiling a plan of action. It was explained how sea levels have increased based statistics surveyed throughout the years and has concluded that flooding has intensified Countywide. Jose Lopez, Director of Environmental Engineering, Project Manager, and a representative of Bermello, Ajamil & Partners, presented the study s data analysis that addressed in detail the portions of project prioritization. It was mentioned that the analysis phase included input from the Town of Medley public works, utilities, and the building department. Alejandro Toural, Assistant Project Manager, and representative with Kimley-Horn and Associates discussed in detail the modeling process and scenarios depicted in the study. In continuance, Mr. Lopez expressed projected priorities commencing with Pump Station #1, followed by the Medley Municipal Services Facility (MMSF), and the Lakeside Retirement Home Community Center. It was also stated that the projections are based on no activity from South Florida Water Management and that the report does address the newly annexed area within the Town of Medley. To conclude, it was explained that a survey will be prepared to be accessed on the Town s website. The feedback will be provided in the final report estimated to be ready for approval by the EDP and presented by January or February. segs.head: - Approval/Corrections of the Minutes of the Regular Council Meeting of October 2, 2023.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion to approve the minutes of the October 2, 2023, regular council meeting as presented, Councilperson Pacheco seconded, and the minutes were adopted unanimously.

Vice-Mayor Ayala then made a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda with the announced removal and additions. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and the meeting s agenda was approved by the Council unanimously.
segs.text: - Approval/Corrections of the Minutes of the Regular Council Meeting of October 2, 2023. Mayor Martell made a motion to approve the minutes of the October 2, 2023, regular council meeting as presented, Councilperson Pacheco seconded, and the minutes were adopted unanimously. Mayor Martell then announced the removal of the following item to be tabled for the December 4, 2023, regular council meeting, - 12 (F) Resolution Approving a Professional Services Agreement between KW HR Consulting, LLC. and the Town of Medley, Florida for Human Resources Consulting Services; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Execute the Agreement; Authorizing the Town Mayor and Town Officials to Take all Action Necessary to Implement the Terms and Conditions of the Services Agreement; and Providing for an Effective Date Additionally, Vice-Mayor Ayala announced the addition of the following Town of Medley items, - 13 (4) 1. Discussion and Action for the Request for a Moratorium for the Sale of Parcel B. - 13 (5) 2. Discussion and Action on Legislative Priorities for the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Without further discussion, Vice-Mayor Ayala then made a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda with the announced removal and additions. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and the meeting s agenda was approved by the Council unanimously. The public comment section was then announced. It was noted that no public comments were made. segs.head: - Presentation of Award by Cigna to the Town of Medley for Long-Term Partnership.
votes: Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE RENEWAL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY COMMERCIAL INSURANCE POLICIES AND APPROVE THE RENEWAL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY EMPLOYEE MEDICAL BENEFIT INSURANCE POLICY. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Presentation of Award by Cigna to the Town of Medley for Long-Term Partnership. Jennifer Gambill, client advisor, Lissette Calderon, accounts benefit executive, Ted Konstantopoulos, regional growth leader for employee benefits, and Allison Velilla account executive for commercial property casualty with Morris and Reynolds a division of World Insurance Associates LLC approached the Council. Mrs. Gambill then announced that Morris and Reynolds have merged with World Insurance Associates, LLC and informed the Council that after thirty years of working with the Town of Medley Mr. Bob Reynolds has retired, therefore he chose her to be his replacement to work alongside the Town. It was expressed how the Town has reached an amazing outcome during this year s negotiations due to the combined efforts of staff and the Mayor resulting in a zero increase to the Cigna healthcare to both the Town and employees as well as a zero-cost increase to any of the Town s employee benefits despite a small increase in the employee assistance program of $175.00. Additionally, it was noted that the Towns five-year average for increases is seven percent better than the rest of the industry nationwide which is a testament to the Town s well managed plan. Workers Compensation claims have decreased which is a positive result supported by the Town proactive approach to safety and loss control. The Mayor and Council then thanked staff present from Morris and Reynolds for their continued support in managing the Town s employee benefits policies. Without further discussion, Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE RENEWAL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY COMMERCIAL INSURANCE POLICIES AND APPROVE THE RENEWAL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY EMPLOYEE MEDICAL BENEFIT INSURANCE POLICY. Councilwoman Rodriguez addressed the Town Attorney for clarification on this item. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi then explained that the federal government HUD has millions of dollars in block grants that are made available, and municipalities must go through the State or County government to apply for those grants. One grant is the (CDBG) block grant which provides federal funds for home improvements, affordable housing, public facilities, and homeowner assistance programs. Therefore, the County received funds of over millions of dollars for these programs, and by the Town signing the interlocal agreement, it will be eligible from 2024 through 2026 to put in applications to receive funding for projects that assist residents. segs.text: Resolution C-2123 Appointing Michael Salem as the Deputy Director and Executive Assistant to the Town of Medley Social Services and Parks and Recreations Department; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Michael Pizzi announced a change to the Resolution presented which said language will now state Resolution appointing Michael Salem as Assistant to the Town of Medley Social Services and Parks and Recreations Department . Town Clerk Victoria Martinez acknowledged the changes made. Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed that the administration has been disrespectful in hiring employees, who have already begun working, and bringing Resolutions months later for ratification and approval by the Council after the fact. Additionally, she stated that there is no Resolution or legislation in the Town that allows for this process and reiterated how disrespectful it is. Councilwoman Rodriguez further stated that as elected officials the administration should not bypass the appointment of staff and exclude them from the process which is both unethical and against the democratic process. Therefore, Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed her disagreement, and that she will not support the item. Mr. Pizzi interjected to explain that Mr. Salem has an extensive resume, working with the Town of Medley for over 20 years, a background which includes a Master s degree in public administration, a member of the alliance for aging organization, and is the Chairman for Neighbors for Neighbors organization. Additionally, it was noted that Mr. Salem has multi-faceted uses, and has assisted multiple departments because of his knowledgeable background and experience. Therefore, the recommendation is to approve Mr. Salem based on his credentials. It was noted that the salary would be sixty- five thousand dollars a year. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2123. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala- No Councilmember Lizelh Ayala- No Councilmember Karina Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Ivan Pacheco- Yes The motion was carried by majority of vote. segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY OCTOBER 16, 2023 SAFETY COMMITEE MEETING A public meeting of the Town of Medley Safety Committee was called to order on October 16, 2023 at 10:30 am. The following were present: TOWN CLERK VICTORIA MARTINEZ ASSISTANT TOWN CLERK JENNY DIGIACOMO Department heads were also in attendance and a sign-in sheet was provided. Christopher Kittleson from Preferred Governmental Claim Solutions (PGCS) representative of the Town s workers compensation insurance policy introduced himself and opened the meeting giving a general overview of the topics of discussion, as well as the goal of the safety committee in general. Mr. Kittleson explained that the Town can offer group trainings and reiterated the importance of documenting such trainings taken and the staff members taking them for record purposes. Mr. Kittleson further stated that the Town needed to establish a minimum mandatory training practice for post-accident procedures as well as an assessment to investigate the loss history of each department to determine what kind of reoccurring claims are taking place. Additionally, Mr. Kittleson briefly defined preventative action and restated the importance of the safety committee and its role in analyzing claims and incidents to prevent them from reoccurring. He continued to announce that on May 2, 2024 Preferred Governmental Claim Solutions (PGCS) is hosting a members education training and extended an invitation to all members of the Medley staff that were present, as well as a webinar scheduled for November 9, 2023 targeted for the law enforcement sector regarding Florida Statute 112.18, commonly referred to as the Heart and Lung Bill . Town Clerk Victoria Martinez who also serves as the Town s Risk Manager, highlighted the decrease in property damage claims, and acknowledged the Public Works department for implementing a new section process which monitors Town roadways to better address and document maintenance schedules to improve and further prevent roadway claims. Ms. Martinez continued to review the items as listed on the agenda and affirmed that the directors have a clear grasp on post-accident procedures. Also, the police department was acknowledged for their progressive discipline policy and practices which reinforces the prevention of claims recurrence. PIZZI Town Attorney Michael Pizzi started the meeting explaining that at the last workshop, a detailed presentation of the amendment process was had and further stated that it is healthy to conduct a charter review process every five years or so given that there may be law changes that could potentially render existing language invalid. Mayor Martell proposed to have the matter of future compensation increases for the Mayor and Council brought to the electoral voters. Mayor Martell further explained that since the annual compensation for Mayor and Councilmembers have been established and capped, future increases should be at the will of the voters. Vice-Mayor Ayala expressed disagreement with the proposal and stated to leave the compensation matter, including increases out of the charter review process. Vice-Mayor Ayala further stated that term limits is a matter that will be much more appreciated instead. Councilperson Pacheco also agreed to leave the compensation matter out of the process. Mr. Pizzi stated that to move forward with the proposed amendments a majority of the council or general consensus would be best to better understand the direction desired by the Town Council. Therefore,the matters proposed were presented as follows, - Proposal of Amendment to Article III. segs.head: First Reading of Ordinance C-470 Adopting Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-2024.
votes: Councilwoman Rodriguez made a motion as follows, TO CAP THE MAYOR S ANNUAL COMPENSATION AT $ 230,871.72 AND THE COUNCIL S ANNUAL COMPENSATION AT $ 59,879.53 FOR THE FORSEABLE FUTURE. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: First Reading of Ordinance C-470 Adopting Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-2024. Finance Director Charmaine Parchment presented an overview of the proposed budget for fiscal year 2023-2024 which detailed the expected revenues and expenses. Ms. Parchment continued to state that the Town has already tentatively established a millage rate of 3.0 and that the Town s property value has increased due to the annexed properties which accounted for an approximately a 62% increase. In continuance, director Parchment recommended the 3.00 mills for every $1000.00 dollars which would be a reduction by 0.2 mills from the year prior. She then continued to present the revenues and expenses as listed on her presentation, and it was clarified to the Vice Mayor and Council that although it is required Minutes of September 11, 2023 Special Council Meeting- 1*t Budget Public Hearing and custom to have anywhere from five to ten percent in reserves the Town has budgeted way over the recommended amount at approximately 20% of its operating budget in reserves. Councilwoman Rodriguez then addressed the Mayor and Council with a concern and stated that the Mayor and Council were well compensated and requested support on the following matter. Councilwoman Rodriguez then referenced Article 3, Section 8 of the Town Charter which references the Mayor and Council salary Compensation of the Mayor and council members shall be prescribed by ordinance and fixed in annual budget . Councilwoman Rodrigues further stated that Ordinance C-424 adopted in 2017 approved an increase for the Mayor and council members totaling to $187,000.00 annual salary for the Mayor and an annual salary of $39,000.00 for the Council. Thus, as of this fiscal year 2022/2023, the Mayor s annual salary stands at $ 230,871.72, and the Council s annual salary at $ 59,879.53. Councilwoman Rodriguez continued to explain that her proposal to set salary caps for the Mayor and Councilmembers is both, responsible and ethical, given that serving in public office shouldn t be an intrinsic decision motivated by salary. Therefore, Councilwoman Rodriguez made a motion as follows, TO CAP THE MAYOR S ANNUAL COMPENSATION AT $ 230,871.72 AND THE COUNCIL S ANNUAL COMPENSATION AT $ 59,879.53 FOR THE FORSEABLE FUTURE. Mayor Martell seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.

Vice-Mayor Ayala asked for clarification on the resolution presented. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi clarified that several Town departments such as the building department have contractors to provide support services for the department. Therefore, this item would authorize the request for companies to submit bids to determine how much it would cost the Town the support services for the CIP department. In addition, Mr. Pizzi explained that the department lost its only staff member thus losing time and resources. Whereas if there was an outside contractor available, they could provide support to the department because they have the experience to do so. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Request to Hire One (1)Part-Time Code Compliance Officer I for the Town of Medley Code Compliance Department. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded and the motion carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Request to Hire One (1) Full-Time Accountant for the Town of Medley Finance Department. Finance Director Charmaine Parchment approached the council and requested the hiring of an Accountant for the finance department to assist with additional duties such as grants,reporting,revenue expenditures and review of payment receipts for projects that were put off bidding, as well as audits. It was noted that the position does not exist, but that an annual salary of$55,000.00 was budgeted for the position which was established based on.research. Councilwoman Rodriguez interjected to express that the salary being set seemed low given the requirements of a bachelor's degree education and three years of experience. Director Parchment recommended to bring back the matter before Council to further discuss the selected applicant and a negotiated salary. Without further discussion, Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion as follows, "TO APPROVE THE REQUEST TO HIRE ONE(1)FULL-TIME ACCOUNTANT FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY FINANCE DEPARTMENT. Councilwoman Rodriguez seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously. It was then announced that the Finance Department and the Police Department requested to table item 12D to be addressed and further discussed at the budget meeting of September 11, 2023. Vice-Mayor Ayala placed a motion to table the item as requested and the motion was carried unanimously. Since there was no other business to address, Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 7:38 pm. segs.head: Resolution C-2152 Approving an Amendment to Development Agreement between the Town of Medley and Waste Management Inc. of Florida for Property Consisting of Approximately 144.908 Acres and Generally Located at the Corner of N.W. 106" Street and N.W. 95" Avenue; Authorizing the Mayor to Execute the Development Agreement; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date.
votes: Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2152 on first reading. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala- Yes Councilmember Karina Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Lizelh Rodriguez- No The motion was carried by majority of vote.
segs.text: Resolution C-2152 Approving an Amendment to Development Agreement between the Town of Medley and Waste Management Inc. of Florida for Property Consisting of Approximately 144.908 Acres and Generally Located at the Corner of N.W. 106" Street and N.W. 95" Avenue; Authorizing the Mayor to Execute the Development Agreement; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. No public comments were received on this item. David Myhan, President of Waste Management of Florida residing at 6858 NW 58 St, Parkland Florida approached the Council and expressed his gratitude to the Town for their partnership and continued support. Mr. Myhan continued to explain that it may take four to five years before expanding to the new proposed location. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked for clarification on the calculation used to produce the proposed new rate of $2.49 per ton of solid waste and Mr. Myhan explained that a financial model was created based on operating expenses, capital invested, and an internal formula to come up with a fair price for the Town of Medley. Additionally, it was explained that the rate will continue to increase from the initial $2.49 yearly due to the consumer price index (CPI). Vice-Mayor Ayala expressed that he would not be an obstacle in this initiative and expressed his gratitude to Alex Gonzalez for being an asset to Waste Management. Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed her stance on the matter and explained that her background in public health has allowed her to study and know how health is impacted in marginalized groups. Councilwoman Rodriguez further stated that she has explored how waste sites are always located in marginalized areas where there are people of color, and low-income communities because the people do not have the political pull, are unable to express concerns, and do not have the knowledge of the long- term outcomes of these waste sites. Councilwoman Rodriguez then read a health study into the record for educational purposes and expressed her opposition to this item reiterating that the financial gains have been explained but the potential hazards to the community have not been discussed. Alex Gonzalez, representative for Waste Management approached the Council and reiterated Mr. Myhan s statement that the Town of Medley waste site does not receive any hazardous waste, only solid waste. segs.head: - Presentation by Councilwoman Rodriguez in Collaboration with the University of Miami DAWN Alzheimer s Research Team: Empowering the Community Through Education and Advancing Understanding Through Genetic Research.
segs.text: - Presentation by Councilwoman Rodriguez in Collaboration with the University of Miami DAWN Alzheimer s Research Team: Empowering the Community Through Education and Advancing Understanding Through Genetic Research. Vanessa Rodriguez, BA, Research Manager residing at 1810 W 56 ST Hialeah, FL 33012 and Karina Celis, MD, Scientific Associate residing at 2511 SW 26 Lane Miami, Florida 33133 from the DAWN Alzheimer s research team at the University of Miami School of Medicine approached the Council and gave a brief overview of their initiative and proposed partnership with the Town of Medley to host a community event to spread Alzheimer awareness and recruit participants for their genetic research study. It was clarified that they do not conduct clinical trials but require volunteers to provide their genetic records for participants that fall under the criteria of the study. Councilwoman Rodriguez also clarified that the matter would be discussed and acted upon later on another agenda item.

Interim Building and Zoning Director Miguel Nunez approached the Council and introduced Scarlett Hammons, Town s Zoning consultant. Mr. Nunez then continued to explain that the presented plat is governed under Florida Statue and allows for the waiver of the plat with Council s approval. Mr. Felix Lasarte with offices located at 3250 NE 1*' Ave, on behalf of WMG storage partners and Mr. Brian Adler from the law firm of Bilzin Sumberg, also was present, presented the item. Mr. Lasarte then explained that once there is parcel of land that is going to be subdivided, it is required to have a platting action to plat the property, but in this case the owners, WMG Medley Owner LLC, have an existing warehouse on that same parcel of land where a plat already exists. Mr. Lasarte further explained that the owner will be putting another building within the same parcel, therefore it is common for there to be a waiver of plat in these instances because a plat already exists. Attorney Pizzi explained that Miami-Dade County Elections Department has asked the Town of Medley to pass legislation that would give them four weeks to schedule a run-off election. segs.text: Resolution C-2208 Approving the Purchase of Bypass Pumps from Thompson Pump & Manufacturing Co., Inc. Pursuant to Prices Obtained through the Florida Sheriff's Association Bid Pricing and not to Exceed a Total of $97,090.00; Providing for Waiver of Competitive Procurement Pursuant to Section 2-131 of the Town of Medley Code; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Attorney Pizzi explained that piggybacking off other contracts allows the Town to waive the competitive bid process which was already performed by another source of government, allowing for the best price and the fulfillment of the services without the time constraints of the Towns procurement procedure. Attorney Pizzi further stated that the item is recommended by staff and reviewed to legal sufficiency by the legal department. Councilmember Ayala stated that the equipment can be acquired for a better price, therefore he does not agree with the recommended items to be purchased by the Town. Councilmember Ayala proposed that the item be tabled for further review. Utilities Director Jorge Soto approached the Council and stated that he had included three other items and their quotes for review. Director Soto also expressed that the items he presented fulfill the services required by the Town. Moreover, he recommended the Town to hire a procurement employee that would better specialize in assisting departments with purchases of this nature. Mayor and council agreed with the suggestion. Mayor Stefano then requested additional time to review the matter further. Councilwoman Lizelh Rodriguez reiterated that the Town is focusing on correcting the bypass of processes. It was clarified the Town has paid approximately $2,500.00 for the rental of this equipment for two months. In addition, it was proposed that a workshop specific to the utilities department functions be held to discuss old systems and overall improvements. Without further discussion, Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion as follows, TO TABLE THE ITEM AND FURTHER DISCUSS THE MATTER IN THE FORM OF A COUNCIL WORKSHOP. Councilwoman Lizeth Rodriguez seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Reclassification to Grants Specialist Position. Mayor Stefano explained that the proposed reclassification aligns with the job duties being performed currently by Mr. Michael Salem. Therefore, Mr. Salem would only be overseeing grants associated with the Capital Improvement Projects Department. Mr. Salem approached the podium and expressed his agreement and thanked the Council for the | opportunity to work in what he specializes in. Councilwoman Lizelh Rodriguez requested a Council workshop to discuss a breakdown of all the Town s grants. It was unanimously agreed upon to schedule a future Council Workshop for the matter. Vice-Mayor Jinete addressed the item by proposing the creation of a property manager position for the Lakeside Retirement Park. It was expressed that there is a need for Lakeside to have an onsite manger to fulfill daily roles that are not feasible by the Town Clerk s office which is located at Town hall. Councilmember Ayala asked for clarification on the role as it relates to both the Town Clerk Victoria Martinez and the Hot Meal Program director Fatima Fuentes. Vice-Mayor Jinete reiterated that the proposal is to acknowledge the Town s need to create the position, and further proposes a Council Workshop to discuss what the duties and the job description will be inclusive of all the Councils thoughts for the position. It was noted that the position would be posted and applied for with the criteria set by the Town. Consequently, Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE CREATION OF A PROPERTY MANAGER POSITION FOR THE LAKESIDE RETIREMENT PARK, AND TO SCHEDULE A COUNCIL WORKSHOP TO DISCUSS THE DUTIES OF THE POSITION FURTHER TO BRING A FINAL RECOMMENDATION TO COUNCIL Councilmember Ayala seconded, and the motion carried unanimously. **A brief recess was held at 8:16pm and resumed 8:21pm**

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Employee Benefits Insurance Policy.
votes: Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion as follows, TO RENEW THE HEALTH INSURANCE BENFIT WITH CIGNA AND ACCEPT THE NINE PERCENT (9%) INCREASE FOR THE 2025 YEAR. Councilmember Ayala seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Employee Benefits Insurance Policy. Jennifer Gambil with World s Insurance approached the Council and explained the organization s long term historical partnership with the Town. Ms. Gambil continued to state that the Town has expressed how Cigna has provided excellent customer care to the employees. The loss ratio on medical insurance was explained which was said to be at 112% and how the 2024 renewal had no increase to the Town s plan rates. Nonetheless, it was explained that for the 2025 year the Town is left with two options, a (9%) increase to the insurance policy to keep the current benefits as status quo for the employees, and the alternative option of a (3.5%) renewal rate increasing employee deductibles, medical co-payments, and prescription costs. After a brief discussion on the matter, it was agreed upon to keep the status quo on all benefits, thus the Town to accept the 9% increase option totaling to a $216,000.00 increase. Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion as follows, TO RENEW THE HEALTH INSURANCE BENFIT WITH CIGNA AND ACCEPT THE NINE PERCENT (9%) INCREASE FOR THE 2025 YEAR. Councilmember Ayala seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Update and Discussion on New Federal Overtime Regulations.
votes: Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion to adjourn, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Update and Discussion on New Federal Overtime Regulations. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi stated that under the fair labor act anyone that works over 40 hours is required to get overtime. The only exemption to getting overtime is if your classified in an executive position. Attorney Pizzi further stated that effective January 28, 2025 a law goes into effect mandating that if an employee is making below $58,000.00 a year regardless of employee s classification, they would be required to receive overtime. Thus, the Attorney s recommendation is that the Mayor, Town Attorney, and Finance Department have a meeting to keep up with the status of this legislation and see what impact it would have to the Town. Moreover, return the item to Council if there is a need for direction or change. Without further discussion, Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion to adjourn, and it was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 9:27 pm. ei ia ERP, CMC, Town Clerk a" sera i

STEFANO VICE-MAYOR ARTURO JINETE COUNCIL MEMBERS: EDGAR AYALA LIZELH RODRIGUEZ LOURDES RODRIGUEZ TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: MICHAEL A. segs.text: Mayor Stefano then opened the meeting for public comments. It was noted that no comments were made. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi read the New Business items into the records and the matters were discussed and acted upon as follows, - Presentation and Discussion of Utilities Maintenance and Improvement Projects. Utilities Director Jorge Soto introduced the workshop and explained that the purpose of the presentation was to provide the Town Council, particularly the newly elected members, with a comprehensive overview of the Town's water and wastewater utility system, current maintenance practices, regulatory obligations, and future capital improvement needs. He emphasized that wastewater operations remain one of the Town's most critical responsibilities due to the extensive state and federal regulatory requirements governing them. Mr. Soto introduced the Town's consulting utility engineer, Tommy Ruiz explaining that the engineering firm had worked alongside the Town for many years in planning, regulatory compliance, system maintenance, and infrastructure improvements. He noted that the presentation (See attached) was intended as an open workshop, encouraging Council Members to ask questions throughout the discussion and offering additional individual briefings if desired. The engineering presentation included an overview of the Town's water distribution and wastewater collection systems, with emphasis placed on: Minutes of December 11, 2024 Public Meeting e Federal and State regulatory compliance requirements; e Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) oversight; e Miami-Dade County environmental regulations; e Operation and maintenance of the wastewater collection system; e Preventative maintenance programs; e Sewer system inspections and rehabilitation; e Inflow and infiltration reduction efforts; e Smoke testing and closed-circuit television (CCTV) inspections; e Pump station operations; e Emergency response procedures; e Long-term capital planning. Council Members received an overview of the history of the Town's utility system, including how infrastructure has expanded over time to accommodate industrial growth while continuing to meet increasingly stringent environmental regulations. Staff explained that continuous maintenance and proactive rehabilitation are essential to preserving the integrity of the collection system and avoiding sanitary sewer overflows. segs.text: Resolution C-2146 Approving and Instructing Town Staff to Issue a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) for Road Paving and Resurfacing Services; Providing for Authorization; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Vice-Mayor Ayala inquired about Resolution C-2145 and the proposed road surfacing of NW 105" Way area and stated that the narrowness of the existing road and a potential buffer zone should be considered with the intention of a possible expansion. Mayor Martell explained that a component of the proposed project is to assess the project areas and address any issues including areas that are part of the road and corrected them if needed in accordance with standard road regulations. It was also clarified that the proposed project includes milling and resurfacing of the existing surface areas and drainage improvements are not part of the scope of work. It was also discussed that the existing elevation is to be maintained and that if old manholes are discovered during the milling and resurfacing project of the NW 68" Court and NW 68" Place, for them to be salvaged if possible. Councilwoman Rodriguez inquired about the proposed resurfacing of the NW 68" Court and NW 68" Place area and stated whether or not it could possibly include drainage improvements to alleviate flooding issues in the area. Utilities director Jorge Soto explained that drainage improvement projects require more funding than what is allocated for due to the environmental permitting process that is required for projects where drainage systems are addressed. It was also discussed that the existing elevation is to be maintained and that if old manholes are discovered during the milling and resurfacing process for them to be salvaged, if possible. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi stated that a Capital Improvement Projects (CIP) workshop will take place in the near future which will give the Town Council an opportunity to get an update of the status of the projects, make proposals and suggestions while revising the program and adjusting the funding allocations to fit the needs of the Town. Without further discussion Vice-Mayor Ayala made a motion to adopt Resolutions C-2143, C-2144, C- 2145 and C-2146. Councilwoman Rodriguez seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously. The next agenda items were discussed and acted upon as follows,

segs.head: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on the Proposed Declaration of Certain Real Property Owned by the Town of Medley as Surplus Property.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 5:49 pm.
segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on the Proposed Declaration of Certain Real Property Owned by the Town of Medley as Surplus Property. Mayor Martell explained that afer assessing the details of the property and speaking with staff, he would like to revisit the matter and put the property for sale. Vice-Mayor Ayala inquired about the Mayor s need for the sale of the property. Mayor Martell explained that after the Council s decision to expand the hours of operations of the community pool and the budget issues it creates, the revenue from the sale of this property can help fund the operations and the budget gap. Town attorney Michael Pizzi clarified and further explained that the matter at hand is not being considered for action to sell the property rather than for the Council to authorize staff, upon approval of the Town Council, to bid the property which would then give the Council full authority to consider whether it is desired to sell the property. Councilperson Pacheco stated that he has supported the sale of Town property in the past with the goal to achieve funding sources for Town road and drainage projects that are very much needed in areas such as the Lakeside Retirement Park. Councilman Pacheco further stated that the extension of community pool hours of operation is another financial concern that needs to be resolved, hence his support for the sale of the property. After final comments on the matter, Mayor Martell made a motion as follows, TO AUTHORIZE STAFF TO BID THE SALE OF THE PROPERTY AND FOR THE MATTER TO COME BACK TO COUNCIL FOR FURTHER DISCUSSION AND/OR ACTION. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala- No Councilmember Lizelh Ayala- No Councilmember Karina Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Ivan Pacheco- Yes The motion was carried by majority of vote. Since there was no other business to address, Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 5:49 pm. Victofia' Martingz, FRP, CMC, Town Clerk fA vy dain artell, Mayor

segs.text: (2) YEARS MUST PASS BEFORE A FORMER ELECTED OFFICIAL IS AUTHORIZED BY LAW TO RUN FOR OFFICE. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion passed unanimously. In continuance, Councilwoman Rodriguez announced that as elected officials one of the primary goals should be to have the greatest voter turnout rates. Therefore, Councilwoman Rodriguez placed a motion as follows, TO SUBMIT THE CHARTER AMENDMENT BALLOT QUESTIONS FOR THE NOVEMBER 5, 2024 GENERAL ELECTION Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell- No Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala- Yes Councilmember Lizelh Rodriguez- Yes Councilmember Karina Pacheco- No Councilmember Ivan Pacheco- No The motion did not pass by majority of vote. Mayor Martell then placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2131 subject to the to the amendments voted upon to Article III. Section 6 Form of Government- Ballot Question No. 2 and Article III. Section 5 Election and Term- Ballot Question No. 3. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala- No Councilmember Lizelh Rodriguez- No Councilmember Karina Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Ivan Pacheco- Yes The motion passed by majority of vote. Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed disagreement and stated that having this matter purposely voted on in the August primary elections instead of the November general election, the Town is perpetrating voter restriction by openly knowing there is a lower turn out rate in August and by purposely doing this, the message sent to the residents is that the Council wishes for there to be the least amount of participation so that these items are approved. She continued to state that this decision is a huge disservice to the voters. Mayor Martell announced that he would make every effort to disseminate the information to the residents and voters to have the maximum number of voters turn out for these items.

segs.head: Resolution C-2132 Declaring Certain Real Property Owned by the Town of Medley and Legally Described In Exhibit A Attached Hereto as Surplus Property; Authorizing the Town Mayor and Town Officials to Provide for the Sale or Disposition of the Surplus Property; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date.
segs.text: Resolution C-2132 Declaring Certain Real Property Owned by the Town of Medley and Legally Described In Exhibit A Attached Hereto as Surplus Property; Authorizing the Town Mayor and Town Officials to Provide for the Sale or Disposition of the Surplus Property; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Town Attorney Pizzi explained that the proposed property is approximately 18,946 sq. ft. rectangular shaped parcel, the easement contains approximately 13,200 sq. ft., 16x220sq. ft., the use of the land area for storage is approximately 5,746 sq. ft., between NW South River along the canal to the right when heading west. Mr. Machado, owner of the property next to it Alexandria Investment LLC, has indicated that if the Town had no use for the parcel, then he would be interested in purchasing the land from the Town. Therefore, the intent is to present this for the Town Council to discuss whether it wishes to declare the property as surplus. It was clarified that the Town did conduct an appraisal. Mayor Martell stated that he does not see a purpose for the property, but also stated that waiting to sell the property can allow for the property s value to increase. Councilwoman Rodriguez asked for clarification on the funds obtained from the sale, and it was confirmed that the funds would go to general funds. Councilwoman Rodriguez further stated that this interested buyer had approached the administration over a year ago, thus she cannot support back ended stories. Additionally, she explained that an appraisal was done and paid for by the interested party and by the time items are presented to the Council, arrangements have been made which does not sit well with her. Attorney Pizzi joined the discussion and expressed that this matter has been addressed with transparency and placed on a public agenda and presented to the Council for discussion. Also, attorney Pizzi stated that it is better for the interested party to pay for the appraisal instead of the taxpayers. Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that he does not see an urgency to sell the property. Thus, he expressed his disagreement. Mayor Martell reiterated that he is not in a rush to sell this property and has no intent to second the motion. Without further discussion, Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2132. Motion was not seconded, thus no action was taken.

segs.text: Resolution C-2138 Approving an Agreement between Donerite Pumps, Inc., and the Town of Medley for Electric Motor Rewind Pump Repairs and Maintenance Services; Providing for Waiver of Competitive Procurement Pursuant to Section 2-131 of the Town of Medley Code; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Execute the Contract for the Services; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that this item is presented with the waiver of the RFP process due to its urgency and for emergency purposes, but he continues to urge the Council to follow the correct procurement and RFP process. Jorge Soto Director of the Water and Sewer Department approached the Council and explained that this service was put out for competitive bidding by Miami Beach and the Town is proposing to piggyback off its procurement process. Director Soto continued to explain that for the bidding purpose, interested companies will need to take apart the motors to determine the amounts for their bid submittal, thus making it a complicated process. Vice-Mayor Ayala reiterated that although he supports Director Soto in this initiative, he urges the Town to responsibly follow the Town s procurement process. Therefore, he proposed to approve this item for a shorter period to allow for the Town to put out a request for proposal and follow the correct procurement protocols. Director Soto also stated that if an emergency were to occur and the anticipated cost exceeded five thousand dollars, he would come before Council for approval. Councilperson Pacheco added that emergencies are costly, and the Director need support, thus he agrees with this item. Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE RESOLUTION C-2138 FOR A PERIOD OF SERVICE OF SIX (6) MONTHS AND FOR THE TOWN TO PUT OUT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) FOR ELECTRIC MOTOR REWIND PUMP REPAIRS AND MAINTENANCE SERVICES. Councilperson Pacheco expressed his intent to have a pay scale established for all Town of Medley employees. Mayor then recommended a workshop for the further discussion on this item once numbers are gathered. Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed her concern with this matter and stated that setting salary wages and scales should be done by a third-party expertise and that the common practice is for this task to be done by a consulting firm. Hence, she suggested the Town to contract a consultant firm so that the process can be done completely unbiased. Mayor Martell stated that the Council will be setting the wage scales, and Councilwoman Rodriguez reiterated that it should be performed by a professional. Without further discussion, Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion as follows, MOTION TO DIRECT THE TOWN ATTORNEY AND FINANCE DIRECTOR TO CREATE A PAY SCALE FOR ALL TOWN OF MEDLEY EMPLOYEES, AND PRESENT THE NUMBERS IN THE FORM OF A COUNCIL WORKSHOP FOR DISCUSSION AND ACTION Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala- Yes Councilmember Lizelh Rodriguez- No Councilmember Karina Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Ivan Pacheco- Yes The motion passed by majority of vote.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action Request to Retain Five (5) Consultants for Child Care Attendant Positions for the Social Services and Parks and Recreation Department.
votes: Councilwoman Rodriguez placed a motion as follows, A MOTION TO HIRE FOUR (4) PART-TIME CHILD CARE ATTENDANT POSITIONS FOR THE SOCIAL SERVICES AND PARKS AND RECREATION DEPARTMENT WITH THE EXISTING POSITION REQUIREMENTS Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and the motion passed unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action Request to Retain Five (5) Consultants for Child Care Attendant Positions for the Social Services and Parks and Recreation Department. Director of the Social Services and Parks and Recreational Department Lizmari Valido approached the Council and stated that her department is short staffed and there is an urgency to fill the positions. Mayor Martell stated that the plan is to allow for the opening of five consultant childcare attendant positions, for a flyer to be distributed town wide, and for a special meeting to be called once the applicants have been chosen. Councilwoman Rodriguez asked for clarification on the intent to hire consultants. It was explained that the Town would hire independent employees that would perform the same duties, but they would be 1099 employees like the current tutor. Mrs. Rodriguez continued to suggest that the hires be at least college age, and that because she was not given supporting documentation, she was not fully prepared to recommend anything further. Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion as follows, TO RETAIN FIVE (5) CONSULTANTS FOR CHILD CARE ATTENDANT POSITIONS FOR THE SOCIAL SERVICES AND PARKS AND RECREATION DEPARTMENT Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and further discussion was held. Director Valido explained that there have been over eight vacancies in the department and further stated that her preference would be not to hire consultants. Councilperson Pacheco then suggested to hire six employees. Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that there could be political implications to restricting the applicant pool, to consultants when it could be anticipated that Town residents apply for the positions. Councilwoman Pacheco added that the positions require qualified individuals. Councilwoman Rodriguez stated the importance of not rushing these matters and providing documentation to support discussion. Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that this proposal is to eliminate hiring employees that the Town would be required to provide benefits. Councilperson Pacheco then asked if this matter can be further discussed ina shade meeting, and it was clarified by attorney Pizzi that this matter needs to be discussed and acted upon in this public forum as dictated under the sunshine law. Councilperson Pacheco rescinded his motion. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Rodriguez placed a motion as follows, A MOTION TO HIRE FOUR (4) PART-TIME CHILD CARE ATTENDANT POSITIONS FOR THE SOCIAL SERVICES AND PARKS AND RECREATION DEPARTM

votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion passed unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 8:12 pm.
segs.text: - Finance Director Report on the Town of Medley Community Pool. Finance Director Charmaine Parchment approached the Council and stated that she has received the cost associated with adjusting the community pool opening hours as requested in the December Council meeting. Ms. Parchment further stated that from March 1** to November 2024, the cost estimate is $109,950 and that $50,000 budgeted is already budgeted for the summer, leaving a shortage of approximately $ 60,000. Director Parchment requested direction on the allocations to budget the needed funding for this directive. Councilwoman Rodriguez asked for a monthly breakdown, and it was stated that from March to June 2024 the cost is quoted at $41,600, from July to September 2024 is $47,200, and lastly $ 21,150 for October 1 to November 24, 2024. It was noted that the last range of October through November would fall into the 2024/2025 fiscal year s budget, therefore the Town only needs to budget funds for the remaining $44,400. Attorney Pizzi recommended, that at minimum, the Town Council should meet twice a year to discuss a budget amendment, such as in this occasion where the Council can have the opportunity to review the numbers once again and determine priorities and expenses. Councilwoman Rodriguez then suggested that the $ 50,000 previously budgeted for summer be used to cover the expenses of opening the pool in March which would allow for the Town Council to then meet and further discuss a budget amendment to cover the remaining cost of extending the community pool hours. After the instruction to staff was clarified, said instructions were agreed upon unanimously by the Council. Since there was no other business to address, Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion passed unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 8:12 pm. ie id Tr aii iain FRP, CMC, Town Clerk ell, Mayor
