segs.text: Resolution C-2176 Amending the Town of Medley Budget for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 to Increase the Funding and Budgeted Amount Allocated to Provide for Additional Compensation of Town Employees; Authorizing the Town Mayor and Town Officials to Implement the Amendments to the Town of Medley Budget for Fiscal Year 2023- 2024; and Providing for an Effective Date. Councilwoman Rodriguez asked for clarification on the employee s dollar increase. Mayor Martell explained that the increase would not apply to employees who have received a raise within the year, or managerial positions such as directors and assistant directors. It was stated that three employees were excluded due to receiving raises within the year and Councilwoman Rodriguez urged the Council and requested that the three individuals be included in the increase. Finance Director Charmaine Parchment approached the Council and clarified that the total cost for the increase is $37,000.00, up until September 30, 2024. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked if the budget is being amended solely for the employe increase, but it was stated that there are other revenues and expenditures that were included in the amendment. In addition, Councilwoman Rodriguez asked for clarification on the amended budget and the allocation previously set aside for the Capital Improvements Projects department, including the professional fees expenditures. It was explained that the department previously had 5 employees and it is now handled by consultants, thus the allocations were adjusted accordingly. Town attorney Michael Pizzi explained that before the budget for FY 2024-2025 is adopted, a capital improvements projects workshop will be held to go over all pending projects in detail which will provide the Town Council an opportunity to assess and make changes to open projects should they wish to. Mayor Martell proceeded to place a motion to approved Resolution C-2176 as presented, Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion. Councilwoman Rodriguez then placed a motion to amend Resolution C-2176 to include the (3) employees that have been excluded from the increase. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously. Mayor Martell then withdrew his initial motion on this item and Councilperson Pacheco withdrew his second as well. Additionally, Mayor Martell then placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2176 with the previous amendment. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously.

No public comments were made. - Discussion on the Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2024, through September 30, 2025. Town Attorney Pizzi began the discussion and explained that the millage rate to be set by the Council tonight would preliminarily cap that number. Thus, the Council could set a lower rate but cannot go past the preliminary millage rate. Finance Director Charmaine Parchment discussed the Town s preliminary 2024-2025 budget and announced the 2024 certified taxable property value to be $5,795,357,513 which reflects an increase of $602,757,161 in taxable property value. Director Parchment further stated that the recommended millage rate for fiscal year 2024-2025 is 3.2 mills per $1,000 and reiterated that the millage rate can be lowered but not set any higher than the preliminary millage rate. Additionally, director Parchment stated a gross tax revenue of $2,967.342. Director Parchment also discussed the preliminary 2024-2025 general fund s revenues and expenses, as well as the budget timeline for fiscal year 2024-2025. Director Parchment further informed the Council that a final budget recommendation will be given prior to the first budget hearing in September. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez announced that the first budget public hearing is scheduled to be held on Tuesday September 10, 2024 at 6:00 pm and the second and last public hearing is scheduled for Tuesday September 24, 2024, also at 6:00 pm. Councilwoman Rodriguez asked for clarification on several departmental budget revenues presented on the draft preliminary budget circulated to the Council. Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed that it is necessary to pay close attention to the funds allocated to all departments for office supplies and postage needs. Councilwoman Rodriguez further stated that the professional fees, especially the $ 550,000 proposed for the capital improvement projects department, and overall IT consultant fees were also high. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi explained that the presented budget is preliminary and agreements for these services can be reviewed and reassessed before the budget for fiscal year 2024-2025 is adopted. - Discussion on the Proposed Tentative Millage Rate Based Upon the Certification of Taxable Value of Real and Personal Property Within the Town of Medley

segs.head: - Section 13.
segs.text: - Section 13. Public Facilities and Concurrency. Additionally, Councilwoman Rodriguez asked why the contract is being re-negotiated if it is not close to its expiration date. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Part-Time Social Services Coordinator Position (Reclassification) for the Social Services and Parks and Recreation Department.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Part-Time Social Services Coordinator Position (Reclassification) for the Social Services and Parks and Recreation Department. Social Services and Parks and Recreation director Lizmari Valido approached the Council and stated that she did not request this item, therefore does not have anything to provide to the Council. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked for clarification stating that the item did not include a recommendation memo stating the name of the person recommended to be reclassified. Director Valido stated the need for her department to have an afterschool supervisor, but the proposed item is for a social services coordinator position which would assist in covering reception and the assigned personnel would be away from her department. Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed that it is troublesome if the recommendation does not come from the supervisor and would be happy to further discuss this item and bring it back at a later day. Councilwoman Rodriguez further stated that due to lack of supporting documentation, she cannot support this item. Vice-Mayor Ayala encouraged the administration to consider the supervisor's recommendations when dealing with the reclassification of employees. Vice Mayor Ayala continued to suggest tabling the item. Mayor Martell stated that he met with director Valido and instructed her to recommend someone for the position, and Amy Carballo was director Valido's selection. Director Valido stated that although she agreed that Ms. Carballo was qualified to fulfill the position, she did not agree with the position Ms. Carballo is being reclassified too. After a brief discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT AMY CARBALLO TO THE POSITION OF PART-TIME SOCIAL SERVICES COORDINATOR FOR THE SOCIAL SERVICES AND PARKS AND RECREATION DEPARTMENT" Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala- Yes Councilmember Karina Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Lizelh Rodriguez-No The motion was carried by majority of vote.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Full-Time Economic Development Coordinator Position(Reclassification) for the Capital Improvement Projects Department. Town Attorney Pizzi stated that the Social Services and Parks and Recreation department just received approval to hire a coordinator and no longer needs the services Mr. Michael Salem's provides for the department. Mr. Pizzi continued to state that Mr. Salem is currently assisting multiple departments with his many years of experience,therefore proving to be an asset by other means for the Town. Thus,to fit an accurate job description for the work Mr. Salem is currently doing for the Town,the recommendation is to appoint Mr. Salem to the position of economic development coordinator. Vice Mayor Ayala noted that this matter contradicts the process that has been established for the addition of items to the agenda, and that the item did not include any backup documentation. Vice-Mayor Ayala encouraged the administration to correct this method. It was clarified that Mr. Salem would no longer have the title of assistant to the social services and parks and recreation department. Vice Mayor Ayala placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT MICHAEL SALEM TO THE POSITION OF FULL-TIME ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COORDINATOR FOR THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS DEPARTMENT" Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO INSTRUCT THE LEGAL AND POLICE DEPARTMENT TO LOOK INTO THE ABILITY TO IMPLEMENT A POLICY TO PROHIBIT CARRYING FIREARMS WITHIN THE LAKESIDE RETIREMENT PARK RECREATIONAL CENTER" Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on Public Safety and Prohibition to Carry Firearms at the Town of Medley Lakeside Retirement Park. Councilperson Pacheco stated that his intent is to prohibit firearms from being entered into the Lakeside Retirement Home Recreational Center. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked if the proposal by councilmen Pacheco can legally be done. Chief Jeanette Said-Jinete approached the Council and clarified that the proposed item requires legal review to confirm that the Town would not violate citizen's second amendment right to carry. Attorney Pizzi explained that the state of Florida has become a constitutional carry state and municipalities have constrained ability to restrict the carrying of firearms. After a brief discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO INSTRUCT THE LEGAL AND POLICE DEPARTMENT TO LOOK INTO THE ABILITY TO IMPLEMENT A POLICY TO PROHIBIT CARRYING FIREARMS WITHIN THE LAKESIDE RETIREMENT PARK RECREATIONAL CENTER" Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MARCH 12, 2024 A public meeting was called to order on March 12, 2024, at 6:14 p.m. the following were present: MAYOR: ROBERTO MARTELL VICE-MAYOR: EDGAR AYALA COUNCIL MEMBERS: IVAN PACHECO KARINA PACHECO LIZELH RODRIGUEZ TOWN CLERK: VICTORIA MARTINEZ TOWN ATTORNEY: MICHAEL A. PIZZI Town Attorney Michael Pizzi started the meeting referring to a power point presentation (see the attached) that was circulated and discussed in detail. Attorney Pizzi further explained the principles and importance of parliamentary law such as quorum, orderly conduct, decorum, the right of transparent debate, and the duties and responsibilities of the chair/presiding officer in council meetings. It was also explained that Robert Rules of Order serves as a default provision, but the Town s rules and procedures govern since adopted as its own. The rules of order were discussed as well as the role of the Town attorney as the parliamentarian during these proceedings which is advisory and consultative in nature. The point of order and point of personal privilege were explained along with the Citizens Bill of Rights which protects an individual s right to speak especially during the public comment section of a public meeting. The role of the Sergeant in Arms and the distinction of disruptive and unruly behaviors were explained to determine the types of conduct that could potentially result in ones removal from a public meeting. In addition, the proposed language for the Town s amendment to the Council meeting procedures were discussed and was stated that the Council could propose any additional language and/or changes deemed necessary, including but not limited to mechanisms that address the removal of an elected official when the chair/presiding officer enforces said right. Since there was no further matters to address, Mayor Martell made a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 7:47 pm.

segs.text: Resolution C-2148 Amending Resolution C-1478 Adopting Town Council Meeting and Agenda Procedures ; Amending Section II Procedural Rules ; Providing for Implementation and Providing for an Effective Date. Vice-Mayor Ayala began the discussion by proposing the following changes to the agenda procedures as presented. His first proposal was to instruct staff to purchase a timer and to assign the Town Clerk to monitor and enforce the allocated three minute per public comment rule. Additionally, Vice-Mayor Ayala proposed that language be added to the presiding officer duties section, stating that the chair would advise the public that their comments must not be personal in nature, but they should address the board in its entirety. Lastly, Vice-Mayor Ayala reiterated his comment made during the Council Workshop proposing language to exempt elected officials from expulsion of the Council Chambers. Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed her agreement with the proposals and stated that she hopes for the Council to have healthy debate on items while acting professional with one another. Councilperson Pacheco agreed with proposal to purchase a timer, but suggested the Mayor oversee monitoring the public comment time. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi suggested language that would fulfill the purpose of Vice-Mayor Ayala s intent. Therefore, it was agreed upon to add language as follows, In order for a public official to be removed, the public official must engage in acts of violence or if after several warnings, the elected official continues to act in a disruptive manner. Without further discussion, Vice-Mayor Ayala placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2148 with the agreed upon changes to the language. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Part-Time Meal Program Driver/Helper/Attendant for the Town of Medley Hot Meal Department. Mayor Martell announced that he would recuse himself from the discussion and action of this matter due to a conflict of interest. A recess was had at 7:24 pm and the meeting resumed at 7:26 pm with all councilmembers present. Vice-Mayor Ayala then announced the item open for discussion. Councilperson Pacheco then proceeded to place a motion as follows, TO APPROVE MS. EULALIA E. LOPEZ FOR THE POSITION OF PART-TME MEAL PROGRAM DRIVER/HELPER/ATTENDANT. Motion was not carried due to lack of a second motion. Vice-Mayor Ayala then continued to address the item presented and the need of the meal program to hire additional personnel. It was explained that due to the Council s previous instructions to adjust the language requirement currently as Fluent English Speaking on the job description, many of the applicants do not qualify. Therefore, the applicant pool for selection was very small. Thus, Vice-Mayor Ayala proposed to reverse the previous motion and modify the language on the job description to state, effectively communicate in the English language. It was announced that the item for which the Mayor had recused himself was no longer on the floor for consideration and was closed. Therefore, Mayor Martell was called to re-enter the Council Chambers to join in on the discussion of Vice-Mayor Ayala s proposal. Vice-Mayor Ayala reiterated his proposal and further suggested that the Council review applications from qualified individuals that did not meet the prior language requirement. Fatima Fuentes, Director of the Meal Program joined the discussion to explain that the hiring process began in September of last year, and more than 70 applications have been received thus far. Director Fuentes further explained that due to the language requirements many did not qualify and out of 10 qualified applicants, only two individuals showed up for the interview process and the previously selected applicant was one of those two interviewed. Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed her agreement with Vice-Mayor Ayala s proposal to consider a less stringent language requirement for certain positions and to require fluent English language for more professional positions such as those in the general administration. segs.head: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MARCH 18, 2024 A public meeting of the Town of Medley was opened on March 18, 2024, at 5:30 p.m.
segs.text: MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA MARCH 18, 2024 A public meeting of the Town of Medley was opened on March 18, 2024, at 5:30 p.m. Jose Lopez, Director of Environmental Engineering, Project Manager, and a representative of Bermello, Ajamil & Partners, opened the meeting and addressed the audience stating that the purpose of this second public meeting is to present and explain the vulnerable areas identified in the Resiliency Assessment and Adaptation Action Plan study to be able to mitigate them in the future. Mr. Lopez further conducted a presentation of the Adaptation Action Plan Strategies (see attached) which included essential information such as focus areas, risks and impacts, adaptation strategies and projects selected to seek funding in accordance with priorities. It was explained in detail how the risks of loss of power, natural resources, flooding, and social disruption amongst others, seriously impact the Town. In continuance, Mr. Lopez detailed the adaptation action strategies for the Town to promote mitigation of the existing risks, including but not limited to drainage improvements, floodplain protection, relocation of utilities and integrated surface water management, and flood control pump stations. A list of Town projects was explained in detail for purposes of funding and impact strategy. To conclude, it was further explained that the main goal is to encourage safer and more resilient community development through policy and enforcement as well as seeking funding sources and working with other agencies such as South Florida Water Management and Miami-Dade County to maximize efforts. Isis Acuna resident of 8181 NW South River Drive, Lot E534 stated several concerns such as how the Town should have a way to provide public notices Townwide and how she was unaware that the Town has TSA check in and was manually searched when attending a public meeting. Additionally, Ms. Acuna commented on the elected official s behavior towards one another, and lastly, her concern for the lack of human resources in the Town. To conclude Ms. Aleman stated that the Council should consider resuming services with the current food provider. segs.text: Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that although the Mayor had called for this special meeting, the last decision taken by the Council on this matter was to have a Council workshop to discuss the financial options in funding the price increase. Vice-Mayor Ayala thanked Councilwoman Pacheco for her support on that matter. It was explained that the food service provider sent an email notifying the Town of the suspension of the services indefinitely, not leaving room for discussion. However, the purpose of the meeting is to address the renewal of the contract. Vice-Mayor Ayala further stated that the amount of the price increase was not budgeted for. Therefore, the Council must consider solutions to cover the finance shortfall of the remaining months of March through September 2024 and until the new fiscal year budget is approved and adjusted to include the increase. Vice-Mayor Ayala then proposed that the finance shortfall be absorbed by the Council s contribution of a seven percent of each member s salary to cover said additional cost. Councilwoman Rodriguez joined the discussion and stated that certain members of the public and residents received a correspondence titled Emergency Meeting to Continue the Hot Meal Program Come to Meeting This Wednesday at 5:15pm at Town Hall and read said correspondence into the record as follows, Dear Medley Neighbor, I have called an emergency Town meeting for Wednesday March 20" at 5:15pm in the Town Council Chambers, 7777 NW 72"4 Ave, on the second floor. I will be asking the Town Council to continue to provide your family with high quality food under the meal program. If the Town council does not vote to renew the hot meal contract this Wednesday Medley residents may stop getting their food starting Monday. We cannot allow anyone cancel the meal program and take away your food. Please come to the Town Council Meeting this Wednesday and make sure that you tell the Town Council to continue the meal program that provides food to all your Medley families. As long as 1 am Mayor, I will make sure that the Town of Medley residents continue to receive the best quality meals that are with the pride of this community. God bless you and your families very truly yours the Mayor. Mayor Martell announced that he would recuse himself from the discussion and action on this matter due to a conflict of interest. Therefore, Attorney Pizzi explained that the third district court of appeal issued an opinion related to this instance in which to hold quorum the Town Council needs to have three voting members. However, in the instance where there is a total of three elected officials, and one recuses the body loses quorum. Attorney Pizzi further stated that given the circumstances, this matter could no longer be addressed and would be tabled for another meeting of the Town Council. segs.text: - Request by Councilwoman Rodriguez for Discussion and Action on Public Meetings: Protocols and Decorum. Councilwoman Rodriguez began the discussion by addressing the memorandum circulated to the Council in reference to public meetings, protocols, and decorum. Councilwoman then continued to read the memorandum into the record as follows, The purpose of this memorandum is to express my deep concern with the format in which public meetings have been taking place. At the most recent council meeting on February 21, 2024, we witnessed the unprofessionalism in its highest form and a violation of our right to speak as elected officials. By limiting the legislative body from having on-going discussions is a violation of our rights as elected officials. Most importantly, it infringes on our First Amendment rights. As someone who loves this county and honors the sacrifices of our founding fathers, I will not continue to tolerate this behavior, which has only worsened since I joined this council in November 2020. The practice of limiting open discussions in public meetings is a threat to the democratic process that makes the United States the great nation that it is. I encourage this administration to honor the oath we took and stop this practice as it is detrimental to the duties of an elected official. Councilwoman Rodriguez further stated her disagreement with the actions taken by the administration after the last meeting which directed staff to take steps that do not follow the Town s Charter. Councilwoman Rodriguez then continued to place a motion as follows, TO ALLOW ALL ELECTED OFFICIALS THE ABILITY TO SPEAK DURING THE DISCUSSION PERIOD FOR ALL AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor Martell then requested that the Town attorney clarify the matter. Attorney Pizzi explained that the administration plans to have a Council workshop to educate and discuss the protocols and procedures for public meetings with the elected body. Attorney Pizzi further stated that after receiving said training, the Council could vote upon any modifications they wish to make to the Town Council meeting and agenda procedures. Vice-Mayor Ayala expressed his support for the Police Department and stated that he does not agree with the retaliatory action taken against the police department after the last council meeting. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 112.3143, FLORIDA STATUTES A person holding elective or appointive county, municipal, or other local public office MUST ABSTAIN from voting on a measure which would inure to his or her special private gain or loss. Each elected or appointed local officer also MUST ABSTAIN from knowingly voting on a measure which would inure to the special gain or loss of a principal (other than a government agency) by whom he or she is retained (including the parent, subsidiary, or sibling organization of a principal by which he or she is retained); to the special private gain or loss of a relative; or to the special private gain or loss of a business associate. Commissioners of community redevelopment agencies (CRAs) under Sec. 163.356 or 163.357, F.S., and officers of independent special tax districts elected on a one-acre, one-vote basis are not prohibited from voting in that capacity. For purposes of this law, a relative includes only the officer's father, mother, son, daughter, husband, wife, brother, sister, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law, and daughter-in-law. A business associate means any person or entity engaged in or carrying on a business enterprise with the officer as a partner, joint venturer, coowner of property, or corporate shareholder (where the shares of the corporation are not listed on any national or regional stock exchange). segs.head: - Presentation on"Freebee Medley"Program Proposal Claudia Miro, Business Development and Government Affairs representative with Freebie and with office located at 371 NE 61 Street Miami approached the Council and gave a brief presentation of the on-demand transportation services and what it can offer to the Town as a micro transit door to door service.
segs.text: - Presentation on"Freebee Medley"Program Proposal Claudia Miro, Business Development and Government Affairs representative with Freebie and with office located at 371 NE 61 Street Miami approached the Council and gave a brief presentation of the on-demand transportation services and what it can offer to the Town as a micro transit door to door service. It was emphasized that the Freebie transportation services can be personalized based on the residential populations needs. Additionally, it was noted that grant funding by the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) has been awarded to the Town of Medley for services such as Freebie to offset the costs for the first three years. It was also noted that the desired wait time would determine the amount of vehicles needed, thus the overall cost for the services. Ms. Miro also stated that due to the grant fund disbursement schedule, it was suggested to initiate the program in July, with an estimated total cost of$100,000.00 per year for which the FDOT grant would cover 50% of the expense totaling to about $50,000 to the Town. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi stated that after negotiations the Town was able to get Waste Management to increase their host fee from $15,000 a year to $75,000 a year thus providing an avenue to offset the Town's expense associated with this service. In addition, attorney Pizzi stated that under the live local act, one of the requirements of the new palmetto station project is to donate to the Town of Medley for transportation related matters such as the Freebie transportation services. A consensus of the Town Council was had to instruct the Town attorney to negotiate terms allowing for one year of service and bring back a contract with Freebie once the details have been finalized. The Public Hearing items section of the agenda were then announced. The items were read into the record, addressed, discussed, and acted upon as follows.

segs.text: Resolution C-2161 Denying a Variance of the Alcoholic Beverages Requirements of Chapter 5, Section 5-3(d) of the Medley Municipal Code for Property Located at 11590 N.W. South River Drive. Paytagai Stewart, General Manager for WAWA located at 11590 NW South River Dr, Medley, FL 33178 approached the Council to respond to any questions or concerns. It was clarified that the resolution presented reflected a denial to the variance application which determined that the variance could not be granted in accordance with the Town's Code of Ordinances. Mayor Martell suggested to amend the Town code to extend the hours of the permitted alcoholic beverage sales. Attorney Pizzi recommended, upon Council approval, to approve the changes to the alcoholic beverage requirements section of the Town code, therefore the approval will apply to all business and not only to WAWA. Ms. Stewart joined the discussion and stated that WAWA is dedicated to the community and will abide by the laws and/or conditions imposed by the Town regarding the selling of alcoholic beverages. Councilperson Pacheco expressed his disagreement to approving the application and changing the hours of alcohol permitted sales. - After a brief discussion, Vice-Mayor Ayala made a motion to approve the variance application reflected in Resolution C-2161 and to approving said variance application with the following conditions, a. The applicant shall be limited to the sale of beer and wine alcoholic beverages only from 11:01 am through and until 12:00 am. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously. The next order of business was the First Reading of the Ordinances section of the agenda. segs.head: Ordinance C-481 Amending Chapter 29- Environment, Article IV- "Water Conservation" of the Town of Medley Code of Ordinances to Provide for Local Implementation of the Mandatory Year-Round Landscape Irrigation Conservation Measures Rule of the South Florida Water Management District (40E-24, F.A.C.); Providing Definitions; Providing for the Applicability of the Ordinance; Providing the Landscape Irrigation Schedule; Providing Exceptions to the Landscape Irrigation Schedule; Providing for a Requirement to Operate Technology that Inhibits or Interrupts an Irrigation System During Periods of Suffi

segs.text: Ordinance C-481 Amending Chapter 29- Environment, Article IV- "Water Conservation" of the Town of Medley Code of Ordinances to Provide for Local Implementation of the Mandatory Year-Round Landscape Irrigation Conservation Measures Rule of the South Florida Water Management District (40E-24, F.A.C.); Providing Definitions; Providing for the Applicability of the Ordinance; Providing the Landscape Irrigation Schedule; Providing Exceptions to the Landscape Irrigation Schedule; Providing for a Requirement to Operate Technology that Inhibits or Interrupts an Irrigation System During Periods of Sufficient Moisture; Providing for Variances from the Specific Day of the Week Limitations; Providing for Enforcement of the Ordinance; Providing for Penalties for Violation of the Ordinance; Providing for Codification; Providing for the Repeal of All Conflicting Ordinances; Providing for Severability; and Providing for an Effective Date. Town Attorney Pizzi explained that the South Florida Water Management District regulates water consumption, and all municipalities still have internal regulations codified,whereas Medleys is detailed in Chapter 29 of the Town Code. In addition, attorney Pizzi stated that periodically the South Florida Water Management District will implement changes to the regulations for the benefit of water consumption. Therefore, the Town needs to make changes to the legislation as presented, to reflect the new regulations. Vice-Mayor Ayala placed a motion to approve the first reading of Ordinance C-481. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Emergency Notifications Systems/Methods Councilwoman Rodriguez addressed the Council and expressed the urgency to have a form of communication with the residents for notifications such as utility emergencies or any other matters of emergency in nature.
votes: Councilwoman Rodriguez placed a motion as follows, "TO INSTRUCT THE CHIEF OF POLICE TO RESEARCH AND EXTEND THE USE OF THE POLICE DEPARTMENT'S EMERGENCY NOTIFICATION SYSTEM TO THE UTILITIES AND PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENTS FOR MATTERS RELATED TO UTILITES, PUBLIC WORKS AND EMERGENCIES IN NATURE." Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Emergency Notifications Systems/Methods Councilwoman Rodriguez addressed the Council and expressed the urgency to have a form of communication with the residents for notifications such as utility emergencies or any other matters of emergency in nature. Mayor Martell explained that the Riverstone management office for the 8181 area has a system to send out notifications. Mayor Martell then suggested using their system and notifying them whenever there is a utility emergency so they can send out notification messages to their tenants. Chief Said-Jinete then approached the Council and explained that the Police Department has a notification system through the Florida Department of Emergency Management called Everbridge that provides notification services, but the funding ends after June of this year. Councilwoman Rodriguez explained that she is a resident of the 8181 mobile home park and has never received the Riverstone management notifications, and once again urged for the Council's support for the use of CodeRed, the Town's previous notification system management software. Councilwoman Rodriguez further stated that although something had occurred with CodeRed,it is pivotal to have a form of communication with the residents for emergency matters. It was then agreed upon by the Town Council to research the use of the Medley police department's emergency management software to be used for the purpose of disseminating emergency information to Town of Medley residents. Therefore, Councilwoman Rodriguez placed a motion as follows, "TO INSTRUCT THE CHIEF OF POLICE TO RESEARCH AND EXTEND THE USE OF THE POLICE DEPARTMENT'S EMERGENCY NOTIFICATION SYSTEM TO THE UTILITIES AND PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENTS FOR MATTERS RELATED TO UTILITES, PUBLIC WORKS AND EMERGENCIES IN NATURE." Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley & University of Miami Alzheimer's Research Event Councilwoman Rodriguez began the discussion by asking the Council to view the draft flyer for the Town of Medley and University of Miami Alzheimer's Research event and asked for input. Councilwoman Rodriguez further stated that the event consists in 2 separate events in which the first event could be hosted at the Lakeside Retirement Center,possibly on June 22,2024 commencing at 1:00 pm. Councilwoman Rodriguez continued to explain that the first event includes food and interactive bingo and that any interested party, once enrolled in the research study, would be entitled to a $ 50.00 study compensation. Councilwoman Rodriguez also stated that the second event will constitute of the presentation of the study. It was agreed upon by the Council to allow the tentative date of June 22' 2024 for this event and Councilperson Pacheco agreed to not host the previously scheduled bingo event on that date. The Town Council further agreed on the two proposed separate events, for the Town to provide transportation for both events, and the proposed designated location. Vice-Mayor Ayala then began a discussion about garbage collection and garbage trash can placement on the section of South River Drive where there is one-way traffic. Attorney Pizzi explained that the Town has a new person in charge of residential trash pick up and the new coordinator wanted to come and see the Mayor, Vice-Mayor, and Council to address any questions and concerns. Since there was no other business to address, Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion to adjourn was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 8:40 pm. Town Attorney Pizzi explained that the proposed item is for the approval to receive a grant of $132,000 to support the Freebie on-demand transportation program. It was noted that this is a matching grant, therefore the Town must match 50% which the Town has agreed to do with CITT funding as well as other donations received from business like Waste Management. Mayor Stefano expressed concerns with the boundaries of the Freebie transportation program. Attorney Pizzi informed the Council that the Town will discuss with Freebie the expansion of limits to frequently visited locations by the residents, such as the local Walmart, or a commonly visited medical clinic. Councilperson Ayala stated that the Town previously provided transportation services that many residents benefitted and preferred using. It was clarified that the Town is currently using alternative transportation services to assist residents. Vice-Mayor Jinete made a motion to approve Resolution C-2202. Mayor Stefano seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.text: r MINUTES OF A PUBLIC MEETING OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY, FLORIDA NOVEMBER 7, 2024 A Council Swearing-In ceremony of the Town of Medley, Florida was held on November 7, 2024 at 7:08 pm. The following were present, Mayor Elect: Ana L. segs.text: - Page 4 Section 9.2 language added, In connection with his employment as Chief of Police under this agreement the employee agrees that he will not re-enroll in the Town s DROP program upon completion . Interim Chief of Police Jack Young agreed with the proposed changes as stated by the Town Attorney. Councilwoman Rodriguez asked for clarification on the impact the salary and DROP program proposed for this item, and it was stated that the DROP program is for a three-year period offered Minutes of October 21, 2024 Special Council Meeting to all eligible employees and currently Chief Young has one remaining year where he will continue to receive his retirement benefit. It was further explained that the Town Council can extend the period of the DROP program. Additionally, it was stated that any employee participating in the DROP program will continue to receive their salary while working and concurrently receive their retirement benefit which is deposited into their DROP fund which is received at the end of their DROP period. Vice-Mayor Ayala then proposed to extend the contract terms by two months so its expiration date would fall in the month of January to which the Mayor and Council expressed their agreement. Therefore, the Town Clerk was instructed to include changes to section B2.1 to the term of the agreement as proposed by Vice- Mayor Ayala. Councilwoman Rodriguez then asked for clarification on the employees salary in its entirety when calculating both the DROP benefit and the proposed salary amount. After a brief recess Attorney Pizzi announced that Chief Young s salary under the contracted amount retroactive to October 7, 2024, is $166,254.59 as shown on section 4.1 of the contract. Town attorney Pizzi further stated that the DROP program contributes a payment of $11,374.80 monthly into the DROP pension fund to be received once he takes his retirement at the end of the three-year period. Thus, the total of both the contract amount and the DROP pension contribution is $302,752.19 annually. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVING AN EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT FOR POLICE CHIEF OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY WITH JACK A YOUNG, WITH THE CHANGES PRESENTED AS FOLLOWS, 1. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi addressed Mr. Aaron Parkinson co-owner of Xtreme Action Park and announced the sponsorship of an annual free entry event to Xtreme Action Park for the Medley Youth Social Club and the Town of Medley Police Explorers. The Mayor and Council then thanked Mr. Parkinson for his generous donation. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez then announced the rules of conduct for the public comment section of the agenda. Therefore, the public comment section of the meeting was then announced. Andrew Axelrod, residing at 1971 SW 32 Place, Miami FL 33145 approached the Council and stated that although he works for the PBA, he comes as a member of the public to speak on item 13(A)2 of the agenda. Mr. Axelrod further explained that it is a false legal opinion to state that it is not a violation or aconflict for candidate s to vote on a contract for the spouse of an opposing candidate and further urged that item 13(A) 2: Discussion and Action on the Renewal of an Employment Agreement for Police Chief of the Town of Medley to be tabled until a formal opinion from the commission on ethics be received, and at a minimum, there is an appearance of impropriety. Additionally, Mr. Axelrod stated that item 12F was deferred due to the appearance of impropriety and that same reasoning should apply to item 13.A.2. Lastly, Mr. Axelrod stated that it is shameful for the Council to consider the termination of the contract with the Chief after her many years of service to the Town, whereas the decision is not performance based but solely personal and shameful. David Greenwell, residing at 10680 NW 28 St., explained how lucky the Town of Medley is because Chief Said-Jinete is one of the hardest, hardworking, and sacrificing individuals and that the Town Council is considering on doing something terrible. Mr. Greenwell continued to state that he has been a police officer for forty-two years, and second vice president of the Police Benevolent Association (PBA) dealing with thousands of police officers, police chiefs, and municipalities and stated that the Town of Medley has one of the best police chiefs in South Florida, who should be commended for her hard work and has made the community proud. Attorney Pizzi explained that the Town has been cited for non-compliance by the State of Florida Department of Environmental Protection, and since then the Town have reach full compliance thus mitigated a much lower fine to be paid. Councilwoman Rodriguez stated that although reaching compliance is the goal, the Town s job is to be fiscally responsible and in compliance prior to there being fines issued. segs.text: Resolution C-2198 Declaring State of Emergency Town of Medley- Hurricane Milton. Attorney Pizzi stated that the proposed Resolution would authorize the Town to take steps towards emergency services and allows the Council s input for the emergency readiness. Mayor Martell stated that public works and maintenance departments were assisting senior citizens with the installation of their shutters and that with continued monitoring it will be determined whether the Town facilities will open for the remainder of the week which at that point, information will be circulated to staff and Council. It was also clarified that the Town does not provide sandbags, and Councilwoman Rodriguez requested that the Town reach out to Miami-Dade County to see what resources are made available to municipalities for assistance. segs.head: * Michael Salem - Grants / Economic Development Coordinator Capengineerin: Executive Summary C.A.P.
segs.text: * Michael Salem - Grants / Economic Development Coordinator Capengineerin: Executive Summary C.A.P. Engineering, Inc. (CAP) was charged with the responsibility to work closely with the Town of Medley CIP Department to review and assess the progress of on-going and new projects with an emphasis on those that have grants. We were to schedule and provide recommendations, and to revise prioritization schedules, as necessary. CAP reviewed all the available documents and assessed the status of each project, this included: project progress, reporting, extensions, progress of achievements to date, identification of problems, and other issues. Our goal remains to provide engineering support, project management, restructuring of project priorities, troubleshooting, and other technical assistance. CAP is to support engineers, contractors and other stakeholders, as may be needed to ensure timely completion of all projects. Upon completion of the review, CAP found that the current schedule prioritization is based on grant projects which we highly recommend. CAP was instrumental in enhancing current levels of documentation to ensure timely compliance and achievements of each project goals. All current projects are up to date and moving forward towards timely completion. segs.text: - Discussion and Establishment of a Proposed Tentative Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2024, through September 30, 2025. Finance Director Charmaine Parchment presented an overview of the proposed budget for fiscal year 2024-2025 which detailed the expected revenues and expenses. Ms. Parchment continued to state that the Town has already tentatively established a millage rate of 3.2 mills and announced the ad valorem revenue as $18,545,144.00. Director Parchment further stated that the budget is at 95% of the expected Minutes of September 10, 2024 Special Council Meeting- 1' Budget Public Hearing revenue in the amount of $17,617.887.00 projecting an increase in revenue of $2.9 million and that the roll back rate is 2.6671 mills per $1,000.00. Additionally, it was announced that the 2024 taxable property value is $5,795,357,513 whereas the 2023 taxable property value was $5,192,600,352 presenting a change of $602,757,161.00. In continuance with her presentation, Ms. Parchment went into detail on each the following key points,

segs.head: - Capital Improvement Plan - FY 25 through FY 29 - Projects by Year Summary Vice-Mayor Ayala asked for clarification on several matters reflected in the proposed fiscal year 2024- 2025 budget book.
segs.text: - Capital Improvement Plan - FY 25 through FY 29 - Projects by Year Summary Vice-Mayor Ayala asked for clarification on several matters reflected in the proposed fiscal year 2024- 2025 budget book. The Vice-Mayor then addressed page 27 and it was clarified that the term physical environment refers to the public works department. It was also noted that the departmental budget increased because of several proposed road resurfacing projects. Ms. Parchment stated that the total expenditure for all Town of Medley funds is $40,632,410.00. Vice-Mayor Ayala referred to page 35 and expressed his disagreement with the language under the budget highlights. Councilwoman Rodriguez joined the discussion and noted that throughout the proposed budget book there are numerous debt line items, therefore clarification was asked for the Town s total debt amount. Councilwoman Rodriguez then requested to include a line item within the proposed budget to indicate the Town s total debt amount because the line item did not exist. Additionally, Councilwoman Rodriguez noted a discrepancy in the language on page 38 defining the Mayor as the Chief Executive Officer and requested to correct the term to read in accordance with the Town Charter. Councilwoman Rodriguez then asked for information on the capital improvement department budget, and it was explained that two million dollars will be budgeted for the twelve projects included and for the completion of existing ongoing projects. Moreover, questions of salary wages were clarified. Vice-Mayor Ayala requested to amend page 16 to include Waste Management and Florida Wood as part of businesses located in the Town of Medley.

segs.head: Mayor Martell then opened the meeting for public comments.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE HIRING PROCESS FOR THREE (3) POLICE OFFICERS POSITIONS FOR THE MEDLEY POLICE DEPARTMENT. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: Mayor Martell then opened the meeting for public comments. It was noted that no comments were made. The agenda item was then read into the record, discussed, and acted upon as follows, - Discussion and Action on the Request to Hire Three (3) Replacement Police Officers for the Town of Medley Police Department. Councilperson Pacheco asked for clarification about the replacement positions and what officers were being replaced. Chief of Police Said-Jinete explained that two positions were to replace officer Joe Rodriguez and lieutenant Arturo Jinete who will be retiring, and the remaining position is a budgeted position previously approved by the Town Council when the recent annexation approval took place. Chief Said-Jinete further stated that one position will be brought back to Council for final approval in the month of October and the other two positions will be presented to the Town Council in December. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE HIRING PROCESS FOR THREE (3) POLICE OFFICERS POSITIONS FOR THE MEDLEY POLICE DEPARTMENT. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

Councilwoman Rodriguez then stated that September is Childhood Cancer Awareness Month and that she would be attending the Gold Ribbon parade where she will present a proclamation on behalf of the Town of Medley. Councilwoman Rodriguez extended an invitation to the Mayor, Vice Mayor and fellow Councilmembers and thanked the Medley Police Department for their support of the cause and participation on the parade. segs.head: - Check Presentation by Waste Management, Inc. to the Town of Medley Foundation.
segs.text: - Check Presentation by Waste Management, Inc. to the Town of Medley Foundation. Alex Gonzalez, representative of Waste Management and David Myhan, president of Waste Management Inc., of Florida residing at 6858 NW 58 St, Parkland Florida presented a ceremonial check in the amount of sixty thousand dollars ($ 60,000.00) and expressed their gratitude for the long-standing partnership between the Town of Medley and Waste Management. Both representatives thanked the Mayor and Council, as well as the Town of Medley community, for allowing Waste Management to contribute to the Medley Foundation and especially for taking part in the scholarships granted to the Medley residents. Mayor Martell thanked Waste Management for their continued support.

segs.text: Ordinance C-484 Amending Ordinance C-442 to Amend Chapter 62, Zoning , Section 62-66- Food Trucks of the Town of Medley Code of Ordinances to Revise the Regulations within the Permitted Locations; Providing for Codification; Providing for Severability; and Providing for an Effective Date. Councilwoman Rodriguez asked for clarification on this item, and it was explained that there has been an influx of food truck businesses in Medley, therefore prompting the need to change legislation limiting distances between same use businesses. Mr. Pizzi continued with an example which occurred in the City of Ft. Pierce where a court held in accordance with Florida law that limiting the distance from other operating businesses under the equal process division of Florida law was unconstitutional. Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-484 on first reading. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.text: Ordinance C-483 Providing an Amendment to Ordinance C-470, as Adopted on September 26, 2023, which Adopted and Approved the Budget of the Town of Medley, Florida for the Fiscal Year Beginning October 1, 2023 and Ending September 30, 2024; Acknowledging and Providing for Certain Modifications of Revenues; Authorizing Certain Modifications of Expenditure of Funds Appropriated in the Budget for Various Unanticipated Items; Repealing Conflicting Provisions in Ordinance C-470; Providing for Severability; and Providing for an Effective Date. Councilwoman Rodriguez addressed the item and asked for clarification and Finance Director Charmaine Parchment indicated, on the documentation provided, where the requested information could be located. Additionally, Councilwoman Rodriguez explained that there have been no progress reports given in over a year for the Capital Improvement Projects department and although a workshop is scheduled, she reiterated the importance of having periodical workshops providing project statuses and funding information prior to budget meetings. Director Parchment stated that this amendment is for fiscal year 2023/2024 and that the capital improvement projects meeting for September 10, 2024 will address project s status and expenditures and the impact to fiscal year 2024/2025. Councilwoman Rodriguez then asked about the financial implications associated with the two new development projects and it was explained that those projects would not affect the next fiscal year budget but may impact the budget in approximately four years. In addition, Director Parchment explained that she has been studying the interest amounts accrued on Town accounts, and after meeting and discussions held with several banks, said banks have increased the interest rates from 4% to 5% causing an increase in revenue. Vice-Mayor Ayala then requested a copy of the approved fee schedule from CAP and the fee schedule of MT Causley for cost comparison. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-483 on second reading. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously. segs.head: Resolution C-2188 Approving a Community Benefits Agreement between the Town of Medley and Magic Waste Youth Foundation, Inc., and Res-Des Palmetto, LLC for the Development of a Mixed-Use Workforce Housing Project; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Execute the Agreement; and Providing for an Effective Date.
segs.text: Resolution C-2188 Approving a Community Benefits Agreement between the Town of Medley and Magic Waste Youth Foundation, Inc., and Res-Des Palmetto, LLC for the Development of a Mixed-Use Workforce Housing Project; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Execute the Agreement; and Providing for an Effective Date. Town Attorney Pizzi began the discussion by explaining that the state of Florida passed the Live Local Act to address the affordable housing crisis which allowed developers to build and bypass the city processes with the condition that 60% of the dwellings be dedicated to workforce housing. Therefore, concurrent with Miami Dade rapid transit zones Miami-Dade County has negotiated agreements with developers to allow them to build multifaceted mixed-use buildings to be located near the palmetto metro station and the other near the animal shelter center in Medley. Mr. Pizzi continued to explain that he has met with the developers to discuss the matter, and they have agreed to assist the Town with its needs and that although the developers do not have to provide permits to the Town, the Town will still provide police and water services as well as zoning, planning and code enforcement services. In addition, Mr. Pizzi stated that said developers have agreed to not overwhelm the Town s social services programs and that they will pay for services such as water and any utilities upgrades that may be needed. It was also noted that the Town will receive the tax revenue. Mr. Jose Gonzalez, representative for both development projects approached the Council and explained that he and his partner Alex Rafita have been the first to create private development on a public zoning to create transit related development. Mr. Gonzalez further stated that together they have accomplished the approval for the development located at Palmetto station in partnership with Mr. Gus Cabrera with Resia development which will be the formal developer on the project. Mr. Gonzalez also stated that the palmetto station development will be 100% work force housing and that Red-Des is the name decided on for the partnership with Resia Development producing approximately 948 units with approximately a three-year build plan, including the installation of a new water and sewer system. Additionally, Mr. Gonzalez stated that there is a partnership with a Magic Waste Youth Foundation that assists individuals that have aged out of foster care who can live in these units if they qualify under certain condit
